engine:callClosureFuncType.description: Build a (externref^(N+1)) -> externref WasmFuncType for the $dyn: path's callClosure_<N> imports. N+1 because the closure handle is the first param.

engine:callDomainOf.label: Call domain of
engine:callDomainOf.description: Map a source-level call (fnId × arity) to its (argDomains, resultDomain) pair. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:callDomainOf — precise per-fnId typings for std arithmetic / comparison / boolean / concat / string ops, with a default `DomRef^arity → DomRef` for the runtime-helper fallback path.

engine:callMappingOf.label: Call mapping of
engine:callMappingOf.description: Fenel translation of compile-js.ts's CALL_MAPPING table. Maps a canonical codeName to its lowering shape (BinOp / Unary / Concat) or `NoMapping` (default `$fenel.<fnId>` fallback).

engine:callSiteClassifyParameter.label: Call-site classify one class parameter
engine:callSiteClassifyParameter.description: Read one class parameter back through the solved substitution and add it to the classification: a still-unknown parameter is unfixed, a nullary nominal is solved, anything else (an application, a structural type) is non-nominal.

engine:callSiteClassifyParameters.label: Call-site classify class parameters
engine:callSiteClassifyParameters.description: Classify every class parameter in class-header order (see callSiteClassifyParameter).

engine:callSiteMembershipActive.label: Call-site membership active
engine:callSiteMembershipActive.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — the μ variable of the innermost enclosing unfolding of the same application (same owner identity, structurally equal arguments), or Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipBind.label: Call-site membership bind
engine:callSiteMembershipBind.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — the environment under a μ or inline-opaque binder: the binder's source name now denotes the fresh variable, and the depth grows by one. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipBinderScope.label: Call-site membership binder scope
engine:callSiteMembershipBinderScope.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — pair a declaration's binders with an application's arguments, in order. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipFact.label: Call-site membership fact
engine:callSiteMembershipFact.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — the declaration fact of one owner identity, or Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipFreshName.label: Call-site membership fresh name
engine:callSiteMembershipFreshName.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — the fresh binder name for nesting depth n: `call-site μ` followed by n primes (built without rendering a number, so it is the same under every dispatch context). Two binders on one nesting chain never share a name, and an argument unfolded at depth n refers only to binders of smaller depth, so substitution cannot capture. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipNominal.label: Call-site membership nominal
engine:callSiteMembershipNominal.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — one resolved owner occurrence (a TtNamed with no arguments, or a TtApp with its unfolded arguments). No fact ⇒ Nothing. An opaque owner ⇒ its named face only when it is nullary and the exact system owner of its spelling (TtNamed spelling), else Nothing. A non-opaque owner ⇒ the μ variable of an enclosing unfolding of the same application, else its declaration unfolded (callSiteMembershipUnfold); a bare reference to the parameterized declaration being walked is its own application (the parser's self-reference). An argument count that differs from the declared binders ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipProjection.label: Call-site membership projection
engine:callSiteMembershipProjection.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — close a call-site ground type (a TraversalType whose TtNamed / TtApp nodes carry the host-attached `nominalIdentity`) over its nominal owners and project it for strict membership: every non-opaque owner is unfolded into its declaration (binders substituted, recursion through a synthesized μ), the exact system owner of a scalar spelling keeps its named face, and anything else (an opaque owner that is not the exact system owner of its spelling, an unresolved spelling inside a declaration, a value-dependent or malformed node, an inline opaque other than the parser's List) abstains. `facts` holds one record per reachable owner identity: { identity, opaque, systemSpelling ("" unless the identity is the exact system owner of its own spelling), binders, body }. Just the typeToSetProjection envelope, or Nothing (no verdict).

engine:callSiteMembershipRawSpelling.label: Call-site membership raw spelling
engine:callSiteMembershipRawSpelling.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — a TtNamed with no identity and no binder: admitted unchanged only at the top level of the call-site type, only as a `$ref`, and only as the intrinsic compatibility spelling the inference kernel equates with the system scalar owner (inferenceGroundBuiltinNominalIdentity: String, Number, Boolean); Nothing otherwise. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipScopeLookup.label: Call-site membership scope lookup
engine:callSiteMembershipScopeLookup.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — the innermost replacement bound to a source name, or Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipUnfold.label: Call-site membership unfold
engine:callSiteMembershipUnfold.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — unfold one application of a non-opaque owner: walk its declaration body in a scope holding ONLY its binders (bound to the already unfolded arguments), with the application pushed as active under a fresh μ variable; wrap the result in that μ when the body refers back to it. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipWalk.label: Call-site membership walk
engine:callSiteMembershipWalk.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — close one TraversalType node over its nominal owners (see callSiteMembershipProjection). env: { scope (binder name ⇒ replacement), active (applications being unfolded ⇒ their μ variable), selfIdentity / selfArgs (the declaration whose body is being walked), depth (binder nesting, for fresh names and the bound), envFacts, admitRaw (top level only) }. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipWalkCases.label: Call-site membership walk cases
engine:callSiteMembershipWalkCases.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — callSiteMembershipWalkFields over every case of a TtVariant; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipWalkFields.label: Call-site membership walk fields
engine:callSiteMembershipWalkFields.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — callSiteMembershipWalk over the types of a TtField list, every other slot kept; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipWalkParams.label: Call-site membership walk params
engine:callSiteMembershipWalkParams.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — callSiteMembershipWalk over the types of a TtArrowParam list, every other slot kept; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteMembershipWalkTypes.label: Call-site membership walk types
engine:callSiteMembershipWalkTypes.description: modules-as-values Phase 2d — callSiteMembershipWalk over a list of TraversalTypes; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:callSiteRejection.label: Call-site rejection
engine:callSiteRejection.description: Build a CallSiteRejected outcome carrying one stable inference diagnostic.

engine:callSiteSolvedOutcome.label: Call-site solved outcome
engine:callSiteSolvedOutcome.description: Discharge refinement residuals, then publish the solved class parameters, the solved argument parameter types and the solved result. An indeterminate residual while a class parameter is still unknown reports the unknown parameters; every other discharge failure rejects.

engine:callSiteUnifyArguments.label: Call-site unify argument evidence
engine:callSiteUnifyArguments.description: Unify each known argument type (the inferred side) with its declared parameter (the declared side), in calling order. An unknown argument (Nothing) constrains nothing; ground evidence with a free variable fails closed at the traversal boundary.

engine:callSiteUnifyExpected.label: Call-site unify expected type
engine:callSiteUnifyExpected.description: Unify the method result (the inferred side) with the written expected type (the declared side); no expected type constrains nothing.

engine:canAnalyze.label: assign: can analyze
engine:canAnalyze.description: Can this canonical SetExpr be meaningfully analyzed statically? SeAll / SeNone / SeInterval / SeEnum / SeRef ⇒ True; SeUnion / SeIntersect ⇒ every branch analyzable; SeDiff ⇒ both sides; SeWhere / SePattern / SeComplement / deep formers ⇒ False. floor-kernel Phase 4 retired the parallel TS SetMarker classifier.

engine:canAnalyzeAll.label: assign: can analyze (branch list)
engine:canAnalyzeAll.description: True when EVERY canonical SetExpr in the list is analyzable (the SeUnion / SeIntersect arm — empty list ⇒ True, mirroring `[].every`). Internal helper.

engine:capLookup.label: solve: capLookup
engine:capLookup.description: Phase 5 — find a name in the captures env (a list of {name, value} records); Just value on hit, Nothing otherwise. Internal helper.

engine:caseEmpty.label: empty: caseEmpty
engine:caseEmpty.description: Phase 6 Step 3 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — one already-whole-gated variant payload, reusing the single-product anyEmpty gate before its factor fold. A ready nullary payload is inhabited.

engine:caseNames.label: iso: caseNames
engine:caseNames.description: Helper: collect the `name` of every variant case in a list. Internal helper.

engine:caseNamesAcc.label: iso: caseNamesAcc
engine:caseNamesAcc.description: Helper: accumulator-threaded collect of every variant case `name` (order-preserving). Internal helper.

engine:caseTagsCover.label: Case tags cover
engine:caseTagsCover.description: The D3-unity ELIM face (containment-substrate Phase 2 Step 2): does a match's `caseTags` cover the scrutinee's constructor `scrutineeTags`? `True` iff every scrutinee tag is in caseTags (exhaustive). This is exhaustiveness as set-containment, the ELIM side of the §1 thesis 'exhaustiveness IS set disjointness' — the VP harness demonstrates the trio's STATIC `subset`/`empty` verdict over the case-tag union AGREES with this. A decidable-fragment predicate (finite singleton tag-equality); proof = evaluation to True.

engine:ceConvertCall.label: Convert ECall (reconstituting)
engine:ceConvertCall.description: Convert an ECall: recognises `ECall "if" [c,t,e]` (arity 3) ⇒ CeIf and `ECall "$" [ELambda [p] body, v]` chains ⇒ CeLet/CeDo (run-split), else generic CeCall. The single sanctioned CeIf/CeLet/CeDo reconstitution site for the expr-substrate Phase 4b CoreExpr→Expr replace.

engine:ceReconApply.label: Reconstitute apply chain
engine:ceReconApply.description: Run-split flattened (param,value) pairs + innermost body into nested CeLet (named runs) / CeDo ("_" runs), threading the visible-bindings set for correct sequential scope. Empty pairs ⇒ convert body alone.

engine:ceReconDoRun.label: Reconstitute CeDo run
engine:ceReconDoRun.description: Peel the maximal leading "_" run of (param,value) pairs into one CeDo (statements convert under the unchanged visible set); the CeDo's final expr is ceReconApply on the remaining pairs (or convert body when exhausted).

engine:ceReconDollar.label: Reconstitute CeLet/CeDo
engine:ceReconDollar.description: Flatten an `ECall "$" [ELambda [p] body, v]` chain into (param,value) pairs and run-split into CeLet (named runs) / CeDo ("_" runs), inverting desugar's applied-ELambda encoding byte-equal to the old CoreLet/CoreDo→CeLet/CeDo mappings. Non-matching `$` shapes stay CeCall. Genuine inline applied single-param lambdas canonicalise to CeLet (strict-eval-identical).

engine:ceReconIf.label: Reconstitute CeIf
engine:ceReconIf.description: ECall "if" [c,t,e] (arity exactly 3) ⇒ CeIf with all three sub-exprs converted; any other arity falls back to a generic CeCall (unreachable via the adapter).

engine:ceReconIfThree.label: Reconstitute CeIf (3-arg)
engine:ceReconIfThree.description: Positional destructure of a 3-element ECall "if" arg list into CeIf { cond, then, else }. Helper to ceReconIf; Nothing branches are unreachable totality fall-throughs.

engine:ceReconLetRun.label: Reconstitute CeLet run
engine:ceReconLetRun.description: Peel the maximal leading NAMED run of (param,value) pairs into one CeLet, converting each value under progressively-extended visible scope (sequential let). The body recurses via ceReconApply on the remaining pairs (or convert body when exhausted).

engine:censusFunctions.label: Totality census over a function registry
engine:censusFunctions.description: The ADVISORY totality census (the phase's headline output): run the analyze skeleton over a function list and aggregate into {total, unknown, partial, unanalyzable, unknownIds} — the per-bucket function COUNTS plus the Unknown id worklist (the triage list for the 3g flip: each Unknown is either a real fence — ≠0/ℕ guard, non-sub measure, outside-the-abstraction — or a checker gap to close before the global Unknown→reject flip). Counts are by member-id count (a 2-member Unknown group contributes 2). The Unanalyzable functions (bodies that did not lower to core Expr) are counted separately and NEVER folded into Total (D-3f-4). SOUND: the finite graph's reachability closure is exact; conservative call-graph over/under-approximations and unlowerable bodies still push toward Unknown/Unanalyzable, never a false Total — so the census is a sound LOWER bound on the work remaining before the flip. ADVISORY ONLY — does not touch the kernel, does not flip any verdict (D-3f-5).

engine:chainGetFieldNamed.label: Chain getFieldNamed
engine:chainGetFieldNamed.description: Append (I32Const segIdx, Call litStrIdx, Call getFieldNamedIdx) for each remaining segment in a dotted CeVar chain. Recursion via head/tail to follow the snoc-list convention.

engine:chainGetFieldNamedLlvm.label: LLVM lowering: chainGetFieldNamedLlvm
engine:chainGetFieldNamedLlvm.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:charAt.label: Char at
engine:charAt.description: The 1-char String at index `i` of the source string `cs`, or "" when out of range (so downstream eq-compares are total). Implemented via `slice` (a 1-char substring) — `at` over an exploded char list returns the raw element, not a `Maybe`, and slice is O(1) + total at the boundary. Internal lexer helper.

engine:charCodeIsScalar.label: set-algebra: charCodeIsScalar
engine:charCodeIsScalar.description: signature-substrate slice 3jw §2a — is a Number a Unicode SCALAR VALUE? True exactly on [0, 0x10FFFF] MINUS the surrogate block D800–DFFF (55296–57343), which UTF-16 reserves for pair encoding and which therefore denotes no Char constructor. This is the closed form ⟦Char⟧ ≅ SeDiff (SeInterval 0 0x10FFFF) (SeInterval 0xD800 0xDFFF) read as a predicate. Total on all Numbers and CORRECT over the whole declared domain: the range bounds are not redundant with the caller's guard — a review round observed that a surrogate-exclusion-only version answered true for -1, 0x110000 and Infinity, none of which is a scalar. Premise-free (numeric comparison only). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:charListToArray.label: enumerable: charListToArray
engine:charListToArray.description: solver-extension Phase 2 — fold a pure cons-spine `List Char` (the Enumerable Char stepper's output) into the native witness array: Nil ⇒ []; Cons h t ⇒ concat [h] (recurse). The Char analogue of intListToNumberArray, but identity on each element (a Char IS already its own witness value — no numeric conversion). Internal helper.

engine:checkAcceptOnly.label: check: acceptOnly
engine:checkAcceptOnly.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — soften a decideSubset verdict to accept-only: Just true stays; Just false and Nothing both become Nothing (the over-approximation rule — an over-approximating set's Just false is not a term refutation). Internal helper.

engine:checkAllParamsNonempty.label: check: all params nonempty?
engine:checkAllParamsNonempty.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — every goal param domain decidably NONEMPTY (setAlgebraDecideEmpty = Just false)? The lambda-refutation gate: a refutation of `∀x∈P. …` needs a witness binding, so every P must be decidably inhabited; any Just true / Nothing ⇒ false (the refutation softens). Internal helper.

engine:checkArmClassify.label: check: match arm classify
engine:checkArmClassify.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — classify ONE arm pattern against ONE branch and build its narrowed env in the same pass: returns `{ kind, env }` with kind ∈ "always" (fires whenever a branch value reaches it) | "never" (EXACT non-match — ctor-tag mismatch / scalar lit vs a $tag record) | "might" (could dodge structurally — scalar sub-PatLits) | "fence" (out of fragment: PatWildcard [the egress marshal has no arm — the operational wildcard is PatLit "_"], non-scalar lits, nested ctor sub-patterns, positional args without fields metadata, unknown field names). The env narrows: an EVar scrutinee re-binds to the branch (checkMatchScrutNarrow), a top-level PatVar binds the whole branch, PatConstruct PatVar sub-binders bind their field sets (checkArmCtorArgs) — all PREPENDED newest-first (the checkBindParams/runtime-spread convention: later bindings win). Internal helper — ALSO the narrowing convention Commit-B synthesis (synCase) reuses, so the synthesis env and the re-check env agree BY CONSTRUCTION.

engine:checkArmCtor.label: check: match ctor arm
engine:checkArmCtor.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 / type-substrate P1(a.12) — classify a PatConstruct against a branch: a branch outside the JUDGMENT FENCE (seCtorFieldsFenceOk — upgraded from the embedded-wire-only fieldSemanticSlotsValid, so this arm abstains exactly where membership does) ⇒ fence; a pattern ctor name that is empty or in the reserved `@ctor/` namespace ⇒ fence, NOT never: matchPattern projects the pattern's own `$tag` through _constructorWireNames (constructorPatternWireName), so an exact-target tag can match a short-tag branch the raw comparison calls distinct, and an unprojectable one yields the invalid-wire sentinel (chk.match.pattern-tag); ctor-tag mismatch ⇒ never (EXACT — matchPattern requires $tag equality); tag match with NO sub-patterns ⇒ always (a tag-only wire pattern `{$tag: C}` matches ANY C-value — pattern keys ⊆ scrutinee keys, probe-verified); args with DUPLICATE or empty slot wires ⇒ fence (marshalPatterns writes one host property per slot, so a duplicate silently drops the earlier binder); args WITHOUT fields metadata ⇒ fence (the positional pairing needs the wire key names; index arithmetic is banned under the decider ctx — the boxed-Number toString landmine); args WITH metadata ⇒ the parallel sub-pattern walk (checkArmCtorArgs). Internal helper.

engine:checkArmCtorArgs.label: check: match ctor sub-patterns
engine:checkArmCtorArgs.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 / type-substrate P1(a.12) (chk.match.path-wire) — walk a matching-ctor pattern's sub-patterns in parallel with its resolved CompileFieldSlot metadata (list-parallel — NO index arithmetic): each pattern slot resolves against the branch by FieldKey, never spelling, and then its OWN wire is CONSULTED (checkArmSlotWireOk) because the runtime matcher reads the pattern's spelling, not its key — a slot whose spelling the runtime would read elsewhere, or refuse as stale under _strictPatternFields, fences instead of classifying; each PatVar sub-binder PREPENDS `{name, semanticKey, wirePath, set}` from the matched branch slot, with wirePath the EFFECTIVE (seCtorFieldReadWire) projection rather than the embedded one. A PatLit `"_"` binds nothing; a scalar PatLit DEMOTES the arm to might-match (the arm can dodge on the field value — obligations still count, coverage doesn't); more sub-patterns than metadata slots, an unknown semantic key, nested PatConstructs, PatWildcard, or non-scalar lits ⇒ fence. Returns `{ kind, env }`. Internal helper.

engine:checkArmLit.label: check: match lit arm
engine:checkArmLit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — classify a PatLit against a $tag-ctor branch: the string "_" is the OPERATIONAL WILDCARD (matchPattern's `pattern === "_"` arm — always-match, binds nothing); any other scalar (number / string / boolean) NEVER matches a $tag record (scalar-vs-object: no matchPattern arm applies — EXACT, probe-verified); a non-scalar lit (a record value could structurally match) ⇒ fence. Internal helper.

engine:checkArmPatFields.label: check: match pattern fields (tolerant)
engine:checkArmPatFields.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — read a PatConstruct's `fields` metadata tolerantly: the authored shape carries the slot (possibly []); the jlsTaggedPattern lift OMITS the key for unregistered ctors (its no-named arm constructs without it). Missing ⇒ []. Internal helper.

engine:checkArmSlotWireOk.label: check: match slot wire ok?
engine:checkArmSlotWireOk.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) (chk.match.path-wire) — may this pattern slot carry a DEFINITE arm classification? The runtime matcher reads the pattern's OWN spelling and, under _strictPatternFields, REFUSES the whole arm when that spelling is not a current wire of the constructor (patternMatchPlan's stale set); in the legacy and raw-plan modes it raw-reads the spelling instead. So the classifier may only stay definite where all three policies provably agree. POSITIONAL spellings are the certified case: isNamedPatternField excludes `_i` from the identity plan entirely, so every context reads the property raw, and the branch fence has already forced the branch's own positional slot onto that same `_i` — hence spelling equality against seCtorFieldReadWire is exactly the agreement condition. A NAMED spelling is policy-dependent: proving it non-stale needs the ctx's _ctorFieldKeys plan and _strictPatternFields, which this face does not read, so it fences. Internal helper to checkArmCtorArgs.

engine:checkArmSlotsOk.label: check: match pattern slots ok?
engine:checkArmSlotsOk.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — a constructor pattern's slot metadata must be a FUNCTION from slots to host properties: no empty wire and no two slots on the same wire. marshalPatterns writes one property per slot, so a duplicate wire silently drops every binder but the last, and the classifier would credit bindings the runtime never makes. Internal helper to checkArmCtor.

engine:checkArmUnguarded.label: check: match arm unguarded?
engine:checkArmUnguarded.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — true when a match arm carries NO guard field. A guarded arm can DODGE at runtime (falsy guard ⇒ continue to later arms — probe-verified against json-logic.ts matchOp), so only unguarded always-match arms count for branch COVERAGE. Internal helper.

engine:checkAssignable.label: Check assignable
engine:checkAssignable.description: The assignability decision: is `source` assignable to `target` (source ⊆ target)? Grades a ProofResult marker from subsetProven (source ⊆ target decided through the kernel: PropSubset → DecidableSetResult → kernel:verify), the exact normalized gap SetExpr, and the canonical source / target SetExpr values. subsetProven OR gap = SeNone ⇒ { ok = True, confidence = "proven" }; otherwise a gap exists ⇒ { ok = False, confidence = "forward" } when both sides are analyzable (canAnalyze), else "unknown". Fenel owns the gap-emptiness case split; the TS delegate only computes the normalized gap and attaches it to the real { ok, gap?, confidence } when ok = False. The port of fenel-check's checkAssignable onto the Fenel prover / set-algebra substrate. unified-static-analysis Phase 2.

engine:checkBindParams.label: check: bind params
engine:checkBindParams.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r — bind a lambda's param names (a list of strings) to the goal SeArrow's per-param domains (SetArrowParam.set) for the body check. PREPENDS each {name, set} entry (cons — envLookup scans HEAD-FIRST, so the NEWEST binding must sit in front: appending gave reverse-lexical scoping where an OUTER binding shadowed the inner param — the 8λ.2-r probe-confirmed KERNEL-REACHABLE FALSE ACCEPT via nested same-name lambdas `\x -> \x -> x`; prepend order also matches the runtime's last-param-wins data binding for duplicate names). Positional pairing; stops at the shorter list (the N<M narrow arm binds exactly the closure's params). Internal helper.

engine:checkCall.label: check: ECall
engine:checkCall.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r — a call term checks in SYNTH mode, with ONE check-mode special: `if` (desugar lowers EVERY surface if to `ECall "if"` — expr.fenel header) checks BOTH branches against the goal directly (checkIfArm — both-true ⇒ true, both-refuted-EXACTLY ⇒ false: a 3-arg if's value is always one of the two branch values; the Opus pass had no if arm, fencing every conditional body). Everything else: synthCall produces an over-approximating set for the call's image, then decideSubset synthset goal, ACCEPT-ONLY (the synth set only ⊆-approximates the true image ⇒ its Just false is not a term refutation). Internal helper.

engine:checkCallableFree.label: check: callable-free set?
engine:checkCallableFree.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — is a SetExpr PROVABLY free of callable values (no `{$ref}` / `{__fenelFn}` / `{__fenelPartial}` member possible)? The N>M arity-refutation gate: the under-applied value is a partial (a callable), so it is definitely ∉ a callable-free codomain. v1 shapes: SeInterval / SeNone (empty) ⇒ true; a KNOWN atom-tower SeRef (seNamedEmpty = Just false — numbers/strings/chars/bools are never callable) ⇒ true; SeEnum with every value a scalar (checkEnumScalarsOnly) ⇒ true; everything else (SeCtor could degenerately carry callable-shaped fields, SeAll/SeWhere/… unknown) ⇒ false (the refutation softens). Internal helper.

engine:checkCombineField.label: check: combine field
engine:checkCombineField.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — combine a non-false field verdict v (Just true or Nothing) with the folded rest of the fields: rest Just false ⇒ Just false; rest Nothing ⇒ Nothing; rest Just true ⇒ (v Just true ⇒ Just true, else Nothing). Internal helper (shared by EConstruct + ERecord folds).

engine:checkCombineUnion.label: check: combine union
engine:checkCombineUnion.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — combine a non-true branch verdict v (Just false or Nothing) with the folded rest of the union branches: rest Just true ⇒ Just true; rest Just false ⇒ (v Just false ⇒ Just false [all refute], else Nothing); rest Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkConstruct.label: check: EConstruct
engine:checkConstruct.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r / type-substrate P1(a.12) — a constructor term checks against a SeCtor / SeUnion-of-SeCtor goal (the 8μ.1a membership rule on open terms). A COERCING ctor (True/False) routes through the ELit singleton face ONLY at arity 0 (chk.ctor.bool-arity): the B5 coercion arm fires exactly when the construct call has no payload arg, so `True 5` is the ordinary tagged record `{$tag:"True",_0:5}` and the blanket literal route was a false accept against `{true}`. A source ctor name that is empty or in the reserved `@ctor/` namespace ⇒ Nothing (chk.ctor.reserved-name): the runtime THROWS there, so no value exists and NEITHER polarity is entitled — and the compiler's short-tag projection is not available at this face. Everything else takes the physical-wire ctor path. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorAgainst.label: check: ctor against goal
engine:checkCtorAgainst.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r / 8λ.5 — dispatch a (non-coercing) constructor term against the goal shape: SeCtor ⇒ direct physical-wire fieldwise; SeUnion ⇒ member iff a member of SOME branch (all branches refute ⇒ Just false); SeMu ⇒ ONE face-ok-gated equi-recursive unfold then the same two arms (chk.ctor.mu — checkCtorMu); any other goal ⇒ the accept-only ⊤-fallback (`decideSubset SeAll goal`, softened — a constructed value is a value, so ⟦e⟧ ⊆ ⊤ ⊆ goal). Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorDsGuardOk.label: check: ctor declared-name guard
engine:checkCtorDsGuardOk.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — a constructor's declared field names may not collide with any key a lifted Expr's raw JSON-Logic preimage can carry, or the sole-argument write becomes IR-shape dependent. The guarded set is jlsSingleKey's CLOSED op cascade (var/if/?:/let/do/fn/call/construct/match/and/or/where/method/ann; `ann` since modules-as-values Phase 2d) plus the tagged and pattern meta keys ($tag/$bind/$guard) plus every operator NOTATION (opNotationToCodeName's closed table — `{+:[…]}` lifts to ECall "add", so the raw key is the notation, not the code name). Any declared name inside that set ⇒ the plan abstains. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorFindWire.label: check: ctor find wire
engine:checkCtorFindWire.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — look one physical wire up in the source write plan, returning Just its expression or Nothing when the plan does not bind that axis. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorIrKeyReserved.label: check: ctor IR key reserved?
engine:checkCtorIrKeyReserved.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — membership of jlsSingleKey's closed recognised-op cascade plus the tagged/pattern meta keys. A census pin (check-face-differential) asserts this list still covers that cascade, so a future adapter arm fails loudly instead of silently reopening the sole-argument hole. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorMu.label: check: ctor vs SeMu (chk.ctor.mu)
engine:checkCtorMu.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — a constructor term vs a μ goal: gate positivity + support + guardedness (seMuFaceOk ∧ seMuGuarded — the mem.mu/chk.match.mu condition set), unfold ONCE (`μv.F = F[v:=μv.F]` — substSet, the arms-only identity exposure), and dispatch to exactly the two base arms (SeCtor / SeUnion); a μ-headed or other unfold shape (or a gate failure) ⇒ the accept-only ⊤-fallback (never a guess, no unfold loop — the checkMatchBranchesMu no-re-entry discipline). Both verdicts propagate: equi-recursion makes the μ's members EXACTLY the unfold's, so a fieldwise/all-branch refutation against the unfold is a refutation against the μ. This is the arm that lets a lifted recursor witness (`case n of Z -> {Z-value} | S -> S (f n._0)`) kernel-re-certify: the tagged-literal arm body lifts back as an EConstruct, whose goal is the μ. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorMuGo.label: check: ctor vs SeMu (unrolled)
engine:checkCtorMuGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — dispatch the one-level μ unfold: SeCtor ⇒ checkCtorSeCtor; SeUnion ⇒ checkCtorUnion; anything else ⇒ the accept-only ⊤-fallback against the ORIGINAL μ goal. Internal helper to checkCtorMu.

engine:checkCtorNameFenced.label: check: ctor name fenced?
engine:checkCtorNameFenced.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — true for a source constructor name the runtime construct op REFUSES: the empty name and any name inside the reserved `@ctor/` exact-target namespace (json-logic.ts throws on both AFTER applying `_constructorWireNames`). `_constructorWireNames` is keyed by `@ctor/…` target ids ONLY (registryConstructorTargetId), so an ordinary short tag projects to itself and this predicate is exactly the throwing set that survives projection. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorPairFold.label: check: ctor pair by wire
engine:checkCtorPairFold.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / type-substrate P1(a.12) — fold the GOAL's fields against the source write plan by EFFECTIVE PHYSICAL WIRE: each goal field projects through seCtorFieldReadWire (membership's OWN primitive — key→CURRENT wire when the process registry knows the key, the embedded persisted wireName as the codec-hint fallback), and the plan is looked up at that wire. A goal wire the plan does not write ⇒ Just false: the plan is TOTAL (it enumerates exactly the axes the construct op binds) and membership's own rule for a missing host property is the same unconditional Just false. A wire the plan writes ⇒ the sub-expression checkExpr-ed against the field's set. Any Just false ⇒ Just false; all Just true ⇒ Just true; any Nothing (none false) ⇒ Nothing. EXTRA source axes are irrelevant — ctor membership is open-width. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorPositionalWires.label: check: ctor positional wires
engine:checkCtorPositionalWires.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — the positional write plan `[{wire = "_i", expr = arg_i}]`, the axes the construct op's else-branch binds. Ordinal rendering reuses fieldNaturalDecimal (digit recursion — never toString, which boxes under the decider ctx). Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorRecordNamesIn.label: check: ctor record names declared?
engine:checkCtorRecordNamesIn.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — every field name of a record-shaped sole argument is a declared constructor field name (the construct op's `keys(arg) ⊆ ctorDef` named-branch test). True ⇒ the named branch fires and the plan abstains, because the record's own preimage may equally be a `{do:[…]}`-wrapped object whose only key is `do`. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorSeCtor.label: check: ctor vs SeCtor
engine:checkCtorSeCtor.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / field-identity Phase 4 / type-substrate P1(a.12) (chk.ctor.pair) — a constructor term vs a SeCtor, judged by EFFECTIVE PHYSICAL WIRE. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and mirrors membership's (setAlgebraCtorContains): (1) the goal outside the judgment fence (seCtorFieldsFenceOk — slot validity ∧ no RESOLVED reserved wire ∧ resolved-wire injectivity) ⇒ Nothing; (2) a COERCING goal ctor ⇒ Nothing (the ledger-B5 exclusion, membership's own arm); (3) the SOURCE write plan (checkCtorSourceWires) — computed BEFORE the tag leg because the legacy named branch can OVERWRITE `$tag` from the payload, so a tag mismatch is not a refutation until the plan is known; (4) the tag leg, which a `""` goal ctor SKIPS entirely (the anonymous-record former — membership is ""-agnostic, and P1(a) already retired ""-as-a-distinct-tag in the subset and disjointness legs); (5) fieldwise by wire. A goal wire absent from the (total) source plan ⇒ Just false, membership's own unconditional shape-mismatch rule. Declared ARITY is NOT consulted: it is not part of the write model. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorSoleArgWires.label: check: ctor sole-arg wires
engine:checkCtorSoleArgWires.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — the ONE genuinely ambiguous cell of the write model. With exactly one payload argument the construct op takes the NAMED branch iff the argument's RAW JSON-Logic node is a plain non-array object whose keys are all DECLARED (an UNREGISTERED ctor makes ANY plain object named — the legacy heuristic). The judgment sees the lifted Expr, not the raw node, so this decides by the lift's CLOSED preimage schema. Unregistered ⇒ ALWAYS Nothing: every Expr shape has at least one plain-object preimage (a `{do:[…]}` wrapper if nothing else). Registered ⇒ positional is entitled only when NO preimage key can be declared: every raw key of every preimage is a RESERVED IR KEY (jlsSingleKey's closed cascade plus `$tag`/`$bind`/`$guard`), an operator NOTATION (opNotationToCodeName's closed table), the callee fnId (checked for ECall), or a record field name (checked for ERecord). Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorSourceWires.label: check: ctor source wires
engine:checkCtorSourceWires.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — the TOTAL decoder for the runtime construct op's write plan: `Just [{wire, expr}]` when the physical axes the value will carry are determined by the term alone, `Nothing` when the write is IR-shape dependent. Arity 0 ⇒ no axes. A NON-EMPTY `fields` provenance slot ⇒ Nothing (chk.ctor.src-fields): the slot's own egress reading is decided by the KEY (positional keys re-emit positionally), so the metadata alone does not pin the wires — an empty slot is the established POSITIONAL sentinel (synCtor emits `fields = []`; partial-evaluate's egress reads it that way) and falls through. Arity ≥ 2 ⇒ positional `_0 … _(n-1)` UNCONDITIONALLY (`useNamed` requires exactly one payload arg). Arity 1 ⇒ checkCtorSoleArgWires. Finally the source axes must themselves be sane: no RESERVED wire ($tag/$ref/__fenelPartial/__fenelFn — the axis would collide with the tag/callable coordinate the faces read out of band) and no two axes on one host property. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorSrcWiresGate.label: check: ctor source wires gate
engine:checkCtorSrcWiresGate.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — admit a computed source write plan only when its axes are sane: checkCtorSrcWiresOk. Internal helper to checkCtorSourceWires.

engine:checkCtorSrcWiresOk.label: check: ctor source wires ok?
engine:checkCtorSrcWiresOk.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — the SOURCE-side mirror of seCtorWiresOk: no planned axis lands on a RESERVED host property ($tag/$ref/__fenelPartial/__fenelFn) and no two axes land on the same one (a later write would silently overwrite an earlier). Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorTermFields.label: check: EConstruct term fields
engine:checkCtorTermFields.description: type-substrate P1(a.12) — read an EConstruct's `fields` provenance slot TOLERANTLY (the desugar without-fields arm omits the key; the kernel-side bodyToExpr lift passes no ctorDefs, so lifted terms never carry it). Missing ⇒ []. Internal helper.

engine:checkCtorUnion.label: check: ctor vs SeUnion
engine:checkCtorUnion.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — a constructor term vs a SeUnion of branches: member iff a member of SOME branch. Any branch Just true ⇒ Just true; ALL branches Just false ⇒ Just false (definitely not in any, EXACT); else Nothing. Empty union ⇒ Just false (∅ membership). Internal helper.

engine:checkEnumScalarsOnly.label: check: enum all scalars?
engine:checkEnumScalarsOnly.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — every enum value a scalar (number / string / boolean — never a record, so never callable-shaped)? Internal helper to checkCallableFree.

engine:checkEnvLookup.label: check: env lookup
engine:checkEnvLookup.description: Exact check-local lexical lookup over normalized Env rows. Scans head-first so newly prepended lambda and match bindings shadow older entries. Internal helper.

engine:checkExpr.label: Check expr membership
engine:checkExpr.description: The bidirectional CHECK judgment (decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.4): decide whether an open term `e` (the 7-case core Expr), under a variable→set env, is a member of a GIVEN goal set. `Just true ⇒ ⟦e⟧env ⊆ goal` (sound sufficient membership); `Just false` only from EXACT derivations (ELit / ELambda arity / EConstruct ctor-tag / EMatch all-covered-all-refuted); `Nothing` = out of the fragment. Check-mode: ELit (the singleton {v}⊆goal face), EVar (env lookup, accept-only), ELambda-against-SeArrow (the intro rule — arity + bind params + check the body against the codomain), EConstruct-against-SeCtor/SeUnion (ctor match + FieldKey-aligned fieldwise reasoning), ERecord-against-SeCtor "" (key-bearing goal slots projected once through current wire names), EMatch (8λ.4 — the scrutinee synth's SeCtor decomposition, per-branch first-match arm walk under the narrowed env, coverage-gated). Synth-mode: ECall delegates to the propagate transfer leaves (op fragment) + fnTypeMarker return signatures (registered calls), accept-only. Makes type-checking a lambda kernel-reachable: setAlgebraArrowContains calls this to decide {closure} ⊆ SeArrow, so verifyWitnessMembership re-certifies a proposed lambda with zero kernel edits.

engine:checkExprFix.label: Check recursive lambda membership (chk.fix)
engine:checkExprFix.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the RECURSIVE-lambda CHECK rule (the ONE new trusted rule; TCB row chk.fix, SIDE-CONDITIONED): `checkExprFix fixName e env goal` decides membership of a fix-marked lambda in a SeArrow goal. Premise: bind fixName ↦ the WHOLE goal arrow in Γ (self-calls become assumed members via the shipped synthDynName arm — no new transfer math) + bind params + checkExpr the body against the codomain, ACCEPT-ONLY. Side condition (fixDescentAny): a syntactic arm-aware descent scan — ∃ one param position, common to ALL self-calls, at which every self-call passes an env-bound dotted strict-component path var (`x.tail` — minted only by the match narrowing under a proven branch tag); any other occurrence of the fix name (value escape, wrong arity, unverifiable subtree) fails. Vacuous ∀ (some param domain decidably empty) ⇒ Just true (the checkLambda mirror). Exact arity only; dotted/colliding binders fence; refutations are NOT emitted (accept-only — the honest v1). Sound by structural induction on the descent argument (finite trees; positive-μ decomposition is seMuFaceOk-gated): descent ⇒ total, premise ⇒ outputs in R ⇒ a member of the signature-space arrow.

engine:checkFixLambda.label: check: fix lambda
engine:checkFixLambda.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the chk.fix gate ladder: SeArrow goal only; fixName/params well-formed (checkFixNamesOk — non-empty, dot-free, fixName ∉ params, params pairwise distinct); vacuous ∀ ⇒ Just true; EXACT arity only; the global binder fence (fixBindersOk); then the PREMISE (checkExpr body ⇐ returns under Γ + f + params) and the SIDE CONDITION (fixDescentAny) — BOTH must hold; accept-only. Internal helper.

engine:checkFixNamesOk.label: check: fix names ok?
engine:checkFixNamesOk.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — well-formedness of the fix name + λ-param names: fixName non-empty, dot-free, ∉ params; every param dot-free; params pairwise distinct. Dots are reserved for the machinery-minted field-path binds — a dotted binder could ALIAS a path var and steal descent credit; a param equal to fixName would shadow the fixpoint. Internal helper.

engine:checkIfArm.label: check: if arm
engine:checkIfArm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — check-mode `if`: a 3-arg if's VALUE is always one of {then-value, else-value} (the condition only selects), so checkExpr BOTH branches against the goal: both Just true ⇒ Just true; both Just false ⇒ Just false (EXACT — each branch refutation is itself exact by the file discipline, and the value is one of the two); else Nothing. A 2-arg if (missing else ⇒ host-null value) or malformed arity ⇒ Nothing (the fence). Internal helper.

engine:checkIfCombine.label: check: if combine
engine:checkIfCombine.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — combine the two if-branch verdicts: both Just true ⇒ Just true; both Just false ⇒ Just false; else Nothing. Internal helper to checkIfArm.

engine:checkIsELit.label: check: is ELit?
engine:checkIsELit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — true when an Expr is an ELit (the body-exactness gate for the lambda refutation propagation). Internal helper.

engine:checkLambda.label: check: ELambda
engine:checkLambda.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r — the lambda INTRO rule against a SeArrow goal, CURRY-AWARE + VACUOUS-GATED (the calling-convention semantics in the file header): (1) any goal param domain decidably EMPTY ⇒ Just true (vacuous ∀ — regardless of arity or body; refuting inhabit's own vacuous witness was the probe-confirmed 8λ.2-r false refutation); (2) closure arity N == goal arity M ⇒ bind + check the body against the codomain (refutations gated by checkLambdaBody); (3) N > M ⇒ an arrow-shaped codomain RE-ASSOCIATES into the params (under-application yields a partial — currying) and retries, a non-arrow codomain refutes ONLY when provably callable-free + all params decidably nonempty (the under-applied value is a partial, a callable), else Nothing; (4) N < M ⇒ bind the first N and check the body against the remainder arrow ACCEPT-ONLY (over-application SPILLS onto callable results but DROPS onto non-callables — the drop path makes refutation unsound). A non-SeArrow goal ⇒ Nothing. THIS is the arm that makes type-checking a lambda kernel-reachable. Internal helper.

engine:checkLambdaBody.label: check: lambda body verdict
engine:checkLambdaBody.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r — combine a lambda body's check verdict with the refutation discipline: Just true ⇒ Just true; Just false propagates ONLY when the body is an ELit (an exact const-lambda refutation) AND every goal param domain is decidably NONEMPTY (the vacuous gate — a maybe-empty domain could make the ∀ vacuous ⇒ member), else Nothing; Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkLambdaNarrow.label: check: lambda narrow (N < M)
engine:checkLambdaNarrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — a closure with FEWER params than the goal: bind the first N goal domains (checkBindParams stops at the shorter list) and check the body against the REMAINDER arrow SeArrow(aps[N:], returns) — sound via over-application SPILL (a callable body-value absorbs the leftover args). ACCEPT-ONLY: a NON-callable body-value silently DROPS leftovers (json-logic.ts:1894 returns the result unchanged), so a body refuted against the remainder arrow could still be a member via the drop path ⇒ Just false softens to Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkLambdaWide.label: check: lambda wide (N > M)
engine:checkLambdaWide.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — a closure with MORE params than the goal: an arrow-shaped goal codomain RE-ASSOCIATES (goal params ++ codomain params → codomain returns — sound via under-application/partials: f(a) behaves as the residual lambda) and retries checkLambda (terminates — the codomain arrow depth strictly decreases); a non-arrow codomain: the goal-applied value is a PARTIAL (a callable), so a provably CALLABLE-FREE codomain refutes (Just false, gated on all goal params decidably nonempty — the ∀ must be non-vacuous), else Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkLit.label: check: ELit
engine:checkLit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — a literal term checks by the singleton subset face: decideSubset (SeEnum [v]) goal. EXACT (a singleton IS the value) ⇒ both Just true and Just false propagate. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatch.label: check: EMatch
engine:checkMatch.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — the match CHECK arm: synth the scrutinee's set, decompose it into SeCtor branches (checkMatchBranches — SeCtor / SeUnion-of-SeCtor only, non-coercing, non-empty ctor names), then per branch walk the arms in first-match order (checkMatchWalk) and combine the branch verdicts by the n-ary checkIfArm discipline (all-true ⇒ true, all-false ⇒ false, else Nothing — checkMatchFold). A non-decomposable scrutinee synth or an empty decomposition ⇒ Nothing (the honest fence). Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchAcc.label: check: match obligation acc
engine:checkMatchAcc.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — fold ONE arm-body verdict into the branch obligation accumulator: Just true keeps/enters "true", Just false keeps/enters "false", any Nothing or true/false disagreement ⇒ "bot" (the branch verdict can only be Nothing). "none" = no obligations yet. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchAccOut.label: check: match acc out
engine:checkMatchAccOut.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — project the branch obligation accumulator onto the branch verdict at coverage: "true" ⇒ Just true, "false" ⇒ Just false (EXACT — every folded refutation is itself exact), anything else ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchBranchList.label: check: match branch list
engine:checkMatchBranchList.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — validate a SeUnion's branches as usable SeCtors, returning Just the list (any unusable branch ⇒ Nothing — the whole decomposition fences). Internal helper to checkMatchBranches.

engine:checkMatchBranchOk.label: check: match branch usable?
engine:checkMatchBranchOk.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 / type-substrate P1(a.12) — is a decomposition branch a usable ctor set (SeCtor, INSIDE the judgment fence, non-empty ctor name, non-coercing)? The fence (seCtorFieldsFenceOk) runs BEFORE any arm classification or wildcard/PatVar narrowing: an operand whose resolved wires are reserved or alias onto ONE host property breaks the field independence every per-arm narrowing assumes, and membership already abstains for it. Internal helper to checkMatchBranches.

engine:checkMatchBranches.label: check: match branches
engine:checkMatchBranches.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 / 8λ.5 — decompose a scrutinee synth set into its ctor branches: a usable SeCtor ⇒ the singleton list; a SeUnion whose branches are ALL usable SeCtors ⇒ the branch list; a SeMu ⇒ ONE face-ok-gated equi-recursive unfold (8λ.5 — checkMatchBranchesMu; the arms-only μ-identity exposure, the b-side-unroll precedent) then the same two base shapes; anything else ⇒ Nothing (the fence — SeAll / SeRef / SeInterval scrutinees are out of the fragment). Usable = a genuine `$tag`-carrying ctor set: tag SeCtor, ctor name non-empty (the `""` record ctor's values carry NO $tag), non-coercing (True/False values are JS booleans, not records). Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchBranchesMu.label: check: match branches (μ unfold)
engine:checkMatchBranchesMu.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — decompose a SeMu scrutinee by ONE equi-recursive unfold: gate positivity + support + guardedness (seMuFaceOk ∧ seMuGuarded — the mem.mu condition set; a non-positive μ NEVER decomposes, which is what keeps fix-intro/chk.fix off negative recursion), substSet the μ into its own body (`μv.F = F[v:=μv.F]` — the arms-only identity exposure, the Park-b-side-unroll precedent: NOT a normalize rewrite), then accept exactly the two base shapes (a usable SeCtor / a SeUnion of usable SeCtors). NO re-entry into checkMatchBranches — a μ-headed unfold (μ-of-μ) ⇒ Nothing, so there is no unfold loop. This is what makes a μ-typed param case-splittable: the Cons branch's tail field carries the WHOLE μ back (substSet), so the narrowed `x.tail` path bind is exactly the recursive component chk.fix's descent rule credits. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchBranchesMuGo.label: check: match branches (μ unfold, unrolled)
engine:checkMatchBranchesMuGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — validate the ONE-level μ unfold as a decomposition: exactly the checkMatchBranches base shapes (a usable SeCtor / a SeUnion of usable SeCtors); a μ-headed or any other unfold shape ⇒ Nothing (no re-entry — no unfold loop). Internal helper to checkMatchBranchesMu.

engine:checkMatchFieldSlot.label: check: match field set
engine:checkMatchFieldSlot.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — resolve a pattern's already-identified CompileFieldSlot against a validated branch slot by FieldKey. Renames therefore preserve meaning and equal spellings with distinct UUIDs remain distinct; wireName is retained only as the runtime projection carried into the narrowed binding. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchFold.label: check: match fold branches
engine:checkMatchFold.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — fold the per-branch verdicts across the scrutinee decomposition: each branch walks the arms (checkMatchWalk, acc seeded "none"); verdicts combine by checkIfCombine (all Just true ⇒ Just true; all Just false ⇒ Just false — the n-ary checkIfArm widening, EXACT per the header enumeration; else Nothing). Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchPathBinds.label: check: match field-path binds
engine:checkMatchPathBinds.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 / type-substrate P1(a.12) (chk.match.path-wire) — PREPEND a dotted field-path binding per branch field through its EFFECTIVE wire: `{name = x ++ "." ++ seCtorFieldReadWire field, set = field.set}`. It reads through the SAME primitive membership uses (key→CURRENT wire when the process registry knows the key, the embedded persisted wireName as the codec-hint fallback); the older embedded-only read minted a path the runtime does not resolve after a field rename, while this very prose already claimed the current one. A field whose effective wire CONTAINS a dot mints NO bind at all: the runtime resolveVar splits dotted names into a property walk, so `x.a.b` would not denote the single property `a.b`, and the use site then misses in the env and abstains. This is a runtime projection path only; the semantic slot identity remains key. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchScrutNarrow.label: check: match scrutinee narrow
engine:checkMatchScrutNarrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — when the scrutinee is an EVar, PREPEND its branch re-binding ({name = x, set = branch}) AND one FIELD-PATH binding per branch field ({name = "x.<field>", set = the field's set} — the runtime's dotted var-path resolution reads exactly that projection, so `EVar "x._0"` in an arm body is the payload). Matching a branch's pattern PROVES the value carries that branch's $tag ⇒ both bindings over-approximate the true path values (sound for accept and exact-refute). The path bindings are what case-split SYNTHESIS emits bodies against (tag-only patterns + path vars — the shape that round-trips the jlsTaggedPattern lift byte-identically; binder metadata does NOT survive the lift for unregistered ctors). A non-var scrutinee narrows nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkMatchWalk.label: check: match arm walk
engine:checkMatchWalk.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — walk the arms in order for ONE branch, threading the obligation accumulator ("none" | "true" | "false" | "bot"): a never-match arm skips; a fence classification ⇒ Nothing; an always/might arm's body checkExpr (under the classify-narrowed env) folds into the acc (any disagreement / Nothing ⇒ "bot" ⇒ the walk short-circuits to Nothing); the first UNGUARDED always-match arm COVERS the branch and emits the folded verdict (later arms are unreachable for this branch — first-match order); running out of arms without unguarded coverage ⇒ Nothing (the runtime null path — probe-verified: an uncovered value / an all-guards-dodge run yields host-null). Internal helper.

engine:checkMutualTotality.label: Check mutual-recursion totality (rung 3c)
engine:checkMutualTotality.description: Rung-3c MUTUAL-recursion totality check over a function GROUP (a `List {id, params, body}` of the mutually-recursive set). Generalizes the single-function size-change closure (slice B) to a CALL GRAPH over a set of functions (Lee–Jones–Ben-Amram general form): each call site `fₐ → fᵦ` yields a size-change graph `{from = fₐ, to = fᵦ, edges}` whose edges run from the caller's params to the callee's param-slots (the per-position oracle totPosIsLt/totPosIsEq reused verbatim); composition `G ; H` is defined ONLY when G.to == H.from (matching intermediate function); the fuel-bounded transitive closure is taken; the program is size-change terminating iff every IDEMPOTENT graph (`from == to` AND `g ; g = g`, necessarily an `f → f` cycle) has a strictly-descending self-edge. Returns Total when the group is size-change terminating (incl. the structural mutual win `f x = …g t…` / `g y = …f t…`, the measure mutual win, the 3-function cycle whose `f → f` idempotent surfaces only at closure depth 3), or there is no call-graph graph at all; Unknown when some idempotent `f → f` graph has no strict self-edge (the mutual non-termination canaries `f a = g a` / `g b = f b`, the permutation ping-pong), or the closure exceeded the fuel bound, or for the inherited fences (`≠ 0`/ℕ-typed equality guards need a type — `== 0`-guarded even/odd stays Unknown; k ≥ 2 / non-`sub` measures). SOUND: every edge asserts a relation the per-position oracle proved; composition only derives relations holding along call-graph paths; a missing edge (a call outside the group, an unrecognized shape) only weakens the criterion ⇒ Unknown, never a wrong Total. A passed group that is not mutually closed loses edges (sound). A missing GRAPH is different from a missing edge: a call site the walk fails to recognise removes an obligation and could fake Total, so call heads match members by spelling (totHeadMayName: canonical, dotted, bare and var-head spellings), and a member taken as a value or a var-head call to an unbound non-member name refuses first (totGroupUnchecked ⇒ Unknown; 2026-10-02). Never returns Partial — the @partial escape-hatch is folded by totalityVerdict.

engine:checkRecFieldsFold.label: check: record fields fold
engine:checkRecFieldsFold.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / field-identity Phase 4 (D4) — fold validated SeCtor "" fields against a record term: for each semantic slot, project through seCtorFieldReadWire (key→CURRENT wire when the registry knows the key; the embedded persisted wireName as the fallback codec hint — never key equality by spelling), look up that source property, and checkExpr its value against the set. Any field Just false ⇒ Just false; all Just true ⇒ Just true; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:checkRecFindField.label: check: record find field
engine:checkRecFindField.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / field-identity Phase 3 — read a source record term through the already-selected semantic slot's current wire projection, returning Just its value Expr or Nothing. This source lookup never establishes field identity. Internal helper.

engine:checkRecord.label: check: ERecord
engine:checkRecord.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r — a record term checks against a validated SeCtor "" goal (the type-to-set $record projection's synthetic record ctor): each semantic field projects through wireName to find the source record property (missing ⇒ Nothing, soft) and checkExpr its value against the field set, combined by the shared field-fold discipline (WIDTH subtyping: extra record fields are fine). A malformed slot plan fences. A non-SeCtor/non-"" goal uses the conservative accept-only top route because an unresolved source record has no authority to mint semantic field identities. Internal helper.

engine:checkStructuralTotality.label: Check structural + measure + lexicographic + size-change totality (rung 1 + 2 + 3a + 3b)
engine:checkStructuralTotality.description: Single-function totality check (rung 1 structural-recursion + rung 2 guarded measure + rung 3a lexicographic + rung 3b size-change graph closure) over a function's core Expr body. As of slice C (rung 3c) this is SINGLETON SUGAR over checkMutualTotality — the function becomes a one-member group `[{id = selfId, params, body}]`, so the mutual call-graph closure reduces to the single-function self-call closure (the one-object special case): Total iff the recursion is size-change terminating (every IDEMPOTENT graph in the transitive closure under composition has a strictly-descending self-edge), or there is no self-call. COMPLETE for the size-change abstraction: subsumes rungs 1+2+3a (structural / measure / lexicographic-identity descents) AND proves PERMUTED / reordering / multi-step-rotation descents for which no fixed parameter order works (`f a b = if a>0 then f b (a-1) else 0` ⇒ Total). SOUND throughout: every edge asserts a relation the per-position oracle proved, composition only derives two-call relations, a missing edge only makes the criterion harder (⇒ Unknown, never a wrong Total); the cross-position soundness repairs (`f (Cons h t) t`, `f (b+1) (a-1)`) stay Unknown (G = {a →↓ b}; G ; G = {} empty idempotent, no strict self-edge). Returns Unknown when the closure has a non-descending idempotent, or the fuel-bounded fixpoint is exhausted, or for the inherited fences (`≠ 0`/ℕ-typed guards need a type; k ≥ 2 / non-`sub` measures). Never returns Partial — folded by totalityVerdict. Sound: variable shadowing removes re-bound names from ALL of scrut/origins/pos.

engine:checkVar.label: check: EVar
engine:checkVar.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — a variable term checks by env lookup, ACCEPT-ONLY: the bound set decideSubset-ed against the goal, softening Just false to Nothing (the env set may over-approximate the var's true values). Unbound ⇒ Nothing. Uses the check-local exact Env lookup. Internal helper.

engine:classifyIntervalValue.label: set-algebra: classifyIntervalValue
engine:classifyIntervalValue.description: Phase 3b-3 — raw value → IntervalValue (IvNumber / IvString / IvOther). Mirrors marshalIntervalValue: non-NaN number → IvNumber, string → IvString, else IvOther.

engine:classifyLegacyFieldPresentation.label: Classify legacy field presentation
engine:classifyLegacyFieldPresentation.description: Lift legacy inline field label/UI slots onto UUID facets after the field-identity kernel has adopted UUID-as-name or resolved a supplied stable mint. The returned definitions are expected to write the same readable codeName with an explicit NamedField key and clear both inline slots.

engine:classifyTT.label: Classify ident token type
engine:classifyTT.description: The TT for an identifier run's text: `bool` for true/false (`fenel-parser.ts:239`), the keyword text itself for a KW-set member (let/if/then/else/case/of/do/end/where/in/infixl/infixr/infix, `:250`), else `ident` (`:251`). No-locale path (decision 7 — locale word-op projection is Phase 5). Internal lexer helper.

engine:closeAll.label: Close all contexts
engine:closeAll.description: Emit a `vclose` for every remaining real layout context (skipping bracket-suspend sentinels) — run at `eof` to balance every block. Internal layout helper.

engine:closeCascade.label: Close cascade
engine:closeCascade.description: Emit `vclose` for every layout context whose column exceeds `col` (a dedent can close MANY blocks), then a `vsemi` if the landing context column equals `col` (sibling statement); a `>` column is a continuation (nothing). Stops at the bracket-suspend sentinel. Returns `{ out, stack }`. Internal layout helper.

engine:closedAnd.label: Closed and
engine:closedAnd.description: Tri-state `and` over closed children: any proven-false ⇒ Just false; else any undecided ⇒ Nothing; else Just true. Threads { f = false-seen, u = unknown-seen }. Internal helper.

engine:closedCall.label: Closed call
engine:closedCall.description: Route a closed `ECall` head to its decider: and/or/not compositions, eq, and the four comparisons; any other head ⇒ Nothing (undecided). Internal helper.

engine:closedCompare.label: Closed compare
engine:closedCompare.description: Decide a closed comparison (lt/lte/gt/gte): both sides must constant-fold to numbers (affineOf ""), then applyCompare; otherwise Nothing (undecided). Internal helper.

engine:closedEq.label: Closed eq
engine:closedEq.description: Decide a closed `eq`: numeric equality when BOTH sides constant-fold (affineOf ""); else structural deepEqValue when both are ELit (so a closed residual `eq status Active` over a variant/record/list cell decides correctly, not reference-shallow — solver-extension Phase 5 swapped the non-numeric fallback from shallow `eq` to `deepEqValue`); else Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:closedEval.label: Closed eval
engine:closedEval.description: Decide a CLOSED predicate Expr ⇒ Maybe Bool (Just true / Just false proven; Nothing undecided / out-of-language). ELit true/false leaves; and/or/not compositions; eq/lt/lte/gt/gte over closed affine numeric terms (via P12's affineOf "") or shallow eq on non-numeric ELit pairs. Internal helper.

engine:closedNot.label: Closed not
engine:closedNot.description: Tri-state `not`: flip a proven child verdict; an undecided / empty operand ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:closedNum.label: Closed num
engine:closedNum.description: Constant-fold a closed Expr to a number via P12's affineOf "" (a var name that cannot match ⇒ any closed numeric term extracts as coeff 0, k = its value); Just k when ok and coeff 0, else Nothing (non-numeric / contains a var). Internal helper.

engine:closedOr.label: Closed or
engine:closedOr.description: Tri-state `or` over closed children: any proven-true ⇒ Just true; else any undecided ⇒ Nothing; else Just false. Threads { t = true-seen, u = unknown-seen }. Internal helper.

engine:coerceDomain.label: Coerce domain
engine:coerceDomain.description: Append box/unbox helper calls when the produced domain doesn't match the target. Returns a LowerOutput with the augmented instrs + target domain. 6 productive arms (DomNum→Ref boxNum, DomRef→Num unboxNum, DomBool→Ref boxBool, DomRef→Bool unboxBool, DomBool→Num F64ConvertI32S, DomNum→Bool F64Const 0 + F64Ne) + 2 short-circuits (target=DomUnknown, produced=target).

engine:coerceLlvmDomain.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:coerceLlvmDoubleToPtr.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:coerceLlvmI1ToPtr.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:coerceLlvmPtrToDouble.label: LLVM lowering: coerceLlvmPtrToDouble
engine:coerceLlvmPtrToDouble.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:coerceLlvmPtrToI1.label: LLVM lowering: coerceLlvmPtrToI1
engine:coerceLlvmPtrToI1.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.
