engine:decomposeMatchesVariantType.label: decompose: matchesVariantType
engine:decomposeMatchesVariantType.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — distinguish canonical Maybe from ordinary variants after the root semantic-slot preflight. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:dedupNums.label: Dedup numbers
engine:dedupNums.description: Order-preserving de-duplication of a number list (eq-based). Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:dedupNumsInto.label: Dedup numbers into
engine:dedupNumsInto.description: dedupNums' accumulator pass: append each unseen number. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:dedupPats.label: Dedup pats
engine:dedupPats.description: Order-preserving de-duplication of an alt-branch list by showPat key (idempotence). Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:dedupStr.label: Dedup strings
engine:dedupStr.description: Order-preserving de-duplication of a string list. Internal helper.

engine:dedupStrInto.label: Dedup strings into
engine:dedupStrInto.description: dedupStr's accumulator pass: append each unseen element. Internal helper.

engine:dedupeRows.label: Dedupe rows
engine:dedupeRows.description: Deduplicate a row list by structural row equality (set semantics; O(n²) — acceptable v1), preserving first-seen order. Internal helper.

engine:dedupeValues.label: enumerate: dedupeValues
engine:dedupeValues.description: Phase 15 / decide-substrate Phase 3 Step D — deduplicate a value list by STRUCTURAL equality (deepEqValue — scalars byte-identical to the old shallow std `eq`; records/variants/rows now dedupe structurally, correct set semantics), preserving first-seen order. Internal helper.

engine:deepEqEntries.label: Deep eq entries
engine:deepEqEntries.description: Structural equality of two `entries` lists (records/variants/arrays as {key, value} pairs): equal length AND every entry of the first finds a matching key in the second with deep-equal values (key-set semantics, order-robust — mirrors the evaluator's deepEqual). Internal helper for Phase-5 deep matching.

engine:deepEqEntriesAll.label: Deep eq entries all
engine:deepEqEntriesAll.description: True when EVERY {key, value} entry of the first list finds a same-key entry in the second whose value is deepEqValue-equal (the per-key half of deepEqEntries; lengths are pre-checked equal). Internal helper for Phase-5 deep matching.

engine:deepEqValue.label: Deep eq value
engine:deepEqValue.description: Structural deep equality over an arbitrary value (solver-extension Phase 5): scalars (Number/String/Bool/Char/null) via the std `eq` leaf; arrays element-wise (index-keyed entries); records/variants by key-set + per-key recursion over `entries` (reads `$tag`/fields as plain data). Agrees with shallow `eq` on scalars (so scalar queries are byte-identical) but matches structurally-equal variant/record/list cells where shallow `eq` is reference-shallow. Entry-free cells use the host equality boundary: empty plain records compare structurally, while opaque host values retain identity. THE substrate-wide structural equality (decide-substrate Phase 3 Step D): the relational matching (matchOne / rowEq / closedEq), the containment structural-eq tail (seenPair), the enum-trio element-eq (setAlgebraEnumContainsLoop — contains/⊆/∩ over enums, completing the kernel's witness rule for OBJECT witnesses), and enumerate's dedupe/intersection (valueMember) all bottom out here. Internal helper.

engine:defFrame.label: Def frame
engine:defFrame.description: Assemble a `{def: {name, params, body, directives?}}` frame; body lowered via syntaxToJsonLogic. parser-substrate Phase 5a.

engine:defaultFixityTable.label: Default fixity table
engine:defaultFixityTable.description: The parser's default operator fixity as DATA: STRUCTURAL_FIXITY ($/|>/&/in/.) ∪ the std Infixable projection (the 14 canonical + &&/|| aliases + >>=/<> qualified-method ops), exactly the merge getDefaultFixity builds (fenel-parser.ts:365). Each row { notation, fnId, prec, assoc } — fnId the emission codeName (`+` ⇒ `add`), prec/assoc from STRUCTURAL_FIXITY + parser-fixities.fenel. Closure-captured by exprGrammar (decision 3); LIVE Infixable / block-scope sourcing is Phase 5. parser-substrate Phase 3.

engine:depTypesAnyMember.label: dependent-types: anyMember
engine:depTypesAnyMember.description: Phase 7a — does the input keys list contain at least one key from the known keys list? Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:derivAtom.label: Derive under atom
engine:derivAtom.description: The Brzozowski derivative of a Pat under an atom (the set of firing predicate keys), at this state's localKeys. PMatch: empty when its key is outside the state OR not firing, else eps. PSeq captures the nullable-left tail via cAlt. PRep mirrors pattern.ts (max 0 dead; min floors at 0; the -1 unbounded sentinel preserved by decMax). Internal helper.

engine:derivPat.label: Derive pattern
engine:derivPat.description: The single-result Brzozowski derivative of `pat` w.r.t. token `t`, at step suffix `k`, threading the OLD env's nullability (`naIdx`) + parseNull (`paIdx`) fixpoint INDEXES (7h S2: name→value `fromEntries`-built records read O(1) via `mapGet`, built once per step by the caller). PMatch ⇒ PEpsV t when `wsMember`, else PEmpty. PSeq with a nullable left captures the left's null VALUE at derivation time via a red (the M&D `δ(a)∘D(b)` rule); the right tail is KEPT LITERAL so its refs stay pointed at the FRESH (un-derived) productions — that is what lets `"1" S "2"` re-enter a fresh S. PRef m ⇒ PRef m@k (the derived SIBLING, NOT a recursion into m's body) — the strict-step that makes left/mutual recursion terminate. PRep mirrors `pattern.ts` (min floors at 0, the -1 unbounded sentinel stays -1). parser-substrate Phase 1.

engine:derivWsPat.label: Derive under representative
engine:derivWsPat.description: The Brzozowski derivative of a Pat under a CONCRETE representative element `rep` (the structured-partition counterpart of derivAtom): PMatch ⇒ eps when `wsMember (wsOf k) rep`, else empty; PSeq captures the nullable-left tail via cAltC; PRep mirrors pattern.ts (max 0 dead; min floors at 0; the -1 unbounded sentinel via decMax). Uses the ACI-canonical cAltC (not cAlt) so deep-`.*` derivative states stay finite + bounded. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:deriveFmapAppHasParam.label: derive-functor: appHasParam
engine:deriveFmapAppHasParam.description: Phase 6c — does an applied-type's arg list carry the functor param directly (one-level nesting)? A nested TtApp arg (compound nesting) does NOT count — D-6c-2 fence. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFmapArgIsParam.label: derive-functor: argIsParam
engine:deriveFmapArgIsParam.description: Phase 6c — is a single TraversalType arg the functor param (TtVar paramName)? Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFmapFindCase.label: derive-functor: findCase
engine:deriveFmapFindCase.description: Phase 6b — locate the TtVariantCase matching the value's $tag. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFmapFold.label: Derive fmap (generic fold)
engine:deriveFmapFold.description: Phase 6b — the generic schema-directed `fmap`: any `* -> *` type without an authored Functor instance gets fmap free. Maps the functor-param leaves (TtVar paramName), recurses self-recursive fields (TtNamed typeName), leaves the rest (multi-param sound, the structuralMap repair). The decision half of the derived Functor instance; the engine:deriveFmap bridge supplies (g, value, schemaView, paramName, typeName). Total: descends only into strictly-smaller self-recursive sub-values.

engine:deriveFmapMapField.label: derive-functor: mapField
engine:deriveFmapMapField.description: Phase 6b/6c/1a — classify a field by its TraversalType: TtVar paramName ⇒ apply g (the functor param); TtNamed typeName ⇒ recurse (self-recursive); TtApp carrying the param ⇒ re-dispatch Functor.fmap on the nested functor value (D-6b-5, one level, 6c); TtMap whose values carry the param ⇒ mapFmap g over the map values (D-6c-3, closed Phase 1a); else leave (other vars / fixed types / compound nesting). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFmapRebuild.label: derive-functor: rebuild
engine:deriveFmapRebuild.description: Phase 6b — rebuild a case's value: thread acc from value (preserves $tag + untouched fields), set each declared field to its mapped value. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFmapRebuildGo.label: derive-functor: rebuildGo
engine:deriveFmapRebuildGo.description: Phase 6b — accumulator-threaded fold: walk the declared fields, assoc each mapped value onto the accumulator. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFmapStepField.label: derive-functor: stepField
engine:deriveFmapStepField.description: Phase 6b — one field: read the value's field (absent ⇒ leave acc untouched), classify+map, assoc onto acc. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFoldrAppHasParam.label: derive-foldable: appHasParam
engine:deriveFoldrAppHasParam.description: Phase 6c — does an applied-type's arg list carry the functor param directly (one-level nesting)? A nested TtApp arg (compound nesting) does NOT count — D-6c-2 fence. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFoldrArgIsParam.label: derive-foldable: argIsParam
engine:deriveFoldrArgIsParam.description: Phase 6c — is a single TraversalType arg the functor param (TtVar paramName)? Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFoldrFields.label: derive-foldable: foldFields
engine:deriveFoldrFields.description: Phase 6c — right-fold over a case's declared fields: recurse the tail to a folded-rest accumulator, then step the head field on top (last-to-first). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFoldrFindCase.label: derive-foldable: findCase
engine:deriveFoldrFindCase.description: Phase 6c — locate the TtVariantCase matching the value's $tag. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFoldrFold.label: Derive foldr (generic fold)
engine:deriveFoldrFold.description: Phase 6c — the generic schema-directed `foldr`: any `* -> *` type without an authored Foldable instance gets foldr free. Folds the functor-param leaves (TtVar paramName) into the seed with the binop, recurses self-recursive fields (TtNamed typeName), re-dispatches one-level nested foreign functors (TtApp carrying the param), skips the rest (multi-param sound, the structuralFold repair). The decision half of the derived Foldable instance; the engine:deriveFoldr bridge supplies (f, seed, value, schemaView, paramName, typeName). Right-fold order; total: descends only into strictly-smaller self-recursive sub-values.

engine:deriveFoldrFoldField.label: derive-foldable: foldField
engine:deriveFoldrFoldField.description: Phase 6c/1a — classify a field by its TraversalType: TtVar paramName ⇒ fold into acc (the functor param); TtNamed typeName ⇒ recurse (self-recursive); TtApp carrying the param ⇒ re-dispatch Foldable.foldr on the nested functor value (D-6b-5, one level); TtMap whose values carry the param ⇒ mapFoldr f acc over the map values (D-6c-3, closed Phase 1a); else leave (other vars / fixed types / compound nesting). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveFoldrStepField.label: derive-foldable: stepField
engine:deriveFoldrStepField.description: Phase 6c — one field: read the value's field (absent ⇒ leave acc untouched), classify+fold onto acc. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveProductions.label: Derive productions
engine:deriveProductions.description: Derive the bodies of the named (reachable) productions of `g` w.r.t. token `t` at step `k`, threading the fixpoint INDEXES `naIdx`/`paIdx` — the env half of the strict whole-grammar step. 7h S2: builds the env's name→Pat index once (`fromEntries`) so each `bodyOf` is O(1). Each reachable production `n` yields a derived sibling named `n@k`. Returns the new `[{ name, pat }]` siblings. Internal helper.

engine:deriveTraverse.label: Derive traverse (bridge)
engine:deriveTraverse.description: Phase 6d — the reflection + marshal bridge behind `Traversable.traverse`: resolves the dispatched value's owning type and the applicative `g` (from `f`'s declared return type, else a first element), marshals the schema, and delegates the sequencing to `deriveTraverseFold` / `deriveTraverseList`. Returns the value unchanged when the applicative cannot be resolved. Implemented by a context native of the `derive-functor` container.

engine:deriveTraverseAp.label: derive-traversable: ap
engine:deriveTraverseAp.description: Phase 6d — combine a traversed field onto the g-accumulator: fmap a one-field setter over acc, then ap against the field's g-wrapped value. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseAppHasParam.label: derive-traversable: appHasParam
engine:deriveTraverseAppHasParam.description: Phase 6d — does an applied-type's arg list carry the functor param directly (one-level nesting)? A nested TtApp arg (compound nesting) does NOT count — D-6d-4 fence. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseArgIsParam.label: derive-traversable: argIsParam
engine:deriveTraverseArgIsParam.description: Phase 6d — is a single TraversalType arg the functor param (TtVar paramName)? Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseCombineField.label: derive-traversable: combineField
engine:deriveTraverseCombineField.description: Phase 6d/1a — classify a field by its TraversalType: TtVar paramName ⇒ f the value (g b); TtNamed typeName ⇒ recurse (self-recursive); TtApp carrying the param ⇒ re-dispatch Traversable.traverse on the nested functor value (D-6d-4, one level); TtMap whose values carry the param ⇒ mapTraverse f over the map values (D-6c-3, closed Phase 1a); else leave. Combine the traversed effect onto the g-accumulator via deriveTraverseAp. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseFields.label: derive-traversable: fields
engine:deriveTraverseFields.description: Phase 6d — sequence a case's fields: acc starts at `pureFn value` (g-wrapped original), each traversed field is combined via ap. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseFieldsGo.label: derive-traversable: fieldsGo
engine:deriveTraverseFieldsGo.description: Phase 6d — accumulator-threaded fold: walk the declared fields, combine each traversed field's effect onto the g-accumulator via ap. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseFindCase.label: derive-traversable: findCase
engine:deriveTraverseFindCase.description: Phase 6d — locate the TtVariantCase matching the value's $tag. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseFold.label: Derive traverse (generic sequence)
engine:deriveTraverseFold.description: Phase 6d — the generic schema-directed `traverse`: any `* -> *` type without an authored Traversable instance gets traverse free. Sequences the functor-param leaves (TtVar paramName) with the threaded applicative, recurses self-recursive fields (TtNamed typeName), re-dispatches one-level nested foreign functors (TtApp carrying the param), leaves the rest. The decision half of the derived Traversable instance; the engine:deriveTraverse bridge supplies (f, value, schemaView, paramName, typeName, pureFn, apFn) — pureFn/apFn the resolved applicative g (D-6d-2). Total: descends only into strictly-smaller self-recursive sub-values.

engine:deriveTraverseList.label: derive-traversable: list
engine:deriveTraverseList.description: Phase 6d — the array-repr arm: traverse a List left-to-right, sequencing with the threaded applicative. `traverse f [] = pure []`; `traverse f (x:xs) = ap (fmap (:) (f x)) (traverse f xs)`. Called by the engine:deriveTraverse bridge for JS arrays. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseListCons.label: derive-traversable: listCons
engine:deriveTraverseListCons.description: Phase 6d — the List cons step: ap (fmap prepend (f x)) (traverse f rest). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraversePrepend.label: derive-traversable: prepend
engine:deriveTraversePrepend.description: Phase 6d — cons an element onto the front of a list (List traverse's builder). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseSetter.label: derive-traversable: setter
engine:deriveTraverseSetter.description: Phase 6d — one-field record setter: assoc nv onto v at fldName. Curried so fmap+ap thread it. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:deriveTraverseStepField.label: derive-traversable: stepField
engine:deriveTraverseStepField.description: Phase 6d — one field: read the value's field (absent ⇒ leave acc), classify+combine its effect onto acc. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:descriptionOfValue.label: identifiable: descriptionOfValue
engine:descriptionOfValue.description: Phase 10b sub-step 2 — description for a specific value, falling back to its type's Describable instance. Same shape as labelOfValue (canonical-lifted) over the `__description` / `description` fields. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/identifiable.ts:descriptionOfValue.

engine:desugar.label: Desugar
engine:desugar.description: Map the surface Syntax ADT (14 cases, sugars intact) to the irreducible core Expr ADT (7 cases). The 6 sugars lower: SIf ⇒ ECall "if", SLet ⇒ right-nested applied-ELambda over single bindings, SDo ⇒ the same template with "_" params (singleton ⇒ bare, empty ⇒ unit ERecord), SOp ⇒ ECall of the parse-time-RESOLVED head, SWhere ⇒ the SLet lowering (scoped-let), SMethod ⇒ a dotted-fnId ECall (cls ++ "." ++ method) — qualified-method heads ride as dotted fnId strings, no EMethod (compile-path fenced; interpreter evaluates {method} reflectively). SAnn (a type annotation) is transparent, except over an SMethod (the written type selects the instance): that one is kept as ECall "ann" and rejected by jsonLogicToExpr. The 7 mirrors are structural case-renames with sub-trees recursed; patterns pass through untouched. Total — no Result wrap. expr-substrate Phase 2; P4's compiler re-layer consumes these encodings as pass #0.

engine:desugarAnn.label: Desugar annotation
engine:desugarAnn.description: Lower a type annotation `(e : T)`: transparent (desugar e) unless e is a qualified method call (SMethod), whose written type selects the instance — that one keeps the wire meaning as `ECall "ann" [desugar e, ELit T]` (never erased; no function resolves it, and jsonLogicToExpr rejects the shape first via desugarAnnotationError). modules-as-values Phase 2d.

engine:desugarAnnotationError.label: Desugar annotation error
engine:desugarAnnotationError.description: Walk a Syntax tree for the first type annotation over a qualified method call (`(Class.method … : T)` — SAnn over SMethod), returning Just a readable reason (the written type selects the instance, so erasing it would change which instance runs) or Nothing. jsonLogicToExpr turns Just into Err Unsupported (the compiler-boundary rejection). modules-as-values Phase 2d.

engine:desugarAnnotationErrorList.label: Desugar annotation error (list)
engine:desugarAnnotationErrorList.description: desugarAnnotationError over a list of Syntax nodes: the first Just reason, else Nothing. modules-as-values Phase 2d.

engine:desugarArmSyntaxes.label: Desugar arm Syntax children
engine:desugarArmSyntaxes.description: Collect the Syntax children of a list of match arms — each arm's optional guard, then its body — onto an accumulator. modules-as-values Phase 2d.

engine:desugarArms.label: Desugar match arms
engine:desugarArms.description: Walk a list of {pattern, body} match arms, desugaring each arm body while passing the pattern through UNTOUCHED (one shared Pattern ADT — P1 decision 1). Threading helper for the SMatch case.

engine:desugarDoChain.label: Desugar do chain
engine:desugarDoChain.description: Build SDo's sequence as the applied-ELambda template with discarded-binding name "_" (decision 5): ECall "$" [ELambda ["_"] <rest>, desugar e1], bottoming at desugar of the last expr (the chain's value). Singleton ⇒ desugar the one expr bare; empty ⇒ ERecord [] (unit record, totality). Singleton discriminated via head-of-tail (std:tail returns Just [] for singletons).

engine:desugarFields.label: Desugar record fields
engine:desugarFields.description: Walk a list of {name, value} record fields, desugaring each field's value while preserving the field name. Threading helper for the SRecord case.

engine:desugarLetChain.label: Desugar let chain
engine:desugarLetChain.description: Right-nested applied-ELambda builder over SLet bindings (decision 4): each binding ⇒ ECall "$" [ELambda [name] <rest>, desugar value], <rest> recursing on the remaining bindings and bottoming at desugar body. One binding per lambda preserves sequential scope (binding N's value sits inside lambdas 1..N-1). Empty bindings ⇒ desugar body (totality fallback).

engine:desugarList.label: Desugar Syntax list
engine:desugarList.description: Walk a list of Syntax children (SCall.args / SConstruct.args / SOp.operands), desugaring each via `desugar` and appending to the accumulator. Threading helper for the list-carrying Syntax cases.

engine:diffToFloor.label: Diff to floor
engine:diffToFloor.description: floor-kernel Phase 1 — the `∖ = ∩ ∘ ¬` derivation witness (fwd): rewrite `SeDiff a b` to its Layer-0 definition `SeIntersect [a, SeComplement b]` (§3.2 `∖ = ∩ ∘ ¬`). Identity on values — the iso is denotational; the equality claim is lawDiffDef. Non-diff input passes through unchanged.

engine:directComparisonOp.label: Direct comparison op
engine:directComparisonOp.description: Map a canonical codeName to its direct-Wasm-op for the six f64 comparison ops (lt/lte/gt/gte/eq/neq, each producing i32 0/1 → DomBool). Returns WDNoDirectOp for everything else. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:DIRECT_COMPARISON_OPS.

engine:directNumericOp.label: Direct numeric op
engine:directNumericOp.description: Map a canonical codeName to its direct-Wasm-op + result-domain pair for the four standard f64 numeric ops (add/sub/mul/div). Returns WDNoDirectOp for everything else — caller falls through to the runtime-helper-import path. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:DIRECT_NUMERIC_OPS.

engine:directivePolicyTable.label: Directive policy table
engine:directivePolicyTable.description: The closed set of directive names the loader admits, one DirectivePolicy row each. The source of truth for fenel-module.ts's DIRECTIVE_POLICY mirror (pinned byte-for-byte by fenel-directive-policy.test.ts). Adding a directive name means adding a row HERE first.

engine:dischargeGrade.label: Discharge grade
engine:dischargeGrade.description: The 6a hook's grade policy, Fenel-bodied (expr-substrate Phase 6b0): a kernel-verified SolverChecked on an Ok proposal ⇒ Discharged; a WitnessError proposal ⇒ Refuted with the representation/structure refutation message (the new, wanted failure mode — distinct from 'missing'); every other combination (Undecided / OutOfScope / kernel-declined) ⇒ None — honest non-evidence, the law stays 'missing'. The TS hook replays the marker into ProveMissingOutcome + the stats tally.

engine:disjoint.label: Disjoint types
engine:disjoint.description: set-algebra-to-fenel Phase 6 / floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5)+P1(a.6) — decide TraversalType disjointness. Void proves; opaque peels; the two `$tagged` peels are RETIRED and abstain (P1(a.8), `t.dis.tagged`); Boolean formers recurse; refined leaves keep only positive proofs. Exact Maybe is partitioned from ordinary tagged variants: exact/exact proves overlap only after eager-plan readiness, mixed pairs abstain, and ordinary variants require unique/default-discriminator plus keyed-product coordinate/occurrence gates before tag reasoning. Cross-former facts remain limited to unpeeled live host-carrier partitions.

engine:disjointFold.label: Disjoint fold
engine:disjointFold.description: Fold the satisfiable atoms of a disjoint state: skip atoms where a OR b derives empty (the dead-branch skip); recurse on (da, db); short-circuit false; thread visited. Internal helper.

engine:disjointFoldS.label: Disjoint fold (structured)
engine:disjointFoldS.description: Fold the partition representatives of a structured disjoint state: skip representatives where a OR b derives empty (the dead-branch skip); recurse on (da, db); short-circuit false; thread visited. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:disjointGo.label: Disjoint go
engine:disjointGo.description: One coinductive step of the disjointness walk over (pa, pb), threading the visited memo. Either side empty => true (disjoint); both nullable => false (empty string shared); memo cycle => true; no preds => true; over 16 preds => conservative false; else fold the satisfiable atoms skipping dead branches. Internal helper.

engine:disjointGoS.label: Disjoint go (structured)
engine:disjointGoS.description: One coinductive step of the structured disjointness walk over (pa, pb), threading the visited memo. Either side empty ⇒ true; both nullable ⇒ false; memo cycle ⇒ true; no preds ⇒ true; else derive under each partition representative skipping dead branches. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:disjointIntersectOp.label: disjoint: disjointIntersectOp
engine:disjointIntersectOp.description: Phase 2 Step 1b / type-substrate P1(a.5) — the intersect arm of disjoint: an intersect is disjoint from `other` if ANY branch is (A∩B ⊆ A). mOr-fold of emTrueOnly(disjointW rp branch other); Just true on a proof else Nothing. THREADS `rp` for the same reason disjointUnion does — an intersect that is a peeled `$opaque`'s pure view still rides that opaque's representation. Internal helper.

engine:disjointLeaf.label: disjoint: disjointLeaf
engine:disjointLeaf.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5) — sound TraversalType leaf disjointness: refined leaves accept only positive set/base disjoint proofs; named pairs use Fenel-owned domain classification (and exact-name inhabitance for Just false); a named atom is disjoint from a rigid former only on the host sorts that former genuinely refuses (ttNamedSortExclusive); two rigid formers are disjoint only when their host carriers are exclusive (ttHostSortExclusive — the Array.isArray partition, `tuple` vs `record`/`unit`). BOTH rules additionally require rp = false (no `$opaque` peel). Every other cross-kind pair, and variables/unknowns/aliases, abstain. The former-as-sort model is RETRACTED: distinct formers no longer prove disjointness. Internal helper.

engine:disjointNamed.label: disjoint: named
engine:disjointNamed.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5) — named-leaf disjointness. Two names: exact known-inhabited name ⇒ Just false; otherwise differing known value domains ⇒ Just true. A known atomic name is disjoint from a rigid former only where that former's live membership genuinely refuses the atom's host sort (ttNamedSortExclusive): `map` refuses nothing (its key domain is unresolved at the leaf — Fin-n maps take arrays, locale maps take strings, enum-keyed maps accept identically) and `arrow` accepts fnId STRINGS, so String-vs-arrow and every atom-vs-map pair now abstain. Unknown names and array-domain aliases abstain. Internal helper.

engine:disjointNonFormer.label: disjoint: disjointNonFormer
engine:disjointNonFormer.description: Phase 2.4 / floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5)+P1(a.6) — two unpeeled variants enter disjointVariant's exact-Maybe/ordinary partition and face gates; everything else uses the sound leaf cascade. After an opaque peel, tags describe the pure ADT rather than the live carrier, so variant pairs abstain.

engine:disjointRefined.label: disjoint: refined
engine:disjointRefined.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — refined r=base∩set is disjoint from another refined when their predicate sets OR their bases are provably disjoint; against any other type, a positive base-disjoint proof suffices. emTrueOnly deliberately drops Just false: overlapping predicates/bases do not prove the intersections inhabited. Internal helper.

engine:disjointUnion.label: disjoint: disjointUnion
engine:disjointUnion.description: Phase 2 Step 1b / floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5) — a TraversalType union is disjoint from other iff every branch is; mAnd-fold the unified disjoint member. Commutativity serves a union on either side. THREADS `rp` rather than resetting it (round-3 review): when the union IS the `pure` view of a peeled `$opaque`, that opaque's representation still transports its branches, so a branch is NOT "a written type in its own right" and the carrier rules must stay refused. Propagating an already-set flag is strictly conservative — a top-level union arrives with rp already false. Internal helper.

engine:disjointVariant.label: disjoint: disjointVariant
engine:disjointVariant.description: Phase 2.4 / floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.6) — partition variant disjointness by the exact Maybe authority. Exact/exact returns plan-ready Just false because both accept null; an exact/ordinary pair abstains. Ordinary/ordinary first requires unique names, the live default discriminator, and complete keyed-product face gates, then folds shared-tag payload disjointness.

engine:disjointVariantFold.label: disjoint: disjointVariantFold
engine:disjointVariantFold.description: Phase 2.4 / floor-kernel Phase 3c — mAnd-fold over the first variant's TtVariantCases; exhausted means every shared tag payload was disjoint (or no tag was shared). Internal helper.

engine:disjointVariantOne.label: disjoint: disjointVariantOne
engine:disjointVariantOne.description: Phase 2.4 / floor-kernel Phase 3c / field-identity Phase 3 — one TtVariantCase's contribution: absent tag in the other case list ⇒ Just true; a shared tag delegates to FieldKey-aligned productDisjoint over the two validated TtField lists. Internal helper.

engine:disjointW.label: disjoint: disjointW
engine:disjointW.description: type-substrate P1(a.5) — the representation-peel-aware core of disjoint. Threads `rp`, set when an `$opaque` wrapper has been peeled to reach the current operands, and consumes it wherever a carrier-sensitive verdict could otherwise escape: the two host-carrier rules at the leaf (ttHostSortExclusive / ttNamedSortExclusive), `disjointNonFormer`'s tag arm (disjointVariant, whose constructor-tag rule is a claim about the PURE ADT), and both `$complement` handoffs to `subsetW`. None may decide a peeled operand: `$opaque` separates the pure ADT from the runtime representation, so after the peel the kind describes `pure` while the operand's live population is the REP's. ⚠ ROUND 20: what entitles `rp` is the INTENDED `Reprable` semantics plus the concrete false cell P1(a.5) measured — NOT the face behaviour of the registered NAME route, which is a SIBLING. The raw `$opaque` nodes that actually reach this peel (`Int.opaque` / `Nat.opaque` / `Bool.opaque` in the corpus) accept NOTHING at either measured face and witness nothing either way, and an INLINE `$opaque{pure=Number}` recurses into `pure` at both. Reading the name route as the evidence is what would license the blanket transplant to `ttTopCover` that rounds 10 and 12 REFUSED, losing the sound `empty(¬$opaque{pure = Number}) = Just false` (Int peels to $record but holds numbers; Nat/Bool/List peel to $variant but hold numbers/booleans/arrays). In particular, a peeled operand no longer describes the live carrier, and `subsetW` has no representation flag with which to justify the complement reduction, so those arms abstain when `rp` is set. `$refined` peels do NOT set it — a refinement does not change the carrier. **type-substrate P1(a.8): the two `$tagged` peels are RETIRED — BOTH operand orders now abstain unconditionally (ledger `t.dis.tagged`), and they are SEPARATELY REACHABLE arms: the LEFT peel fires when the left operand is `$tagged` AND no earlier arm has already decided — the void checks sit above both peels, so `dis(Tag(Number), $void)` is `Just true` at the void check and never reaches the peel — so the RIGHT peel is reached only when the left is not tagged, and a census of left-operand cells pins one of the two fences. Ground: validation reads a `$tagged` by UUID syntax only while `matchesShape` recurses into the value slot, so `<uuid>` is admitted by every `$tagged` type and a "disjoint" pair CAN share a live witness. The cell where that actually bites is `dis(Tag($void), Tag($void))` — both operands admit `<uuid>` while value-recursion makes both empty, so the two readings disagree and the arm must abstain. The MIXED cells are NOT contradictions and are PRICED rather than repaired: `<uuid>` does not validate against `Number` (MEASURED), so `dis(Tag($void), Number)` is disjoint under both readings. MEASURED at entry: `dis(Tag($void), Tag($void))`, `dis(Tag($void), Number)` and `dis(Number, Tag($void))` were all `Just true`.** The union and intersect arms THREAD the flag rather than resetting it (round 4); every remaining arm retains its pre-round-4 logic (the leaf and tag arms did change when `rp` was introduced, so "byte-identical to the pre-flag body" is NOT the right claim about them). Internal core.

engine:displayCategory.label: identifiable: displayCategory
engine:displayCategory.description: Phase 3j (module-substrate) — category for an id with a read-time fallback chain: `getCategory id` (the Categorizable instance, when present) → the id's module-prefix (the segment before `:`, e.g. `dispatch:sample` → `dispatch`) → "uncategorized" for an unprefixed id. Always returns a String. Replaces the module-name default the `.fenel` loader used to STORE as a Categorizable on every function. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedDisplayCategory`.

engine:displayLabel.label: identifiable: displayLabel
engine:displayLabel.description: Phase 3j (module-substrate) — display label for an id with a read-time fallback chain: `getLabel id` (the Labelable instance, when present) → the humanized canonical codeName (`humanizeCodeName (canonical codeName)`) → the id string itself. Always returns a value (never Nothing). Replaces the humanized-codeName default the `.fenel` loader used to STORE as a Labelable on every function; the loader is now symmetric with `defineFunction` (Labelable only when explicitly declared). Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedDisplayLabel`.

engine:dnfAnd.label: rel-solve: dnfAnd
engine:dnfAnd.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — fold an `and`'s args: the running branch list starts at the unit [[]] and cartesian-products with each arg's own dnfBranches (dnfProduct — each pair concatenates conjunct lists, preserving order). Over-cap (>64 branches) or a Nothing arg ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:dnfBranches.label: rel-solve: dnfBranches
engine:dnfBranches.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — DNF-distribute a query Expr over its rel-bearing connective skeleton ⇒ Maybe (List of conjunct-lists). `and` ⇒ bounded cartesian product (dnfAnd); a REL-BEARING `or` ⇒ per-arg branch concat (dnfOr — the disjunctive split); a REL-FREE `or` / `not` / any other Expr ⇒ one leaf conjunct (rel-free or stays a closedEval residual; not classifies at expandOne). Nothing = the 64-branch blowup guard. Internal helper.

engine:dnfLeaf.label: rel-solve: dnfLeaf
engine:dnfLeaf.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — one leaf conjunct as a DNF: Just [[expr]]. Internal helper.

engine:dnfOr.label: rel-solve: dnfOr
engine:dnfOr.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — concatenate a rel-bearing `or`'s args' branch lists (each arg's own dnfBranches — nested and/or recurse). Over-cap (>64) or a Nothing arg ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:dnfProduct.label: rel-solve: dnfProduct
engine:dnfProduct.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — the cartesian product of two branch lists: every (left, right) pair concatenates its conjunct lists (left ++ right — conjunct order preserved). Internal helper.

engine:dnfProductOne.label: rel-solve: dnfProductOne
engine:dnfProductOne.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — one left conjunct-list crossed with every right conjunct-list (concat per pair). Internal helper.

engine:doStmts.label: Re-nest do statements
engine:doStmts.description: The ≥2-statement re-nest (jlsDoOp mirror): collect leading lets into SLet bindings; if nothing follows ⇒ SLet with body = SVar lastName; else the tail ⇒ SDo (mid-stream lets nest recursively), wrapped in SLet when leading bindings exist. Internal expr-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 3c.

engine:domAddBounds.label: fork: dom-add-bounds
engine:domAddBounds.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — merge a domain's `{ ltes, lts }` bounds delta (domBoundsAtoms) into the full `{ eqs, neqs, ltes, lts }` atoms accumulator (eqs/neqs unchanged). Internal helper.

engine:domAllNumeric.label: fork: dom-all-numeric
engine:domAllNumeric.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — true when a value list is non-empty and every element passes isNumber (the all-numeric enum gate). Internal helper.

engine:domAllNumericRest.label: fork: dom-all-numeric-rest
engine:domAllNumericRest.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the tail loop of domAllNumeric: true when every remaining element is numeric (empty ⇒ true). Internal helper.

engine:domBoundAtom.label: fork: dom-bound-atom
engine:domBoundAtom.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the order atom of one interval bound (isLo = the lo side): a present numeric bound ⇒ the delta from domBoundDelta; Nothing / non-numeric ⇒ empty. Internal helper.

engine:domBoundAtomJust.label: fork: dom-bound-atom-just
engine:domBoundAtomJust.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the order-atom delta of a PRESENT interval bound: a numeric value ⇒ domBoundDelta; a non-numeric (string/expr) bound ⇒ empty delta. Internal helper.

engine:domBoundDelta.label: fork: dom-bound-delta
engine:domBoundDelta.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — build the order-atom delta for a numeric bound value `n`: the atom is `ELit n ≤/< term` on the lo side (isLo) or `term ≤/< ELit n` on the hi side; inclusive ⇒ an lte atom, exclusive ⇒ an lt atom. Internal helper.

engine:domBoundNum.label: fork: dom-bound-num
engine:domBoundNum.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — extract the numeric value of an interval bound, tolerating BOTH the wire shape (`{ value, inclusive }` with a bare scalar `value`) AND the registered `SetBound { value = BvNumber { value = n } }` ADT shape; a non-numeric (string / expr) bound ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:domBoundNumeric.label: fork: dom-bound-numeric
engine:domBoundNumeric.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — true when a Maybe-bound is present with a numeric value (domBoundNum ⇒ Just). Internal helper.

engine:domBoundsAtoms.label: fork: dom-bounds-atoms
engine:domBoundsAtoms.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — extract the numeric BOUNDS ATOMS a domain implies for a read `term`, as a `{ ltes, lts }` delta: a SeInterval with numeric-lit bounds ⇒ `lo ≤/< term` + `term ≤/< hi` (strict per the bound's inclusive flag); an all-numeric SeEnum ⇒ `min ≤ term ≤ max` (inclusive); every other shape (SeAll / non-numeric / unions / SeWhere) ⇒ empty. Sound: the bounds are implied by domain membership. Internal helper.

engine:domEnumAtoms.label: fork: dom-enum-atoms
engine:domEnumAtoms.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the SeEnum arm of domBoundsAtoms: an all-numeric non-empty enum ⇒ the inclusive min/max bounds `min ≤ term ≤ max` (both lte atoms); a non-numeric / empty enum ⇒ empty delta. Internal helper.

engine:domEnumAtomsMM.label: fork: dom-enum-atoms-mm
engine:domEnumAtomsMM.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — build the inclusive min/max bounds atoms `min ≤ term ≤ max` from a { min, max } (both lte); Nothing ⇒ empty delta. Internal helper.

engine:domEnumAtomsVs.label: fork: dom-enum-atoms-vs
engine:domEnumAtomsVs.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the enum-values arm of domEnumAtoms: an all-numeric non-empty list ⇒ the min/max bounds (domEnumAtomsMM ∘ domMinMax); else empty delta. Internal helper.

engine:domEnumNumeric.label: fork: dom-enum-numeric
engine:domEnumNumeric.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — true when a SeEnum's values are all numeric (non-empty). Internal helper.

engine:domHiAtom.label: fork: dom-hi-atom
engine:domHiAtom.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the upper-bound atom of an interval: a numeric hi bound ⇒ `term ≤ hi` (inclusive) or `term < hi` (exclusive); Nothing / non-numeric ⇒ empty delta. Internal helper.

engine:domInstLookup.label: fork: dom-inst-lookup
engine:domInstLookup.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — find the explicit `SymbolicDomain` domain SetExpr for (typeName, methodName) in the domInsts list; Just domain on hit, Nothing otherwise. Internal helper.

engine:domIntervalAtoms.label: fork: dom-interval-atoms
engine:domIntervalAtoms.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the SeInterval arm of domBoundsAtoms: the lo bound (numeric) ⇒ `lo ≤ term` (inclusive) / `lo < term` (exclusive); the hi bound (numeric) ⇒ `term ≤ hi` / `term < hi`; a non-numeric / absent bound contributes nothing. Internal helper.

engine:domIntervalNumeric.label: fork: dom-interval-numeric
engine:domIntervalNumeric.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — true when a SeInterval has at least one numeric-lit bound (lo or hi) — a numeric-bounded interval certifies its read term numeric. Internal helper.

engine:domLoAtom.label: fork: dom-lo-atom
engine:domLoAtom.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the lower-bound atom of an interval: a numeric lo bound ⇒ `lo ≤ term` (inclusive) or `lo < term` (exclusive); Nothing / non-numeric ⇒ empty delta. Internal helper.

engine:domLookupVar.label: fork: dom-lookup-var
engine:domLookupVar.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — find a minted var's domain in the witness domMap (a list of { varName, domain }); Just domain on hit, Nothing otherwise. Internal helper.

engine:domMinMax.label: fork: dom-min-max
engine:domMinMax.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the { min, max } of a non-empty numeric value list (folded via lt); empty ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:domMinMaxFold.label: fork: dom-min-max-fold
engine:domMinMaxFold.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — fold a numeric value list into the running { min, max } (lt comparisons). Internal helper.

engine:domNumeric.label: fork: dom-numeric
engine:domNumeric.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the certificate SOURCE predicate: true when a Maybe-domain is a numeric-bounded SeInterval (at least one numeric bound) OR an all-numeric non-empty SeEnum — the shapes over which a read term is certified numeric (the negated-order flip source). Nothing / SeAll / non-numeric ⇒ false. Internal helper.

engine:domReconstructRead.label: fork: dom-reconstruct-read
engine:domReconstructRead.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — rebuild the original read `ECall` term for a value-number group: `ECall { fnId = $effect:<typeName>:<methodName>, args = argTerms }` — eufValEq-equal to the predicate's read occurrences (the refutation face's term-identity for domain atoms). Internal helper.

engine:domSeedEntry.label: fork: dom-seed-entry
engine:domSeedEntry.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — seed one (typeName, methodName, term) against the domains into the running `{ atoms, certs }`: no domain ⇒ unchanged; a domain ⇒ merge its bounds atoms (domAddBounds) and, when the domain is numeric (domNumeric), append the term to certs (the negated-order certificate source). Internal helper.

engine:domSeedRefute.label: fork: dom-seed-refute
engine:domSeedRefute.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — build the refutation face's seeded `{ atoms, certs }` by folding the value-number GROUPS (symBuildGroups): for each group, reconstruct the read term (`ECall $effect:<class>:<method> argTerms`) and seed its domain's bounds atoms + numeric cert (domSeedEntry). Reads stay AS terms (no mint) — the reconstructed term is eufValEq-equal to the predicate's read occurrences ⇒ the bounds atoms prune congruently. Internal helper.

engine:domSeedWitness.label: fork: dom-seed-witness
engine:domSeedWitness.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — build the witness face's seeded `{ atoms, certs, domMap }` by folding the mint TABLE (symbolizeSharedDetailed): for each row, the minted `?sym:` `EVar` term seeds its domain's bounds atoms + numeric cert (domSeedEntry), AND — when a domain exists — a `{ varName, domain }` row joins domMap (the witness-solve domain lookup, keyed by the free var name). Internal helper.

engine:domTypeLookup.label: fork: dom-type-lookup
engine:domTypeLookup.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — find the effect method's declared return type for (typeName, methodName) in the domTypes list, project it via `typeToSetExpr`; a `SeAll` projection carries no information ⇒ Nothing (else Just the SetExpr). Internal helper.

engine:domTypeProject.label: fork: dom-type-project
engine:domTypeProject.description: Project a method's return TraversalType to its domain with typeToSetProjection; degradation or SeAll carries no information and becomes Nothing, otherwise return Just the SetExpr. Internal helper.

engine:domainEq.label: Domain equal
engine:domainEq.description: Structural equality on WasmDomain values. Used internally by tests + by coerceDomain's no-op short-circuit (when produced and target agree).

engine:domainFor.label: fork: domainFor
engine:domainFor.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the per-read DOMAIN lookup: an explicit scoped `SymbolicDomain` instance for (typeName, methodName) WINS (domInstLookup); else the effect method's declared return type projected via `typeToSetExpr` (domTypeLookup — a `SeAll` result carries NO information ⇒ Nothing). Returns Maybe SetExpr. Internal helper.

engine:domainOf.label: Domain of expression
engine:domainOf.description: Light CeExpr-domain inferrer. CeLit → number/bool/null/string → DomNum/Bool/Ref. CeVar → lookupLocal's domain or DomUnknown. CeCall → callDomainOf's resultDomain. Everything else → DomUnknown. Used by inferBranchDom to pick the CeIf result domain.

engine:domainOfLit.label: Domain of literal
engine:domainOfLit.description: Map a JS literal to its source-level domain: number → DomNum, boolean → DomBool, null/string → DomRef.

engine:domainOfLlvmLit.label: LLVM inference: domainOfLlvmLit
engine:domainOfLlvmLit.description: Phase 21.8.1 — LLVM inference body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:domainOfVar.label: Domain of CeVar
engine:domainOfVar.description: Resolve a variable name to its domain via HasWasmBuilder.lookupLocal. Out-of-scope name returns DomUnknown.

engine:domainToValType.label: Domain → ValType
engine:domainToValType.description: Map a source-level WasmDomain to its Wasm 3.0 numeric / reference value type. DomNum → F64; DomBool → I32; DomRef / DomUnknown → Externref (the safe boundary type for unknown). Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:domainToValType.

engine:dotIndexFrom.label: Dot index from
engine:dotIndexFrom.description: Index of the first `.` at or after `i` in `s`, or `length s` when absent (a total `indexOf('.', i)`). Internal expr-grammar helper. fenel-surface-extensions Phase 6.

engine:dottedHead.label: Dotted head
engine:dottedHead.description: Strip everything from the first '.' onward, returning the substring before the '.'. If no '.' is present, return the input. Used by `maybeAddFreeVar` to map dotted CeVar leaf names like `c.x` to the bound head `c` so the elem-checks compare against the outer/local binding sets correctly. Phase 5b28 — substrate fix for the closure-conversion dotted-capture bug class.

engine:dropBack.label: Drop back N
engine:dropBack.description: Drop the last `n` elements of a list (take length − n). Internal parse-file helper. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:dropFront.label: Drop front N
engine:dropFront.description: Drop the first `n` elements of a list. Internal parse-file helper. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:dropNl.label: Drop leading newlines
engine:dropNl.description: Drop leading `nl` tokens from a token list (the TS `parseSetForm` `this.skip()` before reading the first set-body token). Internal decl-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 4i.

engine:dtChildEqs.label: dt: childEqs
engine:dtChildEqs.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — zip two equal-length child-index lists into { lhs, rhs } term equalities, SKIPPING pairs already same-root (the fixpoint-termination guard — an already-merged pair must not re-derive). Terms recovered via dtTermAtIx. Internal helper.

engine:dtCoercingCtor.label: dt: coercingCtor
engine:dtCoercingCtor.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — true for a constructor name whose `construct` COERCES to a native rep instead of a `$tag`-tagged record: exactly True/False (the permanent ledger-B5 Bool arm; verified the only coercion at HEAD). Coercing ctors are excluded from every datatype rule (distinctness/injectivity key on the preserved `$tag`). A language-fact constant (the euf `$effect:`-prefix class). Internal helper.

engine:dtConflict.label: dt: conflict
engine:dtConflict.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D (D1 + D3) — true when two universe terms with DIFFERENT non-empty datatype tags (tag-preserving EConstruct ctors, or `$tag`-carrying lit records) share a union-find root: distinct `$tag`s can never be structurally equal (Step-1 eq compares `$tag` like any key) ⇒ the forcing equalities are unsat. Pairwise scan over the tagged entries. Internal helper.

engine:dtConflictScan.label: dt: conflictScan
engine:dtConflictScan.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the pairwise outer loop of dtConflict: each tagged entry against the entries after it (each unordered pair tested once). Internal helper.

engine:dtConflictWith.label: dt: conflictWith
engine:dtConflictWith.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — true when a tagged entry shares a root with some later tagged entry whose datatype tag DIFFERS (the D1/D3 conflict witness). Internal helper.

engine:dtCtorApps.label: dt: ctorApps
engine:dtCtorApps.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the universe entries that are NON-COERCING EConstruct applications (ctor name non-empty, not True/False) — the injectivity-scan candidates. Internal helper.

engine:dtCtorName.label: dt: ctorName
engine:dtCtorName.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the constructor name of an EConstruct term, or "" for every other Expr shape (the datatype-theory term view). Internal helper.

engine:dtDerive.label: dt: derive
engine:dtDerive.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D (D2 injectivity) — the equalities entailed by same-class same-shape constructs: every pair of tag-preserving (non-coercing) EConstruct entries with the SAME full signature (eufSig — ctor + field names) + same arity sharing a root emits pairwise child equalities for child pairs NOT already same-root (the fixpoint-termination guard). Same-shape tagged records are structurally equal iff their fields are (sound under Step-1 structural eq). The exchange payload feeding EUF, beside R3's. Internal helper.

engine:dtDeriveOuter.label: dt: deriveOuter
engine:dtDeriveOuter.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the pairwise outer loop of dtDerive: each ctor-app entry against the entries after it. Internal helper.

engine:dtDeriveWith.label: dt: deriveWith
engine:dtDeriveWith.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — pair one ctor-app entry u against the later entries v: same root + same eufSig + same arity ⇒ emit the not-yet-same-root child-pair equalities (dtChildEqs). Internal helper.

engine:dtLitTag.label: dt: litTag
engine:dtLitTag.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the `$tag` of an ELit whose value is a non-array, non-scalar record carrying an own `$tag` property (read through the dynamic-key `mapGet` boundary — no `$`-key authoring), or "" otherwise. The D3 lit-vs-ctor view. Internal helper.

engine:dtTagOf.label: dt: tagOf
engine:dtTagOf.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the datatype tag of a universe term under the rules: a tag-preserving EConstruct's ctor name, or a `$tag`-carrying ELit record's tag (D3); "" when neither (or when the ctor is coercing). The one string every dt rule keys on. Internal helper.

engine:dtTaggedEntries.label: dt: taggedEntries
engine:dtTaggedEntries.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the universe entries carrying a non-empty datatype tag (dtTagOf) — the distinctness-scan candidates, annotated { ix, expr, app, sig, childIxs }. Internal helper.

engine:dtTermAtIx.label: dt: termAtIx
engine:dtTermAtIx.description: decide-substrate Phase 6D — the Expr of the universe entry at a given index (Just / Nothing) — recovers child TERMS from the precomputed childIxs for the injectivity payload. Internal helper.

engine:durableFieldFromStorageData.label: Durable Field from storage data
engine:durableFieldFromStorageData.description: Attach an entity_instances row UUID to its typed Field data value.

engine:durableFieldStorageData.label: Durable Field storage data
engine:durableFieldStorageData.description: Project a durable Field entity to the ordinary entity_instances data value. The row id carries the UUID; the Field value carries the retained Codeable/lifecycle/reuse facts.

engine:effectSiteName.label: symbolize: effectSiteName
engine:effectSiteName.description: Phase 14a — the dot-free deterministic site namer: `?<fnId>@<path>`. Distinct effect-call sites get distinct structural paths ⇒ distinct names ⇒ no gensym counter is threaded. The name avoids `.` (field-access truncation in collectFreeVars — the load-bearing Step-0 constraint); `?`/`@`/`:`/`$`/`/` are all safe. Internal helper.

engine:effectfulFunctionsWith.label: Effectful functions with
engine:effectfulFunctionsWith.description: structural-dispatch Phase 3 — the universe-view `effectfulFunctionsWith(C)`: the ids of every function whose `requires` carries the effect / capability class `typeName` (membership over the seam-extracted constraint class-name list `f.requiresClasses`). `effectfulFunctionsWith("HasStateIO")` ⇒ the state-touching functions. A no-match ⇒ []. The LIGHT arm — a membership fold over the Phase-2 `requires` constraint shape, no decider. The function list is supplied by the TS reflection seam.

engine:effectfulFunctionsWithFold.label: universe-views: effectfulFunctionsWithFold
engine:effectfulFunctionsWithFold.description: structural-dispatch Phase 3 — the head/tail fold behind effectfulFunctionsWith: walk the marshalled function list, appending `f.id` when `typeName` is a member of `f.requiresClasses`. Internal helper.

engine:elemByShow.label: Elem by show
engine:elemByShow.description: True when some Pat in `xs` renders to the same showPat key as `key` (structural membership for the alt dedup). Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:elementToFrame.label: Element to frame
engine:elementToFrame.description: Map one `{frame, directives}` program element to its loader frame: def ⇒ {def:…}, sig ⇒ {type_sig:…}, module ⇒ {module_decl:…}, typedef ⇒ {type_def:…}, import ⇒ {import_decl:{module,names}} (signature-substrate Phase 4-prep; key order module-then-names matches the TS oracle; a directive-carrying import emits the empty frame the loader marshal REJECTS — mirroring the TS parser's directives-on-import throw). parser-substrate Phase 5a.

engine:elimDoubleComplement.label: Eliminate double complement
engine:elimDoubleComplement.description: floor-kernel Phase 1 — the `¬¬A = A` (classical involution) derivation witness: `SeComplement (SeComplement x)` rewrites to `x` (§3.2; data-fragment classicality — design/floor-kernel.md §4). The equality claim is lawDoubleComplement. Any other shape passes through unchanged.

engine:elimDoubleComplementInner.label: floor-axioms: elimDoubleComplementInner
engine:elimDoubleComplementInner.description: floor-kernel Phase 1 — elimDoubleComplement helper: inner also a complement ⇒ its inner; else the original. Internal helper.

engine:eliminateEmpty.label: Eliminate empty
engine:eliminateEmpty.description: The empty-language ELIMINATION pass that bounds `|g|` (parser-substrate Phase 8). Compute the empty-set fixpoint of `g`; when EMPTY (the common case) keep the OLD reachability prune over `(g, root)` VERBATIM (byte-identical to the pre-8 `stepGrammarWith` tail). When there ARE empties: simplify the root + every kept body propagating them (refs to `∅` annihilate via the smart constructors), DROP the empty rows, and re-prune to the productions reachable from the simplified root. Returns `{ g, root }`. Sound — a `∅` production contributes to no accepting parse and carries no reduction value, so the residual root's `parseNull` is byte-identical; only the live grammar shrinks from O(k) rows to O(grammar). Internal helper. parser-substrate Phase 8.

engine:emTrueOnly.label: empty: emTrueOnly
engine:emTrueOnly.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — forward ONLY a Tri's positive empty-proof: Just true ⇒ Just true, Just false ⇒ Nothing (drop the inhabited-claim), Nothing ⇒ Nothing. The soundness gate on the decideEmpty arm of emptyRefined (a decideEmpty Just false over a refined base is not a sound refined-inhabited proof). Internal helper.

engine:emitArmBody.label: Emit arm body
engine:emitArmBody.description: Wrap a match arm's body in a JsLet introducing the bindings introduced by the arm's pattern. When the pattern introduces no bindings (PatLit / PatWildcard at top), return the body verbatim.

engine:emitCall.label: Emit call
engine:emitCall.description: Four-way CeCall dispatch (after args have been lowered): 1) CALL_MAPPING[fnId] → binop / unary / concat shape; 2) `$dyn:` prefix → direct JsCall on a JsVar; 3) parseEffectFnId match → `$fenel.$effect.<Class>.<method>(...)`; 4) default → `$fenel.<fnId>(...)`.

engine:emitCaptureLoadPrologue.label: Emit closure capture-load prologue
engine:emitCaptureLoadPrologue.description: Emit the body's capture-loading prologue. For each i in 0..captures.length-1: LocalGet $env_idx + I32Const i + Call envGet + allocLocal name DomRef + LocalSet. Runs INSIDE the body frame so allocLocal pushes into the body's declaredLocals + sets the name in the body's locals map. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:910-922.

engine:emitClosureConstruction.label: Emit closure construction
engine:emitClosureConstruction.description: Emit the closure-construction sequence into the caller's out (after the body WasmFunc has been registered). For each capture i: LocalGet envLocalIdx + I32Const i + <capture-mini-instrs> + Call envSet. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:965-975.

engine:emitConstructDefault.label: Emit construct default
engine:emitConstructDefault.description: Canonical fall-through emit for a CeConstruct arm. Phase 5b13 factored this out so the True/False short-circuit at the top of emitExpr's CeConstruct arms can fall through to the standard `{$tag: ctor, ...}` JsObject shape on every other ctor.

engine:emitConstructGuardSubs.label: Emit construct guard subs (iteration)
engine:emitConstructGuardSubs.description: Per-sub-pattern iteration for PatConstruct's guard. Walks subs alongside an index counter; per sub: presence check (hasField/hasFieldNamed based on fieldNames[idx]) + I32And, then if sub is non-trivial, field-load + allocLocal + LocalSet + recursive emitWasmPatternGuard + I32And.

engine:emitExpr.label: Emit expression
engine:emitExpr.description: Main 10-arm CeExpr walker. Each arm produces the corresponding JsAst shape. CeLit / CeVar / CeIf produce JsLit / JsVar / JsTernary directly (a `$fn:<key>` CeVar, a global function passed as a value, produces the `$fenel` member a call of it uses); CeLet / CeDo / CeClosure / CeRecord follow the structural shape; CeCall dispatches through `emitCall`; CeConstruct splits on `fields` presence for named-key vs positional fallback; CeMatch builds a chained ternary right-to-left via `buildMatchChain`.

engine:emitExprList.label: Emit expr list
engine:emitExprList.description: Iterate over a list of CeExpr children, lowering each via `emitExpr` and accumulating into a JsAst list. Used by CeCall.args, CeDo.exprs, and CeConstruct.args.

engine:emitGuardFieldLoad.label: Emit guard field load
engine:emitGuardFieldLoad.description: Push the field-load instructions (I32Const + Call litString + Call getFieldNamed) for named, or (I32Const idx + Call getField) for positional. Sibling of emitGuardPresence but with the LOAD imports instead of HAS imports; shared by emitGuardSubRecurse + bindOneConstructSub.

engine:emitGuardPresence.label: Emit guard presence check
engine:emitGuardPresence.description: Emit the presence check (hasField / hasFieldNamed) instructions for one PatConstruct sub-position. Named path: I32Const nameIdx, Call litString, Call hasFieldNamed. Positional path: I32Const idx, Call hasField. Returns the updated accumulator; the caller appends I32And.

engine:emitGuardSubRecurse.label: Emit guard sub recurse
engine:emitGuardSubRecurse.description: Emit the field-load + recursive sub-guard for one PatConstruct sub-position. Skips on PatVar / PatWildcard (the presence check above already covers them); returns acc unchanged. Else: LocalGet scrut + field-load + allocLocal + LocalSet + recursive emitWasmPatternGuard + I32And.

engine:emitJs.label: Emit JsAst
engine:emitJs.description: Lower a ClosuresExplicitProgram to a JsModule. Maps the Fenel std-op set to direct JS operators (`add` → `+`, `eq` → `===`, …) where the semantics align; routes other calls through `$fenel.<fnId>(…)` runtime helpers. Effect-dispatch sentinels (`$effect:<Class>:<method>`) lower to `$fenel.$effect.<Class>.<method>(...)` via cross-call dispatch to `engine:parseEffectFnId`. Pattern matching emits chained ternaries over `$tag` and field access, with `$fenel.matchFail($scrut)` at the innermost else position. Mirrors the TS oracle at implementations/typescript/engine/src/modules/compile-js.ts:emitJsNative. Phase 21.6 — the fifth Fenel-authored engine pass; closes the JS pipeline end-to-end (modulo serializeJsModule's TS-only encode step).

engine:emitLetBindings.label: Emit let bindings
engine:emitLetBindings.description: Walk a CeLet.bindings list, lowering each value and accumulating `{name, value}` records (anonymous-record shape mirroring the TS oracle's JsLet.bindings).

engine:emitPatternGuard.label: Emit pattern guard
engine:emitPatternGuard.description: Produce a JS expression that evaluates to true when scrut matches the CorePattern. 4-arm walker. PatLit emits `===`; PatVar / PatWildcard emit JsLit(true) (bindings handled by collectPatternBindings); PatConstruct emits a `&&`-chain over `$tag === <ctor>` plus each sub-pattern's recursive guard. Two-arm PatConstruct dispatch for fields-present vs absent.

engine:emitPatternGuardLoop.label: Emit pattern guard (loop)
engine:emitPatternGuardLoop.description: Iterate over a PatConstruct's sub-patterns, building `&&`-conjoined guard chain. Each sub-pattern's scrut is `JsMember { object = parentScrut, property = fieldName_or_pos }`.

engine:emitRecordFields.label: Emit record fields
engine:emitRecordFields.description: Walk a CeRecord.fields list, lowering each value and accumulating `{key, value}` records (note `key`, not `name` — mirrors the TS oracle's JsObject.fields shape).

engine:emitWasmMatchArmThen.label: Emit Wasm match arm then-branch
engine:emitWasmMatchArmThen.description: emitWasmMatchArms sub-helper: snapshot locals, bind pattern + lower body for the then-branch, restore locals, then recurse on remaining arms for the else-branch and wrap in If(externref). Split out from emitWasmMatchArms so each case-of layer's body stays at manageable depth.

engine:emitWasmMatchArms.label: Emit Wasm match arms
engine:emitWasmMatchArms.description: Recursive walker for a CeMatch's arms list. Base case (arms exhausted): emit LocalGet scrut + Call matchFail → DomRef. Inductive case: emit guard onto acc, then If wrapping (bind + body) and (recursion into remaining arms). Per-arm locals snapshot/restore preserves bindings scope. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:emitWasmMatchArms.

engine:emitWasmPatternGuard.label: Emit Wasm pattern guard
engine:emitWasmPatternGuard.description: Emit i32 pattern-match-result (0/1) instructions for a CorePattern against the scrutinee local. PatVar / PatWildcard match trivially (I32Const 1); PatLit calls $fenel.litEq; PatConstruct emits tag-check + AND-folded per-sub-position presence + recursive sub-guard. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:emitWasmPatternGuard.

engine:empty.label: Empty (uninhabited) type
engine:empty.description: set-algebra-to-fenel Phase 6 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — structural Tri emptiness. Record products and ordinary/exact variant sums pass their complete face gates before structural verdicts. Exact validation-recognized runtime Lists are inhabited by `[]` when their eager element plan is ready, through the narrow opaque/immediate-mu arms; non-Lists retain ordinary recursion.

engine:emptyArrow.label: empty: emptyArrow
engine:emptyArrow.description: Phase 6 Step 3 / type-substrate P1(a.7) / type-substrate P1(a.8) — the arrow arm, INHABITED-CLAUSES ONLY and now FACTOR-GATED. The exponential law `empty(P1->…->Pn->R) ⟺ empty(R) ∧ every param inhabited` still computes, but only its Just false half is emitted: R provably nonempty ⇒ constant functions inhabit, and some param provably empty ⇒ the vacuous function inhabits. P1(a.7) entitled those two clauses on the claim that `validationValidateArrow` accepts the empty string for EVERY arrow type, so no arrow's live population is empty. **P1(a.8) MEASURED that claim FALSE.** `validationRuntime` runs `validationTypePlanError` FIRST (validate.fenel:1583), and its `VtArrow` arm audits the parameter ACCESS PLAN and then the return (`:1095-1101`) before `validationValidateArrow` is ever reached — so a factor whose plan validation cannot hold makes the arrow refuse every value, `""` included. Witness: `empty(({$ref:<catalog name with a duplicate semantic field key>}) -> Number)` = `Just false` at entry while `validate(…, "")` is INVALID. The gate is `ttSlotsPlanReady` over the PARAMS (the slot predicate, not a per-param TYPE fold — validation audits identity/projection as well as type) and `ttValidationPlanReady` over the RETURN: the same ledgered readiness doctrine (`t.sub.plan-ready-gate`) the record arm already uses, applied to the factors the preflight actually visits. This is a same-shape sibling of the map repair, found by design review and repaired at the source rather than masked by the map gate. The Just true (empty) leg remains fenced. Fenced inside this function, not at emptyKC, because arrowSub reads it directly for its empty-have short-circuit. Internal helper.

engine:emptyArrowInhabited.label: empty: emptyArrowInhabited
engine:emptyArrowInhabited.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — the retained inhabited half of the exponential law, reached only through `emptyArrow`'s factor gate. Split out so the gate is a separate, revertible clause with its own DISCRIMINATES pin. Internal helper.

engine:emptyB.label: Empty type (Bool)
engine:emptyB.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — the Bool-collapsed boundary helper over empty (Nothing → false), for callers that need a clean Bool rather than a Tri (the subsetB / decideSubsetB precedent, C-1). emptyB t = mGet (empty t) false.

engine:emptyBodyNames.label: Empty body names
engine:emptyBodyNames.description: The names of the productions of `g` whose body is `∅` under the current empty INDEX `empt` (name→true) — one round of the empty-set fixpoint. Internal helper. parser-substrate Phase 8.

engine:emptyIntersect.label: empty: emptyIntersect
engine:emptyIntersect.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — the intersect (∩) emptiness fold: empty iff ANY branch is provably empty OR some pair of branches is provably disjoint (= the `empty (Intersect[A,B]) ≡ disjoint A B` rule). mOr of intersectAnyEmpty (any-branch-empty, emTrueOnly so a non-empty branch never refutes) and intersectAnyDisjoint (pairwise ttDisjoint over refined leaves). SOUND: only emits Just true on a genuine proof; else Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:emptyK.label: empty: emptyK
engine:emptyK.description: Phase 6 Step 3 / type-substrate P1(a.6) / type-substrate P1(a.8) — kind dispatch after var/void: refined retains its recursive rule; **tagged now ABSTAINS unconditionally** (its recursion into the value slot was a verdict across the two live faces' disagreement about what a `$tagged` denotes — ledger `t.emp.tagged`, the emptiness twin of `t.sub.tagged`; MEASURED at P1(a.8) entry, `empty($tagged{value=$void})` = `Just true` while `validate($tagged{value=$void}, <uuid>)` is VALID); opaque and immediate-mu first recognize the exact validation List grammar and otherwise recurse normally. Remaining forms enter emptyKC.

engine:emptyKC.label: empty: emptyKC
engine:emptyKC.description: Phase 6 Step 3 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — composite emptiness tail: records enter the single-product face gate before anyEmpty; variants enter the whole-variant unique/discriminator/payload gate before allCasesEmpty; tuples remain structural. **P1(a.8): map is now the reading-invariant rule behind its well-formed-card and plan-readiness gates (`t.emp.map`, `t.map.wellformed-card`), arrow is factor-gated (`t.emp.arrow`), and the tagged tail abstains (`t.emp.tagged`).** Boolean formers, named and unknown tails retain their existing rules.

engine:emptyKF.label: empty: emptyKF
engine:emptyKF.description: Phase 2 Step 1b / floor-kernel Phase 3c / decide-substrate 8λ.1-r — the tier-2 former tail of emptyKC: union ⇒ all branches empty; intersect ⇒ an empty branch or disjoint pair; complement ⇒ ttTopCover(ttNnf inner), the shared exact top-equivalence presentation; named ⇒ emptyNamed; else Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:emptyList.label: subset: emptyList
engine:emptyList.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — Just true iff the list is empty, else Just false (the tuple/arrow arity-exhaustion check). Internal helper.

engine:emptyLiveList.label: empty: live List
engine:emptyLiveList.description: type-substrate P1(a.6) — exact runtime-List inhabitance: `[]` is a witness on both validation and matchesShape faces, so a validation-recognized List is Just false when its eager element plan is ready. Occurrence readiness is deliberately irrelevant because the empty array has no element occurrences; an unready element plan abstains. Internal helper.

engine:emptyMapAgreed.label: empty: emptyMapAgreed
engine:emptyMapAgreed.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — the two clauses on which the PARTIAL-dictionary and TOTAL-function readings of `$map` AGREE, and nothing else. (1) a provably EMPTY key domain ⇒ `Just false`: the unique empty function IS the empty dictionary, so the map is inhabited under both readings. (2) a provably INHABITED value type ⇒ `Just false`: a constant function inhabits under the total reading and `{}` witnesses the partial one. There is NO `Just true` clause and there may never be one — proving a map EMPTY is precisely the claim the partial reading denies, so a `Just true` here would be a false definite under a documented reading. Everything else abstains. Internal helper.

engine:emptyMapFace.label: empty: emptyMapFace
engine:emptyMapFace.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — map emptiness, READING-INVARIANT and twice gated. Replaces `emptyKC`'s unconditional `Just false`, which was a false definite: `empty(Vec 3 Void)` claimed INHABITED while ⟦Vec 3 Void⟧ = ∅ under the TOTAL denotation the repo commits to in three places, including this judgment's OWN projection (type-to-set.fenel:231 — "the canonical JSON-Logic predicate for a TOTAL Fin n map: exact length"). GATE 1, WELL-FORMEDNESS (`ttWellFormedMapCard`, ledger `t.map.wellformed-card`): a claimed finite card no host array length can satisfy admits no verdict at all. GATE 2, PLAN READINESS: the EXISTING ledgered `ttValidationPlanReady` (`t.sub.plan-ready-gate`) applied to the VALUE type — deliberately the same readiness doctrine rather than a second one, and deliberately at the FACE so NEITHER clause can lift a verdict over a value type validation does not plan. Two independent measured witnesses forced gate 2 to sit here rather than on the keys-empty clause alone: (i) `validationTypePlanError` descends `VtMap.values` UNCONDITIONALLY before any value is examined (validate.fenel:1082, run first at :1583), so a catalog-registered name with a malformed body makes `validate(Vec 0 <name>, [])` INVALID while `empty` said `Just false`; and (ii) `emptyNamed`'s hardcoded tower is WIDER than `validationPrimitiveName`, so `notEmpty` can be `Just true` from a table for a name whose live plan validation resolves from the registry and may refuse — the values-inhabited clause is the same lift, not a safe sibling. Ledger `t.emp.map`. Internal helper.

engine:emptyMuFace.label: empty: mu face
engine:emptyMuFace.description: type-substrate P1(a.6) — carrier-honest immediate-mu emptiness. An exact validation-recognized List uses the live-array witness rule; every other mu retains the least-fixpoint voidVar recursion. Internal helper.

engine:emptyNamed.label: empty: emptyNamed
engine:emptyNamed.description: decide-substrate 8λ.1-r — the named-atom inhabitance arm of emptyKF: the KNOWN atom tower (Number/Int/ℤ/Nat/ℕ/**ℝ**/String/Boolean/Bool/Char) ⇒ Just false (claimed decidably NONempty); any other name (a registered entity could be Void-like) ⇒ Nothing (the closed-world abstention). ⚠ **TWO CORRECTIONS, type-substrate P1(a.8) review round 9.** (i) The list here OMITTED ℝ while the body has always returned `Just false` for it, so the "any other name ⇒ Nothing" half was false for exactly the name the filing is about. (ii) "Inhabited BY CONSTRUCTION" is the claim `t.emp.named-atoms` FILES AS UNSOUND-KNOWN: the tower is WIDER than `validationPrimitiveName`, and ordinary validation refuses every sampled value for ℤ / ℕ / ℝ / Bool — so for those names the `Just false` is a false definite, exported through `anyEmptyT`, `emptyUnion` and the top-cover transit. Read the tower as a TABLE this arm trusts, not as a proof. The widening that lets emptyArrow certify param-inhabitance — pre-8λ.1-r `empty((Int)→Void)` was Nothing because paramsInhab(Int) couldn't decide, which ALSO meant the arrowSub emptiness gate could never certify a nonempty have ⇒ every arity refutation would have softened. The 8λ.1-r widening was `Nothing→Just false` only — which is monotone in the WIDENING direction but NOT a soundness argument, and the sentence that used to end here ("Strictly-better … on definitionally-inhabited names") is RETRACTED: `t.emp.named-atoms` files exactly that claim as a live defect, and `empty({$ref:"ℝ"}) = Just false` while ordinary validation refuses the sampled ℝ values. Internal helper.

engine:emptyNamesFix.label: Empty names fixpoint
engine:emptyNamesFix.description: The least fixpoint of empty (`∅`) production names of `g`: start with none, iterate `emptyNamesIter` to convergence. Internal helper. parser-substrate Phase 8.

engine:emptyNamesIter.label: Empty names iterate
engine:emptyNamesIter.description: One-or-more rounds of the empty-set least fixpoint over `g`, fuel-bounded by `|g|+1` (the longest empty-propagation chain) but EARLY-EXITING once a round adds no new empty name. The set is monotone-INCREASING (a larger empty index can only make more bodies empty), so a round of the same length as its input IS the fixpoint. Internal helper. parser-substrate Phase 8.

engine:emptyOpaqueFace.label: empty: opaque face
engine:emptyOpaqueFace.description: type-substrate P1(a.6) — carrier-honest opaque emptiness. An exact validation-recognized List uses the live-array witness rule; every other opaque recursively exposes its pure type exactly as before. Internal helper.

engine:emptyRefined.label: empty: emptyRefined
engine:emptyRefined.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — the refined leaf of emptyK: the refined type denotes base ∩ S. SOUND rule (corrects the brief): mOr (emptyW vv base) (emTrueOnly (decideEmpty set)) — Just true from base-empty OR set-empty; emTrueOnly drops decideEmpty's Just false (base-inhabited ∧ set-non-empty does NOT imply the intersection inhabited — the Nat ∩ {<0} disjoint-refinement gap). decideEmpty resolves to set:decideEmpty via the decideEmptySlice harness. Internal helper.

engine:emptyUnion.label: empty: emptyUnion
engine:emptyUnion.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — the union (∪) emptiness fold: a union is empty iff ALL branches are empty (mAnd-fold of emptyW over the TtUnion branches). An empty branch list ⇒ Just true (∪∅ = ∅). Sound AND complete. Internal helper.

engine:emptyVar.label: empty: emptyVar
engine:emptyVar.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — the type-variable arm of emptyW: a bound var seen under the voidVar flag ⇒ Just true (treated as Void in a μ fixpoint); a free var (vv false, top level) ⇒ Nothing (its denotation is unknown ⇒ undecidable). Internal helper.

engine:emptyW.label: empty: emptyW
engine:emptyW.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — the voidVar-threaded structural-recursive core of empty: a bound type-VAR under vv (set only inside a μ body) ⇒ Just true (the recursive occurrence is Void in the fixpoint check); $void ⇒ Just true; else dispatch on the kind via emptyK. emptyW false is the top-level `empty` (a free var is UNDECIDABLE ⇒ Nothing). Internal core.

engine:endpointOf.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — a one-element list of an interval bound's value when it is INCLUSIVE, else the empty list (exclusive / unbounded contribute no untyped witness). Internal helper for inclusiveEndpoints.

engine:entityRecordType.label: field-meta: entityRecordType
engine:entityRecordType.description: Phase 10c sub-step 1 — resolve an EntitySpec's canonical FenelType. The TS wrapper does asFenelType narrowing + legacy schema lifting TS-side and emits ErtInput (ErtSome resolvedType / ErtNone); the body returns Maybe FenelType. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedEntityRecordType`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/field-meta.ts:entityRecordType.

engine:entitySchemaFields.description: Phase 10c sub-step 1 — extract FieldDef[] from spec.type.$record (or from a lifted legacy schema column for un-migrated DB rows). The TS wrapper does asFenelType narrowing + liftLegacyFields TS-side and emits EsfInput (EsfRecord fields / EsfNone); the body routes the original untagged FieldDef list opaquely. The wrapper returns those records unchanged, preserving auxiliary fields and object identity. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedEntitySchemaFields`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/field-meta.ts:entitySchemaFields.

engine:enumBaseIntersect.label: enumerable: enumBaseIntersect
engine:enumBaseIntersect.description: solver-extension Phase 2 — enumerate a `SeIntersect` of discrete-base interval branches: fold them into ONE combined interval via the SHARED seIntervalFold (inhabit.fenel — tighter lo / tighter hi), then step that interval per base (enumBaseInterval — Int/Nat ℤ-stepping or Char codepoint-stepping). The `x >= lo and x <= hi` / `c >= 'a' and c <= 'e'` headline lowers to a SeIntersect of two half-bounded intervals; this combines them then enumerates. A non-interval branch sets ok=false ⇒ Nothing; a non-discrete base ⇒ Nothing. (Phase 1 had an int-only enumIntIntersect; Phase 2 generalises it to enumBaseInterval.) Internal helper.

engine:enumBaseInterval.label: enumerable: enumBaseInterval
engine:enumBaseInterval.description: solver-extension Phase 2 — the per-base interval router: dispatch a `SeInterval`'s bounds to the right discrete stepper by the base NAME. Integer base (Int / Nat) ⇒ enumIntInterval (ℤ stepping); Char base ⇒ enumCharInterval (codepoint stepping); any other (ℝ — dense, no successor; or unknown) ⇒ Nothing (the honesty fence). The base is PROVIDED from the SetExpr's type context (never invented — the P5 rule). Internal helper (Phase 1's enumerableSet called enumIntInterval directly; Phase 2 inserts this router to add the Char base).

engine:enumBaseUnion.label: enumerable: enumBaseUnion
