engine:lowerNumericFoldPath.label: Lower numeric fold path
engine:lowerNumericFoldPath.description: lowerCall sub-helper: arity-check (>= 2) then lowerNumericFold + LowerOutput wrap with the per-op resultDomain.

engine:lowerNumericFoldRest.label: Lower numeric fold (rest)
engine:lowerNumericFoldRest.description: lowerNumericFold sub-helper: per-iteration emit arg instrs + binop. Recurses through the args list.

engine:lowerOk.label: Lower bound ok
engine:lowerOk.description: The lower-bound half of intervalMember. Internal helper.

engine:lowerOneTaggedRecordField.label: Lower one tagged record field
engine:lowerOneTaggedRecordField.description: Per-field dispatcher: push handle (LocalGet valLocalIdx) + index (I32Const idx), then route to lowerNamedField (when nameAtIdxM = Just name) or lowerPositionalField (when Nothing).

engine:lowerParamVal.label: Lower value-expr (arrow param)
engine:lowerParamVal.description: Lower value-expr type-args inside one arrow-param marker's `type` slot. fenel-surface-extensions Phase 8 (D-G follow-up).

engine:lowerPositionalField.label: Lower positional field
engine:lowerPositionalField.description: Per-field positional mode: lower fieldExpr at DomRef, append its instrs, then Call $fenel.setField. Used when the source-side construct didn't supply named-field metadata (legacy ctors).

engine:lowerRefinedSet.label: Lower refined set marker
engine:lowerRefinedSet.description: Lower a refinement SetExpr marker for the TS `$`-key marshal: a `where` predicate set has its Syntax lowered Fenel-side to `$`-free JSON-Logic (`{mk=where, jl}`, the TS marshal wraps it `{$where: jl}`); enum/interval sets pass through unchanged (their `$enum`/`$interval` keys are authored TS-side). parser-substrate Phase 4h batch 3.

engine:lowerSeq.label: Lower sequence
engine:lowerSeq.description: Lower a JsSequence spine: non-last elements as JsSExpr (effect-position), last element via lowerSpine (tail position). Phase 6b2.

engine:lowerSpine.label: Lower spine
engine:lowerSpine.description: Lower a tail-position JsAst into a `List JsStmt`. Tail self-call (arity-matched) ⇒ temp-first reassign + JsSContinue; JsTernary ⇒ JsSIf whose branches inherit `declared` (so shadowing bindings route through the outer-scope temp, avoiding a TDZ); JsLet ⇒ binding fold (lowerLet); JsSequence ⇒ non-last as JsSExpr + recurse on last; else ⇒ JsSReturn. Phase 6b2 lever B.

engine:lowerTaggedRecordFields.label: Lower tagged record fields (iteration)
engine:lowerTaggedRecordFields.description: lowerWasmTaggedRecord sub-helper: walks fields list with an index counter, dispatching per-field on whether listIndex fieldNames idx is Just (named) or Nothing (positional). Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:1102-1121 for-loop.

engine:lowerTailCall.label: Lower tail call
engine:lowerTailCall.description: Lower a tail self-call into temp-first reassign + continue: `const $t<i> = arg<i>` for every arg (computed from OLD params), then `param<i> = $t<i>`, then JsSContinue. Temp-first is load-bearing. Phase 6b2.

engine:lowerToLlvmAst.label: LLVM lowering: lowerToLlvmAst
engine:lowerToLlvmAst.description: Phase 21.8 — LLVM lowering body. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:lowerToWasmAst.label: Lower ClosuresExplicit to WasmModule
engine:lowerToWasmAst.description: Program-level entry on the Wasm pipeline. Takes a ClosuresExplicitProgram + pre-computed (paramDomains, externalReturn) from the dispatch wrapper's TS-side `inferDomains` walk and assembles a typed WasmModule. Algorithm: seedEntryParams → lowerExprWithTarget at externalReturn → entry WasmFunc assembly via mapDomainsToValTypes + rleLocals → builder-state read via 6 getter natives → closure-export index fixup → WasmFuncImport list reconstruction → component-export metadata → WasmModule envelope. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:lowerProgramToWasm (1713-1815). Phase 21.7 commit 9 — closes the per-CeExpr surface from commit 8 with the program-level entry, making 'Fenel compiles itself to a typed Wasm AST' an end-to-end claim through the engine evaluator (modulo serializeWasmModule, the final binary encode).

engine:lowerValExprs.label: Lower value-expr type-args
engine:lowerValExprs.description: Deep-walk a type `{mk}` marker tree rewriting every `{mk=valexpr, syntax}` (a parenthesised VALUE-level dependent type-arg, `Vec a (n + 1)`) ⇒ `syntaxToJsonLogic syntax` (the `$`-free JSON-Logic the oracle's parseExpr produces, e.g. `{call:["add",{var:"n"},1]}`); every other marker (app/arrow/tuple/record recursed; ref/strlit/numlit + raw-number args passed through). Keeps the lowerer OUT of the parser closure (the predicateBody precedent). Run over each frame's type markers BEFORE the TS walkType marshal, which then carries the lowered `$`-free expr verbatim into the authored `$el`. fenel-surface-extensions Phase 8 (D-G follow-up).

engine:lowerWasmConstruct.label: Lower Wasm CeConstruct
engine:lowerWasmConstruct.description: CeConstruct arm. Delegates to lowerWasmTaggedRecord with the ctor name as the tag. Guards against the `fields` metadata being absent (null/undefined for pre-Phase-21.1 unregistered ctors) by passing through the empty list, which routes every field through positional mode.

engine:lowerWasmExpr.label: Lower Wasm CeExpr
engine:lowerWasmExpr.description: Entry into per-CeExpr Wasm lowering. Dispatches on $tag and delegates to per-arm helpers. Commits 3-7 ship CeLit / CeVar (both halves) / CeIf / CeDo / CeLet / CeCall / CeConstruct / CeRecord / CeMatch; the remaining arm (CeClosure) returns Err Unsupported so the production call site stays gated on the TS oracle until it's ported. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:lowerExprInternal — the central walker — without the explicit target arg (lowerExpr's coerceDomain wrapper threads target through recursive descents instead).

engine:lowerWasmLit.label: Lower Wasm CeLit
engine:lowerWasmLit.description: 5-arm dispatch on JS value type for CeLit lowering. Numbers → F64Const + DomNum; booleans → I32Const 0/1 + DomBool; null → RefNull externref + DomRef; strings → intern + I32Const idx + Call litString import → DomRef; other → Err Unsupported. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:lowerExprInternal CeLit arm.

engine:lowerWasmRecord.label: Lower Wasm CeRecord
engine:lowerWasmRecord.description: CeRecord arm. Anonymous records use sentinel tag "$record". Extracts field values + names from the list of {name, value} entries (always named, by construction) and delegates to lowerWasmTaggedRecord.

engine:lowerWasmTaggedRecord.label: Lower tagged record
engine:lowerWasmTaggedRecord.description: Central CeConstruct + CeRecord helper. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:1060. Algorithm: push tag + n_fields, Call $fenel.construct → externref; stash in fresh allocLocal; per-field push handle + index, then named (Call setFieldNamed with interned name) or positional (Call setField) lower-and-emit; finally LocalGet handle as the result. Returns DomRef.

engine:lowerWasmVar.label: Lower Wasm CeVar
engine:lowerWasmVar.description: CeVar undotted lookup: HasWasmBuilder.lookupLocal n → LocalGet idx + entry.domain. Dotted names are deferred to a follow-on commit and return Err Unsupported here. Out-of-scope name → Err Unsupported. Mirrors the undotted half of compile-wasm.ts:lowerExprInternal CeVar arm.

engine:lowerWasmVarDotted.label: Lower dotted CeVar
engine:lowerWasmVarDotted.description: Dotted CeVar chain: split on '.', look up the head local, push LocalGet + coerce-to-DomRef, then chain a (I32Const segIdx, Call litStr, Call getFieldNamed) triple per remaining segment. Result domain is always DomRef. Out-of-scope head → Err Unsupported. Mirrors compile-wasm.ts:720-748.

engine:lowerWasmVarUndotted.label: Lower undotted CeVar
engine:lowerWasmVarUndotted.description: Undotted-name lookup: HasWasmBuilder.lookupLocal n → LocalGet idx + entry.domain. Out-of-scope name → Err Unsupported. Split out of lowerWasmVar so the dotted vs undotted halves each read cleanly.

engine:mAnd.label: subset: mAnd
engine:mAnd.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — Kleene conjunction over Tri (Maybe Bool): Just false dominates (∧ false = false); Just true ⇒ the other; Nothing ⇒ Nothing unless the other is Just false. The component-wise folds' combiner. Internal helper.

engine:mAndNothing.label: subset: mAndNothing
engine:mAndNothing.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the Nothing-left case of mAnd: Nothing ∧ Just false = Just false (false dominates), else Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:mOr.label: empty: mOr
engine:mOr.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — Kleene disjunction over Tri (Maybe Bool): Just true dominates (∨ true = true); Just false ⇒ the other; Nothing ⇒ Nothing unless the other is Just true. The dual of mAnd; the product (record/tuple) folds' combiner. Internal helper.

engine:mOrNothing.label: empty: mOrNothing
engine:mOrNothing.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — the Nothing-left case of mOr: Nothing ∨ Just true = Just true (true dominates), else Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:makeClosureFuncType.label: Make-closure func type
engine:makeClosureFuncType.description: Build the (externref, externref) -> externref WasmFuncType for the $fenel.makeClosure runtime helper. Used by lowerClosure to materialise the (body-export-name, env-handle) closure value.

engine:makeClosuresExplicit.label: Make closures explicit
engine:makeClosuresExplicit.description: Walk an EffectsExplicitProgram body, convert every CoreLambda to a CeClosure with explicit captures, return a ClosuresExplicitProgram. The captures list at each closure is the intersection of the body's free vars with the OUTER visible-bindings set, sorted lexicographically. Globals don't go through captures (the emitter resolves them by name); the `$dyn:<varName>` sentinel handles indirect calls through captured function values. Mirrors the TS oracle at implementations/typescript/engine/src/ir/closures-explicit.ts. Phase 21.3 — third Fenel-authored engine pass, builds on the Phase 21.2 substrate (`elem` / `appendItem` / `sortLex` for list-as-set ops, two-pass walk inside each CoreLambda case for free-var analysis + body conversion).

engine:makeEffectsExplicit.label: Make effects explicit
engine:makeEffectsExplicit.description: Walk a CoreExpr body, identify all $effect: dispatch sites, and surface them as a structured (handlerSites, effects) inventory. Returns Result CompileError EffectsExplicitProgram; the structural Ok is the only branch in well-formed input today (the TS oracle returns Err only for shapes that aren't yet produced by Phase 5+ pipelines). The `emptyList` arg is the initial accumulator state (passed by the caller as a value, since Core IR rejects bare-array literals at expression position). Mirrors the TS oracle at implementations/typescript/engine/src/ir/effects-explicit.ts. Phase 21.2 — the first real recursive engine pass authored in Fenel: a 10-arm CoreMatch over a registered ADT, state-threaded recursion via the {handlerSites, effects} scan record, side-channel accumulation through `appendItem` / `elem`, and a final `sortLex` over the deduplicated effect inventory.

engine:mapAutoLabel.label: validation-hints: mapAutoLabel
engine:mapAutoLabel.description: containment-substrate Phase 1a — explicit recursion over the canonical Se* branches; calls autoLabel on each and accumulates strings in original order. Internal helper.

engine:mapDomainsToValTypes.label: Map domains to valTypes
engine:mapDomainsToValTypes.description: Extract WasmValType from each {domain} entry in a declaredLocals list. Forward-recursive walk + appendItem snoc; output feeds rleLocals.

engine:mapEmitLlvmValType.label: LLVM serialiser: mapEmitLlvmValType
engine:mapEmitLlvmValType.description: Phase 21.10 — LLVM IR text serialiser. See fenel/modules/engine/lower-to-llvm-ast.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:mapPrependDot.label: validation-hints: mapPrependDot
engine:mapPrependDot.description: Phase 8b sub-step 1 — prepend `.` to each extension. Used by autoLabelPathExt. Internal helper.

engine:markerOrdered.label: Marker ordered
engine:markerOrdered.description: Is a Ws marker in the structured-partition-able (ordered) fragment? WsAll/WsNone/WsEnum/WsInterval ⇒ yes; WsUnion/WsIntersect ⇒ all branches ordered; WsComplement ⇒ inner ordered; WsWhere / anything else ⇒ no (route the whole decision to the 2^N fallback). Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:matchArgs.label: Match args
engine:matchArgs.description: Walk an atom's args against a fact row in parallel, threading the bindings: an ELit selects (must equal the fact value), an EVar matches (must equal its existing binding) or binds (new), a compound arg fails. Just final-bindings on success / Nothing on any mismatch. Internal helper.

engine:matchArmsFlat.label: Match arms flatten
engine:matchArmsFlat.description: Walk SMatch arms `[{pattern, body}]` into the flat `[pattern0, body0, pattern1, body1, …]` tail (pattern raw, body lowered). The TRAILING `_`-wildcard arm DROPS its pattern, emitting the body as the bare trailing default (`[… , defaultBody]`) — the TS-parser parity for `case … of … _ -> e` (the parser keeps `_` as `PatVar "_"`; TS drops it; only the trailing `_` is valid — TS errors on a non-trailing `_`). parser-substrate Phase 5a (the `_`-arm drop: Phase 4h).

engine:matchFailFuncType.label: matchFail func type
engine:matchFailFuncType.description: Build the (externref) -> externref WasmFuncType for the $fenel.matchFail runtime helper. Called at the terminal fallthrough of a CeMatch's nested-if/else chain when no arm matched; produces a match-failure runtime error.

engine:matchOne.label: Match one
engine:matchOne.description: Match one atom arg against one fact value, threading the bindings: ELit ⇒ require equal; EVar already bound ⇒ require equal (handles tuple-vs-atom AND the SAME var twice in one atom); EVar new ⇒ bind; a compound arg ⇒ Nothing (no match). Internal helper.

engine:matchesShape.label: Matches shape
engine:matchesShape.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — best-effort structural recogniser over the shared identity-total TraversalType. Fenel owns exact Maybe/List recognition, wrapper peeling, constructor selection, recursion, optional fields, and current-wire projection. The TS adapter only snapshots own host data and crosses the ledgered `$`-key boundary.

engine:maxNonEnum.label: enumerate: maxNonEnum
engine:maxNonEnum.description: Phase 15 — tier-2 max for a non-enumerable SetExpr: SeInterval ⇒ maxOfInterval over its hi; SeIntersect ⇒ maxOfIntersect (fold the interval branches, then the hi endpoint); anything else ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:maxNum.label: Max number
engine:maxNum.description: Numeric max of two numbers. Internal helper (min-bound floor in the rep derivative).

engine:maxOfIntersect.label: enumerate: maxOfIntersect
engine:maxOfIntersect.description: Phase 15 — tier-2 max of a SeIntersect: fold the interval branches into one combined interval via the SHARED seIntervalFold (inhabit.fenel, cross-file), then the hi endpoint (maxOfInterval). A non-interval branch ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:maxOfInterval.label: enumerate: maxOfInterval
engine:maxOfInterval.description: Phase 15 — the attained maximum of an interval's hi bound: Just hi.value when INCLUSIVE; exclusive or unbounded ⇒ Nothing (no attained supremum — the ℝ honesty fence). Internal helper.

engine:maxOfSet.label: Max of set
engine:maxOfSet.description: The maximum (argmax) of a SetExpr ⇒ Maybe a. Tier 1 — enumerable (enumerateSet ⇒ Just non-empty) with a SCALAR extension ⇒ the std `maximum` native (orders BOTH numbers AND strings correctly); a NON-scalar extension (binding-rows, records, booleans) ⇒ Nothing — no canonical order (the Stage-B guard). Tier 2 — non-enumerable: SeInterval ⇒ the hi bound when INCLUSIVE, else Nothing (no attained supremum — the ℝ honesty fence); SeIntersect ⇒ fold the interval branches (seIntervalFold) then the hi endpoint. SeAll / SeWhere / SeComplement / union-of-intervals ⇒ Nothing; the empty set ⇒ Nothing. Objective-driven optimization is Phase 8, fenced out. expr-substrate Phase 15.

engine:maybeAddFreeVar.label: Maybe add free var
engine:maybeAddFreeVar.description: Dedup'd append: add `name` to `free` only if it's not already in `local` (bound) AND not already in `free` (already collected). Phase 5b28 — strips dotted CeVar leaf names (`c.x` → `c`) via `dottedHead` BEFORE the elem-checks so dotted captures contribute the bound head to the free set. Used by collectFreeVars's CoreVar / CoreCall cases.

engine:maybeEnumerate.label: enumerate: maybeEnumerate
engine:maybeEnumerate.description: Phase 15 — bind a `Maybe SetExpr` (relSolveSet's result) through enumerateSet: Nothing ⇒ Nothing (the fence preserved); Just w ⇒ enumerateSet w. The Maybe-bind shared by solveRelAll + solveFnRelAll. Internal helper.

engine:meetVerdict.label: Meet verdict
engine:meetVerdict.description: The 2-ary conservative meet over two totality verdict tags (unified-static-analysis Phase 3h): Unknown dominates (either Unknown ⇒ Unknown), then Partial (either Partial ⇒ Partial), else Total. The associative/commutative kernel `joinVerdict` folds. Internal helper.

engine:memberFold.label: Member fold
engine:memberFold.description: Fold the per-char Brzozowski derivative of a Pat under each input code point (`derivWsPat infoIdx cp pat`), left to right, until the code points run out — returning the residual Pat. The inductive membership walk (no memo, no atom enumeration; N chars = N steps). Internal helper. named-membership-to-fenel Phase 2.

engine:memberPat.label: Member pattern
engine:memberPat.description: Decide `value ∈ L(pat)` over a pre-built match-Pattern: nullablePat of the residual after folding the per-char derivative under every input code point (the Brzozowski `nullable (foldl deriv p (chars s))` identity). predInfo is the TS-precomputed [{ key, isAll, subsetOf, ws }] table (reused from the containment deciders); codepoints are the input string's per-char code points. Membership is purely inductive + finite — no visited memo / atom enumeration / fuel. The WsWhere fence is in the TS shim (dispatchedPatternMember pre-scans + falls back). The port of pattern.ts patternMatch over the structured Ws derivative. named-membership-to-fenel Phase 2.

engine:membershipBoolean.label: set-algebra: membership Boolean/Bool
engine:membershipBoolean.description: named-membership Phase 1 — boolean membership (Boolean / Bool). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `Boolean`/`Bool` closures.

engine:membershipBytes.label: set-algebra: membership Bytes
engine:membershipBytes.description: Strict membership in the Uint8Array host carrier of Bytes, whose pure view is List Byte. The isBytes native supplies only the host representation fact; ordinary named Membership dispatch selects this Fenel predicate.

engine:membershipChar.label: set-algebra: membership Char
engine:membershipChar.description: signature-substrate slice 3jw §2a — Char membership with UNICODE-SCALAR semantics over the native one-code-point-string carrier: a String of exactly one code point whose code point is a scalar (i.e. outside the surrogate block D800–DFFF). Denotes ⟦Char⟧ = SeDiff (SeInterval 0 0x10FFFF) (SeInterval 0xD800 0xDFFF) transported along Reprable JsRuntime Char. `isString` is load-bearing: `length [97]` is 1, so a length-only test admits the array carrier. Does NOT contradict `std:charCode`, which is total on the wider declared domain `String`. TCB row `mem.char` (THEORY-PLUGIN on `env.primordials`).

engine:membershipFormatDate.label: set-algebra: membership format:date
engine:membershipFormatDate.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:date / format:datetime: the defined clean acceptance set — ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD), ISO datetime (date (T|space) HH:MM(:SS)?(.fff)?(Z|±HH:MM)?), or the month-name form (Mon[th] D[D] YYYY). Replaces the host `new Date()` leniency (Decisions #1 = A; cross-engine-stable, zero new TS).

engine:membershipFormatIp.label: set-algebra: membership format:ip
engine:membershipFormatIp.description: named-membership Phase 3c — format:ip: IPv4 dotted-quad with each octet 0..255, else IPv6 full (8 hex groups) or the loose `::` shorthand. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:ip` closure (the buggy `::` regex reproduced exactly — D-ipv6).

engine:membershipFormatPath.label: set-algebra: membership format:path
engine:membershipFormatPath.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path (non-empty path-shaped string, no NUL byte). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathAbsolute.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:absolute
engine:membershipFormatPathAbsolute.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:absolute (leading '/', drive+separator, or UNC '\\'). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:absolute` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoAltStream.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-alt-stream
engine:membershipFormatPathNoAltStream.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-alt-stream (no ':' after the optional drive prefix — NTFS alternate streams). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-alt-stream` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoCurrent.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-current
engine:membershipFormatPathNoCurrent.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-current (no '.' segment). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-current` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoEmptySegmen.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-empty-segment
engine:membershipFormatPathNoEmptySegmen.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-empty-segment (no interior empty segment; a leading/trailing separator is allowed). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-empty-segment` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoHidden.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-hidden
engine:membershipFormatPathNoHidden.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-hidden (no dotfile segment). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-hidden` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoNullByte.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-null-byte
engine:membershipFormatPathNoNullByte.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-null-byte (no NUL byte). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-null-byte` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoReserved.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-reserved
engine:membershipFormatPathNoReserved.description: named-membership Phase 3c — format:path:no-reserved: no segment (split on both separators) is a Windows reserved device name CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM[1-9]/LPT[1-9], optionally followed by `.ext`, case-insensitively. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-reserved` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoTrailingSep.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-trailing-sep
engine:membershipFormatPathNoTrailingSep.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-trailing-sep (length > 1, no trailing separator). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-trailing-sep` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoTrailingSpa.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-trailing-space-or-dot
engine:membershipFormatPathNoTrailingSpa.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-trailing-space-or-dot (no segment ends in a space or a dot). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-trailing-space-or-dot` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathNoTraversal.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:no-traversal
engine:membershipFormatPathNoTraversal.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:no-traversal (no '..' segment). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:no-traversal` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathPortable.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:portable
engine:membershipFormatPathPortable.description: named-membership Phase 3c — format:path:portable: non-empty, no NUL byte, no backslash, none of `<>:"|?*`, no trailing space or dot, every char in `[A-Za-z0-9._-/ ]`. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:portable` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathPosix.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:posix
engine:membershipFormatPathPosix.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:posix ('/'-separated, no backslash, no drive prefix). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:posix` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathRelative.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:relative
engine:membershipFormatPathRelative.description: named-membership Phase 1 — format:path:relative (non-empty, not '/'-rooted, not drive-prefixed, not UNC). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:relative` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPathWindows.label: set-algebra: membership format:path:windows
engine:membershipFormatPathWindows.description: named-membership Phase 3c — format:path:windows: bare drive 'C:' ⇒ true; 'C:\'/'C:/' ⇒ body is the tail; 'C:foo' (CWD-relative) ⇒ false; '\\server\share[\rest]' UNC ⇒ body is rest; else body is the whole value; body must contain none of `<>:"|?*`. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:path:windows` closure.

engine:membershipFormatPhone.label: set-algebra: membership format:phone
engine:membershipFormatPhone.description: named-membership Phase 3c — format:phone: strip `[\s\-().]` (realistic `\s` members), then `^\+?[0-9]\d{6,14}$` (optional leading '+', then 7-15 digits). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:phone` closure. Exotic-`\s` divergence documented.

engine:membershipFormatPostalCode.label: set-algebra: membership format:postal-code
engine:membershipFormatPostalCode.description: named-membership Phase 3c — format:postal-code: `^[A-Z0-9]{2,5}[\s-]?[A-Z0-9]{2,5}$` case-insensitively (2-5 alnum, optional single `[\s-]` separator, 2-5 alnum). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:postal-code` closure. Exotic-`\s` divergence documented.

engine:membershipFormatUrl.label: set-algebra: membership format:url
engine:membershipFormatUrl.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url. Accepts a valid absolute-URL scheme (rejecting javascript:/vbscript:), or a schemeless input whose http://-prefixed host ends in a TLD dot. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url` two-try closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlFtp.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:ftp
engine:membershipFormatUrlFtp.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:ftp (scheme ftp / ftps). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:ftp` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlNofragment.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:nofragment
engine:membershipFormatUrlNofragment.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:nofragment (no '#'). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:nofragment` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlNolocalhost.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:nolocalhost
engine:membershipFormatUrlNolocalhost.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:nolocalhost (reject '://localhost' / '://127.' / '://[::1]' or a leading localhost). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:nolocalhost` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlNoport.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:noport
engine:membershipFormatUrlNoport.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:noport (no explicit port). Parse failure ⇒ true. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:noport` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlNoprivate.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:noprivate
engine:membershipFormatUrlNoprivate.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:noprivate (reject loopback / link-local / RFC1918 private ranges / cloud-metadata IMDS / IPv6 ULA + .localhost/.internal/.local). Parse failure ⇒ false. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:noprivate` SSRF cascade.

engine:membershipFormatUrlNoquery.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:noquery
engine:membershipFormatUrlNoquery.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:noquery (no '?'). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:noquery` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlNosubdomain.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:nosubdomain
engine:membershipFormatUrlNosubdomain.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:nosubdomain (the hostname is a bare apex domain: one label + a 2+-alpha TLD). Parse failure ⇒ true. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:nosubdomain` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlSecure.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:secure
engine:membershipFormatUrlSecure.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:secure (scheme https / wss / ftps). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:secure` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlStrict.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:strict
engine:membershipFormatUrlStrict.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:strict (has a valid URL scheme). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:strict` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlWeb.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:web
engine:membershipFormatUrlWeb.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:web (http(s) or schemeless, rejecting localhost / 127. / [::1] when http(s)://-rooted). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:web` closure.

engine:membershipFormatUrlWs.label: set-algebra: membership format:url:ws
engine:membershipFormatUrlWs.description: named-membership Phase 3 — format:url:ws (scheme ws / wss). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `format:url:ws` closure.

engine:membershipInt.label: set-algebra: membership ℤ/Int
engine:membershipInt.description: named-membership Phase 1 — integer membership (ℤ / Int). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `ℤ`/`Int` closures.

engine:membershipListAscending.label: set-algebra: membership list:ascending
engine:membershipListAscending.description: named-membership Phase 1 — list:ascending (strictly increasing). Non-array or < 2 elements → vacuously true. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `list:ascending` closure.

engine:membershipListDescending.label: set-algebra: membership list:descending
engine:membershipListDescending.description: named-membership Phase 1 — list:descending (strictly decreasing). Non-array or < 2 elements → vacuously true. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `list:descending` closure.

engine:membershipListDistinct.label: set-algebra: membership list:distinct
engine:membershipListDistinct.description: named-membership Phase 1 — list:distinct (all elements distinct). Non-array → false. Dedup via structural `eq` (object-key-order divergence noted in the file header). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `list:distinct` closure.

engine:membershipListNondecreasing.label: set-algebra: membership list:nondecreasing
engine:membershipListNondecreasing.description: named-membership Phase 1 — list:nondecreasing (each ≥ previous). Non-array or < 2 elements → vacuously true. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `list:nondecreasing` closure.

engine:membershipListNonincreasing.label: set-algebra: membership list:nonincreasing
engine:membershipListNonincreasing.description: named-membership Phase 1 — list:nonincreasing (each ≤ previous). Non-array or < 2 elements → vacuously true. Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `list:nonincreasing` closure.

engine:membershipNat.label: set-algebra: membership ℕ/Nat
engine:membershipNat.description: named-membership Phase 1 — non-negative integer membership (ℕ / Nat). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `ℕ`/`Nat` closures in set-algebra.ts.

engine:membershipNonEmpty.label: set-algebra: membership NonEmpty
engine:membershipNonEmpty.description: named-membership Phase 1 — non-empty-string membership (NonEmpty). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `NonEmpty` closure (code-point count vs UTF-16: a non-empty string has length > 0 in both).

engine:membershipProp.label: law: membershipProp
engine:membershipProp.description: decide-substrate Phase 2 (K2) — build an enum-membership law claim JUDGMENT-NATIVE: `JEmpty (SeIntersect [SeEnum [witness], SeComplement (SeEnum allowed)])` via jopSubset (the kernel's judgmentOfProposition iso builder) — the {witness} ∩ ¬allowed set is empty ≡ witness ∈ allowed (subsethood). Emits the one lattice judgment, NOT the closed PropSubset marker; the TS seam shape-recognizes SeIntersect [s, SeComplement t] ⇒ PropSubset for the still-Prop* proposer (byte-identical; the back-map dies at K3). Canonical `$tag` Se* payloads. Internal helper.

engine:membershipReal.label: set-algebra: membership ℝ/Number
engine:membershipReal.description: named-membership Phase 1 — finite-real membership (ℚ / ℝ / Rational / Real / Number). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS finite-number closures.

engine:membershipString.label: set-algebra: membership String
engine:membershipString.description: named-membership Phase 1 — string membership (String). Mirrors the NAMED_SETS `String` closure.

engine:mergeIntervals.label: set-algebra: mergeIntervals
engine:mergeIntervals.description: Phase 7b-continuation — merge overlapping/adjacent intervals. Input pre-sorted by lo bound at the TS boundary.

engine:mergeLegacyFieldFacets.label: Merge legacy field facets
engine:mergeLegacyFieldFacets.description: Preserve current optional account facets and add inline-presentation facets lifted by migration. Same logical facet with equal methods dedupes; differing methods are a structured ambiguity, making dry-run/apply/dry-run convergent.

engine:mergeType.label: Merge type
engine:mergeType.description: Merge identity-total record fields by FieldKey. Same key with conflicting current projection and same projection with different key reject.

engine:minNonEnum.label: enumerate: minNonEnum
engine:minNonEnum.description: Phase 15 — tier-2 min for a non-enumerable SetExpr: SeInterval ⇒ minOfInterval over its lo; SeIntersect ⇒ minOfIntersect (fold the interval branches, then the lo endpoint); anything else (SeAll / SeWhere / SeComplement / union-of-intervals) ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:minNum.label: Minimum number
engine:minNum.description: The minimum of a non-empty number list (0 when empty — unobservable, partitionReps guards). Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:minNumGo.label: Minimum number go
engine:minNumGo.description: minNum's tail fold: keep the smaller of the accumulator and the head. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:minOfIntersect.label: enumerate: minOfIntersect
engine:minOfIntersect.description: Phase 15 — tier-2 min of a SeIntersect: fold the interval branches into one combined interval via the SHARED seIntervalFold (inhabit.fenel, cross-file — tighter lo / tighter hi), then the lo endpoint (minOfInterval). A non-interval branch sets ok=false ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:minOfInterval.label: enumerate: minOfInterval
engine:minOfInterval.description: Phase 15 — the attained minimum of an interval's lo bound: Just lo.value when INCLUSIVE; exclusive or unbounded ⇒ Nothing (no attained infimum — the ℝ honesty fence). Internal helper.

engine:minOfSet.label: Min of set
engine:minOfSet.description: The minimum (argmin) of a SetExpr ⇒ Maybe a. Tier 1 — enumerable (enumerateSet ⇒ Just non-empty) with a SCALAR extension (number/string head) ⇒ the std `minimum` native (orders BOTH numbers AND strings correctly — unlike `lt`/`gt`, which are numeric-only); a NON-scalar extension (relational binding-rows, records, booleans) ⇒ Nothing — no canonical order (the guard that replaced the WsTuples short-circuit, decide-substrate Phase 1 Stage B). Tier 2 — non-enumerable: SeInterval ⇒ the lo bound when INCLUSIVE, else Nothing (no attained infimum — the ℝ honesty fence); SeIntersect ⇒ fold the interval branches (the shared seIntervalFold) then the lo endpoint. SeAll / SeWhere / SeComplement / union-of-intervals ⇒ Nothing; the empty set ⇒ Nothing. Objective-driven optimization (`minimize f over S`) needs evaluate-over-Expr — that is Phase 8, fenced out. expr-substrate Phase 15.

engine:mkAlt.label: mkAlt
engine:mkAlt.description: Alternation smart constructor: a `PEmpty` branch drops out (the other wins); otherwise `PAlt`. Internal helper.

engine:mkArrow.label: Make arrow type
engine:mkArrow.description: signature-substrate Phase A — build a TtArrow (the Fenel-authorable TraversalType face of `$arrow`) from a list of param TYPES and a return type. Params are wrapped as computed TtArrowParams with ordinal positional identity (the field-identity container law for unnamed slots); the node carries the synthetic raw sentinel (no host `$` envelope exists for a computed value). The arrow value has no requires slot — capability obligations are contextual, never part of the arrow denotation.

engine:mkArrowClosure.label: inhabit: mkArrowClosure
engine:mkArrowClosure.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.1 — build the const/vacuous-witness closure `{__fenelFn: true, params, body, closure: {}}` (the Ref substrate's isClosure shape). Assembled via the mapSet dynamic-key native rather than a record literal: a `{__fenelFn: true, …}` LITERAL is the evaluator's closure SENTINEL — it would leave `params`/`body` as UNEVALUATED JSON-Logic (`{var:"pnames"}`), so the fields are set as DATA via mapSet (the seWitnessCtor $tag-authoring precedent). Internal helper to seWitnessArrow.

engine:mkModuleProg.label: Module program
engine:mkModuleProg.description: Assemble a headered Program's element list: the `{kind = "module", name}` frame FIRST (directives []), then `buildDecls` of the inner decl lines (parse emits the module_decl frame ahead of the body decls). parser-substrate Phase 4 (D1).

engine:mkPair.label: subset: mkPair
engine:mkPair.description: Phase 5 (R-resolve) — a co-induction memo entry: the (have, want) marshalled-type pair pushed onto the resolve stack. Internal helper.

engine:mkRed.label: mkRed
engine:mkRed.description: Reduction smart constructor: `mkRed PEmpty f = PEmpty`; `mkRed (PEpsV v) f = PEpsV (f v)` (THE load-bearing eager compaction); `mkRed (PRed c g) f = mkRed c (\x -> f (g x))` (RED-FUSION, 6b lever-A rule 1 — collapses stacked reduction layers so derivation-step PRed chains never accumulate; a plain composition lambda, NOT std:compose, since PRed lambdas-in-Pat are 6a-p3-proven); otherwise `PRed`. Arm order: PEmpty → PEpsV → PRed → catch-all. Internal helper.

engine:mkSeq.label: mkSeq
engine:mkSeq.description: Sequencing smart constructor: `PEmpty` on either side annihilates to `PEmpty`. EPS-VALUE COLLAPSE (6b lever-A rule 2): `mkSeq (PEpsV v) b = mkRed b (\x -> { fst = v, snd = x })` and `mkSeq a (PEpsV v) = mkRed a (\x -> { fst = x, snd = v })` — a settled left/right factor folds into a reduction over the other side, producing the EXACT `{ fst, snd }` nesting PSeq's parseNull builds (the pair-shape contract every grammar reduction reads). KEEPS bare `PEps` (valueless) as PSeq — only PEpsV appears mid-derivation (PMatch ⇒ PEpsV), so the PEps arms are unreachable (pinned, not assumed). Recognition is identical. Internal helper.

engine:mkSmInterval.label: propagate: make interval
engine:mkSmInterval.description: Build an interval marker from two Maybe bounds; both unbounded (Nothing) ⇒ SeAll (the lattice top — mirrors the legacy mkInterval's both-Nothing collapse). Internal helper.

engine:namedContains.label: set-algebra: namedContains (Membership dispatch)
engine:namedContains.description: named-membership Phase 1 — decide `value ∈ {$named: name}` via the Membership registry: dispatchLookupOne resolves the per-name instance and applies its `member` predicate (Just verdict); on a miss, the prefix-parameterized families (multiple/list:maxdiff/list:span/format:path:max-*/ext); on no match, Nothing (the TS wrapper falls through to the un-ported NAMED_SETS — the dual-registry transition). `+`-composition + account precedence stay in the wrapper this phase. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/set-algebra.ts:containsNamed (the ported slice).

engine:namedDomain.label: set-algebra: namedDomain
engine:namedDomain.description: Phase 7c-continuation / floor-kernel Phase 3c soundness repair — value-domain category for built-in named sets. Prefix/whole-name facts run before the hierarchy fallback, so str:* remains string after its Subsumable migration; char:* remains Nothing because it accepts both numeric codepoints and one-character strings. Numeric/Bool/String hierarchy-only aliases then use the legacy hierarchy classifier. Boundary adapter.

engine:namedFieldType.label: Named field type
engine:namedFieldType.description: The type marker of a named ctor field from its accumulated atom list: the application of the head atom to the rest (`List Char` ⇒ app(List,[Char]); `Number` ⇒ the bare ref). Empty ⇒ a Unit ref (defensive; a named field always has ≥1 type atom). Internal decl-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 4 (D2).

engine:namedSubset.label: Named set: a ⊆ b
engine:namedSubset.description: Phase 7b proof-of-pattern — is named set `a` provably a subset of named set `b`? Returns true when a == b OR b ∈ HIERARCHY[a]. The hierarchy table is data, passed in from TS as a list of {name, supers} rows; the body is the pure traversal. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/set-algebra.ts:namedSubset.

engine:narrowAndFold.label: narrow: and fold
engine:narrowAndFold.description: Left-fold the env pair through each conjunct of an `and`: narrow each arg into both branches, threading the accumulated pair. Internal helper.

engine:narrowCmpArm.label: narrow: comparison arm
engine:narrowCmpArm.description: Narrow a comparison op application: exactly two args ⇒ narrowComparison over the two arg markers; any other arity ⇒ no-op. Internal helper.

engine:narrowComparison.label: narrow: comparison
engine:narrowComparison.description: If the left arg is a var and the right a numeric literal ⇒ applyComparisonNarrow; else if the right is a var and the left a numeric literal ⇒ flipOp then applyComparisonNarrow; else (two vars / non-numeric / two literals) ⇒ no-op. Internal helper.

engine:narrowFalseC.label: narrow: false constraint
engine:narrowFalseC.description: The canonical false-branch SetExpr constraint for a comparison against a numeric literal (> ⇒ (-∞,lit]; >= ⇒ (-∞,lit); < ⇒ [lit,∞); <= ⇒ (lit,∞); ==/=== ⇒ all ∖ {lit}). Internal helper.

engine:narrowFromCondition.label: Narrow from condition
engine:narrowFromCondition.description: Liquid-type narrowing: given an if-condition (as an ExprMarker) and a variable→type env (the `$`-free assoc list), compute the narrowed true-branch and false-branch envs as a pair { trueEnv, falseEnv } (both `$`-free assoc lists). Comparisons against a numeric literal tighten the variable's interval/enum (age > 18 ⇒ true (18,∞) / false (-∞,18]); == ⇒ the {lit} / complement pair); `and` narrows each conjunct into both branches; `or` narrows only the false-branch (each disjunct false); `!`/`not` swaps the branches. Two-variable comparisons + non-numeric literals are a no-op. The port of fenel-check's narrowFromCondition onto immutable env-pair threading. unified-static-analysis Phase 3b-3c.

engine:narrowInto.label: narrow: into
engine:narrowInto.description: Narrow a condition ExprMarker into the env pair: Op markers dispatch by op string (comparisons / and / or / !/not); everything else is a no-op. Internal helper.

engine:narrowIsCmp.label: narrow: is comparison?
engine:narrowIsCmp.description: True for the six narrowable comparison ops (> >= < <= == ===). NOTE: !=/!== are deliberately EXCLUDED — the legacy narrowComparison switch covers only these six. Internal helper.

engine:narrowLeftVar.label: narrow: left var
engine:narrowLeftVar.description: left=var, op, right: narrow when the right arg is a numeric literal, applying the op directly. Internal helper.

engine:narrowNot.label: narrow: not
engine:narrowNot.description: Narrow !/not: recurse into the first arg with the true/false envs swapped, then swap the result pair back. ≥1 arg required; else no-op. Internal helper.

engine:narrowOp.label: narrow: op
engine:narrowOp.description: Dispatch a narrowing op: the six comparison ops ⇒ narrowCmpArm; and ⇒ fold each conjunct into both branches; or ⇒ fold each disjunct's false-narrowing into falseEnv; !/not ⇒ swap-recurse-swap; any other op ⇒ no-op. Internal helper.

engine:narrowOrArm.label: narrow: or arm
engine:narrowOrArm.description: Narrow an `or`: the true-branch is unchanged (≥1 disjunct true ⇒ no precise narrowing); the false-branch folds each disjunct's false-narrowing (all disjuncts false). Internal helper.

engine:narrowOrFold.label: narrow: or fold
engine:narrowOrFold.description: Left-fold the falseEnv through each `or` disjunct: for each arg, narrow it against the current falseEnv (as both temp branches) and keep the arg's false-narrowing as the new falseEnv. Internal helper.

engine:narrowRightVar.label: narrow: right var
engine:narrowRightVar.description: left, op, right=var: narrow when the left arg is a numeric literal, applying the flipped op (lit > var ≡ var < lit). Internal helper.

engine:narrowTrueC.label: narrow: true constraint
engine:narrowTrueC.description: The canonical true-branch SetExpr constraint for a comparison against a numeric literal (> ⇒ (lit,∞); >= ⇒ [lit,∞); < ⇒ (-∞,lit); <= ⇒ (-∞,lit]; ==/=== ⇒ {lit}). Internal helper.

engine:needsNesting.label: Needs nesting
engine:needsNesting.description: Flat-vs-nested IIFE predicate for JsLet. Mirrors the TS oracle's `ast.bindings.some((b, i) => ast.bindings.slice(0, i).some((earlier) => referencesName(b.value, earlier.name)))`. Iterates bindings forward, threading a `seen` name list.

engine:needsNestingLoop.label: Needs nesting (loop)
engine:needsNestingLoop.description: Recursive worker for needsNesting. For each binding in turn, checks whether any seen-so-far name is referenced in the current binding's value; if so returns True. Otherwise extends `seen` with the current binding's name and recurses on the tail.

engine:neg3.label: empty: neg3
engine:neg3.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — Tri (Maybe Bool) negation: Just b ⇒ Just (not b), Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper (avoids std:not — inlines the flip).

engine:negArgsGrounded.label: rel-solve: negArgsGrounded
engine:negArgsGrounded.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — one negated atom's arg list: EVar ⇒ must be in the positive grounded set; ELit ⇒ fine; anything else (compound) ⇒ false. Internal helper.

engine:negAtomMatches.label: rel-solve: negAtomMatches
engine:negAtomMatches.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — true when SOME fact row matches the negated atom's args under the row's bindings (matchArgs — grounded vars require equality, literals select; deepEqValue cells). Internal helper.

engine:negAtomsSafe.label: rel-solve: negAtomsSafe
engine:negAtomsSafe.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — true when EVERY negated atom's args are safe (negArgsGrounded): each an EVar grounded by the positive atoms or an ELit constant; any compound arg or ungrounded var ⇒ false (the branch fences to Nothing). Internal helper.

engine:negOpaque.label: fork: neg-opaque
engine:negOpaque.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — record a negated condition RAW in opaque (the sound abstention arm of negateCondInto): append `not(cond)` to opaque, atoms unchanged. Internal helper.

engine:negOrder.label: fork: neg-order
engine:negOrder.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — the CERTIFIED negated-order flip: when BOTH operands of the order call are certified numeric (forkBothCertNumeric over certs), emit the flipped atom (`¬(a≤b) ⇒ b<a`, `¬(a<b) ⇒ b≤a`, `¬(a≥b) ⇒ a<b`, `¬(a>b) ⇒ a≤b`); otherwise the RAW `not(cond)` opaque abstention (the Phase-3 same-type-only fence). Internal helper.

engine:negOrderAtom.label: fork: neg-order-atom
engine:negOrderAtom.description: decide-substrate Phase 7 — build the flipped order atom into the atoms accumulator: `¬(lte a b)` ⇒ lt (b,a); `¬(lt a b)` ⇒ lte (b,a); `¬(gte a b)` ⇒ lt (a,b); `¬(gt a b)` ⇒ lte (a,b) (via the theory-combine adders over the original / reversed arg list). Internal helper.

engine:negUnionInner.label: floor-axioms: negUnionInner
engine:negUnionInner.description: floor-kernel Phase 1 — negUnionToIntersect helper: the complement's inner must be a SeUnion; un-complement every branch. Internal helper.

engine:negUnionToIntersect.label: Neg-union to intersect
engine:negUnionToIntersect.description: floor-kernel Phase 1 — the De Morgan derivation witness (bwd, partial): `SeComplement (SeUnion bs)` with EVERY branch a SeComplement merges back to `SeIntersect [inner …]`; any other shape ⇒ Nothing. Left-inverse of intersectToNegUnion.

engine:negateCondInto.label: fork: negate-cond
engine:negateCondInto.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 3 / decide-substrate Phase 7 — the NEGATION TABLE for the else-world (¬cond) into { atoms, opaque }, threading the numeric-certified term list `certs`: `¬(eq a b)` ⇒ a neq atom; `¬(neq a b)` ⇒ an eq atom; `¬(not d)` ⇒ assume d (splitCondInto d); an ORDER atom (lte/lt/gte/gt) whose BOTH operands are certified NUMERIC (numeric-ELit or eufValEq-member of certs) ⇒ the flipped strict/nonstrict atom (`¬(a≤b) ⇒ b<a`, `¬(a<b) ⇒ b≤a`, `¬(a≥b) ⇒ a<b`, `¬(a>b) ⇒ a≤b` — EXACT within one type, since both-numeric ⇒ same type ⇒ trichotomy); an UNCERTIFIED order atom (cross-type-possible), an `and`/`or`, or any other call ⇒ the RAW `not(cond)` in opaque (NO atom — the sound cross-type abstention). Internal helper.

engine:noAddEq.label: NO addEq
engine:noAddEq.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — add an `eq` atom (two args, via eufTwoArgs) to the accumulator's eqs; non-2-arg dropped. Internal helper.

engine:noAddGtFlip.label: NO addGtFlip
engine:noAddGtFlip.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — a `gt lhs rhs` (lhs > rhs) atom flips to the swapped `lt` edge { lhs = rhs, rhs = lhs } (rhs < lhs); non-2-arg dropped. Internal helper.

engine:noAddGteFlip.label: NO addGteFlip
engine:noAddGteFlip.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — a `gte lhs rhs` (lhs ≥ rhs) atom flips to the swapped `lte` edge { lhs = rhs, rhs = lhs } (rhs ≤ lhs); non-2-arg dropped. Internal helper.

engine:noAddLt.label: NO addLt
engine:noAddLt.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — add an `lt` atom (lhs < rhs, via eufTwoArgs) to the accumulator's lts; non-2-arg dropped. Internal helper.

engine:noAddLte.label: NO addLte
engine:noAddLte.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — add an `lte` atom (lhs ≤ rhs, via eufTwoArgs) to the accumulator's ltes; non-2-arg dropped. Internal helper.

engine:noAddNeq.label: NO addNeq
engine:noAddNeq.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — add a `neq` atom (two args, via eufTwoArgs) to the accumulator's neqs; non-2-arg dropped. Internal helper.

engine:noAtomsEffectful.label: NO atomsEffectful
engine:noAtomsEffectful.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — true when any extracted atom (eq/neq/lte/lt) carries an `$effect:`-prefixed ECall head in either side's term tree (the defensive decider fence: effectful sites must never be congruence-merged / ordered by the ambient decider without a memory model). Reuses eufTermHasEffect. Internal helper.

engine:noAtomsEmpty.label: NO atomsEmpty
engine:noAtomsEmpty.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — true when all four atom lists (eqs, neqs, ltes, lts) are empty (no verdict possible ⇒ Nothing). Internal helper.

engine:noDecideWhere.label: NO decideWhere
engine:noDecideWhere.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the widened emptiness arm over a SeWhere predicate Expr (replaces euf's eufDecideWhere in setAlgebraDecideEmptyEufArm): extract the and-spine's mixed atoms (noWhereAtoms; non-extractable conjuncts DROPPED — sound subset-drop); DEFENSIVELY fence any atom whose term tree carries an `$effect:` head (⇒ Nothing); zero atoms ⇒ Nothing. Then satCombined: unsat ⇒ Just true (empty over every domain + ambient env), else Nothing (never Just false — combined-sat does not certify nonempty for a typed domain). The gain: `{v | v ≥ 5 ∧ v ≤ 5 ∧ f v ≠ f 5}` ⇒ Just true (order derives v = 5, EUF refutes).

engine:noDerivedEqs.label: NO derivedEqs
engine:noDerivedEqs.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R3) — the equalities entailed by nonstrict cycles: every unordered pair of universe terms with DISTINCT current roots that are MUTUALLY reachable (each in the other's reachSet) is emitted as { lhs, rhs } (representatives). After R1 has passed, a mutual-reach cycle has no strict edge ⇒ antisymmetry (same-type, post-Step-1) forces equality — these feed EUF. Internal helper.

engine:noDerivedInner.label: NO derivedInner
engine:noDerivedInner.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R3) — pair one universe term u against the remaining terms v: distinct roots + mutual reachability ⇒ emit { lhs = u.expr, rhs = v.expr }. Internal helper.

engine:noDerivedOuter.label: NO derivedOuter
engine:noDerivedOuter.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R3) — outer loop over universe terms, pairing each against the terms AFTER it (noDerivedInner) so each unordered pair is tested once. Internal helper.

engine:noEdges.label: NO edges
engine:noEdges.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the directed order edges { a, b, strict } over universe indices: each lte ⇒ { a = ix lhs, b = ix rhs, strict = false }, each lt ⇒ same with strict = true. `a ≤ b` (or `a < b`) is a directed edge a → b. Internal helper.

engine:noEdgesFrom.label: NO edgesFrom
engine:noEdgesFrom.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — build order edges { a = ix lhs, b = ix rhs, strict } (endpoints resolved via eufIndexOf) from a { lhs, rhs } pair list at a fixed strictness. Internal helper.

engine:noElemIx.label: NO elemIx
engine:noElemIx.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — numeric membership of an index in an index list (compared with the working `eq` over raw Numbers — the opaque-Number-safe path, never a string key). Internal helper.

engine:noLitPairScan.label: NO litPairScan
engine:noLitPairScan.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R2) — outer loop over numeric lits L1, testing each against the whole numeric-lit list (noLitVsRest). Internal helper.

engine:noLitPathConflict.label: NO litPathConflict
engine:noLitPathConflict.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R2) — true when some numeric lit L1 reaches a numeric lit L2 (under the current roots + projected edges) with value(L1) > value(L2): transitivity forces L1 ≤ L2, so L1 > L2 is unsat. Excludes L1, L2 sharing a root (that is a lit-conflict eufConflict already refutes). Internal helper.

engine:noLitVsRest.label: NO litVsRest
engine:noLitVsRest.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R2) — true when numeric lit n1 reaches some numeric lit n2 (distinct roots) with value(n1) > value(n2). Internal helper.

engine:noNumLits.label: NO numLits
engine:noNumLits.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R2) — the universe entries whose `.expr` is a numeric ELit (annotated { ix, expr, … }). Under the opaque-Number decider ctx a wrapped number fails isNumber ⇒ it is skipped (R2 degrades to Nothing — sound). Internal helper.

engine:noOrderTerms.label: NO orderTerms
engine:noOrderTerms.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the lhs ++ rhs terms of every lte + lt atom (the order-theory universe contributors). Internal helper.

engine:noPairListEffect.label: NO pairListEffect
engine:noPairListEffect.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — true when some { lhs, rhs } atom in the list has an `$effect:` head anywhere in either side's term tree (eufTermHasEffect). Internal helper.

engine:noPairTerms.label: NO pairTerms
engine:noPairTerms.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the lhs ++ rhs terms of a { lhs, rhs } pair list (concatenated; deduped later by eufUniverse). Internal helper.

engine:noProjectEdges.label: NO projectEdges
engine:noProjectEdges.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — re-project every order edge's endpoints onto the CURRENT union-find roots (eufFind under the closed parent map): { a = find a, b = find b, strict }. Re-run each exchange round so the order graph tracks the merged EUF classes. Internal helper.

engine:noReachClose.label: NO reachClose
engine:noReachClose.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the reachability fixpoint: grow the reached-set by one edge-relaxation pass (noReachExpand) until it stabilizes or fuel runs out. Internal helper.

engine:noReachExpand.label: NO reachExpand
engine:noReachExpand.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — one relaxation pass: for each edge { a, b }, if `a` is already reached and `b` is not, append `b` (monotone in the growing accumulator). Internal helper.

engine:noReachSet.label: NO reachSet
engine:noReachSet.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the set of root indices reachable from `src` following the projected order edges (reflexive + transitive; fixpoint-closed, fuel-bounded by |edges| + 1 — cycles converge). Internal helper.

engine:noSatLoop.label: NO satLoop
engine:noSatLoop.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (+6D) — the exchange fixpoint behind satCombined: close EUF over the current eqs; eufConflict / eufNeqViolated ⇒ Just false; else project edges onto roots, R1/R2 ⇒ Just false; dtConflict (ctor/lit-tag distinctness) ⇒ Just false; else pool the derived equalities (R3 nonstrict-cycles + dtDerive injectivity, both not-same-root-filtered) — none ⇒ Nothing (fixpoint), some ⇒ append + recurse with one less fuel. Internal helper.

engine:noStrictCycle.label: NO strictCycle
engine:noStrictCycle.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R1) — true when the projected order graph has a strict cycle: some strict edge { a → b } whose head `a` is reachable FROM `b` (b ⇝ a), forming a → b → ⇝ a with a strict edge. Sound unsat (no total order admits a < … ≤ a). A strict self-loop { a → a } is caught too (reachSet is reflexive). Internal helper.

engine:noStrictCycleScan.label: NO strictCycleScan
engine:noStrictCycleScan.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 (R1) — scan the edges for a strict one whose head is reachable from its tail (the back-edge closing a strict cycle). Internal helper.

engine:noWhereAtoms.label: NO whereAtoms
engine:noWhereAtoms.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — walk a predicate Expr's `and`-spine collecting mixed atoms { eqs, neqs, ltes, lts }: `eq` ⇒ eqs; `neq`/`not(eq …)` ⇒ neqs; `lte`/`lt` ⇒ ltes/lts as { lhs, rhs }; `gte`/`gt` ⇒ swapped ltes/lts (a ≥ b ≡ b ≤ a); every other head DROPPED (sound subset-drop). The Nelson-Oppen collector — a widening of euf's eq/neq-only eufWhereAtoms (which is left untouched).

engine:noWhereFold.label: NO whereFold
engine:noWhereFold.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the and-spine collector for noWhereAtoms: `and` ⇒ recurse each arg; `eq` ⇒ add eq; `neq` ⇒ add neq; `not(eq …)` ⇒ add neq; `lte` ⇒ add lte; `lt` ⇒ add lt; `gte`/`gt` ⇒ add the swapped lte/lt; every other head ⇒ drop. Threads the { eqs, neqs, ltes, lts } accumulator. Internal helper.

engine:noWhereFoldList.label: NO whereFoldList
engine:noWhereFoldList.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — fold noWhereFold over an `and`'s operand list, threading the { eqs, neqs, ltes, lts } accumulator. Internal helper.

engine:noWhereNot.label: NO whereNot
engine:noWhereNot.description: decide-substrate Phase 6 — the `not` arm: `not(eq x y)` ⇒ a neq atom; any other negated head dropped (no De Morgan over the and-spine in v1). Internal helper.

engine:nominalNameOf.label: subset: nominalNameOf
engine:nominalNameOf.description: Phase 5 (E-named) — the nominal entity NAME of a leaf marshalled type as Maybe String: TtNamed ⇒ Just its name; TtOpaque ⇒ Just its `$opaque.name` (Char/Nat/Int/…). Else Nothing (a structural type has no single nominal name). Reproduces isSubtype's name-handle + opaque-name reads (the `$named↔$opaque` bridge + the named hierarchy). Internal helper.

engine:nonEmptyProp.label: law: nonEmptyProp
engine:nonEmptyProp.description: decide-substrate Phase 2 (K2) — build a non-empty-string law claim JUDGMENT-NATIVE: `JEmpty (SeIntersect [SeEnum [witness], SeEnum [""]])` via jopDisjoint (the same composed-set builder the kernel's judgmentOfProposition iso uses) — the {witness} ∩ {empty string} set is empty ≡ witness ≠ "" (disjointness). Emits the one lattice judgment, NOT the closed PropDisjoint marker; the TS seam (unmarshalProposition) shape-recognizes SeIntersect [s, t] ⇒ PropDisjoint for the still-Prop* proposer (byte-identical downstream; the back-map dies at K3). The set payloads are canonical `$tag` Se*. Internal helper.

engine:noneToEmptyUnion.label: None to empty union
engine:noneToEmptyUnion.description: floor-kernel Phase 1 — the `⊥ = ∪∅` derivation witness: `SeNone` rewrites to the nullary join `SeUnion []` (§3.2 `∪∅ = ⊥`). The equality claim is lawNullaryUnion. Any other shape passes through unchanged.

engine:normMarker.label: infer: normalize marker
engine:normMarker.description: Normalize an Se* SetExpr in-body via the Fenel setAlgebraNormalize (the legacy per-step normalize point — D-3b-3-2). The Sm* bridge (smToSe/seToSm) is retired; the body is Se*-native (decide-substrate Phase 1 Stage E). Internal helper.

engine:normaliseToCore.label: Normalise to Core IR
engine:normaliseToCore.description: Lower raw JSON Logic to an Expr tree packaged as a CoreProgram, the first step in every per-target compile pipeline. The shared JSON-Logic adapter preserves identity-bearing constructor slots, rejects ambiguous unscoped constructor metadata, and surfaces unrecognised shapes as structured CompileError.Unsupported. The final Fenel walk resolves bare defining-module call heads through the host-projected binding index to exact canonical fnIds; unlisted, already-qualified, dynamic, and effect heads remain unchanged. A global function passed as a value lowers to the runtime reference a call head of the same spelling lowers to (`$fn:<key>`). A dynamic head or a variable reference whose root is no binder in scope and which names no global function, or an unresolved dotted head, is refused as Unsupported.

engine:normalizeFenelTypeShorthand.label: Normalize FenelType shorthand
engine:normalizeFenelTypeShorthand.description: Phase 7a — recursive rewriter that converts legacy `$maybe` / `$list` / `$result` shorthand encodings of FenelType to their canonical helper-emitted form (`Maybe(T)` / `List(T)` / `Result(E, A)`). Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedNormalizeFenelTypeShorthand` in engine-bodies-dispatch.ts which marshals raw JSON to the TypeNorm ADT and unmarshals rewrite markers via the canonical Maybe/List/Result helpers. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/type-normalize.ts (now a thin shim). First port of the type-algebra arc.

engine:normalizeFieldDeclarations.label: Normalize field declarations
engine:normalizeFieldDeclarations.description: Registry-independent alias of collectFieldIdentitiesKernel for account/draft validation before insertion into a ModuleRegistry.

engine:normalizeFieldOccurrenceDraft.label: Normalize field occurrence draft
engine:normalizeFieldOccurrenceDraft.description: Validate a stable-id field draft. Entropy is supplied once by the host; this body distinguishes mint from explicit reuse and rejects missing/tombstoned reuse without ever minting.

engine:normalizeForDecide.label: Normalize for decide
engine:normalizeForDecide.description: PE-as-normalizer (decide-substrate Phase 7): run `partialEvaluate` over a predicate Expr with NO known inputs (free reads stay residual calls) at the fixed PE budget 8, then project the PEResult back to an Expr (resultToExpr — a folded concrete value re-wraps as ELit). Const-folds pure sub-terms, prunes concretely-dead if-branches, and collapses a whole-concrete predicate to a boolean ELit — the reduction half made a pipeline stage the branching faces run before gate/mint/fork. Semantics-preserving (the Phase-1 oracle contract) and effect-site-preserving, so gating on the residual is sound and strictly wider. decide-substrate Phase 7.

engine:normalizeToArgList.label: Normalise to arg list
engine:normalizeToArgList.description: Canonicalise a single-key JlObject's only field value into a list. Mirrors `argList = Array.isArray(rawArgs) ? rawArgs : [rawArgs]`.

engine:normalizeType.label: type-former: normalizeType
engine:normalizeType.description: P7-5 — the minimal type-level canonicalizer: dispatch the $-free marker the TS boundary built. NtRefined ⇒ apply the envelope lifts to the (already normalized) set; NtVoid / NtOther ⇒ pass through. The inner SetExpr simplification is delegated to setAlgebraNormalize at the boundary (probe 'boundary-delegates'). Internal helper.

engine:notEmpty.label: empty: notEmpty
engine:notEmpty.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — `is this type inhabited?` as a Tri = the negation of emptyW (neg3): Just true ⇒ provably inhabited, Just false ⇒ provably empty, Nothing ⇒ undecided. Used by paramsInhab. Internal helper.

engine:notSeen.label: Not seen
engine:notSeen.description: The elements of `xs` not already in `seen` (the worklist frontier filter). 7h S2: builds a name→True SET from `seen` (`fromEntries`) once per call, then tests membership O(1) via `mapGet`/`isJustVal` — byte-identical to the prior `elem`-scan filter (same order, same kept elements), just sub-linear. Internal helper.

engine:nthArg.label: infer: nth of list
engine:nthArg.description: The i-th element of a list as a Maybe (Nothing when out of range). Internal helper.

engine:nthOf.label: enumerate: nthOf
engine:nthOf.description: Phase 15 — the nth element (0-based) of a list ⇒ Maybe a; an out-of-range index ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper for sampleSet.

engine:nthString.label: Nth string
engine:nthString.description: List-indexing helper for a List<String>. Returns "" on out-of-range; callers guard via `lt idx (length xs)`.

engine:nullValueAssume.label: Null value under assume
engine:nullValueAssume.description: The unwrapped null value of `pat` under a name→(Maybe a) INDEX (`{}` when it doesn't match empty — only ever called where nullability is already established, so the default is unobservable). Captures `a`'s null parse at PSeq-derivation time. 7h S2: `idx` is the O(1) `mapGet` index. Internal helper.

engine:nullableFix.label: Nullable fixpoint
engine:nullableFix.description: Bounded Kleene iteration for the Bool nullability fixpoint over the production env `g`: start all-false, iterate `|g| + 1` times (monotone over a finite env ⇒ converged). Returns the stable `[{ name, val }]` assumption map. Internal helper.

engine:nullableG.label: Nullable G
engine:nullableG.description: Does `pat` match the empty input under the env `g`'s nullability fixpoint? The recognizer's accept test. parser-substrate Phase 1.

engine:nullableIter.label: Nullable iterate
engine:nullableIter.description: One-or-more Kleene steps of the Bool nullability fixpoint, fuel-bounded by `|g|+1` but EARLY-EXITING the moment a round reproduces its input map (converged — 6b lever-A). Internal helper.

engine:nullablePat.label: Nullable pattern
engine:nullablePat.description: Does the Pat match the empty input? PEps true; PEmpty/PMatch false; PSeq and; PAlt or; PRep min==0 or nullable child. Env-free (containment patterns carry no PRef grammar refs). Internal helper.

engine:nullableUnderAssume.label: Nullable under assume
engine:nullableUnderAssume.description: Does `pat` match the empty input, given a name→Bool INDEX (a `fromEntries`-built record) for `PRef`s? PEps/PEpsV ⇒ true; PEmpty/PMatch ⇒ false; PSeq ⇒ and; PAlt ⇒ or; PRep ⇒ min==0 or nullable child; PRed ⇒ nullable child; PRef ⇒ the assumption (default false). 7h S2: `idx` is the O(1) `mapGet` index built once at each fixpoint round / step boundary, not the O(|g|) assoc-list. Internal helper.

engine:numBound.label: propagate: numBound
engine:numBound.description: The marshalBound guard in Fenel: a numeric or string bound value carries; an object/expression bound value collapses to unbounded (Nothing) — the legacy numLo/numHi ±Infinity read on the unsupported fragment. Internal helper.

engine:numLen.label: Number literal length
engine:numLen.description: The length of the numeric literal starting at `i`: radix (`0x`/`0o`/`0b` + digit run) or decimal (integer + optional `.`-not-`..` fractional + optional `e`/`E` exponent). Mirrors `fenel-parser.ts:179–223`. Internal lexer helper.

engine:numberWidgetFor.label: widget-hint: numberWidgetFor
engine:numberWidgetFor.description: Phase 3b-3d — pick the UI widget for a number-typed SetExpr. Enum -> radio(≤4)/dropdown(≤15)/searchable-select by count; interval (finite+integer) -> stepper(≤5)/slider-with-stops(≤20)/slider(≤200) via integerCount; [0,1] non-integer -> percentage slider; finite -> bounded slider; half-bounded -> number-input{min?,max?}; else number-input. Returns a WidgetHint. The `!set` unconstrained-number case is handled by the TS wrapper. Mirrors widget-hint.ts:numberWidgetFor.

engine:numericBound.label: set-algebra: numericBound
engine:numericBound.description: Phase 7b-continuation — Maybe<Bound> + sign → NumericBoundResult 4-state (NbrPos / NbrNeg / NbrNum / NbrNan).

engine:objectHasDollarPrefixedKey.label: Object has $-prefixed key
engine:objectHasDollarPrefixedKey.description: Check whether any field name in the list starts with `$`. Multi-key marker-rejection helper for lowerObjectExpr.

engine:omitType.label: Omit type
engine:omitType.description: Identity-total record omit. Paths are non-empty lists of FieldKey; recursive matching never reads wireName.

engine:opNotationToCodeName.label: Op notation to codename
engine:opNotationToCodeName.description: Operator-notation key (`+`, `==`, `cat`, ...) → canonical codeName (`add`, `eq`, `concat`). Mirrors OPERATOR_NOTATION_TO_CODENAME table.

engine:opTT.label: Operator singleton token type
engine:opTT.description: The TT for a generic op-char run's text: a reserved-multi (`== != <= >= -> <- |> :: ..`) or named singleton (`+ - * / % < > | & $ = : .`) keeps its own TT; anything else is `op` (`fenel-parser.ts:262–290`). Internal lexer helper.

engine:orVerdict.label: Or verdict
engine:orVerdict.description: Final tri-state verdict for closedOr: true-seen ⇒ Just true; else unknown-seen ⇒ Nothing; else Just false. Internal helper.

engine:p2sExtract.label: solve: p2sExtract
engine:p2sExtract.description: Phase 5 — extract `(orientation, literal)` from a two-arg comparison/eq over `varName`: `{ ok = true, left, lit }` when one operand is `EVar varName` and the other an `ELit`, else `{ ok = false }`. Internal helper.

engine:p2sExtractBoth.label: solve: p2sExtractBoth
engine:p2sExtractBoth.description: Phase 5 — try `EVar varName` in the LEFT operand (with the right an ELit); fall through to p2sExtractRight otherwise. Internal helper.

engine:p2sExtractRight.label: solve: p2sExtractRight
engine:p2sExtractRight.description: Phase 5 — `EVar varName` in the RIGHT operand (left an ELit) ⇒ `{ ok = true, left = false, lit }`; else `{ ok = false }`. Internal helper.

engine:pPunct.label: Punctuation matcher
engine:pPunct.description: A `PMatch` over the singleton WsEnum of a static (v==t) token's encoded form — `(`, `)`, `+`, `=`, … Internal expr-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 3b.

engine:pVirt.label: Virtual matcher
engine:pVirt.description: A `PMatch` over the singleton WsEnum of a virtual / empty-`v` token's encoded form — vopen/vclose/vsemi/eof. Internal expr-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 3b.

engine:paramTypes.label: Arrow param types
engine:paramTypes.description: signature-substrate Phase A — the param TYPES of the FLATTENED spine, in positional order (flatten first, then project the types out of the TtArrowParams). Empty for non-arrow values.

engine:paramsInhab.label: empty: paramsInhab
engine:paramsInhab.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — the all-params-inhabited Kleene-AND fold for emptyArrow: mAnd-fold of notEmpty over the TtArrowParam types; an empty param-list ⇒ Just true (vacuous ⇒ a thunk ()->R is empty iff R is). Internal helper.

engine:paramsSub.label: subset: paramsSub
engine:paramsSub.description: Phase 6 Step 2b / field-identity Phase 3 — the contravariant pairwise param fold for arrowSub: zip the two param lists strictly by list position and subset their types (callers pass want first). Param FieldKeys survive as metadata but never reorder variance; flattened curried arrows may therefore contain repeated local positional ordinals. Arity mismatch ⇒ Just false. Internal helper.

engine:parseEffectFnId.label: Parse effect fnId
engine:parseEffectFnId.description: Parse a $effect:<Class>:<method> sentinel fnId into its (typeName, methodName) pair. Returns Nothing for malformed sentinels (missing prefix, missing separator, empty class, empty method). Mirrors the TS oracle at implementations/typescript/engine/src/ir/effects-explicit.ts — the canonical Phase 21.0 canary that proves a real engine pass executes through both the engine evaluator AND each per-target self-host (JS / Wasm / LLVM).

engine:parseEmail.label: input-parsers: parseEmail
engine:parseEmail.description: Phase 9 sub-step 2 PARTIAL — trim + lowercase + empty check email parser. The TS wrapper pre-classifies the raw input into ParseEmailInput (ParseEmailStr s for string inputs, ParseEmailPass passValue for non-string passthrough); the body dispatches on the variant and emits POk{value=normalized} / PFail{error="Empty email"} / POk{value=passValue}. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedParseEmail` in engine-bodies-dispatch.ts. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/input-parsers.ts:parseEmail.

engine:parseExprToks.label: Parse expression tokens
engine:parseExprToks.description: The one-call expression-parse entry: encode the layout token stream (Design E), build the per-input grammar, and run `parseG` from the Root production. Returns `Just Syntax` on a full parse, Nothing otherwise. `table` = the fixity table (closure-captured by the OpSeq + section reductions — resolveOpSeq / buildSection); `nullValue` threads to the Unit primary. parser-substrate Phase 3b.

engine:parseFileFrames.label: Parse file frames
engine:parseFileFrames.description: The per-declaration program parse: split the whole-file layout token stream into decl GROUPS (splitTopLevelDecls), parse each group as a header-less Program via the existing `parseProgToks` (each over a short token run — the 6b2 fast curve), concat the per-group `{frame, directives}` element lists, and prepend the `module_decl` element for headered files. Returns `Just [element]` on a full parse, Nothing if any group fails (the all-or-nothing parity with whole-file parseProgToks). The 5b1 reference orchestrator (NOT a compiled entry). parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:parseG.label: Parse G
engine:parseG.description: Parse the token list `toks` against production `start` of grammar `g`, returning the reduced value (`Just value` on a full match, Nothing otherwise). Folds the strict derivative over `toks` (fixpoints threaded incrementally), then reads the residual root's parseNull value under the residual env — so reductions (`PRed`) build a real `Syntax`-shaped tree end-to-end. parser-substrate Phase 1.

engine:parseGroups.label: Parse groups
engine:parseGroups.description: Parse a list of decl GROUPS, sequencing the Maybe results: each group ⇒ `parseOneGroup` ⇒ `Just [element]`; concat all; Nothing if any group fails. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:parseInput.label: input-layer: parseInput
engine:parseInput.description: Phase 9 sub-step 3 — publish-surface boundary adapter for the unified parseInput contract. The Fenel body resolves the atom name (delegating to resolveAtom); the wrapper handles the parseFns registry lookup + parser invocation TS-side (parseFns map stays TS per Decision 2 — public extension hook via registerParseFn). std:parseInput delegates to input-layer.ts:parseInput which dispatches via `dispatchedParseInput`. Boundary adapter. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/input-layer.ts:parseInput.

engine:parseNullFix.label: Parse-null fixpoint
engine:parseNullFix.description: Bounded Kleene iteration for the Maybe-value parseNull fixpoint over the env `g`: start all-Nothing, iterate `|g| + 1` times. first-Just-wins is deterministic (PAlt left-first; the recursive branch is non-nullable). Returns the stable `[{ name, val }]` assumption map. Internal helper.

engine:parseNullG.label: Parse-null G
engine:parseNullG.description: The value `pat` yields on the empty input under the env `g`'s parseNull fixpoint (Nothing if it doesn't match empty). The parser's accept-value. parser-substrate Phase 1.

engine:parseNullIter.label: Parse-null iterate
engine:parseNullIter.description: One-or-more Kleene steps of the Maybe-value parseNull fixpoint, fuel-bounded by `|g|+1` but EARLY-EXITING the moment a round reproduces its input map's Just/Nothing presence (converged — first-Just-wins ⇒ presence stability is value stability; 6b lever-A). Internal helper.

engine:parseNullUnderAssume.label: Parse-null under assume
engine:parseNullUnderAssume.description: The value `pat` yields on the empty input (Nothing if it doesn't match empty), given a name→(Maybe a) INDEX (a `fromEntries`-built record). PEps ⇒ Just {} (unit); PEpsV v ⇒ Just v; PEmpty/PMatch ⇒ Nothing; PSeq ⇒ Just { fst, snd } when both sides match empty; PAlt ⇒ first Just; PRep ⇒ Just [] when min==0, else min copies of the child's null value; PRed ⇒ fmap the reduction; PRef ⇒ the assumption (default Nothing). 7h S2: `idx` is the O(1) `mapGet` index, not the O(|g|) assoc-list. Internal helper.

engine:parseNumber.label: input-parsers: parseNumber
engine:parseNumber.description: Phase 9 sub-step 2 PARTIAL — number coercion parser. Number passthrough; String → trim + Number() + isFinite check; otherwise passthrough. The TS wrapper pre-computes Number(value)/isFinite/trimmed-empty into ParseNumberInput; the body emits POk{value=n} / PFail{error=msg}. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedParseNumber`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/input-parsers.ts:parseNumber.

engine:parseOneGroup.label: Parse one group
engine:parseOneGroup.description: Parse one decl GROUP token run as a header-less Program: re-wrap as `vopen <group> vclose eof` and call the existing `parseProgToks`, returning its `Just [element]` element list (one element — buildDecls runs over the group's directive+decl lines). parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:parseProgToks.label: Parse program tokens
engine:parseProgToks.description: The one-call program-parse entry: encode the layout token stream (Design E), build the merged decl+expr grammar, run `parseG` from the "Program" production. Returns `Just [{frame, directives}]` on a full parse, Nothing otherwise. `table` = the fixity table (closure-captured by the def-body OpSeq reductions); `nullValue` threads to the Unit primary. parser-substrate Phase 4 (D1).

engine:parseString.label: input-parsers: parseString
engine:parseString.description: Phase 9 sub-step 2 PARTIAL — string coercion parser. String passthrough; null/undefined → PFail "Empty string"; otherwise String(value) coerced. The TS wrapper pre-classifies into ParseStringInput (ParseStrStr s / ParseStrNull / ParseStrCoerce coercedStr); the body emits POk{value} / PFail{error}. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedParseString`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/input-parsers.ts:parseString.

engine:parseUrlParts.label: set-algebra: parseUrlParts
engine:parseUrlParts.description: named-membership Phase 3 — parse a URL string into Maybe (UrlParts scheme host port) via pure string-ops, mirroring `new URL(v.includes('://') ? v : 'http://'+v)`'s acceptance on the ASCII corpus (IDN/punycode not exercised). Nothing ≡ new URL() throwing (empty host / space in host).

engine:partialEvaluate.label: Partial evaluate
engine:partialEvaluate.description: The residualizing evaluator (partial evaluation) as a pure walker over the locked 7-case Expr. Given an Expr, a static prefix of known inputs (a {name, value} list), the foldable-fnId set (the positive fold gate — every registered pure fn by id + codeName), a recursive-inline budget, and the null sentinel, computes as much as possible and returns a PEResult `{ done, value }` — done=true ⇒ concrete value, done=false ⇒ a residual Expr that re-evaluates under any extension of the knowns to the same value. Const-folds pure calls (via the peEval host re-entry), substitutes known vars (with dot-path projection), prunes dead if-branches, short-circuits and/or. The faithful port of the TS partial-evaluator.ts (the parity oracle). partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 1.
