engine:sortNumbersAsc.description: Phase 3b-3 — ascending stable insertion sort over numbers (mirrors numericInsiders.sort).

engine:soundOfValue.label: identifiable: soundOfValue
engine:soundOfValue.description: Phase 10b sub-step 2 — sound identifier for a specific value, falling back to its type's Soundable instance. Same shape as iconOfValue over the `__sound` / `sound` fields. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/identifiable.ts:soundOfValue.

engine:specObligations.label: Spec obligations
engine:specObligations.description: The validateSpecRecord walk, Fenel-bodied (expr-substrate Phase 6b0): for each marshalled field-fact record, skip non-Verified fields; an invalid value (falsy / non-object / array) becomes a prove-candidate when the hook is present AND the value is strictly undefined (the prove-on-missing branch), else the verbatim 'missing Verified value (got <typeof>)' error; malformed evidence becomes its verbatim error; well-formed evidence is graded via gradeEvidence (only a 'fail' status emits — 'uncheckable' is accepted under the permissive policy). Emits the ORDERED outcome list ({ outcome = err, field, reason } / { outcome = prove, field, missingReason }); the TS delegate replays it in order, so the error list is byte-identical to the original single walk.

engine:spliceGo.label: Splice SetExpr bodies (go)
engine:spliceGo.description: spliceSetBodies' walk: on a `value` ident followed by `∈` (op) / `in` (keyword), drop leading body newlines, compute the body span (setBodySpan), cut the verbatim slice `slice src startOff endOff`, and emit `value`, the `∈`/`in` token, and the synthetic setbody token, then continue from the terminator; every other token passes through. Internal decl-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 4i.

engine:spliceSetBodies.label: Splice SetExpr bodies
engine:spliceSetBodies.description: The SetExpr refinement slice pre-pass (run on the lexer stream before layout): replace each `value ∈`/`value in` body with one `{t="setbody", v=<verbatim src slice>}` token, recovering the span the lexer shredded (the TS `parseSetForm` `src.slice` recovery). The decl-grammar's `value ∈ SETBODY` arm hands the verbatim slice to `dispatchedParseSetExpr` at the marshal — the canonical SetExpr parser the TS oracle also uses. `value ∈` occurs only in refinement set-forms (context-safe). parser-substrate Phase 4i.

engine:spliceToks.label: Splice hole tokens
engine:spliceToks.description: Filter a re-tokenized interpolation hole's tokens (drop `eof`/`nl`) and override each token's ln/col/off to the template's (`fenel-parser.ts:168`). The `off` override is the template's opening index (best-effort — hole tokens never feed the SetExpr splice). Internal lexer helper.

engine:splitCondInto.label: fork: split-cond
engine:splitCondInto.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 3 — LOSSLESSLY split a positive assumed condition Expr into { atoms, opaque }: walk the `and`-spine; an atomizing conjunct (eq/neq/not(eq)/lte/lt/gte/gt — via the theory-combine adders noAddEq/noAddNeq/noAddLte/noAddLt/noAddGteFlip/noAddGtFlip) extends atoms; every other conjunct is appended RAW to opaque (so the witness reconstruction is faithful — nothing dropped). Internal helper.

engine:splitCondList.label: fork: split-cond-list
engine:splitCondList.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 3 — fold splitCondInto over an `and`'s operand list, threading the { atoms, opaque } accumulator. Internal helper.

engine:splitDepthGo.label: Split depth (go)
engine:splitDepthGo.description: splitDepthZero's walk: thread `{ depth, cur, chunks }` — flush `cur` to `chunks` on a depth-0 `vsemi`, else accumulate the token (adjusting depth on vopen/vclose). Flushes the trailing chunk at end-of-input. Internal parse-file helper. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:splitDepthZero.label: Split at depth-zero vsemi
engine:splitDepthZero.description: Partition a decls token run into decl-LINE chunks at depth-0 `vsemi` boundaries: thread a bracket-block depth (`vopen` ⇒ +1, `vclose` ⇒ −1); a `vsemi` at depth 0 ends a chunk, a nested `vsemi` (depth ≥ 1 — multi-stmt body, multi-line `|`-variant) is kept. Empty chunks are dropped. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:splitNot.label: fork: split-not
engine:splitNot.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 3 — the `not` arm of splitCondInto: `not(eq x y)` ⇒ a neq atom (noAddNeq); any other negated head is preserved RAW in opaque (no De Morgan in v1). `e` is the whole `not(…)` Expr. Internal helper.

engine:splitTopLevelDecls.label: Split top-level declarations
engine:splitTopLevelDecls.description: Partition a whole-file layout token stream (`layoutTokens(lexAll src)`) into per-declaration GROUPS: detect + strip the module header / program framing, split the inner decls run at depth-0 `vsemi` into decl-LINES, and group leading `@directive` lines with the following real decl (vsemi-joined). Returns `{ headered, name, groups }` (name = "" header-less). The 6b2 budget fix — each group is a short token run (the fast curve). parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:splitVal.label: Split token value
engine:splitVal.description: Recover the in-band VALUE of an encoded token — the substring after the first SEP (Design E step 2). `splitVal "num\042" = "42"`. Leaf reductions call this to read the value class's payload. parser-substrate Phase 3b.

engine:ssApp.label: subset: ssApp
engine:ssApp.description: Phase 5 (E-app) / type-substrate P1(a.7) — the applied-type ($el.call ⇒ TtApp) arm of ssSameKind, split on the picker flag. PICKER mode is BYTE-IDENTICAL (same head ⇒ the pairwise args fold, else Just false — a presentation filter, not a truth claim). SOUND mode ABSTAINS in both polarities. TtApp.head is an ARBITRARY type-level function name, not a fixed ADT constructor, so `same head ⇒ covariant args` is an unchecked monotonicity premise over an OPEN head domain: a head whose result is antitone in its argument (anything producing `(a) -> Bool`, or a typeclass record such as `Eq a = Eq eq: a -> a -> Maybe Bool`) makes the positive conceptually FALSE, and neither live face can refute it because an unresolved VtEl accepts every value (validate.fenel:1551-1552) and matchesShape has no TtApp arm (decompose.fenel:82, `_ -> true`). The head-mismatch negative rides that same one-population fact. App reflexivity is a priced loss recoverable only by the deep-equality reflexivity twin. Internal helper.

engine:ssBRefined.label: subset: ssBRefined
engine:ssBRefined.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — have-not-refined/want-refined. Picker keeps the legacy predicate-forgetting recursion. Sound mode requires both complete operands to be plan/occurrence ready, then preserves the existing rule: a provably top predicate compares against the base; otherwise only a conservative base refutation survives.

engine:ssComposite.label: subset: ssComposite
engine:ssComposite.description: Phase 6 Step 2 — the composite-former arm of ssSameKind (record / arrow / map / tuple): picker mode returns constructor-level Just true (ssCompositePicker, byte-preserved from 2a); SOUND mode (Step 2b) is component-wise (ssCompositeSound — record width+depth, arrow variance, tuple pairwise, map value-subset). Internal helper to ssSameKind.

engine:ssCompositePicker.label: subset: ssCompositePicker
engine:ssCompositePicker.description: Phase 6 Step 2 — the PICKER-mode composite arm (FROZEN, byte-identical to the 2a behaviour the FunctionPicker oracle pins): record / arrow / map / tuple match at constructor level (Just true); anything else ⇒ Just false. Internal helper to ssComposite.

engine:ssCompositeSound.label: subset: ssCompositeSound
engine:ssCompositeSound.description: Phase 6 Step 2b / type-substrate P1(a.7) — the SOUND-mode composite arm. Record keeps the fully gated width+depth rule. Tuple is POSITIVE-ONLY: its arity and slot refutations carried a measured false definite (no have-nonemptiness gate, so a Void-factor tuple refuted while its denotation is empty at both the conceptual reading and the implemented decomposeMatchesTuple face) and its item axis bottoms out in accept-all/refuse-all degrades. Arrow and map ABSTAIN in both polarities: every arrow verdict is refuted at validation's non-circular paramCount axis and by the flatten/written-arity divergence, and ssMap's partial-dictionary key rule contradicts validationValidateMap's total-length finite arm. The unknown kind abstains; the trailing Just false is unreachable over the closed tsKind image and is kept as a receipt. Internal helper to ssComposite.

engine:ssMap.label: subset: ssMap
engine:ssMap.description: Phase 5 (S-mapkeys) / type-substrate P1(a.7) — the partial-dictionary map ⊆ rule: Map<K1,V1> ⊆ Map<K2,V2> iff K1 ⊆ K2 (decideSubset over the carried key SetExprs) AND V1 ⊆ V2 (covariant). UNREACHED from sound mode as of P1(a.7): its key rule contradicts validationValidateMap's total-length finite arm, which accepts a length-3 array only on the have side of Map[3,T] ⊆ Map[4,T], so the positive was face-false at an implemented arm. Retained registered as the anchor for the key-equality recovery slice. Internal helper, currently no caller.

engine:ssMaybeCongruent.label: subset: ssMaybeCongruent
engine:ssMaybeCongruent.description: Phase 6 Step 2 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — picker retains the inclusive legacy tsMaybeInner extraction and fall-through. Sound mode requires exact typeTraversalMaybeInner on both operands and retains only a recursive Just true; inner refutations/unknowns abstain because Maybe forwards non-tagged values.

engine:ssNamedArm.label: subset: ssNamedArm
engine:ssNamedArm.description: decide-substrate (Tt* named-leaf honesty) / type-substrate P1(a.6) — the named-leaf arm of ssSameKind, split on the picker flag. PICKER mode is BYTE-IDENTICAL (Just (namedSubsetCheck na nb) — the UX list-membership: a refutation means 'not in the picker', not a truth claim). SOUND mode is POSITIVE-ONLY: forward namedSubsetCheck na nb ⇒ Just true; else Nothing. P1(a.6) RETIRED the reversed-proper Just false: its own worked example was Number ⊆ Int, and the live faces do not implement that distinction — validationValidateNamed sends Number/Int/Nat to ONE validationValidateNumber (validate.fenel:1250-1251) which rejects only NaN, so 1.5 and -1 validate as Nat, and matchesShape's named leaf is accept-all (decompose.fenel:60). The three names denote ONE population at both live faces, so the refutation was a false definite; witnesses 1.5 / [1.5] lift it through List covariance and every gate-ready product. Among validationPrimitiveName names the reversed-proper pairs are EXACTLY the numeric triple, so no sound negative is lost. Nonprimitive names abstain too: an unresolved name refuses every value (validate.fenel:1258), making ⟦have⟧ = ∅ and the negative vacuously false, and resolved population is caller-registry-scoped while this judgment carries no validation-source context. This makes the Tt named arm shape-identical to its already-positive-only SetExpr sibling. Re-introducing a negative requires a live-face SEPARATION witness, not a hierarchy fact; the named-arm honesty pins enforce that. Internal helper to ssSameKind.

engine:ssNominalBridge.label: subset: ssNominalBridge
engine:ssNominalBridge.description: Phase 5 (E-named) — the named/opaque hierarchy bridge of subsetWKBase: when BOTH operands yield a nominal name (TtNamed or TtOpaque), is have's name a Subsumable subset of want's (namedSubsetCheck)? Reproduces isSubtype's `$named↔$named` hierarchy (Nat ⊆ Int) AND the `$named↔$opaque` bridge ({$named:"Nat"} ⊆ Nat-opaque). A POSITIVE-only gate: true ⇒ the caller short-circuits Just true; false ⇒ FALL THROUGH to the opaque peel (so Char-opaque ⊆ Nat-opaque, NOT a hierarchy fact, still decides via Char.pure's refinement-forget). Checked AFTER the refined arms, BEFORE the opaque peels. Internal helper.

engine:ssRefined.label: subset: ssRefined
engine:ssRefined.description: Phase 6 Step 2 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — picker retains the legacy predicate decision and base fallback. Sound refined/refined requires complete plan/occurrence readiness and returns Just true only when both baseHave subset baseWant and setHave subset setWant are explicitly Just true; every false or unknown coordinate becomes Nothing.

engine:ssRefinedHave.label: subset: ssRefinedHave
engine:ssRefinedHave.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — picker preserves the legacy opaque-reveal/base-forget expression. Sound mode first requires complete plan and occurrence readiness; a revealed refined want uses the positive-only two-coordinate rule, while base-forget keeps only a recursive Just true and drops every negative/unknown.

engine:ssResolve.label: subset: ssResolve
engine:ssResolve.description: Phase 5 (R-resolve) / type-substrate P1(a.5) — the kind-mismatch tail of subsetWKLeaf: picker mode ⇒ Just false (byte-identical; the picker does not resolve refs). The SUBSET half of the P1(a.5) repair is entirely below this split, but the DISJOINT half is NOT unreachable from picker mode — `subsetWK`'s want-side complement arm calls `ttDisjoint` with no picker flag. The picker is nevertheless unmoved because every cell that repair changed went `Just true` → `Nothing`, and typeSubsumes collapses `Nothing → true`; that is pinned, not assumed (type-substrate-p1a5-tt-object-carrier.test.ts, "the ONE un-picker-gated route into disjoint"). SOUND mode ⇒ resolveArm (resolve whichever side is a TtNamed registry alias and recurse on the referent, with a co-induction memo seeded empty; a genuine mismatch then reaches the ttSubsetSortRefute fence). Internal helper.

engine:ssRest.label: subset: ssRest
engine:ssRest.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the tail of a list, or [] when empty (tail Nothing → []). The recursion step for the component-wise walks. Internal helper.

engine:ssSameKind.label: subset: ssSameKind
engine:ssSameKind.description: Phase 6 Step 2 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — same-kind dispatch after former/refined/opaque routing. Named uses the picker/sound nominal split; variant uses the exact-Maybe/ordinary gate; generic mu recurses only in picker mode and abstains in sound mode; tagged recurses through its value carrier ONLY in picker mode and abstains in sound mode (P1(a.8), `t.sub.tagged`); record/arrow/map/tuple enter their picker or component-wise sound arms.

engine:ssSameKindTail.label: subset: ssSameKindTail
engine:ssSameKindTail.description: Phase 5 — the unit/app/composite tail of ssSameKind (split for the per-decl token cap): unit ⇒ Just true (E-unit); app ⇒ ssApp (E-app); else the composite-former arm (record/arrow/map/tuple). Internal helper.

engine:ssTagged.label: subset: ssTagged
engine:ssTagged.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — the `$tagged` arm of ssSameKind, split on the picker flag. PICKER mode is BYTE-IDENTICAL (it recurses through the value carrier exactly as before). SOUND mode emits NOTHING in both polarities. Ground — standing rule C, reading-invariance (design/deciding.md §9.1): the two live faces disagree about what a `$tagged` DENOTES. Validation elaborates every `$tagged` to `VtTagged` and checks UUID SYNTAX ONLY, never reading the value slot (validate.fenel:899, :1240, :1548), while `matchesShape` recurses INTO that slot (decompose.fenel:77). Under the erasure reading every `$tagged` type has the SAME population — the UUID strings — so a refutation between two of them is false; under the recursion reading the wrapper is transparent and the value verdict lifts. A definite whose truth depends on which reading you pick is not entitled. MEASURED contradiction at entry: `validate($tagged{value=$void}, <uuid>)` and `validate($tagged{value=record{_0:Number}}, <uuid>)` are BOTH VALID while this arm returned `Just false` between them, and the emptiness twin called the first EMPTY. A phantom-EQUALITY gate was measured OUT — every contradiction cell already has EQUAL phantoms. Priced: tagged reflexivity, the brand positive (`Id<Bot> ⊆ Id<User>` was `Just true`), and the record-width refutation; recovery rides the `sub.refl.deepeq` slice plus the deferred brand ruling. Ledger `t.sub.tagged`. Internal helper to ssSameKind.

engine:ssVar.label: subset: ssVar
engine:ssVar.description: Phase 6 Step 2 — the type-variable expected-slot arm of subsetW: picker mode accepts ANY have (Just true, the polymorphic-slot accept); SOUND mode ⇒ Nothing (a free type-var's denotation is unknown ⇒ undecidable). Internal helper to subsetW.

engine:ssVarArm.label: subset: ssVarArm
engine:ssVarArm.description: Phase 5 (E-void / E-var) — the want-is-var arm of subsetW: a same-named type-VAR on both sides ⇒ Just true (reflexivity — underpins $mu / List congruence where `tail:X ⊆ X`); else the generous/undecidable ssVar split. (The ∅ ⊆ anything void short-circuit precedes this in subsetW, so `void ⊆ var` is still Just true.) Internal helper.

engine:ssVariant.label: subset: ssVariant
engine:ssVariant.description: Phase 6 Step 2 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — picker preserves the legacy Maybe-shaped congruence/constructor accept expression. Sound mode uses exact typeTraversalMaybeInner on both operands: exact/exact keeps only positive inner congruence after the full gate; exact-have/ordinary-want may emit the plan-ready null refutation; ordinary-have/exact-want abstains; ordinary/ordinary uses the unique/default-discriminator keyed-payload gate before variantSub.

engine:stepGrammar.label: Step grammar
engine:stepGrammar.description: One strict whole-grammar derivative step at suffix `k`, computing the OLD env's fixpoints fresh then delegating to `stepGrammarWith`. The back-compat entry (the lexer's ref-free empty-env driver + the env-growth oracle call it; the grammar path uses the threaded `runSteps`). parser-substrate Phase 1.

engine:stepGrammarWith.label: Step grammar with
engine:stepGrammarWith.description: The core strict whole-grammar derivative step at suffix `k`, taking the OLD env's PRECOMPUTED nullability (`na`) + parseNull (`pa`) fixpoints (so the caller can thread them incrementally across steps — the 6b cache). Derive the root + every reachable production w.r.t. `t` in one finite pass into bounded `base@birth` siblings (refs bump to the derived siblings; kept tails retain their fresh refs — so left/mutual recursion terminate AND re-enter fresh productions). The new env = `newSibs` ++ (the old env MINUS any row a newSib supersedes). DEDUP-BY-NAME, newSibs-first (7h): under bounded naming a re-derived `base@birth` shares its name with its prior-step row, so the naive `concat newSibs g` would carry BOTH (the fresh + the one-step-stale) and re-leak `|g|` — `findEntry`/`bodyOf` would still pick the fresh (first) one, but the stale copy bloats every per-step scan. Dropping ONLY the colliding old rows (those whose name is a newSib name) is correct AND complete: newSibs holds the freshest derivative of every reachable production, while the NON-colliding old rows (the originals the kept tails re-enter, PLUS any prior-step derivative NOT re-derived this step but still referenced by a kept tail — e.g. a multi-argument application's later-argument re-entry) MUST be carried forward (an earlier 7h draft that kept only the non-`@` originals dropped exactly those tails and lost a trailing call argument). With cumulative (pre-7h) names no row ever collided, so this is a no-op there — i.e. semantically identical to the old `concat newSibs g`, plus the bounded-name dedup. Then keep the rows still reachable from the new root, prune the rest. 7h S2 (env-lookup de-superlinearization): the OLD env's `na`/`pa` fixpoints arrive as the threaded assoc-lists and are indexed ONCE here (`naIdx`/`paIdx`, O(1) `mapGet`) for the whole step; the two row prunes (`combined`'s drop-superseded + `g2`'s keep-reachable) use name→True SETS (`newNamesSet`/`keepSet`) for O(1) membership instead of the prior O(|g|) `elem` scans — so the per-step cost drops from O(|g|²) to ~O(|g|) and the corpus curve from cubic toward quadratic. Returns `{ g, root }`. parser-substrate Phase 1 / 6b / 7h. Internal helper.

engine:stepLayout.label: Step layout
engine:stepLayout.description: Process one real token through the layout state: open a context (when armed + not suspended), or cascade-close/`vsemi` on a new line (when not suspended), then emit the token and recompute the arm/bracket state. Returns `{ stack, out, pendingOpen }`. Internal layout helper.

engine:stringMember.label: universe-views: stringMember
engine:stringMember.description: structural-dispatch Phase 3 — true when a string is equal (std `eq`) to some element of a string list. Internal helper for effectfulFunctionsWith's membership fold.

engine:stringWidgetFor.label: widget-hint: stringWidgetFor
engine:stringWidgetFor.description: Phase 3b-3d — pick the UI widget for a string-typed SetExpr. Enum -> radio(≤5)/dropdown(≤20)/searchable-select by count; named format:email/url/phone/uuid -> email/url/phone/text(monospace) inputs; SePattern -> pattern-constrained text-input (regex via rxhPatternToRegex∘rxhReadPat, the 3b-3c serialiser); else text-input. Returns a WidgetHint. The `!set` unconstrained-string case is handled by the TS wrapper. Dual-reads the $tag SePattern then the legacy $-key. Mirrors widget-hint.ts:stringWidgetFor.

engine:subCapArms.label: solve: subCapArms
engine:subCapArms.description: Phase 5 — apply substituteCaptures over EMatch arm bodies, passing each arm's pattern through untouched. Internal helper.

engine:subCapFields.label: solve: subCapFields
engine:subCapFields.description: Phase 5 — apply substituteCaptures over ERecord field values, preserving each field name. Internal helper.

engine:subCapList.label: solve: subCapList
engine:subCapList.description: Phase 5 — apply substituteCaptures over an Expr list (ECall.args / EConstruct.args), threading the accumulator. Internal helper.

engine:subExpr.label: Sub expr
engine:subExpr.description: Substitute each `EVar n` whose name is a rule param with the corresponding argument `Expr` (rule unfolding); all other nodes recurse structurally. The Expr-valued sibling of substituteCaptures (which substitutes VALUES as ELit) — mirrors its 7-case coverage including the EConstruct dual (with/without fields) arms. Internal helper.

engine:subExprArms.label: Sub expr (arms)
engine:subExprArms.description: subExpr over EMatch arm bodies, passing each pattern through untouched. Internal helper.

engine:subExprFields.label: Sub expr (fields)
engine:subExprFields.description: subExpr over ERecord field values, preserving each field name. Internal helper.

engine:subExprList.label: Sub expr (list)
engine:subExprList.description: subExpr over an Expr list (ECall.args / EConstruct.args), threading the accumulator. Internal helper.

engine:subFieldDefs.label: field-meta: subFieldDefs
engine:subFieldDefs.description: Phase 10c sub-step 1 — peel composite FenelType into sub-FieldDefs. The TS wrapper pre-classifies f.type into SfdInput (SfdRecord fields / SfdList elemType / SfdMaybe valueType / SfdNone) using dispatchedPeelList + dispatchedPeelMaybe (already Fenel-bodied per Phase 7c sub-step 1+2). The body dispatches: SfdRecord passes the original untagged FieldDef records through opaquely; SfdList/SfdMaybe synthesize a singleton FldField list with canonical "item"/"value" name+label. The wrapper leaves passthrough records unchanged and unmarshalls only synthesized FldField values. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedSubFieldDefs`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/field-meta.ts:subFieldDefs.

engine:subLookup.label: Sub lookup
engine:subLookup.description: Find a rule-param name in the subs env (a list of { name, expr } records); Just expr / Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:subset.label: Subset of types
engine:subset.description: set-algebra-to-fenel Phase 6 (containment capstone) Step 2 — `subset have want` decides whether ⟦have⟧ ⊆ ⟦want⟧ (every inhabitant of `have` is an inhabitant of `want`), returning Tri (Maybe Bool). The SOUND member of the containment relation — sound MODULO the TCB ledger's open rows (`t.top.opaque` is reachable from here) — = subsetW False: a type-variable expected slot ⇒ Nothing (undecidable); refined leaves surface set:decideSubset's Tri directly; refined/opaque layers transparent; named ⇒ nominal eq; Maybe ⇒ inner congruence; composite formers component-wise (Step 2b). The precise sibling of the picker-view engine:typeSubsumes (which is collapse(subsetW True)).

engine:subsetB.label: Subset of types (Bool)
engine:subsetB.description: Phase 6 Step 2 — the Bool-collapsed boundary helper over subset (Nothing → false), for callers that need a clean Bool rather than a Tri (the isSubsetB / decideSubsetB precedent, C-1). subsetB have want = mGet (subset have want) false.

engine:subsetFold.label: Subset fold
engine:subsetFold.description: Fold the satisfiable atoms of a subset state: skip atoms where a derives empty; recurse on (da, db); short-circuit false; thread visited. Internal helper.

engine:subsetFoldS.label: Subset fold (structured)
engine:subsetFoldS.description: Fold the partition representatives of a structured subset state: skip representatives where a derives empty; recurse on (da, db); short-circuit false; thread visited. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:subsetGo.label: Subset go
engine:subsetGo.description: One coinductive step of the subset walk over (pa, pb), threading the visited memo. Memo cycle => true; nullable a and not nullable b => false; no preds => true; over 16 preds => conservative false; else fold the satisfiable atoms. Internal helper.

engine:subsetGoS.label: Subset go (structured)
engine:subsetGoS.description: One coinductive step of the structured subset walk over (pa, pb), threading the visited memo. Memo cycle ⇒ true; nullable a and not nullable b ⇒ false; no preds ⇒ true; else derive under each partition representative. Internal helper (structured partition).

engine:subsetIntersectHave.label: subset: subsetIntersectHave
engine:subsetIntersectHave.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — LHS intersect ⊆: (A ∩ B) ⊆ want when SOME branch ⊆ want (∃; A∩B ⊆ A, so a branch ⊆ want proves the whole). Just true if any branch proves, else Nothing. Internal helper to subsetWK.

engine:subsetIntersectWant.label: subset: subsetIntersectWant
engine:subsetIntersectWant.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — RHS intersect ⊆: have ⊆ (A ∩ B) iff have ⊆ EVERY branch (∀; mAnd-fold of subsetW). Sound AND complete. An empty branch list ⇒ Just true (∩∅ = ⊤). Internal helper to subsetWK.

engine:subsetOfK.label: Subset-of key
engine:subsetOfK.description: Is the predicate keyed `i` a proven subset of the one keyed `j` (pre-computed TS-side via isSubset)? Reads the name->info index. Internal helper.

engine:subsetUnionHave.label: subset: subsetUnionHave
engine:subsetUnionHave.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — LHS union ⊆: (A ∪ B) ⊆ want iff EVERY branch ⊆ want (mAnd-fold of subsetW over the union branches). Sound AND complete. An empty branch list ⇒ Just true (∪∅ = ∅ ⊆ anything). Internal helper to subsetWK.

engine:subsetUnionWant.label: subset: subsetUnionWant
engine:subsetUnionWant.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — RHS union ⊆: have ⊆ (A ∪ B) when have ⊆ SOME branch (∃). Just true if any branch positively proves, else Nothing (a non-match does NOT refute — have may split across branches). emTrueOnly drops each branch's Just false; mOr-fold keeps the positive. Internal helper to subsetWK.

engine:subsetW.label: Subset (⊆) — parameterized core
engine:subsetW.description: set-algebra-to-fenel Phase 6 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — parameterized structural subset. Picker mode preserves the legacy permissive List peel, bottom-mu shortcut, refined fall-through, and constructor-level composite choices. Sound mode preserves Void, fences bottom/non-live mu, routes top-level Boolean/refined formers first, then classifies each operand as LiveList, FaceBlocked, or NotList; only two ready LiveLists recurse covariantly. Remaining sound forms dispatch through subsetWV and the gated same-kind rules.

engine:subsetWK.label: subset: ssKinds
engine:subsetWK.description: Phase 6 Step 2 / type-substrate P1(a.5)+P1(a.6) — kind dispatch after the var/List prelude. Boolean formers route first; refined and opaque handling lives below; equal residual kinds enter ssSameKind; a genuine unresolved kind mismatch reaches ttSubsetSortRefute, which currently abstains unconditionally.

engine:subsetWKBase.label: subset: ssKindsBase
engine:subsetWKBase.description: Phase 6 Step 2 / Phase 2 Step 1b / type-substrate P1(a.5) — the leaf-cascade tail of subsetWK (after the tier-2 former arms): refined/refined ⇒ ssRefined; mixed refined ⇒ strip + recurse; opaque layers transparent; same non-refined/non-opaque kind ⇒ ssSameKind; kind mismatch ⇒ the ttSubsetSortRefute tail, not a blanket Just false. Split out so subsetWK's tier-2 chain stays single-line. Internal helper.

engine:subsetWKLeaf.label: subset: ssKindsLeaf
engine:subsetWKLeaf.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.5) — the leaf tail of subsetWKBase (split for the per-decl token cap): the named/opaque nominal-name bridge (ssNominalBridge ⇒ Just true) FIRST, then the opaque peels (have/want), then same-kind congruence (ssSameKind), else the kind-mismatch tail ssResolve (which refutes only on a proven host-carrier partition; it no longer refutes on kind difference alone). Internal helper.

engine:subsetWL.label: subset: subsetWL
engine:subsetWL.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — PICKER-only legacy List fast path, preserved textually: permissively peel both operands and recurse covariantly when both peel; otherwise fall through to subsetWV. Sound mode uses the separate exact three-outcome classifier.

engine:subsetWLW.label: subset: subsetWLW
engine:subsetWLW.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — picker-only want-side of the preserved permissive List peel: with a peeled have element, recurse when want also peels; otherwise fall through to subsetWV.

engine:subsetWV.label: subset: subsetWV
engine:subsetWV.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — the var/kind tail after picker List peeling or sound List classification: a type-variable expected slot enters ssVarArm; otherwise dispatch by kind through subsetWK.

engine:substArrowParam.label: set-algebra: substArrowParam
engine:substArrowParam.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.1 — substSet through one SetArrowParam (rebuild with the substituted set). Internal helper to substSet's SeArrow arm.

engine:substMuArm.label: set-algebra: substMuArm
engine:substMuArm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8μ.1b — substSet's SeMu arm: same-var ⇒ SHADOWED (return unchanged — the inner binder rebinds v); colliding binder (w occurs among t's handles) ⇒ freshen w to a primed w', α-rename the inner body (substSet w (SeRef w') b — capture-free since w' is fresh against t, b and v), then continue substituting v; else plain descent. Internal helper.

engine:substSet.label: set-algebra: substSet
engine:substSet.description: decide-substrate Phase 8μ.1b — the ONE new μ algebra op (design/mu-induction.md §3.1): replace every FREE `SeRef {handle=v}` in `body` with `t`. Capture-avoiding: an inner same-var SeMu SHADOWS (descent stops); an inner binder colliding with a handle of `t` is FRESHENED (α-rename to a primed name) before descent. Leaves (SeAll/SeNone/SeEnum/SeInterval/SePattern/SeWhere/non-matching SeRef) unchanged — SePattern is NOT rewritten (seMuSupported fences bodies whose var hides in a pattern). Structural recursion elsewhere (SeCtor fields / SeUnion / SeIntersect / SeDiff / SeComplement / SeMu).

engine:substSetField.label: set-algebra: substSetField
engine:substSetField.description: decide-substrate Phase 8μ.1b — substSet through one SetCtorField (rebuild with the substituted set). Internal helper to substSet's SeCtor arm.

engine:substVarCases.label: type-algebra: substVarCases
engine:substVarCases.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — substituteVar over each variant case's field list, returning one (List StOut) per case (order-preserving). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:substVarCasesAcc.label: type-algebra: substVarCasesAcc
engine:substVarCasesAcc.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — accumulator walk for substVarCases. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:substVarFields.label: type-algebra: substVarFields
engine:substVarFields.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — substituteVar over each record/case field's `type`, returning one StOut per field (order-preserving). Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:substVarFieldsAcc.label: type-algebra: substVarFieldsAcc
engine:substVarFieldsAcc.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — accumulator walk for substVarFields. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:substVarList.label: type-algebra: substVarList
engine:substVarList.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — substituteVar over a marshalled-type list (tuple items / `$el.call` args), order-preserving. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:substVarListAcc.label: type-algebra: substVarListAcc
engine:substVarListAcc.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — accumulator walk for substVarList. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:substituteCaptures.label: Substitute captures
engine:substituteCaptures.description: Inline a closure's captured values into its `Expr` body: every `EVar n` whose name is in the captures env becomes `ELit <captured value>`; all other nodes recurse structurally. Capture values are NOT recursed (the 3a rule). Turns `y = 5; \x -> x == y` into the closed `\x -> x == 5` so solve can witness it — the reify payoff. expr-substrate Phase 5.

engine:substituteVar.label: type-algebra: substituteVar
engine:substituteVar.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — one-step μ-substitution `B[var := replacement]` over the marshalled TraversalType, emitting a StOut marker isomorphic to the input (the TS unmarshal patches it against the raw, preserving metadata). The SOURCE OF TRUTH for set-algebra.ts:substituteVar (a ledgered performance branch). Stops at a shadowing `$mu`; no arm for $arrow/$union/$intersect/$complement/$type (legacy returns them unchanged = StKeep); $refined.set / $map.keys ride raw. Dispatched via dispatchedSubstituteVar / dispatchedUnfold. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:summarizeFieldReuseOccurrences.label: Summarize field reuse occurrences
engine:summarizeFieldReuseOccurrences.description: Deduplicate owner names and occurrence types for one durable Field. Type equivalence is structural and record-key-order independent through eufValEq; the host only marshals occurrence facts.

engine:surfaceBuiltinTypeViews.label: surface: built-in type views
engine:surfaceBuiltinTypeViews.description: Fenel-authored built-in TypeView list consumed by TypeScript's template registry adapter and by the Phase 10 planner as ordinary input views.

engine:surfaceColumn.label: surface: list column
engine:surfaceColumn.description: Construct a table ListColumn with field path and label.

engine:surfaceConditionContext.label: surface: conditionContext
engine:surfaceConditionContext.description: Fenel-native runtime condition context merge for layout predicates. Adds _mode and _channel to the caller-supplied value record.

engine:surfaceConditionScopeForType.label: surface: conditionScopeForType
engine:surfaceConditionScopeForType.description: Fenel-native condition scope planner for TypeView/Layout predicates. Exposes candidate field paths plus the surface-provided _mode and _channel variables.

engine:surfaceDefaultLayoutForType.label: surface: defaultLayoutForType
engine:surfaceDefaultLayoutForType.description: Fenel-native default detail/edit layout planner. Groups top-level field candidates into two-slot rows and sizes structural fields full-width while scalar fields get compact spans.

engine:surfaceDefaultListDisplayForType.label: surface: defaultListDisplayForType
engine:surfaceDefaultListDisplayForType.description: Fenel-native default list-display planner. Uses up to six top-level field candidates as table columns, falling back to stack when no columns exist.

engine:surfaceDefaultTemplateName.label: surface: default template name
engine:surfaceDefaultTemplateName.description: Fenel-owned schema-type default selection. Conditional rules are checked in order, then the fallback default is used.

engine:surfaceEditDisplay.label: surface: edit display
engine:surfaceEditDisplay.description: Construct a canonical EditDisplay record from explicit Maybe slots.

engine:surfaceEmptyEditDisplay.label: surface: empty edit display
engine:surfaceEmptyEditDisplay.description: EditDisplay with every canonical Maybe slot set to Nothing.

engine:surfaceEmptyReadDisplay.label: surface: empty read display
engine:surfaceEmptyReadDisplay.description: ReadDisplay with every canonical Maybe slot set to Nothing.

engine:surfaceFieldCandidates.label: surface: fieldCandidates
engine:surfaceFieldCandidates.description: Fenel-native specialized-surface field candidate discovery. Walks a marshalled SurfaceType, peeling Maybe/refined/opaque/list/record shapes, returning typed field paths plus source/depth metadata. TS supplies resolver IO and raw FieldDef payloads only.

engine:surfaceInventoryCardView.label: surface: inventory card view
engine:surfaceInventoryCardView.description: Fenel-authored inventory card list TypeView. Solid resolves the inventory-card component name.

engine:surfaceLayoutRenderPlan.label: surface: layout render plan
engine:surfaceLayoutRenderPlan.description: Fenel-owned layout render-plan interpretation. Consumes layout/field/value wires whose predicates and templates have already been marshalled at the boundary, then returns the visible section/row/slot plan with field/template/component/display fallback tags.

engine:surfaceListDisplayRenderPlan.label: surface: list display render plan
engine:surfaceListDisplayRenderPlan.description: Fenel-owned list-display render-plan interpretation for the table/list vertical slice. Solid keeps DataTable, routing, and inline-edit handlers; Fenel decides column inclusion, template/component names, and scalar-vs-read-display fallback tags.

engine:surfaceMaybeString.label: surface: maybe string
engine:surfaceMaybeString.description: Normalize empty strings to Nothing for surface helper call-sites that accept optional strings.

engine:surfaceMergeDisplay.label: surface: merge display
engine:surfaceMergeDisplay.description: Fenel-owned right-biased Maybe-aware TypeView display merge. Merges read/edit facets with the same child-Just / parent-fallback semantics as the inner displays.

engine:surfaceMergeEdit.label: surface: merge edit display
engine:surfaceMergeEdit.description: Fenel-owned right-biased Maybe-aware EditDisplay merge. Child Just slots win, child Nothing falls through to parent, both absent yields Nothing.

engine:surfaceMergeRead.label: surface: merge read display
engine:surfaceMergeRead.description: Fenel-owned right-biased Maybe-aware ReadDisplay merge. Child Just slots win, child Nothing falls through to parent, both absent yields Nothing.

engine:surfacePlanForType.label: surface: planForType
engine:surfacePlanForType.description: Fenel-native specialized-surface planner. Owns TypeView cascade, view facet matching, default layout/list fallback, component-name selection, field candidates, and condition scope. TS supplies available views and override names as explicit IO leaves.

engine:surfaceProfileCardView.label: surface: profile card view
engine:surfaceProfileCardView.description: Fenel-authored profile card list TypeView. Solid resolves the profile-card component name.

engine:surfaceReadDisplay.label: surface: read display
engine:surfaceReadDisplay.description: Construct a canonical ReadDisplay record from explicit Maybe slots.

engine:surfaceReadValuePlan.label: surface: read value plan
engine:surfaceReadValuePlan.description: Fenel-owned read-display projection. Applies empty text, label/color maps, deterministic text transforms, prefix/suffix stitching, display kind classification, and host-format tags. TS supplies scalar value marshalling and browser-only date/relative-time rendering remains a leaf.

engine:surfaceResolveDefaultTemplate.label: surface: resolve default template
engine:surfaceResolveDefaultTemplate.description: Fenel-owned default/rule template resolver. Selects the default template name for a schema type and resolves TypeView inheritance before returning it.

engine:surfaceResolveTypeView.label: surface: resolve TypeView
engine:surfaceResolveTypeView.description: Fenel-owned TypeView inheritance resolver. Resolves an extends chain with a cycle guard and applies the registry display/facet merge semantics.

engine:surfaceSlot.label: surface: layout slot
engine:surfaceSlot.description: Construct a LayoutDef slot for one field path and grid span.

engine:surfaceTargetTypeOptions.label: surface: targetTypeOptions
engine:surfaceTargetTypeOptions.description: Fenel-native target-type option classification for the view editor. Dedupes catalog entries and maps catalog categories to surface option groups.

engine:surfaceTypeRef.label: surface: type ref
engine:surfaceTypeRef.description: Build a FenelType name reference for TypeView.targetType. Uses mapSet because Fenel record literals cannot author $-prefixed keys.

engine:surfaceTypeViewsForSurface.label: surface: typeViewsForSurface
engine:surfaceTypeViewsForSurface.description: Fenel-native TypeView facet matching for a target type and surface mode. Returns the raw TypeView rows whose target/facet applies.

engine:svDiff.label: search: svDiff
engine:svDiff.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — search a SeDiff a b as a ∩ ¬b: the generator is `a`, the single filter is `SeComplement b` (a positive contains-check of ¬b IS the negative filter of b — contains(¬b, w) = Just true iff contains(b, w) = Just false). Reuses svIntersectGen — no second composite-witness engine. Internal helper.

engine:svIntersect.label: search: svIntersect
engine:svIntersect.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — search a SeIntersect: partition the branches into the FIRST generator-capable branch (SeEnum / SeInterval / nested SeUnion|SeIntersect) and the rest-as-filters (partitionGen); then svIntersectGen. No generator-capable branch ⇒ SvUnknown "no-generator". Internal helper.

engine:svIntersectGen.label: search: svIntersectGen
engine:svIntersectGen.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — the shared generator+filters engine (fed by both svIntersect and svDiff): materialize the generator's candidate set (seCandidates — with an `exact` flag: a COMPLETE enumeration vs an inexact endpoint/search sample), then scan candidates against the filters (scanCandidates). A generator that produces no candidate set ⇒ SvUnknown "generator-failed". Internal helper.

engine:svLeaf.label: search: svLeaf
engine:svLeaf.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — search a leaf Se* shape (SeEnum / SeInterval / SeAll / SeNone / SeRef / SePattern / SeWhere): `inhabit s` Just w ⇒ SvFound w (the per-shape witness face — first enum value / inclusive interval endpoint); Nothing ⇒ setAlgebraDecideEmptyCore s Just true ⇒ SvEmpty (SeNone, an empty SeEnum), else SvUnknown (SeAll / a both-exclusive interval / out-of-fragment SeRef/SePattern/SeWhere). Calls the connective-algebra CORE, not the widened public decideEmpty — the Phase 4T D′ cycle-break. Internal helper.

engine:svToMaybe.label: search: svToMaybe
engine:svToMaybe.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — project a SearchVerdict onto the `Maybe witness` the inhabit faces return: SvFound w ⇒ Just w; SvEmpty / SvUnknown ⇒ Nothing (both are 'no witness produced'). The adapter the Step-B composite witness faces use (svToMaybe ∘ searchDefault). Internal helper.

engine:svUnion.label: search: svUnion
engine:svUnion.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — search a SeUnion: explore branches in order (svUnionLoop). Each branch is PRUNED first (setAlgebraDecideEmptyCore Just true ⇒ skip — backtrack-as-emptiness; the CORE, not the widened public entry — the Phase 4T D′ cycle-break), else recursed. First SvFound wins; all branches empty/pruned ⇒ SvEmpty; any SvUnknown among the non-Found ⇒ SvUnknown (the honest bar). Internal helper.

engine:svUnionDone.label: search: svUnionDone
engine:svUnionDone.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — the union terminal: sawUnknown ⇒ SvUnknown "union-exhausted" (an undecided branch withheld SvEmpty — the honest bar); else SvEmpty "union-all-empty" (every branch was decidably empty). Internal helper.

engine:svUnionLoop.label: search: svUnionLoop
engine:svUnionLoop.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — the ordered union scan: for each branch, prune (setAlgebraDecideEmptyCore Just true ⇒ skip — the D′ cycle-break) else `searchCore base (fuel-1)`; SvFound ⇒ return; SvEmpty/pruned ⇒ continue; SvUnknown ⇒ continue with the sawUnknown bit set. End: sawUnknown ⇒ SvUnknown, else SvEmpty (every branch decidably empty). Internal helper.

engine:svUnionNext.label: search: svUnionNext
engine:svUnionNext.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — advance the union scan to the tail (svUnionLoop) or finish (svUnionDone) when empty. Internal helper.

engine:swcFields.label: inhabit: swcFields
engine:swcFields.description: decide-substrate Phase 8μ.1b — the seWitnessCtor field fold: witness each field's set via inhabit and mapSet it onto the accumulating record; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:swmKleene.label: inhabit: swmKleene
engine:swmKleene.description: decide-substrate Phase 8μ.1b — the Kleene loop of seWitnessMu: next = substSet v cur F; size-guard (seSize > 512 ⇒ Nothing); inhabit next — Just w ⇒ Just w, Nothing ⇒ recurse with next and fuel−1; fuel exhausted ⇒ Nothing (never a false accept). Internal helper.

engine:symAllSitesParseable.label: symbolize: allSitesParseable
engine:symAllSitesParseable.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — true when every collected effect site is a parseable `$effect:` sentinel (hasClass). A non-parseable site is unattributable to a class ⇒ a possible write to any store ⇒ the global precondition that DISABLES value-numbering (per-site fallback for all). Internal helper.

engine:symAllSitesScopedReads.label: symbolize: allSitesScopedReads
engine:symAllSitesScopedReads.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the lawful-gate predicate: true iff EVERY collected effect site is a parseable declared read (hasClass ∧ class ∈ spec ∧ method ∈ reads class) — i.e. no writes, no unknown/unattributable classes anywhere. Internal helper.

engine:symBuildGroups.label: symbolize: buildGroups
engine:symBuildGroups.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the value-number group table: scan the sites in order; each mint-eligible site whose (class, method, argTerms) is new gets a fresh sequential index. Same-key reads collapse to one group ⇒ one shared unknown. Internal helper.

engine:symBuildGroupsAcc.label: symbolize: buildGroupsAcc
engine:symBuildGroupsAcc.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the accumulator loop behind symBuildGroups: for each remaining site, append a new group { typeName, methodName, argTerms, ix = length acc } when it is mint-eligible and not already grouped. Internal helper.

engine:symClassInScope.label: symbolize: classInScope
engine:symClassInScope.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — true when the effect class has a Symbolic instance in the spec. Internal helper.

engine:symCollectArms.label: symbolize: collectArms
engine:symCollectArms.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — concat symCollectSites over EMatch arm BODIES (patterns carry no effect sites the mint touches). Internal helper.

engine:symCollectFieldVals.label: symbolize: collectFieldVals
engine:symCollectFieldVals.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — concat symCollectSites over ERecord field VALUES. Internal helper.

engine:symCollectList.label: symbolize: collectList
engine:symCollectList.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — concat symCollectSites over an Expr-child list (ECall/EConstruct args). Internal helper.

engine:symCollectSites.label: symbolize: collectSites
engine:symCollectSites.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — collect every effect-call site in an `Expr` (as symSiteOf records), traversing structurally in EXACT mirror of symbolizeAt (ECall effect ⇒ a site else recurse args; ELambda body; EMatch scrutinee+arm-bodies; EConstruct args; ERecord field-values; EVar/ELit ⇒ none). The memory-model gate's site-set. Internal helper.

engine:symFindGroup.label: symbolize: findGroup
engine:symFindGroup.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the group (Just { typeName, methodName, argTerms, ix }) whose typeName+methodName match and whose argTerms are eufValEq-equal (term identity, NOT JS-loose eq), or Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:symIsRead.label: symbolize: isRead
engine:symIsRead.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — true when methodName is a declared observationally-pure read of typeName under the spec (method ∈ reads typeName; false when the class is not in scope). Internal helper.

engine:symMintSite.label: symbolize: mintSite
engine:symMintSite.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — mint one effect site: if the site is mint-eligible (memory-model gate) AND its (class, method, argTerms) resolves to a value-number group, emit the shared `EVar (symSharedName …)`; else fall back to the 14a per-site `EVar (effectSiteName fnId path)`. Internal helper.

engine:symMintTable.label: symbolize: mintTable
engine:symMintTable.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — project the value-number groups to a mint table `List { varName, typeName, methodName, argTerms }` (varName ⇒ the read it stands for; `var` is a reserved keyword) — the future fork-driver + Nelson-Oppen currency (plain records, no entity). Internal helper.

engine:symNoWriteForClass.label: symbolize: noWriteForClass
engine:symNoWriteForClass.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — true when NO site of the given class is a write, i.e. every site whose typeName matches has method ∈ reads (the per-class no-write half of the memory model). Internal helper.

engine:symReadsOf.label: symbolize: readsOf
engine:symReadsOf.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the `reads` roster for an effect class in the Symbolic spec (List { effectClass, reads }), or [] when the class is not in scope. Internal helper.

engine:symSharedName.label: symbolize: sharedName
engine:symSharedName.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the value-numbered var name `?sym:<class>:<method>:<groupIndex>`. Dot-free (the collectFreeVars field-access constraint); the group index is the only stringified number (never an arg value — eufValEq grouping + the opaque-Number toString landmine). Internal helper.

engine:symSiteMintable.label: symbolize: siteMintable
engine:symSiteMintable.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — whether a single site may be value-numbered: the global no-unattributable-site precondition (parseable) AND the site is a parseable read of a Symbolic-in-scope class AND that class is write-free over the whole tree. A failing site falls back to the 14a per-site name (always sound). Internal helper.

engine:symSiteOf.label: symbolize: siteOf
engine:symSiteOf.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — decompose an effect-call site into { fnId, typeName, methodName, argTerms, hasClass }: parseEffectFnId gives (typeName, methodName) with hasClass=true for a `$effect:<Class>:<method>` sentinel; a non-sentinel fnId (matched only via the effectFnIds set) gets typeName/methodName "" + hasClass=false (unattributable ⇒ never value-numbered). Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeArms.label: symbolize: symbolizeArms
engine:symbolizeArms.description: Phase 14a — recurse symbolizeAt over EMatch arm bodies with `/arm/<idx>` structural paths, preserving each arm's pattern (the body is the only sub-expression walked; the arm guard is dropped, mirroring substituteCaptures' subCapArms). Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeAt.label: symbolize: symbolizeAt
engine:symbolizeAt.description: Phase 14a — the path-threaded recursive walker behind symbolizeEffects. At an effect-call site (fnId in effectFnIds OR `$effect:`-marked) emit `EVar (effectSiteName fnId path)`; else recurse structurally (ECall.args / ELambda.body / EMatch.scrutinee+arms / EConstruct.args / ERecord.fields), threading the `/`-separated structural path; ELit/EVar pass through. Mirrors substituteCaptures' structural descent (arm guard dropped, same as the sibling). Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeEffects.label: Symbolize effects
engine:symbolizeEffects.description: Walk an `Expr` and rewrite every effect-call site into a fresh site-named `EVar` — turning an 'IO read' into just-another-unknown the existing solver can witness WITHOUT performing the IO. An `ECall fnId` is an effect site iff `fnId` is in the supplied `effectFnIds` set OR `parseEffectFnId fnId` is Just (the `$effect:` sentinel). The fresh var's name derives deterministically from the effect fnId + the structural path (distinct sites ⇒ distinct names ⇒ no gensym counter); the name is DOT-FREE (`/` path separators, `@` join) since a `.` would be parsed as field access by `collectFreeVars`. Everything else recurses structurally (ECall.args / ELambda.body / EMatch.scrutinee+arms / EConstruct.args / ERecord.fields); ELit/EVar pass through. Pure `Expr -> Expr` — no IO, no native, no new Expr case. The composed `solveSymbolic`/`solveFnSymbolic` feed its output to solve. expr-substrate Phase 14a.

engine:symbolizeFields.label: symbolize: symbolizeFields
engine:symbolizeFields.description: Phase 14a — recurse symbolizeAt over ERecord field values with `/<fieldname>` structural paths, preserving each field name. Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeList.label: symbolize: symbolizeList
engine:symbolizeList.description: Phase 14a — recurse symbolizeAt over a list of Expr children with `/`-indexed structural paths (`<basePath>/<idx>`), threading the accumulator. Used for ECall.args and EConstruct.args. Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeShared.label: Symbolize shared
engine:symbolizeShared.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the VALUE-NUMBERED symbolic mint: rewrite effect-call sites to fresh `EVar`s, but same-KEY reads (same class+method+eufValEq-equal args) of a write-free Symbolic-in-scope class SHARE ONE unknown — turning `(read k) == 42 ∧ (read k) > 40` from solve's two-var fence (Nothing) into a single-unknown enum∩interval witness (Just 42). The memory model v1 (whole-tree no-write gate) makes the sharing sound. Sites failing the gate (a write present anywhere / method ∉ reads / class not Symbolic / unattributable site) fall back to the per-site 14a `effectSiteName` (always sound). `spec` = List { effectClass, reads }, resolved from the scoped `Symbolic` instances at the marshal boundary. Pure `Expr -> Expr`; composes AFTER the PE.

engine:symbolizeSharedArms.label: symbolize: symbolizeSharedArms
engine:symbolizeSharedArms.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — recurse symbolizeSharedAt over EMatch arm bodies with `/arm/<idx>` paths, preserving patterns; threads the mint context. Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeSharedAt.label: symbolize: symbolizeSharedAt
engine:symbolizeSharedAt.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the path-threaded value-numbered walker (mirrors symbolizeAt): at an effect site mint via symMintSite (shared var if grouped, else per-site fallback); else recurse structurally threading the `/`-separated path. Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeSharedDetailed.label: Symbolize shared detailed
engine:symbolizeSharedDetailed.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — the detailed value-numbered mint over an (already-PE'd, lifted) residual `Expr`: returns `{ residual, mintTable }` where mintTable maps each shared var to its { typeName, methodName, argTerms }. The `peSymbolic` composition (PE via the existing seam → this) yields the fork-driver / Nelson-Oppen input currency without a new PE surface.

engine:symbolizeSharedFields.label: symbolize: symbolizeSharedFields
engine:symbolizeSharedFields.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — recurse symbolizeSharedAt over ERecord field values with `/<fieldname>` paths, preserving field names; threads the mint context. Internal helper.

engine:symbolizeSharedList.label: symbolize: symbolizeSharedList
engine:symbolizeSharedList.description: partial-evaluator-substrate Phase 2 — recurse symbolizeSharedAt over an Expr-child list with `/`-indexed paths, threading the mint context + accumulator (ECall/EConstruct args). Internal helper.

engine:synAdmit.label: synthesize: admit tickets
engine:synAdmit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the admitted window `A_b`: the first `b+1` paid tickets in `R` order, with the cursor state from pin 10's structural, non-realizing, uncharged successor peek. Independent of fuel, Point availability, self-check and consumer. Internal helper.

engine:synAdmitGo.label: synthesize: admit tickets (grow the node cap)
engine:synAdmitGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one node-cap round: a full window is `cut` (a successor is proven), no outstanding pruning is `exhausted` (the generator end is proven), and neither at the ceiling is `refused`. The cap grows rather than being guessed, so admission never depends on a hidden third budget. It asks the generator for ONE MORE than the window it needs: the generator truncates before the two count-free root-spine exceptions are removed, so asking for exactly the window would leave at most `b` paid tickets and the successor peek could never be satisfied — every case-bearing goal would climb to the ceiling and refuse. Internal helper.

engine:synAnyMore.label: synthesize: any pruned
engine:synAnyMore.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — did any child generation report node-cap pruning? Internal helper to the compound productions.

engine:synApply.label: synthesize: synApply
engine:synApply.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — the Γ-apply tactic: scan Γ head-first (first entry per name — the synCase shadow discipline) for a SeArrow binding whose RETURN set decidably ⊆ the goal; synthesize each arg against its param set (depth-1 — synApplyArg: base/var only) and emit `ECall "$dyn:<name>" args`. The classic gain: `⟦((String→Int), String) → Int⟧` ⇒ `\f x -> f x` (the row 8λ.3 documented as unreachable). Internal helper.

engine:synApplyArg.label: synthesize: synApplyArg
engine:synApplyArg.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — ONE application argument, DEPTH-1: base (inhabit the param set ⇒ ELit) then var (a Γ binding ⊆ the param set ⇒ EVar). An ARROW-typed param skips base and goes var-ONLY: `inhabit(arrow)` returns a CLOSURE VALUE, and an ELit-embedded closure is exactly the 8λ.3-r nested-closure class — it self-checks (the singleton membership face reaches arrowClosureContains) but the EGRESSED literal lifts back as an ERecord, so the kernel re-check would soften to Nothing (the cross-face inconsistency the -r probes hunt); an intro'd lambda arg is the flagged v2 widening. NO ctor/case/intro/apply recursion — nested apply chains (`f (g x)`) are v2 (§4 NOT-in-scope: registry-wide apply rides the candidate-pool decision). Internal helper.

engine:synApplyArgDescent.label: synthesize: synApplyArgDescent
engine:synApplyArgDescent.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the DESCENT arg selector: scan Γ head-first for a binding whose name starts with `<dname>.` (a machinery-minted strict-component path bind — exists only under a match arm that proved the branch tag) and whose set decidably ⊆ the slot set. The first hit wins (head-first = the innermost narrowing). None ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:synApplyArgDescentTry.label: synthesize: synApplyArgDescentTry
engine:synApplyArgDescentTry.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — test ONE prefix-matched candidate: its set decidably ⊆ the slot set ⇒ the EVar; else keep scanning. Internal helper to synApplyArgDescent.

engine:synApplyArgs.label: synthesize: synApplyArgs
engine:synApplyArgs.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — synthesize one arg per arrow param (depth-1), in param order; any un-synthesizable arg ⇒ Nothing (the whole application is abandoned). Internal helper.

engine:synApplyArgsFix.label: synthesize: synApplyArgsFix
engine:synApplyArgsFix.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the descent-constrained arg builder for a recursion-marked arrow: walk the arrow's param sets ∥ the fix binder names; at the descend name's slot the arg MUST be a strict-component path var (synApplyArgDescent — an env binding named `<dname>.…` whose set decidably ⊆ the slot set); every other slot uses the ordinary depth-1 synApplyArg. Any slot unfillable ⇒ Nothing (the recursive call is abandoned — never a non-descending emission). Internal helper.

engine:synApplyEntryArgs.label: synthesize: synApplyEntryArgs
engine:synApplyEntryArgs.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — build the args for ONE Γ-apply candidate entry: a RECURSION-marked entry (lookup "fixDescend" ⇒ Just — the fix binding synFixGo installs) routes through synApplyArgsFix (descent-constrained at its descend slot); a plain entry keeps the 8λ.4 synApplyArgs path byte-identically. Internal helper.

engine:synApplyScan.label: synthesize: synApplyScan
engine:synApplyScan.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 / 8λ.5 — the Γ scan for synApply: skip shadowed names (EVar resolves head-first — applying a shadowed outer arrow would re-check against the WRONG binding); a SeArrow entry with `decideSubset returns goal = Just true` tries the args — success ⇒ the dynamic call, failure ⇒ keep scanning. 8λ.5: a RECURSION-marked entry (the fix binding — carries `fixDescend`, read tolerantly via lookup; plain entries lack it) may be selected ONLY with a descent-position variable at its descend slot (synApplyArgsFix — the chk.fix side condition enforced at PROPOSAL time, so every candidate is re-checkable by construction). Internal helper.

engine:synBase.label: synthesize: synBase
engine:synBase.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — the base tactic: `inhabit goal` ⇒ `ELit w` (the ground/const witness — subsumes the enum/interval/atom leaves; IS the const-lambda body when reached under intro). Nothing ⇒ no cheap witness. Internal helper.

engine:synBudgetClamped.label: synthesize: budget was clamped
engine:synBudgetClamped.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — did the operational cap fire on this invocation? Recorded in the trace so a clamped run is never mistaken for the requested width. Internal helper.

engine:synBudgetNorm.label: synthesize: normalize admission budget
engine:synBudgetNorm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — pin 9's normalization, IN ORDER: NaN and either infinity become 0 FIRST, and only then a finite value becomes `min(64, floor(max(0, b)))`. Composing the formula naively would send +Infinity to the cap instead of to zero. `admissionCap = 64` is the operational fence and changes only by a Step-D reopen; the default 8 and every gate sweep sit far below it. Internal helper.

engine:synCands.label: synthesize: ordered candidates
engine:synCands.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the complete ordered candidate list a consumer sees: the uncharged root-spine Vacuous FIRST, then the realized, de-duplicated, `P`-sorted paid batch, then the ONE uncharged bare reserve. At most `b` paid expressions plus the reserve reach a consumer. Internal helper.

engine:synCase.label: synthesize: synCase
engine:synCase.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — the case-split tactic: scan Γ head-first (FIRST entry per name — a shadowed outer entry is unreachable by EVar resolution, so splitting it would emit a match the re-check narrows differently) for a binding whose set decomposes to ctor branches (checkMatchBranches — the check arm's own validator), and emit `EMatch (EVar x) [one arm per branch]` with every arm body synthesized under the checkArmClassify-built narrowed env. First splittable binding that yields ALL arm bodies wins; none ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:synCaseArm.label: synthesize: synCaseArm
engine:synCaseArm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — ONE case-split arm: emit the TAG-ONLY pattern `PatConstruct { ctor, args = [], fields = [] }` (probe-verified: a tag-only wire pattern `{$tag:C}` matches any C-value — AND it round-trips the jlsTaggedPattern lift byte-identically, which PatVar binders do NOT: the lift drops fields metadata for unregistered ctors, so a binder-style emission would self-check but fail the kernel re-check — the cross-face inconsistency class), hand it to checkArmClassify (the CHECK arm's classification+narrowing — the arm env is the re-check's env BY CONSTRUCTION; a non-"always" classification ⇒ Nothing, defensive), and synthesize the body against the goal under that env (fuel−1). The env carries the check arm's FIELD-PATH bindings (`x._0` ↦ the field set), so the var tactic reaches the payload as a dotted path var — no minted binder names, no freshening needed. Returns `{ pattern, body }`. Internal helper.

engine:synCaseArms.label: synthesize: synCaseArms
engine:synCaseArms.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — build one match arm per ctor branch: every branch MUST synthesize (coverage — an uncovered branch is the runtime null path); any arm failure ⇒ Nothing (the split is abandoned, the scan continues). Internal helper.

engine:synCaseScan.label: synthesize: synCaseScan
engine:synCaseScan.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — the Γ scan for synCase: walk the remaining env entries threading the seen-names list; skip entries whose name was already passed (shadowed — EVar resolves head-first); a splittable set (checkMatchBranches ⇒ Just non-empty branches) tries synCaseArms — success ⇒ the EMatch, failure ⇒ keep scanning. Internal helper.

engine:synCaseSeen.label: synthesize: synCaseSeen
engine:synCaseSeen.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — has this name already been passed in the Γ scan? (A plain string-list membership scan.) Internal helper to synCaseScan.

engine:synCaseShape.label: synthesize: case-shaped scrutinee
engine:synCaseShape.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the CHEAP structural precondition of a Case: only a `SeCtor`, `SeUnion` or `SeMu` scrutinee can decompose into branches. It exists so that a node whose cap cannot fit any Case (a Case needs at least its own node plus one arm) can report node-cap pruning WITHOUT paying for the full `checkMatchBranches` decomposition, which is one of the two ~second-scale primitives in this search. Conservative in the safe direction: a shape that would decompose to Nothing at a larger cap merely delays the Exhausted proof by one round. Internal helper.

engine:synCmpAddr.label: synthesize: compare addresses
engine:synCmpAddr.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — lexicographic comparison of two canonical structural addresses, PROPER PREFIX FIRST (-1 / 0 / 1). Each token encodes its node's arity, so a complete address is a prefix-free code and comparing the flattened preorder concatenation IS comparing children in leftmost-major order. Internal helper.

engine:synCmpAddrGo.label: synthesize: compare addresses (step)
engine:synCmpAddrGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one step of the address comparison with the left head in hand: an exhausted right side is SMALLER (proper prefix first), otherwise compare heads and recurse on equality. Internal helper to synCmpAddr.

engine:synCmpP.label: synthesize: compare preference
engine:synCmpP.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the SEMANTIC preference key `P = (baseFree < pointDependent, var < ctor < apply < case, primarySourceOrdinal, unique R-rank)`, applied ONLY to the finite admitted window. Provenance DOMINATES position: `g x` beats `f false` however early `f` sits in Γ, and a future Point for Boolean cannot displace a previously returned `g x`. The final component is the ticket's `R` rank, whose address already encodes every leftmost-major child coordinate, so `P` is total and well-founded with no second pairing function. Internal helper.

engine:synCmpR.label: synthesize: compare admission rank
engine:synCmpR.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the FAIR admission order `R = (nodeCount, structuralAddress)`. Node count is PRIMARY, so every address tier is finite and this alphabet cannot create a starvation-producing recursive-lex descent; the result is a total effective well-order giving every paid ticket one natural rank. Admission is coverage mechanics, NOT witness quality. Internal helper.

engine:synCmpTup.label: synthesize: compare tuples
engine:synCmpTup.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the `R` order over child tuples: total node count first, then the concatenated address. Internal helper to the Cartesian fold.

engine:synConsumeChk.label: synthesize: ordinary consumer
engine:synConsumeChk.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — take the FIRST candidate whose self-re-check decides `Just true`. `Nothing` and `Just false` are Reject-and-continue (each having already consumed its admission slot), never a terminal Unknown. Internal helper.

engine:synConsumeLaw.label: synthesize: law consumer
engine:synConsumeLaw.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the combined law pipeline in `P` order: self-check, then Option A's Expr-level safety screen, then conversion, then the predicate. Every non-accepting stage continues. On exhaustion the reason is TOTAL (pin 21): `law-match-unsupported` iff at least one self-check-accepted candidate was excluded by the match rule AND every law-ineligibility among them was that class AND no law invocation returned false — an EMatch-only profile reports it even when the search then exhausts or cuts. Anything mixed uses the general reason. Never `TvEmpty`. Internal helper.

engine:synConsumeLawChk.label: synthesize: law consumer (self-check stage)
engine:synConsumeLawChk.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — a candidate that fails its own re-check is skipped WITHOUT entering the law-ineligibility profile: realization and check failures are not law exclusions. Internal helper.

engine:synConsumeLawPred.label: synthesize: law consumer (predicate stage)
engine:synConsumeLawPred.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — convert the safe candidate and evaluate the law; a falsey result is Reject-and-continue and marks the general profile. The first full acceptance returns TvFound. Internal helper.

engine:synConsumeLawSafe.label: synthesize: law consumer (safety stage)
engine:synConsumeLawSafe.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — Option A's screen runs BEFORE conversion and before any predicate call: a match-excluded candidate consumes its slot and continues with the match profile marked, any other unsafe candidate marks the general profile, and only a safe candidate is converted. A law-invocation spy therefore stays at zero for every excluded eliminator. Internal helper.

engine:synCross.label: synthesize: cross one coordinate
engine:synCross.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — extend every suffix tuple with every candidate of ONE coordinate, leftmost varying slowest. Internal helper to the Cartesian fold.

engine:synCtor.label: synthesize: synCtor
engine:synCtor.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — the ctor tactic: a SeCtor goal ⇒ synCtorBuild (EConstruct over per-field synthesis); a SeUnion goal ⇒ synUnion (the first branch that synthesizes); any other shape ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:synCtorBuild.label: synthesize: synCtorBuild
engine:synCtorBuild.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — build an `EConstruct c` for a SeCtor goal: a coercing ctor (True/False) ⇒ Nothing (the ledger-B5 exclusion — inhabit's base tactic already handles those via the coercion); else synthesize each field's set positionally (synFields, fuel−1) ⇒ `EConstruct { ctor = c, args, fields = [] }` (positional args pair with the SeCtor fields in checkCtorSeCtor). Any field un-synthesizable ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:synDedup.label: synthesize: remove duplicates
engine:synDedup.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — drop duplicate syntax among the realized survivors, retaining the LOWEST-`R` occurrence (the input list is already in `R` order). A later equal candidate has already consumed its own admission slot; suppression only stops it reaching the consumer twice. Internal helper.

engine:synDrop.label: synthesize: drop
engine:synDrop.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — a list minus its first `n` elements. Internal helper.

engine:synDupEq.label: synthesize: duplicate syntax
engine:synDupEq.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — pin 14 duplicate identity: structurally equal expressions are duplicates UNLESS either carries a non-scalar literal, in which case they are conservatively distinct. Internal helper.

engine:synDupSeen.label: synthesize: seen duplicate
engine:synDupSeen.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — is this expression a duplicate of one already retained? Internal helper.

engine:synEmbedAll.label: synthesize: embeddable list
engine:synEmbedAll.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — every element of a list must be embeddable. Internal helper.

engine:synEmbedGo.label: synthesize: embeddable (depth-bounded)
engine:synEmbedGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the depth-bounded worker behind pin 16's recursive embeddability check. The bound is what makes the predicate TOTAL: a canonical point may be an arbitrary host value (a `SeEnum` carries whatever the caller put in it), and a self-referencing value would otherwise recurse until the host stack gives out. Exceeding the bound is NOT embeddable — fail-closed like every other refusal here, so a pathological value costs a charged PointOut rather than a crash. Internal helper.

engine:synEmbedRec.label: synthesize: embeddable record
engine:synEmbedRec.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — a record is embeddable when it is not a closure or partial and every entry value is embeddable. A closure witness (the arrow face callable rep) is refused here, which is what stops a non-arrow union with an arrow branch from embedding a closure in a literal and breaking its own round-trip. Internal helper.

engine:synEmbedRec2.label: synthesize: embeddable record (partial guard)
engine:synEmbedRec2.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the partial-application rep is refused for the same reason as a closure; otherwise fall through to the entry walk. Internal helper.

engine:synEmbeddable.label: synthesize: embeddable value
engine:synEmbeddable.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — pin 16 recursive embeddability: a scalar/null value, or an array of embeddables, or structural record data carrying no callable anywhere beneath it. A non-embeddable Point realizes as a CHARGED miss; ticket topology never depends on this, because the guard is dynamic. Internal helper.

engine:synEngineArrow.label: synthesize: ordered arrow search
engine:synEngineArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the ordinary arrow face: offer the ordered candidates to the self-check consumer and return the first acceptance as a witness value; if none self-certifies, hand off to the UNCHANGED legacy fixed-point tail. Fixed-point preference is out of scope, so the tail is preserved rather than ranked. Internal helper.

engine:synEnvHasName.label: synthesize: synEnvHasName
engine:synEnvHasName.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3-r — does some env entry bind this name? (envLookup returns the SET, which can be any shape — a plain Bool scan is the unambiguous form.) Internal helper to synFreshenName.

engine:synFields.label: synthesize: synFields
engine:synFields.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — synthesize each SeCtor field's set into a positional arg (synTerm per field.set; any Nothing ⇒ Nothing), collected in field order (aligns with checkCtorSeCtor's positional pairing). Internal helper.

engine:synFilterTup.label: synthesize: bound tuples by node cap
engine:synFilterTup.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — keep only the child tuples whose TOTAL node count fits the remaining cap. Children are generated with the whole remaining cap each, so this is where the shared budget is enforced; a dropped tuple means a larger ticket exists and is reported as node-cap pruning. Internal helper.

engine:synFiniteNum.label: synthesize: finite number
engine:synFiniteNum.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — is this Number finite? `x - x` is 0 for every finite value and NaN for NaN and for either infinity, so one subtraction separates the three non-finite cases from the rest without a host predicate. Internal helper.

engine:synFixArm.label: synthesize: synFixArm
engine:synFixArm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — ONE fix-split arm: the tag-only pattern (the synCaseArm round-trip shape), checkArmClassify for the narrowed env (the re-check's env by construction — path binds included), then the arm BODY: the RECURSIVE call FIRST (synFixRecCall — this is what makes the emitted witness recursion-shaped instead of collapsing to the base tactic's constant), the generic synTerm cascade as the fallback (the base branch closes there). A non-"always" classification ⇒ Nothing (defensive — tag-only patterns always classify "always"). Internal helper.

engine:synFixArms.label: synthesize: synFixArms
engine:synFixArms.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — one tag-only arm per μ branch, ALL must synthesize (coverage — the check arm's requirement); fuel decrements per arm (the branch discipline). Internal helper.

engine:synFixCertify.label: synthesize: synFixCertify
engine:synFixCertify.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — certify a genuinely RECURSIVE fix candidate: self-re-check via checkExprFix (the chk.fix premise + descent); Just true ⇒ TvFound (the fix-marked closure), else TvUnknown "self-recheck-failed". Internal helper to synFixGo.

engine:synFixGo.label: synthesize: synFixGo
engine:synFixGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the fix-intro core: validate the goal params (fieldSemanticSlotsValid); pick the FIRST SeMu param that checkMatchBranches-decomposes (positive + guarded — the checkMatchBranchesMu gate; none ⇒ TvUnknown "no-term"); bind params (synIntroBind — collision-freshened), mint a fresh self-name (synFreshenName "f"), install the RECURSION-marked Γ entry ({name, …, set = goal, fixParams, fixDescend}); force the case split on the descend param with recursive-call-first arm bodies (synFixArms); wrap `ELambda`; SELF-RE-CHECK via checkExprFix (the chk.fix rule — premise + descent); Just true ⇒ TvFound (termFixWitnessValue — the fix-marked closure), else TvUnknown "self-recheck-failed". Internal helper.

engine:synFixPick.label: synthesize: synFixPick
engine:synFixPick.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — pick the descent param: walk the goal params ∥ the freshened binder names; the FIRST param whose set is a SeMu that checkMatchBranches decomposes (Just, non-empty — the positive+guarded unfold) wins, returning `{ dname, dset }` (the freshened binder name + the μ set). None ⇒ Nothing (fix-intro inapplicable — the honest v1 trigger is μ-typed params only). Internal helper.

engine:synFixPickMu.label: synthesize: synFixPickMu
engine:synFixPickMu.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — probe ONE μ param as the descent candidate: checkMatchBranches must decompose it (Just, non-empty — the positive+guarded unfold); success ⇒ `{ dname, dset }`, else keep scanning the rest. Internal helper to synFixPick.

engine:synFixPlain.label: synthesize: synFixPlain
