engine:synFixPlain.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — a fix derivation whose arms all closed WITHOUT the recursive call (the fix binding went unused): certify through the ORDINARY checkExpr and emit the UNMARKED plain witness (no `fix` slot — the value is an ordinary lambda; marking it would be noise). Internal helper to synFixGo.

engine:synFixRecCall.label: synthesize: synFixRecCall
engine:synFixRecCall.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — build the arm's recursive call `ECall "$dyn:<fname>" args` under the NARROWED arm env: the goal's RETURN set must cover the goal returns (trivially — f returns the goal's own codomain), and the args build via synApplyArgsFix (the descent-constrained walk: the descend slot takes a `<dname>.…` path bind ⊆ its param set — present only in RECURSIVE branches, so base branches fail here and fall back). Internal helper.

engine:synFixSplit.label: synthesize: synFixSplit
engine:synFixSplit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the FORCED case split on the descent param: decompose its μ set (checkMatchBranches — the same oracle synFixPick consulted), emit `EMatch (EVar dname)` with one tag-only arm per branch, every arm body via synFixArm (recursive-call-first). Internal helper.

engine:synFreeRes.label: synthesize: free reserve candidate
engine:synFreeRes.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the ONE uncharged bare reserve `Intro*;Point(groundReturn)`, offered AFTER the paid window: follow the forced arrow returns to the first non-arrow return and embed its canonical point as syntax, never as an embedded closure. It has required fuel zero, so a law that only the constant satisfies is reachable at every fuel. Absent when the ground point is missing or not embeddable. Internal helper.

engine:synFreeResGo.label: synthesize: free reserve candidate (spine)
engine:synFreeResGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one step of the forced arrow-return spine for the free reserve. Internal helper.

engine:synFreeVac.label: synthesize: free vacuous candidate
engine:synFreeVac.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the uncharged root-spine `Intro*;Vacuous` candidate: follow the forced arrow returns to the FIRST decidably-empty parameter product and emit the nested false-bodied lambda. Offered FIRST, at every fuel and budget — treating vacuity as a top-level-only shortcut is what would lose the shipped nested witness. Internal helper.

engine:synFreeVacGo.label: synthesize: free vacuous candidate (spine)
engine:synFreeVacGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one step of the forced arrow-return spine for the free Vacuous candidate. Internal helper.

engine:synFreshenName.label: synthesize: synFreshenName
engine:synFreshenName.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3-r — freshen a param name against the env: while some env entry already binds it, append `'` (a pure string op — deterministic, arithmetic-free; the decider ctx boxes Numbers so `toString`-based schemes render `[object Object]`). Collision-free ⇒ the name itself. Internal helper to synIntroBind.

engine:synGen.label: synthesize: generate tickets
engine:synGen.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the complete-ticket generator: at most `cap` nodes, `R`-ordered, truncated to `b+1`, with `more` reporting node-cap pruning. Consults NO fuel, NO current `inhabit` success, NO self-check and NO consumer, which is what keeps the admitted window `A_b` stable under all four. Internal helper.

engine:synGenApply.label: synthesize: generate (apply scan)
engine:synGenApply.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the depth-1 Apply productions over EVERY live Γ arrow whose return set is decidably ⊆ the goal. The scan resumes after each choice, so the first applicable binding no longer wins by position. Internal helper to synGenGround.

engine:synGenApplyBuild.label: synthesize: generate (apply, arguments)
engine:synGenApplyBuild.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the COMPLETE argument product for one Apply head: every coordinate independently, leftmost-major, bounded by the remaining node cap. Internal helper.

engine:synGenApplyGo.label: synthesize: generate (apply scan, fold)
engine:synGenApplyGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the head/tail accumulator behind synGenApply, carrying the zero-based live ordinal. Internal helper.

engine:synGenApplyGuard.label: synthesize: generate (apply, return guard)
engine:synGenApplyGuard.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the FIXED static guard: the head binding return set must decide ⊆ the goal. A dynamic outcome never erases a ticket, but this subset decision is fuel- and point-independent, so a miss forms no ticket at all. Internal helper.

engine:synGenApplyOne.label: synthesize: generate (apply, one binding)
engine:synGenApplyOne.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — admit one live binding as an Apply head when its set is a `SeArrow` whose return is decidably ⊆ the goal, then continue the scan. Internal helper.

engine:synGenArgOne.label: synthesize: generate (apply, one argument coordinate)
engine:synGenArgOne.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — pin 2: an argument coordinate ranges over every eligible live `Var` (set decidably ⊆ the parameter set) PLUS the one `Point`, in address order so a projection precedes the canonical point; an ARROW-typed coordinate keeps the existing var-only fence. This is the seam where the live code tried its base first. Internal helper.

engine:synGenArm.label: synthesize: generate (case, one arm)
engine:synGenArm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one arm coordinate: build the tag-only pattern, take the check arm classifier narrowed environment (the re-check environment BY CONSTRUCTION), and run a full recursive term search for the goal under it. A branch the classifier does not accept as `always` forms no ticket — that fact is fuel- and point-independent. Internal helper.

engine:synGenArrow.label: synthesize: generate (arrow goal)
engine:synGenArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — arrow-production exclusivity (pin 3): invalid field slots produce NOTHING (fail-closed, the generation-failure class); a decidably-empty parameter product makes Vacuous the SOLE production; otherwise Intro is. They never compete at one node. Internal helper to synGen.

engine:synGenCase.label: synthesize: generate (case scan)
engine:synGenCase.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the Case productions over EVERY live Γ binding whose set decomposes into ctor branches. The scan resumes after each split, so an early all-points split no longer wins by position over a later payload split. Internal helper to synGenGround.

engine:synGenCaseArms.label: synthesize: generate (case, arm product)
engine:synGenCaseArms.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — build one Case ticket per complete arm tuple, bounded by the remaining node cap; the arm constructor names are carried in branch order for realization. Internal helper.

engine:synGenCaseBuild.label: synthesize: generate (case, arms)
engine:synGenCaseBuild.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the COMPLETE arm product for one scrutinee: every arm body is a full recursive term search under that arm narrowed environment, and the arms are combined leftmost-major. Nested eliminators therefore remain candidates. An empty branch list forms no ticket. Internal helper.

engine:synGenCaseGo.label: synthesize: generate (case scan, fold)
engine:synGenCaseGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the head/tail accumulator behind synGenCase, carrying the zero-based live ordinal. Internal helper.

engine:synGenCaseOne.label: synthesize: generate (case, one scrutinee)
engine:synGenCaseOne.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — admit one live binding as a Case scrutinee when `checkMatchBranches` decomposes it into a NONEMPTY branch list, then continue the scan. Internal helper.

engine:synGenCtor.label: synthesize: generate (ctor)
engine:synGenCtor.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the Ctor productions: a `SeCtor` goal takes the direct arm, a `SeUnion` goal enumerates branch-selecting nodes, anything else forms NO Ctor ticket (pin 4 — that position is covered by Point). Internal helper to synGenGround.

engine:synGenCtorBuild.label: synthesize: generate (direct ctor, build)
engine:synGenCtorBuild.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — generate each field slot, take the bounded leftmost-major product, and bound it by the remaining node cap. Internal helper to synGenCtorD.

engine:synGenCtorD.label: synthesize: generate (direct ctor)
engine:synGenCtorD.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the direct-Ctor production over the COMPLETE Cartesian product of its declared field slots. Invalid semantic slots and a COERCING constructor (True/False, whose construct coerces to a host boolean) form no ticket — pin 4, preserving the live faces exclusion; those positions are covered by Point. Internal helper to synGenCtor.

engine:synGenGround.label: synthesize: generate (ground goal)
engine:synGenGround.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the non-arrow productions merged into ONE `R`-ordered window: Var, Ctor (direct or union-branch), Apply, Case and the one opaque Point. Every production is offered; nothing is skipped because an earlier one succeeded, which is precisely the first-success behaviour this phase replaces. Internal helper to synGen.

engine:synGenIntro.label: synthesize: generate (intro)
engine:synGenIntro.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the forced Intro production: bind the freshened parameter names into Γ (the existing shadow-free synIntroBind) and wrap EVERY body ticket, not only the first. Wrapping preserves the body order because it adds a constant address prefix and one node. Internal helper to synGenArrow.

engine:synGenUnion.label: synthesize: generate (union branches)
engine:synGenUnion.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one branch-selecting Ctor node per ORIGINAL zero-based branch ordinal, each wrapping one complete child ticket for that branch payload. Every branch is enumerated: the union scan no longer stops at the first branch that synthesizes, which is what lets a later base-free branch beat an earlier point-dependent one. Internal helper to synGenCtor.

engine:synGenUnionGo.label: synthesize: generate (union branches, step)
engine:synGenUnionGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one branch of the union enumeration, with the branch in hand. Internal helper to synGenUnion.

engine:synGenVacuous.label: synthesize: generate (vacuous)
engine:synGenVacuous.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the sole production at an arrow whose parameter product is decidably empty: one Vacuous ticket carrying the freshened binder names of that arrow. Internal helper to synGenArrow.

engine:synGenVar.label: synthesize: generate (var scan)
engine:synGenVar.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one Var ticket for EVERY live binding whose set is decidably ⊆ the goal, in live-Γ ordinal order. The live scan resumes after each choice instead of committing to the first success. Internal helper to synGenGround.

engine:synGenVarGo.label: synthesize: generate (var scan, fold)
engine:synGenVarGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the head/tail accumulator behind synGenVar, carrying the zero-based live ordinal. Internal helper.

engine:synGroundGo.label: synthesize: synGroundGo
engine:synGroundGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — a non-arrow (ground) goal synthesizes via `inhabit` (the const/leaf witness IS the ground synthesizer, built with correct value shape): Just w ⇒ TvFound w; Nothing ⇒ TvUnknown "no-ground-witness" (the decidably-empty case was already caught by the honest bar). Internal helper.

engine:synGroundLaw.label: synthesize: ground law face
engine:synGroundLaw.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the non-arrow law path: apply §6.2's scalar test to the ground witness VALUE, then the predicate, over `inhabit`'s sole candidate. A non-scalar ground witness is law-ineligible rather than inspected. Internal helper.

engine:synGroundLawGo.label: synthesize: ground law face (test)
engine:synGroundLawGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the scalar screen and the predicate for a ground witness. Internal helper.

engine:synIntro.label: synthesize: synIntro
engine:synIntro.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 / 8λ.3-r — the intro tactic for a SeArrow goal: (1) VACUOUS first — some goal param decidably EMPTY ⇒ `ELambda names (ELit false)` (∀x∈∅ holds for any body; the nested mirror of the face's top-level vacuous fast path — its omission was the 8λ.3-r Just→Nothing regression); (2) else bind the goal's params under collision-FRESHENED names (declared name + `'` until free — pure string freshening, no arithmetic: the `?syn<n>` scheme hit the decider-ctx boxed-Number `toString` landmine; freshening keeps the env SHADOW-FREE so synVar picks are re-check-consistent — same-name nested params made cross-level projections unreachable), synthesize the BODY against `goal.returns` under Γ′ (fuel−1), wrap in `ELambda { params = names, body }`. Nothing ⇒ the body wasn't synthesizable. Internal helper.

engine:synIntroBind.label: synthesize: synIntroBind
engine:synIntroBind.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3-r — bind the goal params for intro in ONE threading fold: for each param, FRESHEN its declared name against the accumulated env (synFreshenName — collision ⇒ append `'`), PREPEND `{name, set}` (envLookup scans head-first — the checkBindParams newest-front convention), and collect the freshened names in param order. Returns `{ names, env }`. Per-level duplicates freshen too (the env accumulates within the fold). Internal helper.

engine:synIsSpine.label: synthesize: root-spine ticket
engine:synIsSpine.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — is this ticket one of the two canonical root-spine derivations (`Intro*;Vacuous` or `Intro*;Point`)? Those are REMOVED from the paid domain before ranks are assigned, so they never consume a slot and never compete inside `P`. Internal helper.

engine:synIsSpineKid.label: synthesize: root-spine ticket (descend)
engine:synIsSpineKid.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — descend the forced Intro spine of a candidate root-spine ticket. Internal helper.

engine:synL2.label: synthesize: 2-list
engine:synL2.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — build a two-number list without an inline multi-element literal (which parses as an APPLICATION in record-field and case-arm positions — the floor-axioms Phase-1 surprise). Internal helper.

engine:synL3.label: synthesize: 3-list
engine:synL3.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — build a three-number list through the appendItem idiom. Internal helper.

engine:synL4.label: synthesize: 4-list
engine:synL4.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — build a four-number list through the appendItem idiom. Internal helper.

engine:synLeaf.label: synthesize: synLeaf
engine:synLeaf.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 / 8λ.4 — the leaf-tactic cascade for a non-arrow goal, in the fixed order (§2): base (inhabit ⇒ ELit) first, then var (a Γ binding ⊆ goal ⇒ EVar), then ctor (SeCtor ⇒ EConstruct over field synthesis; SeUnion ⇒ first branch), then case (8λ.4 — a splittable Γ binding ⇒ EMatch over its ctor decomposition), then apply (8λ.4 — a Γ-bound arrow whose returns ⊆ goal ⇒ `ECall "$dyn:f" args`, depth-1). The 8λ.4 tactics run on the earlier tactics' Nothing tails only, so every pre-8λ.4 witness is byte-preserved. First tactic that produces a term wins; none ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:synLegacyNonArrow.label: synthesize: legacy non-arrow route
engine:synLegacyNonArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — pin 20: `synthesizeArrow` does NOT refuse a non-arrow goal today, it runs the legacy first-success route and may return a ground witness. That behaviour is preserved BYTE-FOR-BYTE here, under its own name, so nothing keeps dispatching first-success behaviour under the retired `synArrowGo`. Internal helper.

engine:synLive.label: synthesize: live env
engine:synLive.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the shadow-filtered live Γ vector (pin 6): head-to-tail, first occurrence of each emitted binder name wins. Var, Apply and Case all index THIS vector, so a binding's live ordinal is one fact rather than three per-scan positions. Internal helper.

engine:synLiveGo.label: synthesize: live env (fold)
engine:synLiveGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the head/tail accumulator behind synLive: keep a binding when its emitted name has not been seen, else skip it. Internal helper to synLive.

engine:synMaybeOne.label: synthesize: one optional candidate
engine:synMaybeOne.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — project an optional free candidate into a list so the three tiers concatenate uniformly. Internal helper.

engine:synMergeP.label: synthesize: merge (preference order)
engine:synMergeP.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the STABLE merge step over `P` for realized candidate pairs (ticket + its Expr). Internal helper.

engine:synMergePGo.label: synthesize: merge step (preference order)
engine:synMergePGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one comparison of the `P` merge, with the left head in hand. Internal helper to synMergeP.

engine:synMergeR.label: synthesize: merge (admission order)
engine:synMergeR.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the STABLE merge step of the pure-Fenel merge sort over `R`; ties keep the left run's element, so equal keys never reorder. Search ordering stays in Fenel rather than moving into `std:sort`'s sanctioned TypeScript hot path. Internal helper.

engine:synMergeRGo.label: synthesize: merge step (admission order)
engine:synMergeRGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one comparison of the `R` merge, with the left head in hand. Internal helper to synMergeR.

engine:synMergeTup.label: synthesize: merge tuples
engine:synMergeTup.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the STABLE merge step of the pure-Fenel tuple sort. Internal helper.

engine:synMergeTupGo.label: synthesize: merge tuples (step)
engine:synMergeTupGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one comparison of the tuple merge, with the left head in hand. Internal helper to synMergeTup.

engine:synNotSpine.label: synthesize: paid tickets only
engine:synNotSpine.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — remove the two count-free root-spine exceptions from a generated list, leaving exactly the PAID domain. Internal helper.

engine:synOpaque.label: synthesize: opaque literal inside
engine:synOpaque.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — does this expression carry a NON-SCALAR literal anywhere? Such an expression is conservatively distinct from every other for duplicate suppression (pin 14), because its literal payload cannot be compared structurally without inspecting host data. Internal helper.

engine:synOpaqueArms.label: synthesize: opaque literal inside (arms)
engine:synOpaqueArms.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — any non-scalar literal across match arm bodies. Internal helper.

engine:synOpaqueFields.label: synthesize: opaque literal inside (fields)
engine:synOpaqueFields.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — any non-scalar literal across a named-field list. Internal helper.

engine:synOpaqueList.label: synthesize: opaque literal inside (list)
engine:synOpaqueList.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — any non-scalar literal across a list of expression children. Internal helper.

engine:synPaid.label: synthesize: the paid batch
engine:synPaid.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — admit, realize in `R` order, remove duplicate syntax, then stable-sort by `P`. This is where the two orders meet and nowhere else: admission decided WHICH tickets, preference decides IN WHAT ORDER the survivors are offered. Internal helper.

engine:synProd.label: synthesize: bounded Cartesian product
engine:synProd.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the COMPLETE leftmost-major product over a list of coordinate candidate lists, truncated to `b+1` after each coordinate. Truncation is sound for the root top-(b+1): a tuple suffix ranked past `b+1` has `b+1` better suffixes, each of which — with the prefix held fixed — yields a strictly smaller root ticket. This is what makes `Pair x y` reachable where first-child-per-field could only ever build `Pair y y`. Internal helper.

engine:synReal.label: synthesize: realize a ticket
engine:synReal.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — realize a complete ticket at a given fuel: `Nothing` when the ticket static requirement exceeds the fuel (FuelOut), otherwise the structural build, which can still miss on an unavailable or non-embeddable Point. Every one of those outcomes CHARGES the ticket stable admission slot rather than renumbering the window. Internal helper.

engine:synRealApply.label: synthesize: realize (apply)
engine:synRealApply.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the dynamic-callee application over the Γ binding, through the shipped `$dyn:` convention. Internal helper.

engine:synRealApplyGo.label: synthesize: realize (apply, build)
engine:synRealApplyGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — assemble the call once every argument has realized. Internal helper.

engine:synRealArms.label: synthesize: realize (arms)
engine:synRealArms.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — realize every arm body in branch order; any miss fails the whole eliminator, which is the coverage rule. Internal helper.

engine:synRealArmsCons.label: synthesize: realize (arms, cons)
engine:synRealArmsCons.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — prepend one realized arm to the realized tail; either miss fails the eliminator. Internal helper.

engine:synRealArmsCons2.label: synthesize: realize (arms, cons step)
engine:synRealArmsCons2.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the arm record assembly once both the body and the tail are known. Internal helper.

engine:synRealArmsGo.label: synthesize: realize (arms, step)
engine:synRealArmsGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one arm of the eliminator, with its constructor name in hand. Internal helper.

engine:synRealCase.label: synthesize: realize (case)
engine:synRealCase.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the eliminator: one tag-only arm per branch in branch order, payloads reaching the bodies as field-path variables. Internal helper.

engine:synRealCaseGo.label: synthesize: realize (case, build)
engine:synRealCaseGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — assemble the match once every arm has realized. Internal helper.

engine:synRealCtor.label: synthesize: realize (ctor)
engine:synRealCtor.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — a direct Ctor builds `EConstruct` over its realized field children; a union-branch node emits its child expression directly, because a set-level union needs no injection. Internal helper.

engine:synRealCtorGo.label: synthesize: realize (ctor, build)
engine:synRealCtorGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — assemble the constructor once every field child has realized. Internal helper.

engine:synRealGo.label: synthesize: realize (dispatch)
engine:synRealGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the fuel-free structural build over the normative node alphabet. Internal helper to synReal.

engine:synRealIntro.label: synthesize: realize (intro)
engine:synRealIntro.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — wrap the realized body in the lambda whose parameters are the ticket freshened binder names. Internal helper.

engine:synRealIntroGo.label: synthesize: realize (intro, wrap)
engine:synRealIntroGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the lambda wrap once the body outcome is known. Internal helper.

engine:synRealKids.label: synthesize: realize (children)
engine:synRealKids.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — realize a child list leftmost-major; the FIRST miss fails the whole tuple. Internal helper.

engine:synRealKidsCons.label: synthesize: realize (children, cons)
engine:synRealKidsCons.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — prepend one realized child to the realized tail; either miss fails the tuple. Internal helper.

engine:synRealKidsCons2.label: synthesize: realize (children, cons step)
engine:synRealKidsCons2.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the child list assembly once both the head and the tail are known. Internal helper.

engine:synRealPoint.label: synthesize: realize (point)
engine:synRealPoint.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — ask `inhabit` for the subgoal canonical point and embed it as a literal, but ONLY when the value is embeddable data (pin 16). A non-embeddable point realizes as a charged miss; no path ever embeds a closure in a literal, which is the nested-closure round-trip bug this fence exists to prevent. Internal helper.

engine:synRealUnion.label: synthesize: realize (union branch)
engine:synRealUnion.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — a union-branch node emits its single child expression. Internal helper.

engine:synRealize.label: synthesize: realize the admitted batch
engine:synRealize.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — realize the admitted tickets in `R` order, keeping the ticket alongside its expression so preference can sort them afterwards. A ticket that fails to realize has consumed its slot and simply does not reach the consumer. Internal helper.

engine:synRealizeGo.label: synthesize: realize the admitted batch (step)
engine:synRealizeGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — keep one realized pair, or skip a charged miss, then continue in `R` order. Internal helper.

engine:synScalarLit.label: synthesize: scalar literal
engine:synScalarLit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the §6.2 scalar/null literal test, EXACTLY `isNull ∨ isBoolean ∨ isNumber ∨ isString`. When all four are false the value is refused WITHOUT `isArray`, `typeOf`, `entries`, `mapGet` or any property read, so no getter or proxy trap can run first. This is a deliberate completeness fence, not an approximation. Internal helper.

engine:synSortP.label: synthesize: sort (preference order)
engine:synSortP.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — stable-sort the realized admitted batch into `P` order. Internal helper.

engine:synSortR.label: synthesize: sort (admission order)
engine:synSortR.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — a pure-Fenel STABLE merge sort of a ticket list into `R` order. Internal helper.

engine:synSortTup.label: synthesize: sort tuples
engine:synSortTup.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — stable merge sort of child tuples into `R` order before truncation. Internal helper.

engine:synTake.label: synthesize: take
engine:synTake.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the first `n` elements of a list: the admission-window truncation. Internal helper.

engine:synTerm.label: synthesize: synTerm
engine:synTerm.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — the fuel-guarded term-search core: `lte fuel 0` ⇒ Nothing ("fuel"); a SeArrow goal ⇒ synIntro (fresh params + body search + ELambda wrap); every other goal ⇒ synLeaf (base/var/ctor). Fuel strictly decreases at every re-entry (each intro descent, each ctor field, each union branch) ⇒ terminates. Internal helper.

engine:synTermBudget.label: synthesize: term search (budgeted)
engine:synTermBudget.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the engine's Γ-carrying internal entry: an INDEPENDENT root invocation that builds tickets under the given environment, applies the ordinary self-check consumer, and returns the first `P`-ordered accepted candidate's expression, with NO value conversion and NO fixed-point tail. It owns one root exception scope. There is deliberately no wrapper equation from the legacy `synTerm` to it: `synTerm` stays byte-stable as the fixed-point face's private cascade.

engine:synTkApply.label: synthesize: ticket (apply)
engine:synTkApply.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the depth-1 Apply node (pin 2): a live Γ arrow whose return set decidably ⊆ the goal, one child per parameter coordinate, address `[3, ordinal, argCount] ++ children`, required fuel 1 because its depth-1 arguments (a Var or a Point) add nothing. Deepening argument positions is a NAMED follow-up, never implementer discretion. Principal rule `apply`, primary source the Γ ordinal. Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkCase.label: synthesize: ticket (case)
engine:synTkCase.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the recursive Case node: a live Γ binding whose set decomposes into ctor branches, one complete arm ticket per branch in `checkMatchBranches` order, address `[4, ordinal, branchCount] ++ arms`, required fuel `1 + max(arms)`. Nested Case inside an arm STAYS in the grammar — capping it at depth one would delete finite eliminators (the X/Y counterexample of the Step-D note §2). Principal rule `case`, primary source the Γ ordinal. Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkCtorD.label: synthesize: ticket (direct ctor)
engine:synTkCtorD.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the direct-Ctor node: one child ticket per DECLARED field in source order, address `[2,0,0,childCount] ++ children`, required fuel `1 + max(children)` — so a nullary Ctor requires fuel 1, pin 23's `max([]) = 0`. Principal rule `ctor`, primary source 0. Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkCtorU.label: synthesize: ticket (union-branch ctor)
engine:synTkCtorU.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the union-branch Ctor node (pin 1): a COUNTED node selecting original zero-based branch ordinal `j` and wrapping exactly ONE complete child ticket for that branch's payload, address `[2,1,j,1] ++ child`. Its principal rule is `ctor` and its primary source is the BRANCH ordinal, so branch order — not Γ order — breaks ties between two base-free branches. A nullary direct Ctor payload is NOT flattened away: the union node still wraps it. Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkIntro.label: synthesize: ticket (intro)
engine:synTkIntro.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the forced Intro node wrapping ONE complete body ticket: address `[0, paramCount] ++ bodyAddress`, one extra node, required fuel `1 + body`, and TRANSPARENT to preference (provenance, principal rule and primary source pass straight through from the body). Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkPoint.label: synthesize: ticket (point)
engine:synTkPoint.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the Point ticket: ONE opaque canonical `inhabit(subgoal)` request, one node, required fuel 1, point-DEPENDENT, address `[5]`. Arbitrary literal values are never separate tickets, which is what keeps the alphabet locally finite. Its principal rule sorts after `case`, so a bare Point is last among paid candidates when one exists (at a public arrow entry the root-spine Point is the count-free reserve instead). Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkVacuous.label: synthesize: ticket (vacuous)
engine:synTkVacuous.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the Vacuous terminal: at an arrow whose parameter product is decidably empty it EMITS the existing false-bodied lambda (∀x∈∅ — the shipped 8λ.3-r witness), one node, required fuel 1, and BASE-FREE (the `false` body is not a Point). Pin 3 makes it the SOLE production at such an arrow, so Intro and Vacuous never compete at one node. Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTkVar.label: synthesize: ticket (var)
engine:synTkVar.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the Var ticket for live-Γ ordinal `ord`: one node, required fuel 1, BASE-FREE, address `[1, ord]`, principal rule `var` with the Γ ordinal as its primary source. Internal helper to the ticket generator.

engine:synTraceArrow.label: Synthesize trace
engine:synTraceArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the Fenel-owned route/trace artifact required before the behaviour landing: the raw and normalized admission budget with its clamping flag, the cursor state from the structural successor peek, whether each count-free root-spine candidate is present AND whether it satisfies the consumer. `freeVacuousAccepted` genuinely means the FIRST, uncharged exception ENDED traversal, because it is offered before everything else; `freeReserveWouldAccept` is deliberately named as a CONDITIONAL — the bare reserve is offered LAST, so it answers only when nothing before it did, and reading it as “the reserve answered” would report two winners on any goal whose paid batch already succeeded. `winner` is the candidate this recording walk itself selected, published so a consumer can pin it against the live face byte-for-byte instead of inferring agreement from both sides merely finding something, the generated count `admitted` — which CAN exceed `windowed` by the one non-admitted successor peek on a Cut, so `windowed` is the ranked-and-charged window and `admitted` is not, and the two phase-tagged charge lists — realization-phase (`R` order) then consumer-phase (`P` visit order) — each row carrying its one-based admission slot and complete `P` key. Harness TypeScript only invokes and serializes this; it owns no search semantics. The stop condition it exists to check: a mandatory PAID winner outside slots 1..8 reopens Step D rather than raising the default.

engine:synTraceCons.label: synthesize: trace (consumer phase)
engine:synTraceCons.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one row per surviving candidate in `P` VISIT order, carrying its admission slot, its `P` key and the consumer outcome (`accepted` or `check-rejected`). Rows after the first acceptance are `not-reached`, because only an acceptance stops traversal. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceConsGo.label: synthesize: trace (one consumer row)
engine:synTraceConsGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — evaluate one candidate's self-check outcome in `P` order and continue. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceConsOutcome.label: synthesize: trace (consumer outcome)
engine:synTraceConsOutcome.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the consumer-phase outcome for one candidate: everything after the first acceptance is `not-reached`. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceFreeChk.label: synthesize: trace (count-free vacuous, ordinary)
engine:synTraceFreeChk.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — does the UNCHARGED root-spine Vacuous candidate satisfy the ORDINARY consumer? It is offered before the paid batch, so an acceptance here means every paid candidate is `not-reached`. Internal helper to the trace faces.

engine:synTraceHas.label: synthesize: trace (present)
engine:synTraceHas.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — is a count-free candidate present? Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceKept.label: synthesize: trace (retained)
engine:synTraceKept.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — did this ticket survive duplicate suppression? Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceLawArrow.label: Synthesize law trace
engine:synTraceLawArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the LAW-mode route/trace artifact: identical generator, admission window, `R` realization phase and `P` order as the ordinary trace — including `windowed` (the ranked window) versus `admitted` (which can carry the non-admitted successor peek) and both count-free acceptance flags — with the law consumer's staged outcomes (`check-rejected`, `law-match-excluded`, `law-unsafe-excluded`, `law-rejected`, `accepted`, `not-reached`) in `P` visit order. It is a RECORDING CONSUMER over the one engine, never a second search path: the harness only invokes and serializes it. Same stop condition — a mandatory PAID winner outside one-based `R` slots 1..8 reopens Step D rather than raising the default; the count-free Vacuous and the bare reserve have no slot and are exempt.

engine:synTraceLawCons.label: synthesize: trace (law consumer phase)
engine:synTraceLawCons.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one row per surviving candidate in `P` VISIT order under the law consumer, carrying its one-based admission slot, its `P` key and the staged outcome. Internal helper to the law trace face.

engine:synTraceLawFree.label: synthesize: trace (count-free vacuous, law)
engine:synTraceLawFree.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the same question for the LAW consumer: the uncharged root-spine Vacuous is staged through self-check, Option A's screen and the predicate before any paid candidate. Internal helper to the trace faces.

engine:synTraceLawGo.label: synthesize: trace (one law consumer row)
engine:synTraceLawGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — evaluate one candidate's law-consumer outcome in `P` order and continue; only an acceptance stops traversal. Internal helper to the law trace face.

engine:synTraceLawOut.label: synthesize: trace (law consumer outcome)
engine:synTraceLawOut.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one candidate's LAW-consumer outcome, in the pinned stage order: everything after the first acceptance is `not-reached`; a failed self-check is `check-rejected` and never enters the law-ineligibility profile; only a self-checked candidate reaches Option A's screen. Internal helper to the law trace face.

engine:synTraceLawStage.label: synthesize: trace (law screen and predicate)
engine:synTraceLawStage.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — Option A's screen runs BEFORE conversion and before any predicate call, so an excluded candidate is recorded as `law-match-excluded` or `law-unsafe-excluded` and the predicate is never invoked for it (which is exactly what a law-invocation spy pins). A converted candidate is `accepted` or `law-rejected`. Internal helper to the law trace face.

engine:synTraceLawWin.label: synthesize: trace (the law walk's own winner)
engine:synTraceLawWin.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the law-consumer twin of `synTraceWin`, returning the converted witness VALUE because that is what the public law face returns and what the byte comparison must be against. Same offer order: the uncharged Vacuous, then the `P`-sorted batch, then the bare reserve. Internal helper to the law trace face.

engine:synTraceLawWinGo.label: synthesize: trace (law winner scan)
engine:synTraceLawWinGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the first `P`-ordered candidate this law walk's own staged outcome accepts, converted to its witness value. Internal helper.

engine:synTraceOutcome.label: synthesize: trace (realization outcome)
engine:synTraceOutcome.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the realization-phase outcome string for one ticket. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceOutcome2.label: synthesize: trace (realization outcome, miss)
engine:synTraceOutcome2.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — distinguish a ticket that could not build from one suppressed as duplicate syntax. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceReal.label: synthesize: trace (realization phase)
engine:synTraceReal.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — one row per admitted paid ticket in `R` order: its one-based slot, its complete `P` key, its node count and structural address, and the realization-phase outcome (`fuel-out`, `point-or-build`, `duplicate` or `realized`). Every non-accepting outcome charged that slot. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceRow.label: synthesize: trace (one realization row)
engine:synTraceRow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — classify one admitted ticket's realization outcome without re-deciding anything: a static requirement above the fuel is `fuel-out`, a missing realization is `point-or-build`, a realized ticket absent from the survivors is `duplicate`. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceSlot.label: synthesize: trace (slot of a ticket)
engine:synTraceSlot.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the ONE-BASED admission slot of a ticket within the admitted window, found by its unique `R` rank. Internal helper to the trace face.

engine:synTraceValOf.label: synthesize: trace (witness value of a candidate)
engine:synTraceValOf.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — project an optional candidate expression through the SAME Expr-to-runtime-value boundary the law consumer uses, so the law trace's winner is comparable to the public law verdict's payload byte-for-byte. Internal helper.

engine:synTraceWin.label: synthesize: trace (the walk's own winner)
engine:synTraceWin.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the candidate THIS RECORDING WALK selected, mirroring the live candidate order exactly: the uncharged root-spine Vacuous first, then the `P`-sorted admitted batch, then the one count-free bare reserve. It is published so the harness can pin the traced winner against the live face BYTE-FOR-BYTE. Deriving it from the trace's own outcome function rather than by calling the live face is the whole point: an agreement check against a value the live face produced would be vacuous, and both sides merely finding something is not agreement. Internal helper to the trace faces.

engine:synTraceWinGo.label: synthesize: trace (winner scan)
engine:synTraceWinGo.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the first `P`-ordered candidate this walk's own outcome function accepts. Internal helper.

engine:synTupCons.label: synthesize: extend tuple
engine:synTupCons.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — prepend one child ticket to a tuple, aggregating the `R` inputs: node counts SUM, required fuel takes the MAX, provenance is the transitive OR (any internal Point makes the whole derivation point-dependent), and addresses CONCATENATE in leftmost-major order. Internal helper to the Cartesian fold.

engine:synTupNil.label: synthesize: empty tuple
engine:synTupNil.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the empty child tuple: zero nodes, zero required fuel (pin 23 max-of-empty is 0, which is why a nullary Ctor requires fuel 1), base-free, empty address. Takes an ignored argument because a bodyless nullary declaration resolves to a reference handle rather than its value. Internal helper to the Cartesian fold.

engine:synUnion.label: synthesize: synUnion
engine:synUnion.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — synthesize a term for a SeUnion goal: the first branch that synthesizes wins (a member of some branch is a member of the union); fuel-decremented per branch (the search.fenel branch discipline); none ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:synVar.label: synthesize: synVar
engine:synVar.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — the var tactic: scan Γ (head-first) for the first binding whose set `decideSubset goal = Just true` ⇒ `EVar name` (a bound variable of a set ⊆ the goal IS a member of the goal). The identity/projection tactic — synthesizes `\x -> x` where the domain has no cheap point witness. Internal helper.

engine:syntaxToJsonLogic.label: Syntax to JSON Logic
engine:syntaxToJsonLogic.description: Lower a Syntax value to its JSON-Logic value tree — the arm-for-arm inverse of jsonLogicToSyntax (the loader-seam lowering direction). Authors the `$`-FREE JSON-Logic (var/call/construct/if/let/do/fn/match + records + arrays); an appendItem chain bottoming at `SLit []` flattens back to a list literal. Match-arm patterns pass through as raw Pattern ADT values for the ONE ledgered TS `$`-key marshal to author. parser-substrate Phase 5a.

engine:synthArgsFit.label: check: synth args fit params?
engine:synthArgsFit.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — every arg's SYNTH set decidably ⊆ its arrow param set (parallel walk, arity pre-checked)? Anything but Just true ⇒ false (the soundness gate: an arrow member's behavior outside its domain is unconstrained, so the return set only over-approximates the image when the args provably land in the domain). Internal helper.

engine:synthCall.label: check: synth call
engine:synthCall.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r / 8λ.4 + signature-substrate Phase 2 — SYNTH a call's image set. Dynamic `$dyn:` and the `$` application vehicle remain language forms. Every other head first consults fnTypeMarker so an actual registered function, including one whose spelling resembles `if` or a notation op, takes the trust/groundness/exact-arity/domain-checked synthRegistered path that matches runtime registry precedence. Only an unregistered `if` or notation head uses synthIf/synthPropOp; other misses degrade to SeAll. Internal helper.

engine:synthDollar.label: check: synth $ vehicle
engine:synthDollar.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — SYNTH a `$`-headed application (`ECall "$" [callee, …args]` — the egress rendering of a dynamic call): an EVar callee delegates to synthDynName over the REST of the args (one semantics, two spellings — probe 1); any other callee shape (an inline lambda applied, a nested call) ⇒ SeAll (the fence). Internal helper.

engine:synthDynName.label: check: synth dynamic head
engine:synthDynName.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — SYNTH a Γ-bound dynamic call's image set (the Γ-apply v2 arm): the head name resolves through the ENV (not the registry — it is a lambda param / binder); a SeArrow-bound head with EXACT arity whose every arg's synth set decidably ⊆ its param set ⇒ the arrow's RETURN set (f ∈ SeArrow(P→R) maps every p∈P into R — for args within P the image is inside R; for args NOT provably within P a member function's behavior is UNCONSTRAINED, so anything less than Just-true fit degrades to SeAll). Unbound / non-arrow / arity-mismatch (an under-applied partial or the over-application drop-quirk — neither lands in R) ⇒ SeAll. ACCEPT-ONLY downstream like every synth set. Internal helper.

engine:synthExpr.label: check: synth expr
engine:synthExpr.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / 8λ.2-r — SYNTH mode over a sub-term: produce an OVER-APPROXIMATING set (accept-only downstream). ELit ⇒ its singleton (exact); EVar ⇒ the env set (unbound ⇒ SeAll); ECall ⇒ synthCall; True/False EConstruct ⇒ the exact boolean singleton (B5); unresolved source records ⇒ SeAll because CHECK cannot mint semantic field identities; every other shape ⇒ SeAll. Internal helper.

engine:synthFromSig.label: check: synth from signature
engine:synthFromSig.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / signature-substrate Phase 2 — project a floor-admitted registered signature marker to its RETURN synth set through typeToSetProjection; if degraded, carrying SeAll anywhere (the existing seHasAll exactness fence), arity is not exact, or some argument synth set is not decidably within its matching parameter domain, return SeAll. Only an exact, argument-safe call exposes the declared return set. Internal helper.

engine:synthIf.label: check: synth if
engine:synthIf.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2-r — SYNTH an if's image set: ≥3 args ⇒ the normalized UNION of the then/else branch synths (the value is one of the two — the inferIf mirror); anything shorter ⇒ SeAll (the 2-arg if's missing-else value is host-null — not representable, stay ⊤). Internal helper.

engine:synthIsOpFragment.label: check: is op-fragment head?
engine:synthIsOpFragment.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — true when a call head is a NOTATION op propagate recognises (arithmetic / comparison / min / max / cat / boolean-negation). fnIds like `add`/`sub` are NOT notation ops (propagate keys on `+`/`-`) ⇒ they route to the registered-signature arm, matching the brief's `add x 1 via add's registered signature` intent. Internal helper.

engine:synthPropOp.label: check: synth op-fragment
engine:synthPropOp.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 — SYNTH an op-fragment call: infer each arg's synth set, then propagate the notation op over them and normalize (the SAME propagate leaf + normalize inferExprType uses — the interval/enum transfer math exists ONCE; check adds none). Internal helper.

engine:synthRegistered.label: check: synth registered
engine:synthRegistered.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.2 / signature-substrate Phase 2 — SYNTH a registered call's image set from the effective fnTypeMarker row selected by synthCall: effectful (pure=false) or advisory/untrusted (trusted=false) ⇒ SeAll; otherwise require an exact signature projection, exact call arity, and every argument's synth set decidably within its corresponding parameter domain before exposing the RETURN set. Internal helper.

engine:synthTacticCatalog.label: Synthesize tactic catalog
engine:synthTacticCatalog.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 / 8λ.3-r / 8λ.4 — the DECLARATIVE tactic catalog (§3, dispatch-inert): the synthesis tactics as `{name, fnId, note}` records (intro/vacuous/base/var/ctor + the 8λ.4 case — vacuous rides inside synIntro but is its OWN tactic row for honesty). Catalog-visible for the editor's tactic browser; the real per-tactic instance-dispatch flip is gated on typed-fn-refs (fn-by-ref from engine bodies — the 6D blocker), so v1 keeps a fixed pipeline + this declarative list rather than faking dynamic dispatch. `q` is an ignored query placeholder (a single-arg fn — avoids the CAF/value-decl ambiguity; the browser passes `{}`).

engine:synthesize.label: Synthesize
engine:synthesize.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — goal-directed term synthesis over the core `Expr`: `synthesize fuel goal` searches for a term inhabiting `goal`, emitting a WITNESS VALUE the kernel re-checks. A decidably-EMPTY goal ⇒ TvEmpty (the honest bar — `setAlgebraDecideEmptyCore = Just true`; the CORE, not the widened public entry — the Phase 4T D′ / search.fenel cycle-break BY CONSTRUCTION: inhabit→synthesizeArrow→decideEmpty is a back-edge on the SAME term, and the public entry's search arm re-enters inhabit — 8λ.3-r). A SeArrow goal ⇒ `synthesizeArrow` (the vacuous/intro/base/var/ctor tactic search whose lambda witness `checkExpr` self-re-checks + the kernel re-certifies); any other (ground) goal ⇒ `inhabit` (the const/leaf witness). Verdict: `TvFound w` (a witness kernel-certifiable BY CONSTRUCTION), `TvEmpty` (a decidable emptiness refutation), or `TvUnknown` (fuel-out / a fragment miss — Γ-apply, higher-rank, non-var-head application). The proposer half of `inhabit ∘ comprehend`; only what the kernel re-checks counts.

engine:synthesizeArrow.label: Synthesize arrow
engine:synthesizeArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 / 8λ.6 — the SeArrow specialization `seWitnessArrow` delegates to. NOT fast-path-first any more: the adapter has no const or vacuity probe left, so EVERY valid arrow goal arrives here. A decidably-EMPTY arrow ⇒ TvEmpty (the honest bar — `setAlgebraDecideEmptyCore`, the D′ cycle-break by construction, 8λ.3-r). Else run the PREFERENCE-ORDERED candidate search: the uncharged root-spine vacuous candidate first, then the admitted window sorted base-free before point-dependent, then the ONE uncharged bare point reserve — each candidate SELF-RE-CHECKED against the whole goal via `checkExpr`, with a miss charged and skipped rather than terminal. The first acceptance is `TvFound` (the `mkArrowClosure`-assembled witness value); no acceptance hands off to the unchanged fixed-point tail. The two-argument name is a real wrapper passing the literal 8.

engine:synthesizeArrowBudget.label: Synthesize arrow (budgeted)
engine:synthesizeArrowBudget.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the width-carrying entry behind `synthesizeArrow`. A valid SeArrow goal routes through the ordered search, which owns root vacuity, the admitted window and the ONE bare reserve; the fixed-point tail runs unchanged after any bounded ordinary miss. A NON-arrow goal is NOT refused — the live face runs the legacy first-success route and may return a ground witness, so that behaviour is preserved byte-for-byte under its own name with the budget ignored.

engine:synthesizeBudget.label: Synthesize (budgeted)
engine:synthesizeBudget.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the width-carrying entry behind `synthesize`. `admissionBudget` counts complete chargeable SHAPES, not successful expressions: a FuelOut, an unavailable Point, a build miss, duplicate syntax, a failed self-check and a law rejection all consume the same stable slot and none refills it. A decidably-EMPTY goal still yields TvEmpty on the honest bar; a SeArrow goal runs the PREFERENCE-ORDERED candidate search (fair `R` admission, then `P` inside that finite window, then the unchanged fixed-point tail); any other goal delegates unchanged to the ground witness, with the budget ignored. The old two-argument name is a real wrapper passing the literal 8, not a curried partial.

engine:synthesizeFixArrow.label: Synthesize fix arrow
engine:synthesizeFixArrow.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the DIRECT recursion-synthesis face: `synthesizeFixArrow fuel s` forces the fix-intro derivation for a SeArrow goal (bind a fresh recursion-marked `f ↦ s` in Γ, case-split the first μ-decomposable param, recursive-call-first arm bodies, generic fallback), self-re-checks the lambda via `checkExprFix` (the chk.fix premise + structural-descent side condition), and returns `TvFound` with the FIX-MARKED closure value ({__fenelFn, …, fix} — kernel-re-certifiable through arrowClosureContains and runnable through the evaluator's invoke self-bind). A decidably-EMPTY goal ⇒ TvEmpty (the honest bar); no μ-decomposable param / an arm that won't synthesize / a failed self-re-check ⇒ TvUnknown. The consumer-facing 'suggest a RECURSIVE body' seam — witnessOf's ordinary route keeps every pre-8λ.5 witness byte-identical (fix rides only the plain search's Nothing tail there).

engine:synthesizeWithLaw.label: Synthesize with law
engine:synthesizeWithLaw.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.4 — the LAW-CONSTRAINED filter (the smallest honest slice; Commit D): `synthesizeWithLaw fuel goal lawPred` = synthesize, then on `TvFound w` evaluate `lawPred w` (probe 5's route — DIRECT param application, the var-callee invokeCallable path; no new ctx native) — truthy ⇒ the TvFound passes through, falsy ⇒ `TvUnknown "law-rejected"` (an honest abstention: the goal may hold lawful inhabitants the single candidate missed). TvEmpty / TvUnknown pass through untouched. SINGLE-CANDIDATE v1 — multi-candidate enumeration is the FLAGGED v2 (do not build a candidate queue speculatively; the brief's D note). The predicate contract: `lawPred : ⟦goal⟧ → Bool` (truthiness-coerced). KNOWN v1 CONSTRAINT (flagged): the law runs INSIDE the Fenel body, BEFORE the witness-egress pattern marshal — a CASE-SPLIT witness reaches an INVOKING law with raw arm patterns, so its match falls through to host-null and the law REJECTS (⇒ TvUnknown — the safe direction; a law that passes on null is out of contract). Match-free witness classes (const / vacuous / identity / ctor / apply) are marshal-clean and judge exactly. The editor's future "suggest a LAWFUL body" consumes this face.

engine:synthesizeWithLawBudget.label: Synthesize with law (budgeted)
engine:synthesizeWithLawBudget.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.6 — the width-carrying entry behind `synthesizeWithLaw`. It drives the ticket engine DIRECTLY in law-consumer mode — screening at the Expr level BEFORE conversion — rather than wrapping the value-level result, which is what makes law continuation possible at all: a rejected candidate charges its slot and the search moves to the next one. Option A is the boundary: only match-free expressions whose literal leaves are primitive scalars reach the predicate, an excluded candidate never invokes it, and exhaustion reports TvUnknown, never TvEmpty. A non-arrow goal applies the same scalar screen to the ground witness value.

engine:tagEqFuncType.label: tagEq func type
engine:tagEqFuncType.description: Build the (externref, externref) -> i32 WasmFuncType for the $fenel.tagEq runtime helper. PatConstruct's tag-check pushes the scrutinee + the interned ctor-name string then calls tagEq to get a 0/1 i32 on the stack.

engine:tailArgsSafe.label: Tail args safe
engine:tailArgsSafe.description: True when no tail-self-call argument contains a param-capturing closure (a JsArrow whose body references a param). The continue reassigns params in place, so a closure capturing a param would be poisoned — such a tail call must NOT be looped (stays a recursive return-call). Phase 6b2.

engine:tailOr.label: Tail or empty
engine:tailOr.description: The tail of a list, or `[]` when empty/singleton — total list-rest for the layout fold. Internal layout helper.

engine:tailStmts.label: Tail statements
engine:tailStmts.description: Walk the post-leading-let tail of a statement list, collecting expr Syntaxes; a mid-stream let triggers a recursive doStmts on the remaining items (nested SLet scope) and stops (jlsTailExprs mirror). Internal expr-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 3c.

engine:takeN.label: Take N
engine:takeN.description: The first `n` elements of a list (fewer if shorter), built into the accumulator `acc` (call with `[]`). ACCUMULATOR TAIL-RECURSIVE (parser-substrate Phase 7d): the recursive call is the WHOLE result, so the self-host pipeline's lever-B self-tail-call → `while`-loop conversion eliminates the stack growth on big files (the latent non-tail `concat (… (takeN …))` form overflowed the host stack on long inputs — a wrong-at-scale legacy bug, killed here as the split becomes a compiled parser ENTRY). `appendItem` appends to the END so the accumulator is in source order — no reverse needed. Internal parse-file helper. parser-substrate Phase 5b1 / 7d.

engine:takeRun.label: Take run
engine:takeRun.description: Count of consecutive chars from index `i` (bounded by `n`) satisfying predicate `pred` — the greedy char-class run length. Internal lexer helper.

engine:tblLookup.label: infer: return-table lookup
engine:tblLookup.description: Look a fnId up in the return-table INDEX (a key→{key, ret, arity} record) via the O(1) opaque-map `mapGet` native (the parser-substrate 7h-S2 perf branch — the pure assoc-list scan is the conceptual definition; the JS-object index is the rep). Returns Just the entry or Nothing. decide-substrate Phase 1 Stage E fix: the previous per-entry linear-scan recursion was O(|registry|) STACK-deep in the interpreter (~1400 frames) and overflowed the bun-test worker stack on every table MISS (any unknown op / `$`-keyed literal sub-expression) — a pre-existing breakage carried since the registry outgrew the stack; mapGet makes every lookup constant-time AND constant-stack (the editor keystroke path win). Internal helper.

engine:templPairsOps.label: Template pairs to operands
engine:templPairsOps.description: Flatten the template mid pairs `[{chunk, expr}]` into the `cat` operand tail in source order — each pair contributes the chunk `SLit` (DROPPED when the chunk is the empty string) then its interpolation expr. Internal expr-grammar helper. parser-substrate Phase 7e Sn=3.

engine:termFixWitnessValue.label: synthesize: termFixWitnessValue
engine:termFixWitnessValue.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.5 — the FIX-MARKED witness value: the ordinary mkArrowClosure envelope + the `fix` slot (mapSet — the seWitnessCtor dynamic-key precedent) carrying the self-name. arrowClosureContains reads the slot tolerantly (absent ⇒ the plain route); the evaluator's invoke self-bind binds it to the closure itself at call time, making the recursive witness EXECUTABLE; marshalPatterns preserves unknown envelope keys, so the mark survives the witness egress. Internal helper.

engine:termWitnessValue.label: synthesize: termWitnessValue
engine:termWitnessValue.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — the Expr witness → runtime VALUE boundary: an ELambda ⇒ the closure value `mkArrowClosure params (exprToJsonLogic body)` (the Ref-substrate callable rep; body = the egress-rendered JSON-Logic of the lambda BODY, params in the closure envelope — probe 4); an ELit ⇒ its literal value; any other shape ⇒ exprToJsonLogic (a total degrade — the arrow consumer only ever hands an ELambda; the kernel {w}⊆goal re-check is the net). Internal helper.

engine:testFilters.label: search: testFilters
engine:testFilters.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — classify a candidate against every filter branch (setAlgebraContains): a single Just false ⇒ "reject" (decidably not a member — clean, even if an earlier filter was Nothing); all Just true ⇒ "pass"; some Nothing and no Just false ⇒ "poison" (can't certify — withholds SvEmpty). Scans ALL filters so a decidable rejection is preferred over a poison (maximizes honest SvEmpty). Internal helper.

engine:testFiltersLoop.label: search: testFiltersLoop
engine:testFiltersLoop.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — the filter classification scan threading sawNothing: Just false ⇒ "reject" (short-circuit); Just true ⇒ continue; Nothing ⇒ continue with sawNothing set. End: sawNothing ⇒ "poison", else "pass". SeWhere filters are trustworthy at ANY depth since Phase 4T Step W — setAlgebraContains's SeWhere arm threads the candidate as an argument (whereMember), so the old SeWhere poison guard (hasWhereLeaf) is RETIRED. Internal helper.

engine:testFiltersNext.label: search: testFiltersNext
engine:testFiltersNext.description: decide-substrate Phase 4 — advance the filter scan to the tail (testFiltersLoop) or finish (sawNothing ⇒ "poison" else "pass") when the filters are exhausted. Internal helper.

engine:thawTypeFields.label: type-algebra: thaw fields
engine:thawTypeFields.description: Validate the ordered identity-bearing fields read from a `$record` before returning the thawed entry list. The host edge only reads the `$record` envelope.

engine:tighterHi.label: solve: tighterHi
engine:tighterHi.description: Phase 5 / decide-substrate Phase 1 Stage C — the more restrictive upper bound (smaller value, exclusive-on-tie; unbounded loses). Classifies the raw Maybe-bounds to the tagged Bound ADT and delegates to the SHARED setAlgebraIntersectStepHi (the ONE interval tighten), then declassifies. Internal helper.

engine:tighterLo.label: solve: tighterLo
engine:tighterLo.description: Phase 5 / decide-substrate Phase 1 Stage C — the more restrictive lower bound (larger value, exclusive-on-tie; unbounded loses). Classifies the raw Maybe-bounds to the tagged Bound ADT and delegates to the SHARED setAlgebraIntersectStepLo (the ONE interval tighten), then declassifies. Internal helper.

engine:tmplGo.label: Template scan loop
engine:tmplGo.description: The template body loop from `i`: accumulate the DECODED current segment `s`, on `${` emit the segment (str_begin/str_mid) + splice the re-tokenized hole, on the closing backtick (or EOF) emit the final segment (str/str_end). `isInterp` tracks whether any `${` was seen (str vs str_end, str_begin vs str_mid). `openCol` pins every emitted token's column to the backtick's. Internal lexer helper.

engine:tnArrItems.label: type-normalize: tnArrItems
engine:tnArrItems.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — the items list of a TnArray (Nothing for non-TnArray). Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:tnFindNamed.label: type-normalize: tnFindNamed
engine:tnFindNamed.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — find the first TnObject in items whose `name` field equals `name`. Navigates `$variant.cases` / case `fields`. Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:tnGetField.label: type-normalize: tnGetField
engine:tnGetField.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — field-by-name lookup over a TnObject node (Nothing for non-TnObject / absent). Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:tnStringEq.label: type-normalize: tnStringEq
engine:tnStringEq.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — True iff the node is a TnString equal to s. Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:tokTypeAt.label: Token type at
engine:tokTypeAt.description: The `t` field of the list element at index `i`, or `""` when out of range. Used to peek the module-header shape on the raw layout token list. Internal parse-file helper. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:tokValAt.label: Token value at
engine:tokValAt.description: The `v` field of the list element at index `i`, or `""` when out of range. Internal parse-file helper. parser-substrate Phase 5b1.

engine:topSuspended.label: Top suspended
engine:topSuspended.description: True when the top layout context is the bracket-suspend sentinel (`-1`) — inside `( [ {`, layout is suspended. Internal layout helper.

engine:totAddComposedEdge.label: tot: add composed edge
engine:totAddComposedEdge.description: Compose two edges that meet at an intermediate (e1.tgt == e2.src): the composed edge runs src e1 → tgt e2, strict iff EITHER is strict (totOr), inserted strict-dominantly. Helper for totComposeMatch.

engine:totAddCompositions.label: tot: one closure round
engine:totAddCompositions.description: One round of the closure: `graphs` plus normalize(G ; H) for every ordered pair (G, H) of graphs, each inserted only if not already present (deduped by set-equality). Seeds the accumulator with `graphs` itself, so the round is non-shrinking (next ⊇ graphs).

engine:totAddFact.label: tot: add a branch fact
engine:totAddFact.description: Record that the branch proves fact `kind` about variable `v`: "lower" (v > 0), "upper" (v ≤ 2^53, where subtracting 1 from a JS Number is exact) or "number" (v is a Number and not NaN — only a comparison that evaluated to TRUE proves it: std:gt and friends answer false for NaN and for mixed operand types). Facts are records {name, fact} in the `pos` list.

engine:totAddStrongEdge.label: tot: add strong edge
engine:totAddStrongEdge.description: Insert edge `e` into graph `g` preserving canonical form: if an edge with the same (src, tgt) slot already exists, OR the strict flags (strict wins); else append. The graph builder AND composition both route through this.

engine:totAllIdempotentsDescend.label: tot: all idempotents descend
engine:totAllIdempotentsDescend.description: Fold the closure: every IDEMPOTENT graph must have a strictly-descending self-edge; a non-idempotent graph imposes no obligation (True). All obligations must hold (the SCT criterion). Slice C: the idempotent graphs are the `f → f` cycles of the call graph; each must strictly descend some parameter.

engine:totAnd.label: tot: and
engine:totAnd.description: Eager boolean conjunction used by the size-change set/closure folds. Returns y when x is True, else False.

engine:totAppendAll.label: tot: append-all
engine:totAppendAll.description: Append every name in `names` to `list`. Adds a match-arm's constructor-bound (structurally-smaller) vars to the smaller/scrutinizable sets.

engine:totBoolEq.label: tot: bool eq
engine:totBoolEq.description: Boolean equality (the `strict` flag comparison for edge equality). True when both flags agree. Avoids relying on the scalar `eq` native over JS booleans.

engine:totCallSiteGraphCross.label: tot: cross-function call-site graph
engine:totCallSiteGraphCross.description: The size-change graph `G : fromId → toId` of ONE call site `toId(args)` in `fromId`'s body (slice C, generalizing slice B's single-function totCallSiteGraph): seeds the parallel param/arg walk with SOURCE = the caller's param list (callerParams) and TARGET = the callee's param list (calleeParams) — DIFFERENT sets for a mutual call, EQUAL for a self-call — then wraps the edge list in a {from, to, edges} morphism record. totCallSiteGraphGo is REUSED verbatim (it already separates source `allParams` from target `tgtParams`). The edges are built via a `let` then the literal (the inline-record-in-arg surprise).

engine:totCallSiteGraphGo.label: tot: call-site graph walk
engine:totCallSiteGraphGo.description: The parallel walk of target params / arguments (decreasing on the tails via totTail, no indexing): for each (tgtName, arg), accumulate totEdgesForArg over the FULL source param list into the running graph. Ran out of either list ⇒ the accumulated graph (an arity mismatch yields fewer edges — sound: a missing edge only weakens the criterion).

engine:totCanDecrement.label: tot: unit decrement is a strict well-founded descent
engine:totCanDecrement.description: True when `p - 1` strictly decreases `p` in a well-founded order AS JS NUMBERS COMPUTE IT: p > 0 ("lower"), p ≤ 2^53 ("upper": below it subtracting 1 is exact, above it `1e20 - 1 = 1e20` and `Infinity - 1 = Infinity`), and p a non-NaN Number ("number": a NaN or a non-number satisfies every NEGATED comparison, so `if n <= 0 then 0 else f (n - 1)` loops on NaN). Under all three, ⌈p⌉ is a natural number that drops by one per call. 2026-10-03: before, `p > 0` alone (or the else branch of `p <= 0`) was accepted.

engine:totClose.label: tot: closure (fuel-bounded fixpoint)
engine:totClose.description: The transitive closure of the graph set under composition, fuel-bounded: Nothing when fuel is exhausted (a SOUND under-approximation — the caller maps Nothing → Unknown; we NEVER check a partial closure for Total), else the fixpoint (totCloseStep) reached when a round adds no new graph. Structurally recursive on `fuel` (the structural-decreasing measure). The closure is finite (≤ 3^(n²) graphs over n params); fuel 256 is a generous pathological backstop — real code saturates in a handful of rounds via the early no-change exit. Tunable.

engine:totCloseStep.label: tot: closure step
engine:totCloseStep.description: One fuel-bounded fixpoint step: compute the next round; if it added nothing (set-equal to the current graphs) return Just graphs (fixpoint reached), else recurse with one less fuel on the expanded set. Helper for totClose (keeps the fuel guard a single-line if).

engine:totClosureOverApplied.label: tot: closure over-applied
engine:totClosureOverApplied.description: For a local callee spelled exactly `name`: True unless `closures` (checked local closures, {name, arity} records, the innermost first) holds `name` with an arity of at least `argc`. A bound name that is no checked closure is a callback (True); a checked closure applied to more arguments than its lambda literal has params spills the rest onto its result (True).

engine:totCollectAllMembers.label: tot: collect graphs from all group members
engine:totCollectAllMembers.description: Seed S₀ of the call-graph closure: fold over every group member, collecting that member's call-site graphs with THAT member as the caller (fromId = m.id, fromParams = m.params, scrut seeded = its params, origins/pos empty). Concatenate across members. The result is every cross-function (and self) size-change graph in the whole mutually-recursive group's bodies.

engine:totCollectAllVars.label: tot: collect all pattern vars
engine:totCollectAllVars.description: Collect EVERY variable a pattern binds (top-level PatVar + all nested), for shadow removal. PatLit / PatWildcard bind nothing.

engine:totCollectAllVarsList.label: tot: collect all pattern vars (list)
engine:totCollectAllVarsList.description: Fold totCollectAllVars over a list of sub-patterns (a PatConstruct's args).

engine:totCollectCtorVars.label: tot: collect ctor vars
engine:totCollectCtorVars.description: The structurally-smaller variables a pattern introduces: only the vars UNDER a PatConstruct (fields of a destructured value). A bare top-level PatVar binds a same-size alias, NOT a smaller term, so it contributes nothing.

engine:totCollectCtorVarsList.label: tot: collect ctor vars (list)
engine:totCollectCtorVarsList.description: Fold totCtorVarStep over a PatConstruct's sub-patterns — the structurally-smaller variables introduced by destructuring.

engine:totCollectGraphs.label: tot: collect call-site graphs
engine:totCollectGraphs.description: The core totality walk over the 7-case core Expr, COLLECTING the size-change graph of every call to a GROUP member (slice C) in the subtree as a `List Graph`, given the current scrut/origins/pos sets and the caller (fromId, fromParams). ELit/EVar ⇒ no graphs; ECall `if` ⇒ the guard-entry (per-branch pos narrowing), other ECall ⇒ uniform (a call to a group member contributes its cross-function graph, then recurse args); ELambda removes its params from all three sets (shadowing); EMatch threads per-arm via totGraphsInArms (ctor-vars get their scrutinee's root origin); EConstruct/ERecord recurse into args/field-values. The SCT criterion is a GLOBAL decision over the closure of ALL call-graph graphs, so the walk collects, then checkMutualTotality decides once. Generalizes slice B's single-`selfId` walk (the one-object special case).

engine:totCompInner.label: tot: compositions inner (g over all)
engine:totCompInner.description: Fold graph g against every graph in `hs`, maybe-adding each composition g ; h to the accumulator set. Inner loop of one closure round.

engine:totCompMaybeAdd.label: tot: maybe-add a composition
engine:totCompMaybeAdd.description: Slice C: composition is a PARTIAL operation — defined only when the intermediate function matches (g.to == h.from). When they match, compose + dedup-add (totCompMaybeAdd2); when they don't, SKIP the pair entirely (NO graph added — NOT an empty graph, which would pollute the closure with a spurious idempotent). This guard is what keeps the call graph's composition a category morphism restricted to matching intermediates.

engine:totCompMaybeAdd2.label: tot: maybe-add a composition (composable)
engine:totCompMaybeAdd2.description: Compose graphs g and h (precondition g.to == h.from already checked); append the result to the accumulator set only if not already present (by graph set-equality). The deduped one-round expansion step for a composable pair.

engine:totCompOuter.label: tot: compositions outer
engine:totCompOuter.description: Fold every graph of `gs` as the left operand against the full graph list `allG` (via totCompInner), accumulating into the set. Outer loop of one closure round.

engine:totCompose.label: tot: compose graphs
engine:totCompose.description: Graph composition `G ; H` (slice C, PARTIAL — the caller guards G.to == H.from): the morphism `from = G.from, to = H.to`, with edges = for every pair (x → y ∈ G.edges, y → z ∈ H.edges) that meet, the edge x → z, strict iff either step is strict (strict-dominance on collisions). Models the size relation after two consecutive calls through the matching intermediate function. The edge fold (totComposeOuter/Inner/Match/totAddComposedEdge) is REUSED verbatim over the edge lists. Edges built via `let` then the literal (the inline-record-in-arg surprise).

engine:totComposeInner.label: tot: compose inner (one e1 over h)
engine:totComposeInner.description: Fold one edge e1 of G against every edge of H, adding each meeting composition. Inner loop of graph composition.

engine:totComposeMatch.label: tot: compose-match
engine:totComposeMatch.description: Add the composition of e1 and e2 to the accumulator IFF they meet (e1.tgt == e2.src); else leave the accumulator unchanged.

engine:totComposeOuter.label: tot: compose outer (G over H)
engine:totComposeOuter.description: Fold every edge of G as e1 against H (via totComposeInner), accumulating the composed graph. Outer loop of graph composition.

engine:totConcat.label: tot: concat (graph lists)
engine:totConcat.description: Append every element of `xs` to `ys`. Order is irrelevant (the result feeds a deduped graph-SET closure), so a fold of appendItem suffices. Used to combine the self-call graphs collected from sub-expressions.

engine:totCtorVarStep.label: tot: ctor-var step
engine:totCtorVarStep.description: One sub-pattern's contribution to the structurally-smaller var set: a PatVar field is smaller; a nested PatConstruct's vars are smaller too; PatLit / PatWildcard contribute nothing.

engine:totEdgeEq.label: tot: edge eq
engine:totEdgeEq.description: Full edge equality: same (src, tgt) slot AND same strict flag. Needed for set-equality of graphs (idempotency + closure dedup).

engine:totEdgeForSrc.label: tot: edge for one source param
engine:totEdgeForSrc.description: One source param `src`'s contribution to the edges INTO target slot `tgt` (arg `arg`): a strict edge when totPosIsLt (arg ≺ src — structural sub-term or guarded `sub src 1`), a non-strict edge when totPosIsEq (arg = EVar src), else nothing. At most one edge per source.

engine:totEdgeMember.label: tot: edge member
engine:totEdgeMember.description: True when edge `e` (exact src/tgt/strict) occurs in graph `g`. Fold totEdgeEq over g.

engine:totEdgeSameSlot.label: tot: edge same slot
engine:totEdgeSameSlot.description: True when two edges occupy the SAME (src, tgt) slot — same source param AND same target param — regardless of strictness. Used for canonical-form merge + strict-dominance.

engine:totEdgesEq.label: tot: edges eq
engine:totEdgesEq.description: Set-equality of two edge-lists (order-independent): mutual edge-subset. Both are kept in canonical form (one edge per slot, strict-dominant), so set-equality is the right notion for idempotency + closure dedup. (Slice C rename: was totGraphEq, edge-level.)

engine:totEdgesForArg.label: tot: edges for one target arg
engine:totEdgesForArg.description: Fold over the FULL source param list, accumulating each source's edge (strict / non-strict / none) into target slot `tgt` for argument `arg`. Returns the edges into this one slot.

engine:totEdgesForArgTail.label: tot: edges for one target arg (tail)
engine:totEdgesForArgTail.description: Recurse on the tail of the source-param list for totEdgesForArg (keeps it free of case-in-let).

engine:totEdgesSubset.label: tot: edges subset
engine:totEdgesSubset.description: True when every edge of edge-list `g` occurs (exactly) in edge-list `h`. The order-independent half of edge-set-equality. (Slice C rename: was totGraphSubset — graphs are now {from,to,edges} records, so the set ops over the EDGE lists are named tot Edges* and the graph-level eq compares from/to too.)

engine:totFactsForget.label: tot: forget facts about shadowed names
engine:totFactsForget.description: Drop every branch fact about a name in `names` (a binder that re-uses the name hides the variable the fact was about).

engine:totFactsFromCompare.label: tot: facts from a comparison
engine:totFactsFromCompare.description: The facts a trusted comparison `f a0 a1` (std:gt / std:gte / std:lt / std:lte only — totIsTrustedPrimitive) proves about a variable compared with a literal, in its TRUE branch (`truth`) or its FALSE branch. Either orientation (`v > 0`, `0 < v`); any other shape or head proves nothing.

engine:totFactsFromRel.label: tot: facts from a variable-literal relation
engine:totFactsFromRel.description: Extend the branch facts with what `v rel k` proves for a NUMERIC literal k (a non-number literal proves nothing): v > k with k ≥ 0, or v ≥ k with k > 0, gives "lower"; v < k or v ≤ k with k ≤ 2^53 gives "upper"; and when the comparison itself evaluated to TRUE (`direct`), "number".

engine:totGraphEq.label: tot: graph eq
engine:totGraphEq.description: Set-equality of two GRAPHS (slice C): same `from` function, same `to` function, AND set-equal edge lists. A graph is a {from, to, edges} morphism caller→callee; two graphs are equal only when they label the SAME function pair and carry the same canonical edge set. Drives idempotency + closure dedup over the call graph.

engine:totGraphMember.label: tot: graph member
engine:totGraphMember.description: True when graph `g` (by graph set-equality — from/to/edges) occurs in the graph-set `set`. Fold totGraphEq over set.

engine:totGraphSetEq.label: tot: graph-set eq
engine:totGraphSetEq.description: Set-equality of two graph-sets (mutual graph-subset) — the closure fixpoint stop-test (the round added no new graph).

engine:totGraphSetSubset.label: tot: graph-set subset
engine:totGraphSetSubset.description: True when every graph of set `s1` occurs (by set-equality) in set `s2`. Half of the closure fixpoint stop-test.
