engine:totGraphsInArms.label: tot: collect graphs in match arms
engine:totGraphsInArms.description: Per match arm, extend the (scrut, origins, pos) sets exactly as slice A/B's walk did — remove the arm pattern's bound vars from all three (shadowing), then add its constructor-bound (smaller) vars to scrut and to origins WITH their root param (= totRootOrigin of the scrutinee) IF the scrutinee is destructurable (NOT to pos) — and collect the call-site graphs of the arm guard (when present: a guard runs before the body, so a call in it is an executable edge too) and of the arm body. Concatenate across arms.

engine:totGraphsInFields.label: tot: collect graphs in record fields
engine:totGraphsInFields.description: Fold totCollectGraphs over a record's field values ({name, value} records), concatenating the call-site graphs found in each field value.

engine:totGraphsInIf.label: tot: collect graphs in if guard-entry
engine:totGraphsInIf.description: The `ECall "if"` guard entry (rung-2 narrowing, unchanged in shape): split the three args — collect from `cond` with the current `pos`, from `then` with `pos` extended by totPosFromCond cond (true-branch positivity), from `else` with totPosFromCondNeg cond (false-branch positivity) — and concatenate. An `if` with fewer than three args falls back to the uniform collection.

engine:totGraphsInList.label: tot: collect graphs in arg list
engine:totGraphsInList.description: Fold totCollectGraphs over a list of argument/child expressions, concatenating the call-site graphs found in each.

engine:totGraphsUniform.label: tot: collect graphs at a uniform call
engine:totGraphsUniform.description: The non-`if` ECall arm (slice C): when `f` is a group member the call contributes ITS cross-function call-site size-change graph (totHereGraph → totCallSiteGraphCross pairs the caller's params against the callee's via the per-position oracle); then recurse into every argument (a call nested in an argument is still collected). Replaces slice B's `eq f selfId` self-call test with the group lookup — a call to ANY member contributes its cross graph; non-members contribute nothing. Factored so the `if` guard-entry falls back here for short-arg `if`s.

engine:totGroupLookup.label: tot: group lookup
engine:totGroupLookup.description: The callee param-list of function `id` within the group (a `List {id, params, body}`), or Nothing when `id` is not a group member (a call OUTSIDE the mutually-recursive set — contributes no graph, sound: a missing edge only weakens the criterion). Maybe-returning (the totLookupOrigin shape) so callers pattern-match. Folds over the group comparing member.id == id.

engine:totGroupUnchecked.label: tot: group has an unchecked reference
engine:totGroupUnchecked.description: True when any member body, under its own params (and no closures), holds an unchecked route into the group (totUncheckedReference).

engine:totHasFact.label: tot: has a branch fact
engine:totHasFact.description: True when the branch facts `pos` hold fact `kind` ("lower" / "upper" / "number") about variable `v`.

engine:totHasStrictDiagonal.label: tot: graph has strict self-edge
engine:totHasStrictDiagonal.description: True when the edge-list `edges` has a strictly-descending SELF-edge (∃ edge with src == tgt AND strict). The descent witness an idempotent graph must carry for SCT. Called on `g.edges` of an idempotent graph (whose from == to, so a src==tgt edge is a true self-loop on a single parameter).

engine:totHeadMayName.label: tot: head may name a member
engine:totHeadMayName.description: True when a call head or variable spelling may denote the function `id` (a canonical `module:name` id, or a bare id in hand-built groups). Stored bodies keep their source spellings while ids are canonical, so the match is spelling-normalized: a var-head call's `$dyn:` marker is stripped; the exact id matches; a dotted `Module.name` matches the id whose colons read as dots; a bare name matches every id whose code name it is (an over-approximation across modules: an extra match only adds a size-change graph or an escape, never removes one, so it can turn Total into Unknown but never the reverse). A colon spelling other than the exact id names something else.

engine:totHeadNamesMember.label: tot: head names some member
engine:totHeadNamesMember.description: True when the spelling may denote at least one member of the group (totHeadMayName).

engine:totHereGraph.label: tot: here graph (cross-function call)
engine:totHereGraph.description: The size-change graph(s) contributed by a call `f(args)` in `fromId`'s body (slice C): ONE cross-function graph `fromId → m` for EVERY group member `m` the head may denote (totHeadMayName — canonical, dotted, bare and var-head spellings of the same function all count; built by totCallSiteGraphCross pairing the caller's params against m's params via the per-position oracle); a head naming no member contributes no graph. The graph's `to` is the member's canonical id, so composition meets at member ids whatever the call spelling. Generalizes slice B's `if eq f selfId` self-call check to a call to ANY member of the mutually-recursive set.

engine:totIsEmptyList.label: tot: is empty list
engine:totIsEmptyList.description: True when the list is empty (no head). Drives the no-self-call ⇒ vacuously total fast path.

engine:totIsIdempotent.label: tot: graph is idempotent
engine:totIsIdempotent.description: True when graph `g` is idempotent under composition (`g ; g = g`). Slice C: an idempotent graph is NECESSARILY a same-function cycle, so the from == to precondition is checked FIRST (a g with from ≠ to could not equal g ; g, whose from = g.from but whose composition only meets if g.to == g.from); then the edge set must be fixed. An idempotent graph describes a stable infinite call path returning to its function — the graphs the SCT criterion imposes a descent obligation on.

engine:totIsIdempotentEdges.label: tot: idempotent edge-set check
engine:totIsIdempotentEdges.description: Helper for totIsIdempotent (slice C): given a graph g whose from == to is already established, True when composing g with itself leaves its edge set unchanged ((g ; g).edges == g.edges, by edge set-equality). Kept separate to avoid a let-in-then-branch.

engine:totIsListLiteral.label: tot: list literal call
engine:totIsListLiteral.description: True when a core ECall is the synthetic `appendItem` of a list literal (`[a, b]` lowers to an `appendItem` chain marked `lit = true`, the mark desugar keeps). The evaluator builds a literal natively; it never calls std:appendItem, so the walk treats it as a construction: its elements are walked, its head is no call.

engine:totIsTrustedPrimitive.label: tot: trusted primitive id
engine:totIsTrustedPrimitive.description: True when `id` is the canonical registry id of a std primitive whose meaning the size-change oracle relies on: the comparisons std:gt / std:gte / std:lt / std:lte, the connectives std:and / std:or, and the decrement std:sub. Only heads already resolved to one of these ids yield a positivity, bound or descent fact; a bare spelling never does (a user function may share the name).

engine:totLambdaArgClosures.label: tot: lambda-literal argument closures
engine:totLambdaArgClosures.description: The checked local closures an immediately applied lambda binds: for each param whose positional argument is itself a lambda literal, the record {name, arity} (the param, and the literal's param count). The applied body sees that name bound to a closure whose body is the literal (the `let` / `where` lowering binds one name per application).

engine:totLookupOrigin.label: tot: lookup origin
engine:totLookupOrigin.description: The origin param of a smaller var `v` in `origins`, or Nothing when `v` is not a tracked smaller var (a parameter, or an unrelated name). Maybe-returning (not a sentinel string) so callers pattern-match. Folds over `origins` comparing entry.name == v.

engine:totMemberOverApplied.label: tot: member over-applied
engine:totMemberOverApplied.description: True when the spelling may denote a group member (totHeadMayName) whose params are fewer than `argc`: the call spills the extra arguments onto the member's result, an invocation the size-change graphs do not see.

engine:totMergeEdge.label: tot: merge edge (strict-dominant)
engine:totMergeEdge.description: Rebuild graph `g`, OR-ing `e`'s strict flag into the existing edge in the SAME (src, tgt) slot (canonical-form strict-dominance). Non-matching edges pass through. Used only when a slot is already present (else totAddStrongEdge appends).

engine:totMergeEdgeKeep.label: tot: keep merged edge
engine:totMergeEdgeKeep.description: The strict-dominance merge step: build a single edge in `x`'s slot with strict = (x OR e strict), prepended onto the already-rebuilt rest. Helper for totMergeEdge (keeps it free of inline-record-in-then).

engine:totMergeEdgeTail.label: tot: merge-edge tail
engine:totMergeEdgeTail.description: Recurse on the tail of graph `g` for totMergeEdge (keeps it free of case-in-let).

engine:totMergeEdges.label: tot: merge edges into a graph
engine:totMergeEdges.description: Fold totAddStrongEdge over a list of edges into the running graph (canonical-form insert, strict-dominant). Used to accumulate one target slot's edges into the call-site graph.

engine:totNameElem.label: tot: name elem
engine:totNameElem.description: True when `name` occurs in the name-list. List iteration via the head/tail Maybe-returning natives (the engine-body idiom).

engine:totNonStrictEdge.label: tot: non-strict edge
engine:totNonStrictEdge.description: Append a non-strict edge {src, tgt, strict = false} onto the accumulator (the source param is equal-to/≤ the target slot).

engine:totOr.label: tot: or
engine:totOr.description: Eager boolean disjunction used by the totality tree/list folds. Returns True if either operand is True.

engine:totOriginIs.label: tot: origin is param
engine:totOriginIs.description: True when `v`'s origin is EXACTLY `p` — i.e. `v` is a strict structural sub-term of parameter `p`. Drives RelLt-structural at p's OWN position. Folds over `origins` comparing entry.name == v AND entry.origin == p.

engine:totOriginsAddCtor.label: tot: origins add ctor-vars
engine:totOriginsAddCtor.description: Add `{name = ctorVar, origin = root}` for each destructured ctor-var — they all share the scrutinee's root param. Mirrors totAppendAll, attaching the origin (rung 3's per-var root-param tracking).

engine:totOriginsRemoveAll.label: tot: origins remove-all
engine:totOriginsRemoveAll.description: Remove every entry whose name is in `names` from `origins`. Applies a binder's whole bound-var set's shadow-removal to the origin-tracked smaller set (mirrors totRemoveAll).

engine:totOriginsRemoveOne.label: tot: origins remove-one
engine:totOriginsRemoveOne.description: Remove every origins entry whose name is `n` (variable shadowing over the origin-tracked set — a binder re-using a name drops the prior smaller binding). Mirrors totRemoveOne but over the {name, origin} records.

engine:totOriginsRemoveOneTail.label: tot: origins remove-one tail
engine:totOriginsRemoveOneTail.description: Recurse on the tail of `origins` for totOriginsRemoveOne. Internal split (keeps totOriginsRemoveOne free of case-in-let).

engine:totPosFoldAnd.label: tot: fold positivity over and-conjuncts
engine:totPosFoldAnd.description: Fold totPosFromCond over the conjuncts of an `and` (true-branch): every conjunct holds, so each narrowing applies in sequence.

engine:totPosFoldOrNeg.label: tot: fold neg-positivity over or-disjuncts
engine:totPosFoldOrNeg.description: Fold totPosFromCondNeg over the disjuncts of an `or` (false-branch): the else branch of `if (or [..])` holds only when EVERY disjunct is false, so each negated narrowing applies in sequence.

engine:totPosFromBinary.label: tot: binary operands → positivity (true)
engine:totPosFromBinary.description: Extract the two operands of a binary comparison `ECall f args` and apply totPosFromCompare. Fewer than two operands ⇒ pos unchanged.

engine:totPosFromBinaryNeg.label: tot: binary operands → positivity (false)
engine:totPosFromBinaryNeg.description: Extract the two operands of a binary comparison `ECall f args` and apply totPosFromCompareNeg (the else-branch positivity). Fewer than two operands ⇒ pos unchanged.

engine:totPosFromCompare.label: tot: positivity from comparison (true-branch)
engine:totPosFromCompare.description: The facts a binary comparison proves in its TRUE branch, given its fnId and two operands (totFactsFromCompare with truth = True): positivity, the exact-decrement bound and Number-ness of the compared variable. Unrecognized fnId or shape ⇒ pos unchanged.

engine:totPosFromCompareNeg.label: tot: positivity from comparison (false-branch)
engine:totPosFromCompareNeg.description: The facts the negated comparison proves (what the FALSE/else branch knows; totFactsFromCompare with truth = False): positivity or the exact-decrement bound of the compared variable, never its Number-ness (NaN and non-numbers fail every comparison). Unrecognized fnId or shape ⇒ pos unchanged.

engine:totPosFromCond.label: tot: positivity from guard (true-branch)
engine:totPosFromCond.description: Extend `pos` with every variable the condition PROVES `> 0` in its TRUE branch. Handles `and` (fold over conjuncts) and the four binary comparisons; the true-branch CANNOT narrow an `or` (the and/or asymmetry), so an `or` and any unrecognized shape leave `pos` unchanged (sound under-approximation).

engine:totPosFromCondNeg.label: tot: positivity from guard (false-branch)
engine:totPosFromCondNeg.description: Extend `pos` with every variable the condition's NEGATION proves `> 0` (the else branch). Handles `or` (fold the negated narrowing over disjuncts) and the four negated binary comparisons; the false-branch CANNOT narrow an `and` (the and/or asymmetry), so an `and` and any unrecognized shape leave `pos` unchanged (sound under-approximation).

engine:totPosIsEq.label: tot: position RelEq
engine:totPosIsEq.description: True when `arg` is `EVar p` — the position's OWN parameter, unchanged, in its own slot (RelEq). Any other shape ⇒ False.

engine:totPosIsLt.label: tot: position RelLt
engine:totPosIsLt.description: True when `arg` is strictly LESS than the position's OWN param `p` (RelLt): structural (`EVar v` with origin(v) = p — a strict sub-term of p in p's slot) OR guarded measure (`std:sub p 1` — the canonical trusted id — under totCanDecrement). A var whose origin is a DIFFERENT param, a construction, or any unrecognized shape ⇒ False (RelUnknown — the cross-position repair).

engine:totRelFlip.label: tot: flip a comparison
engine:totRelFlip.description: The relation read from the other side: `k > v` is `v < k`. gt ↔ lt, gte ↔ lte.

engine:totRelUnder.label: tot: relation holding in a branch
engine:totRelUnder.description: The relation `v rel k` holding in the TRUE branch (`truth`), or its negation in the FALSE branch: not (v > k) is v ≤ k, and so on. The negation is exact only for non-NaN numbers, which is why a false-branch relation never contributes the "number" fact.

engine:totRemoveAll.label: tot: remove-all
engine:totRemoveAll.description: Remove every name in `names` from `list`. Applies the shadow-removal of a binder's whole bound-var set to a smaller/scrutinizable set.

engine:totRemoveClosures.label: tot: remove closures
engine:totRemoveClosures.description: Drop every checked local closure whose name is in `names` (a binder that shadows it).

engine:totRemoveOne.label: tot: remove-one
engine:totRemoveOne.description: Remove every occurrence of name `n` from the name-list. Used for variable shadowing (a binder re-using a name drops the prior smaller/scrutinizable binding).

engine:totRemoveOneTail.label: tot: remove-one tail
engine:totRemoveOneTail.description: Recurse on the tail of a name-list for totRemoveOne. Internal split (keeps totRemoveOne free of case-in-let).

engine:totRootOrigin.label: tot: root origin of scrutinee
engine:totRootOrigin.description: The ROOT param of a destructurable scrutinee expression: when `s` is `EVar v`, `v`'s origin if it is itself a smaller var (transitively a param), else `v` (a param is its own root). Non-EVar ⇒ "" (unused — only called when canDestr already gated `s ∈ scrut`, so `s` is an EVar). Threads the "sub-term of WHICH param" fact through nested destructuring.

engine:totScrutDecreasable.label: tot: scrutinee destructurable
engine:totScrutDecreasable.description: True when the match scrutinee is a bare variable in the `scrut` set (a parameter or an already-smaller var), so destructuring it yields structurally-smaller bindings.

engine:totSctDecide.label: tot: SCT decide (over a non-empty graph set)
engine:totSctDecide.description: Run the closure and apply the SCT criterion: fuel exhaustion (Nothing) ⇒ False (a sound Unknown), else every idempotent in the closure must strictly descend.

engine:totSctTerminating.label: tot: SCT terminating
engine:totSctTerminating.description: The size-change termination decision for a function GROUP (slice C): no call-graph graph at all (empty set) ⇒ vacuously total; else the closure-based SCT criterion (every idempotent `f → f` graph in the transitive closure under restricted composition has a strictly-descending self-edge; fuel exhaustion ⇒ False/Unknown). The single-function case is the one-object special case (every graph is `f → f`).

engine:totShadowParams.label: tot: shadow source params
engine:totShadowParams.description: The caller's source-param list with every name in `binders` replaced by a `$shadowed:` spelling no variable can have. A binder (lambda param, arm pattern variable) that re-uses a source param's name hides that param for the binder's scope: an argument `EVar n` or `sub n 1` there denotes the BINDER, so the size-change oracle must not read it as the source param `n` (2026-10-03: `loop n` whose body applies a lambda that rebinds `n` and recurses on `n - 1` read Total). Renaming the hidden source slot removes every edge out of it in that scope (RelEq and measure edges compare names; a structural edge whose smaller variable was bound outside the scope is lost too — an under-approximation, never a false edge).

engine:totSlotPresent.label: tot: slot present
engine:totSlotPresent.description: True when graph `g` already has an edge in `e`'s (src, tgt) slot. Decides whether totAddStrongEdge merges (strict-dominance) or appends.

engine:totSpellingRoot.label: tot: spelling root
engine:totSpellingRoot.description: The lexical root of a variable or var-head spelling: the text before the first dot (`row` for `row.args`), with a var-head call's `$dyn:` marker stripped. A spelling whose root a binder binds is a local value or a field of one.

engine:totStrictEdge.label: tot: strict edge
engine:totStrictEdge.description: Append a strict edge {src, tgt, strict = true} onto the accumulator (the source param strictly dominates the target slot).

engine:totSubIsPMinusOne.label: tot: sub is p-minus-one guarded
engine:totSubIsPMinusOne.description: True when the `sub` sub-args `s` are exactly `[EVar p, ELit 1]` (the operand is the position's OWN param `p`) AND the branch facts make the decrement strict and well-founded (totCanDecrement). The k=1 fence (inherited rung-2b): only a unit decrement of p itself. Specialized from the retired rung-2 `totSubVarOne` — the var MUST be `p`, not any var in pos.

engine:totSubPOne.label: tot: sub operands = (p, 1)
engine:totSubPOne.description: Helper for totSubIsPMinusOne: True when `a0` is `EVar p` (the position's own param) and `a1` is `ELit 1`, AND the branch facts make `p - 1` a strict, well-founded descent in the runtime number representation (totCanDecrement: p > 0, p ≤ 2^53, p a non-NaN number). Any other shape ⇒ False (sound under-approximation — cross-position `sub q 1` at p's slot, q ≠ p, is RelUnknown here).

engine:totTail.label: tot: small list tail
engine:totTail.description: The tail of a list, or [] when empty — a total `tail` for the parallel param/arg scan (decreasing on the list, no indexing).

engine:totUncheckedApply.label: tot: unchecked apply
engine:totUncheckedApply.description: The apply form `$ callee args…`. An immediately applied lambda (the `let` / `where` / `do` lowering) walks its arguments in the current scope, then its body with the lambda params bound, each param whose argument is a lambda literal becoming a checked local closure (with the literal's arity) and every other param shadowing any closure of that name; applied to more arguments than it has params, it spills the rest onto its result and is refused. A variable callee is an invocation judged by totUncheckedInvoke with the argument count (no member graph: `$` builds none). Any other callee (a call result, a match, a construction) is a computed callable and is refused.

engine:totUncheckedInList.label: tot: unchecked reference in a list
engine:totUncheckedInList.description: True when any expression of the list holds an unchecked route (totUncheckedReference) under the same binders and closures.

engine:totUncheckedInvoke.label: tot: unchecked invocation of a named callable
engine:totUncheckedInvoke.description: True when invoking the callable spelled `name` with `argc` arguments (a var-head call's name with `$dyn:` stripped, or the variable an apply `$` calls) is a route the size-change walk cannot check. A name whose root an enclosing binder binds is a local: accepted only when it is exactly a checked local closure applied to at most its arity (totClosureOverApplied; not a field read of one); any other local (a parameter, a pattern variable, a field of either) is a callback whose body is never seen. An unbound name is accepted when `memberCallOk` and it may denote a group member applied to at most its params (a var-head call to a member has its size-change graph; totMemberOverApplied); when not `memberCallOk` (an apply `$`, which builds no graph), naming a member is refused and naming anything else is taken as a call outside the group: that such a name denotes a gathered registry function is checked by the kernel-gate entry (verdictTagForIn, anaAppliesUnresolved), not here — a group-only caller (the census, inference trust) must discharge it itself. An unbound var-head name that names no member is an unresolvable dynamic call (a local recursive binding lowers to one).

engine:totUncheckedReference.label: tot: unchecked reference
engine:totUncheckedReference.description: True when the core Expr `e`, under the lexical binders `bound` and the checked local closures `closures`, holds an executable route into the group that the size-change walk cannot check: an EVar whose root is unbound and which may denote a member (totHeadNamesMember — the member escapes as a value); a `$dyn:` var-head call the walk cannot check (totUncheckedInvoke: a callable parameter, pattern variable or field invoked, an unbound name that is no member — e.g. a local recursive binding — or a closure or member over-applied); an apply `$` whose callee is not a checked closure or a lambda literal, or that over-applies one (totUncheckedApply); a string-head call that over-applies a group member (totMemberOverApplied; a list literal's synthetic appendItem excepted). Lambda params and arm pattern vars extend `bound` and shadow `closures` for their bodies; arm guards are walked like bodies. Any extra binder only removes a refusal for a genuinely local name, and the member match over-approximates, so the audit can only turn Total into Unknown.

engine:totalityVerdict.label: Totality verdict
engine:totalityVerdict.description: The three-valued totality verdict for a definition: Partial when declared @partial (an acknowledged escape-hatch — hard-rejected on proof-carrying paths, accepted elsewhere), otherwise the rung-1 structural-recursion verdict (Total | Unknown). The gate consumer reads this: Partial is a hard-reject, Unknown a warning (a reject on proof-carrying paths), Total an accept.

engine:traversalSemanticSlotsError.label: Traversal semantic slots error
engine:traversalSemanticSlotsError.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — recursively validate every record, variant-case, and arrow-param container in a TraversalType. Delegates each container's key/wire/ordinal policy to fieldSemanticSlotsError and returns the first diagnostic. Nothing means the tree is identity-total.

engine:traversalSemanticSlotsErrorWithSo.label: Traversal semantic slots error with SourceHandles
engine:traversalSemanticSlotsErrorWithSo.description: Source-aware recursive semantic-slot validation for compiler/source-registry boundaries. Embedded UUID rules remain strict; only rigorously validated lock-less SourceHandles are additionally admitted.

engine:traversalSemanticSlotsValid.label: Traversal semantic slots valid
engine:traversalSemanticSlotsValid.description: Boolean projection of traversalSemanticSlotsError for already-structured Fenel callers.

engine:tsAppArgs.label: subset: tsAppArgs
engine:tsAppArgs.description: Phase 5 (E-app) — the arg-type list of a TtApp (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsAppHead.label: subset: tsAppHead
engine:tsAppHead.description: Phase 5 (E-app) — the constructor head name of a TtApp (else empty). Internal accessor.

engine:tsArrowParams.label: subset: tsArrowParams
engine:tsArrowParams.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the param list (TtArrowParam) of a TtArrow (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsArrowReturns.label: subset: tsArrowReturns
engine:tsArrowReturns.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the return type of a TtArrow (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsBase.label: type-subsumes: tsBase
engine:tsBase.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the base type of a TtRefined (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsBothMaybe.label: type-subsumes: tsBothMaybe
engine:tsBothMaybe.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — are BOTH marshalled types Maybe-shaped variants (a Just+Nothing case pair)? Internal helper for tsSameKind's variant arm.

engine:tsCaseFields.label: subset: tsCaseFields
engine:tsCaseFields.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the field list of a TtVariantCase payload (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsCaseName.label: subset: tsCaseName
engine:tsCaseName.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the name of a TtVariantCase (else ""). Internal accessor.

engine:tsComplementInner.label: subset: tsComplementInner
engine:tsComplementInner.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — the inner type of a TtComplement (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsFieldKey.label: subset: tsFieldKey
engine:tsFieldKey.description: Field-identity Phase 3 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — the validated semantic FieldKey of a TtField. Named keys carry UUID-backed FieldRefs and positional keys carry ordinals; embedded and scoped-effective wires are separate face coordinates, never identity.

engine:tsFieldRaw.label: subset: tsFieldRaw
engine:tsFieldRaw.description: Phase 5 (E-erasable) — the RAW (un-marshalled) FenelType of a TtField (else passthrough); passed to the isErasableType ctx-native (the Undefinable dispatch needs the raw `$`-keyed type, not the marshalled view). Internal accessor.

engine:tsFieldType.label: subset: tsFieldType
engine:tsFieldType.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the type of a TtField (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsFieldWireName.label: subset: tsFieldWireName
engine:tsFieldWireName.description: Field-identity Phase 3 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — the embedded wire snapshot of a TtField, never the scoped current projection and never identity. The complete face fence compares embedded and effective coordinates separately before this residual missing-key ambiguity check.

engine:tsFirstFieldType.label: type-subsumes: tsFirstFieldType
engine:tsFirstFieldType.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the type of the first TtField in a field list (Maybe TraversalType). Internal helper.

engine:tsIntersectBranches.label: subset: tsIntersectBranches
engine:tsIntersectBranches.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — the branch list of a TtIntersect (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsIsMaybe.label: type-subsumes: tsIsMaybe
engine:tsIsMaybe.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — is the marshalled type a Maybe-shaped variant (cases include both Just and Nothing)? Reuses universe-views' hasCaseNamed. Internal helper.

engine:tsIsVar.label: type-subsumes: tsIsVar
engine:tsIsVar.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — is the marshalled type a TtVar (type variable)? Internal helper.

engine:tsIsVoid.label: empty: tsIsVoid
engine:tsIsVoid.description: Phase 6 Step 3 — is the marshalled type a TtVoid ($void, uninhabited)? Internal helper (tsKind has no void case ⇒ checked directly in emptyW).

engine:tsJustInner.label: type-subsumes: tsJustInner
engine:tsJustInner.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — walk a variant's case list to the case named "Just" and return its first field's type (Maybe TraversalType). Internal helper.

engine:tsJustInnerRest.label: type-subsumes: tsJustInnerRest
engine:tsJustInnerRest.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — tail recursion for tsJustInner. Internal helper.

engine:tsKind.label: type-subsumes: tsKind
engine:tsKind.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the head kind of a marshalled TraversalType as a String tag: var / refined / opaque / named / variant / mu / record / arrow / map / tuple / tagged / other. Internal classifier for typeSubsumes.

engine:tsKindFormer.label: type-subsumes: tsKindFormer
engine:tsKindFormer.description: containment-substrate Phase 2 Step 1b — the tier-2 former tail of tsKind (split off for the per-decl token cap): TtUnion ⇒ "union", TtIntersect ⇒ "intersect", TtComplement ⇒ "complement", else "other". These surface the structural decider arms in containment.fenel (subset / empty / disjoint).

engine:tsMapCanonicalKeys.label: empty: tsMapCanonicalKeys
engine:tsMapCanonicalKeys.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — the CANONICAL key SetExpr of a TtMap. Deliberately NOT the raw `keys` slot: validation canonicalises before it recognises a finite card (`validationCanonicalSet`, validate.fenel:889) and BOTH slots are marshalled, so a judgment rule reading `keys` and a face reading the canonical form can disagree about the same type. Else passthrough. Internal accessor.

engine:tsMapKeys.label: subset: tsMapKeys
engine:tsMapKeys.description: Phase 5 (S-mapkeys) — the allowed-key SetExpr carried on a TtMap (the marshaller defaults an unconstrained map to the universe {$all}); passed opaquely to set:decideSubset for the map-key-domain ⊆ check. Else passthrough. Internal accessor.

engine:tsMapValues.label: subset: tsMapValues
engine:tsMapValues.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the value type of a TtMap (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsMaybeInner.label: type-subsumes: tsMaybeInner
engine:tsMaybeInner.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — extract the inner (Just-field) type of a Maybe-shaped marshalled variant as Maybe TraversalType. Internal helper.

engine:tsMuBody.label: type-subsumes: tsMuBody
engine:tsMuBody.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the body of a TtMu (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsName.label: type-subsumes: tsName
engine:tsName.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the name of a TtNamed (else ""). Internal accessor.

engine:tsParamType.label: subset: tsParamType
engine:tsParamType.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the type of a TtArrowParam (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsPhantom.label: type-subsumes: tsPhantom
engine:tsPhantom.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the phantom type of a TtTagged (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsPure.label: type-subsumes: tsPure
engine:tsPure.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the pure-ADT view of a TtOpaque (else passthrough). Internal accessor.

engine:tsRecordFields.label: subset: tsRecordFields
engine:tsRecordFields.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the field list of a TtRecord (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsRefinedSet.label: type-subsumes: tsRefinedSet
engine:tsRefinedSet.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a — the refinement SetExpr carried on a TtRefined (Phase-4a marshal extension); passed opaquely to set:decideSubset. Else passthrough. Internal accessor.

engine:tsSameVar.label: subset: tsSameVar
engine:tsSameVar.description: Phase 5 (E-var) — are both operands the SAME type-variable (TtVar with equal names)? Internal helper to ssVarArm.

engine:tsTaggedValue.label: empty: tsTaggedValue
engine:tsTaggedValue.description: Phase 6 Step 3 / type-substrate P1(a.8) — the value type of a TtTagged. It is the inhabitance-bearing slot UNDER THE VALUE-RECURSION READING ONLY (the phantom is type-level provenance); the live validation face admits exactly the UUID strings whatever the slot holds, which is why P1(a.8) fenced every SOUND-mode consumer of this accessor and left it serving the PICKER arms, a presentation filter. Carried by marshalTraversalType (engine-bodies-dispatch.ts). Else passthrough. Internal accessor.

engine:tsTupleItems.label: subset: tsTupleItems
engine:tsTupleItems.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the item-type list of a TtTuple (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsUnionBranches.label: subset: tsUnionBranches
engine:tsUnionBranches.description: Phase 2 Step 1b — the branch list of a TtUnion (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:tsVarName.label: subset: tsVarName
engine:tsVarName.description: Phase 5 (E-var) — the name of a TtVar (else empty). Internal accessor.

engine:tsVariantCases.label: subset: tsVariantCases
engine:tsVariantCases.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — the case list of a TtVariant (else []). Internal accessor.

engine:ttArrayExclusiveKind.label: disjoint: arrayExclusiveKind
engine:ttArrayExclusiveKind.description: type-substrate P1(a.5) — the rigid former kinds whose every IMPLEMENTED membership arm refuses host arrays, so a tuple (array-only) cannot share a value with them: record and unit, and ONLY on an un-peeled operand (see disjointW's rp flag). Deliberately excludes `map` (Fin-n key domains denote arrays — Vec(Number,3) is a $map and validate accepts [1,2,3]), `arrow` (the engine's callable gate accepts a decorated array), and — round 2 — `variant`, because canonical Maybe FORWARDS an untagged value to its inner type at the validate face, so a $variant kind does not imply tagged-object membership. Internal helper.

engine:ttArrowAligned.label: subset: ttArrowAligned
engine:ttArrowAligned.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 (STOP-clause soundness fix) — the post-flatten arity dispatch of arrowSub (the setAlgebraArrowSubAligned Tt* mirror): EQUAL flattened arities ⇒ the variance core (arrowSubVariance, nonemptyKnown-gated); arities STILL mismatched after flattening ⇒ the gated callable-tail refutation (ttArrowArityTail). Internal helper to arrowSub.

engine:ttArrowArityTail.label: subset: ttArrowArityTail
engine:ttArrowArityTail.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 (STOP-clause soundness fix) — the residual-arity-mismatch refutation, FULLY GATED (the setAlgebraArrowSubAligned mirror): every want-param must be PROVABLY inhabited (paramsInhab Just true — else the ∀ may be vacuous ⇒ Nothing, the gate the want-vacuous Just-true above makes near-complete), then a longer-have member applied to fewer args is a PARTIAL (a callable) ⇒ a provably CALLABLE-FREE want-codomain refutes, and a shorter-have member's value after its params lies in the have-codomain ⇒ provably CALLABLE-FREE ⇒ it cannot absorb the remaining want-args ⇒ refutes; both refutations still ride the caller's have-NONEMPTY gate (ttRefuteIfNonempty). A codomain not provably callable-free ⇒ Nothing (the refutation softens — e.g. a named alias that could denote an arrow type). Internal helper to ttArrowAligned.

engine:ttArrowCallableRefute.label: subset: ttArrowCallableRefute
engine:ttArrowCallableRefute.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 (STOP-clause soundness fix) — the callable-free-codomain leg of the arity refutation: the given codomain provably callable-free (ttCallableFree) ⇒ refute gated on the have-arrow's known nonemptiness; else Nothing. Internal helper to ttArrowArityTail.

engine:ttArrowFactorsPlanReady.label: empty: ttArrowFactorsPlanReady
engine:ttArrowFactorsPlanReady.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — every factor validation's eager preflight visits for an arrow: the parameter ACCESS PLAN (`ttSlotsPlanReady`, which checks slot identity and current-wire projection as well as each param's own readiness — a per-param TYPE fold would miss the identity half) and the RETURN type (`ttValidationPlanReady`). Mirrors `validationTypePlanError`'s `VtArrow` arm (validate.fenel:1095-1101). Internal helper.

engine:ttArrowFlatten.label: subset: ttArrowFlatten
engine:ttArrowFlatten.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 (STOP-clause soundness fix) — CURRY-NORMALIZE a TtArrow: while the return type is itself a TtArrow, pull its params up (`TtArrow ps (TtArrow qs r)` ⇒ `TtArrow (ps++qs) r`). The Tt* twin of the Se* arrowFlatten (decide-substrate 8λ.2-r): sound at the value-set level because Fenel's calling convention curries both ways, so the flat and curried spellings denote the SAME set of function values. Non-TtArrow ⇒ unchanged. Internal helper to arrowSub.

engine:ttAtomName.label: subset: ttAtomName
engine:ttAtomName.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 — does a Maybe nominal-name resolve to a KNOWN inhabited atom-tower name (emptyNamed = Just false)? The Tt* twin of checkCallableFree's SeRef arm. Internal helper to ttCallableFree.

engine:ttAtomNameKnown.label: subset: ttAtomNameKnown
engine:ttAtomNameKnown.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 — the emptyNamed verdict → callable-free gate: Just false (a known-inhabited atom) ⇒ true; Just true / Nothing ⇒ false. Internal helper to ttAtomName.

engine:ttCallableFree.label: subset: ttCallableFree
engine:ttCallableFree.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 (STOP-clause soundness fix) — is a marshalled TYPE provably free of callable values (the check.fenel checkCallableFree posture, Tt*-side): $void ⇒ true (empty); a KNOWN atom-tower nominal name (TtNamed / TtOpaque via nominalNameOf + emptyNamed — numbers/strings/chars/bools are never callable) ⇒ true; refined ⇒ its base (refined ⊆ base); opaque ⇒ its pure view; everything else (arrow / var / unknown alias / record — a closure object could inhabit an open record) ⇒ false (the refutation softens). Internal helper to ttArrowCallableRefute.

engine:ttDisjoint.label: subset: ttDisjoint
engine:ttDisjoint.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — the former separate refined-only Tt disjoint coarsening now delegates to the unified TraversalType disjoint member. Used by RHS complement subset and intersection emptiness; no second representation or predicate theory table remains. Internal helper.

engine:ttFiniteMapCard.label: empty: ttFiniteMapCard
engine:ttFiniteMapCard.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — the finite card a CANONICAL key SetExpr claims, if any. Mirrors `validationFiniteMapCard` (validate.fenel:787) clause for clause, deliberately including its permissiveness: RECOGNITION must match the face, and the WELL-FORMEDNESS judgment is made separately by `ttHostArrayLength`. A stricter recognition here would make the judgment reason about a different type than the one validation checks, which is the defect shape this phase exists to remove. Internal helper.

engine:ttHostArrayLength.label: empty: ttHostArrayLength
engine:ttHostArrayLength.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — is this number a card a host array length can actually take? Integral, and in [0, 2^32 − 1]. "Is it a Nat?" is NOT sufficient and this is MEASURED: `empty(Vec 4294967296 Number)` was `Just false` at entry while no JavaScript array reaches length 2^32 (the maximum is 2^32 − 1), so the type is uninhabited at the live face while the judgment called it inhabited. NaN and ±∞ are rejected by the RANGE test (NaN fails every comparison), not by the integrality test, so the conjunct order is load-bearing whatever a structural `eq` does with NaN. `-0` passes as card 0, which agrees with validation's `length == -0`. The condition is HOST-REALIZABLE, not mathematically natural. Internal helper.

engine:ttHostSortExclusive.label: disjoint: hostSortExclusive
engine:ttHostSortExclusive.description: type-substrate P1(a.5) — the ONLY surviving rigid-former disjointness rule: two rigid kinds are disjoint iff their live membership carriers are mutually exclusive on a host-value classification axis. Exactly the Array.isArray partition — `tuple` (array-only at its one implemented arm) against `record` / `unit` (each of which every implemented face refuses arrays for) — and its callers additionally require an UN-PEELED operand pair (disjointW's rp flag). `map`, `arrow` and `variant` are NEVER exclusive with anything: a $map's carrier depends on its unresolved key domain (Fin-n gives arrays, locale gives strings, enum accepts everything); arrowhood is a marker on a plain object that the engine's own callable gate reads without consulting Array.isArray; and canonical Maybe is a bare $variant whose validate arm FORWARDS an untagged value to its inner type, so a $variant kind implies nothing about the carrier either. Symmetric, and false on equal kinds (same-kind pairs coarsen elsewhere). Internal helper.

engine:ttNamedSortExclusive.label: disjoint: namedSortExclusive
engine:ttNamedSortExclusive.description: type-substrate P1(a.5) — is a named atom's host sort exclusive with a rigid former's live membership carrier? A scalar atom (number/string/boolean per containmentAtomicNamed) is exclusive with every rigid former EXCEPT: `map`, whose enum-key arm accepts any value identically and whose locale arm accepts bare strings, and — for String only — `arrow`, whose validate arm identity-accepts a fnId string (the Ref substrate's Codeable projection) while the Se arrow face merely abstains. Non-atomic names (array/unknown domains) never justify the claim. Internal helper.

engine:ttNnf.label: containment: ttNnf
engine:ttNnf.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — convert TraversalType union/intersection/complement formers to negation normal form with a parity bit; complements remain only above non-Boolean leaves. Synthetic nodes retain an opaque raw seed that no containment rule inspects. Internal helper.

engine:ttNnfList.label: containment: ttNnfList
engine:ttNnfList.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — map ttNnfPolarity over a TraversalType branch list. Internal helper.

engine:ttNnfPolarity.label: containment: ttNnfPolarity
engine:ttNnfPolarity.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — parity-threaded Tt NNF worker. Union/intersection swap under odd parity; complement flips parity; a negated leaf becomes TtComplement. Internal helper.

engine:ttRefuteIfNonempty.label: subset: ttRefuteIfNonempty
engine:ttRefuteIfNonempty.description: floor-kernel Phase 2 — Just false only when the have-arrow is decidably NONEMPTY (a maybe-empty have is still ⊆ — honest Nothing); the arrowSubVariance nonemptyKnown gate shared by the arity tail. Internal helper.

engine:ttRigidKind.label: disjoint: rigidKind
engine:ttRigidKind.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5) — the closed structural former kinds. Excludes named/refined/var/mu/app/other because aliases, recursion, or unknown denotations can cross shapes. NOTE: membership of this set no longer implies anything about disjointness — the former-as-sort model was RETRACTED; it now only marks that a closed structural former was written here, gating ttHostSortExclusive / ttNamedSortExclusive (which decide) and ttTopCover's not-the-universe arm. Internal helper.

engine:ttSubsetComplement.label: subset: ttSubsetComplement
engine:ttSubsetComplement.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — LHS TtComplement subset: picker mode preserves its generous Just true; sound mode decides ¬A⊆B through the shared Tt top-equivalence presentation topCover(nnf(A∪B)). Outside the exact structural pairing slice it remains Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:ttSubsetSortRefute.label: subset: ttSubsetSortRefute
engine:ttSubsetSortRefute.description: type-substrate P1(a.5) — the cross-kind subset terminal, which ABSTAINS unconditionally. Retained as the named anchor for TCB row t.sub.kind-mismatch and for any future restoration, which must clear three measured blockers: most kinds reaching here are not host sorts at all (mu/var/app/el/tagged/other/unknown were all being refuted); the empty set is a subset of everything and subsetW's only emptiness short-circuits are syntactic; and the subset walk peels `$opaque` without tracking it, so the kind pair at this point describes the pure ADT views rather than the runtime carriers (Int peels to $record but holds numbers; List peels to $variant but holds arrays). The disjoint face keeps its carrier rules because disjointW threads that peel flag. No consumer distinguishes Just false from Nothing here. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCover.label: containment: ttTopCover
engine:ttTopCover.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c / type-substrate P1(a.5) — exact Tt top-equivalence slice: complement leaf via inner emptiness; intersection by Kleene every; union by an already-top branch or P∪¬N=top iff N⊆P; void/known named/rigid structural leaves are provably proper EXCEPT `$map` and `$variant`, whose kinds cannot prove properness — an enum-keyed `$map`'s validation arm accepts ANY value identically, and canonical `Maybe` is a bare `$variant` that FORWARDS an untagged value to its inner type, so `Maybe (Map<enum,_>)` accepts everything measured; refined delegates to its base and, only when the base is top, to decideSubset top set. **type-substrate P1(a.8): the `$tagged` peel is RETIRED — this face now abstains for `$tagged` in every polarity (ledger `t.top.tagged`), because validation reads a `$tagged` by UUID syntax only while `matchesShape` recurses into the value slot, so top-cover reasoning about that slot reasons about a population no single face implements.** Anything else is Nothing. ⚠ RESIDUAL, RESTATED AND NOW MEASURED — the previous wording ("no such type exists in the corpus and none is a measured defect") is RETRACTED as inaccurate: this face still peels `$opaque` without tracking it (the `rp` flag exists only on `disjointW`), and an `$opaque` whose pure view is `¬$void` EXECUTES through the marshal boundary and was READ as defeating both polarities (rounds 9-10 showed it defeats neither — see below). MEASURED at P1(a.8) entry with `O = $opaque{name, pure = ¬$void}`: `empty(O)` = `Just false`, `empty(¬O)` = `Just true`, `sub(¬O, $void)` = `Just true`, while `matchesShape(0, ¬O)` = `true` and `validate(O, 0)` is INVALID — ⚠ but rounds 9 and 10 narrowed this to almost nothing, and the honest reading is now: that `true` comes from decompose's complement WILDCARD (context, not evidence); `validate` refuses every value of every complement except the exact universal `¬$void` (`Anything`, which it accepts), so it says nothing here either; and under the `pure` reading `empty(¬O) = Just true` is CORRECT. `t.top.opaque` is SIDE-CONDITIONED, not an executed false definite: the OPEN question is TOPNESS DISAGREEMENT — an opaque whose `pure` view and whose live carrier disagree on whether they COVER ⊤ — and no such witness exists yet. ⚠ NOT merely a carrier split: `Int` is one (`pure` a `$record`, inhabitants host NUMBERS) and `empty(¬Int) = Just false` is SOUND, because both sides are proper subsets of ⊤. This arm only ever emits "is ⊤" / "is not ⊤", so a split on the same side of ⊤ is invisible to it. It is a DIFFERENT shape from this phase's wrapper family (the `$opaque` carrier, not the `$tagged` denotation split), so under that phase's stop rule 2 it is FILED (ledger `t.top.opaque`) rather than repaired here. Internal helper shared by complement subset and emptiness.

engine:ttTopCoverAnyBranch.label: containment: ttTopCoverAnyBranch
engine:ttTopCoverAnyBranch.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — true iff some union branch independently has a Just-true top-cover proof. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverEvery.label: containment: ttTopCoverEvery
engine:ttTopCoverEvery.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — top covers an intersection iff it covers every branch; empty intersection is top. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverNamed.label: containment: ttTopCoverNamed
engine:ttTopCoverNamed.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — a name with a known value-domain category is a proper subset of the all-values universe; unknown aliases abstain. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverPair.label: containment: ttTopCoverPair
engine:ttTopCoverPair.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — one P∪¬N pairing: empty P asks emptyW N; otherwise ask subsetW N P, constructing only a synthetic TtUnion view when P has multiple branches. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverRefined.label: containment: ttTopCoverRefined
engine:ttTopCoverRefined.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — refined(base,set) top-cover: a proper base makes the refinement proper; a base already proven top delegates top⊆set to the shared SetExpr decider; an unknown base remains unknown. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverUnion.label: containment: ttTopCoverUnion
engine:ttTopCoverUnion.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — top-cover a TtUnion: a top branch wins; otherwise scan complement pairings. Empty union is bottom and therefore proper; a nonempty union without a decided pairing remains Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverUnionOf.label: containment: ttTopCoverUnionOf
engine:ttTopCoverUnionOf.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — collapse a nonempty branch list to its singleton or a synthetic TtUnion for the pairing subset query. Internal helper.

engine:ttTopCoverUnionPairs.label: containment: ttTopCoverUnionPairs
engine:ttTopCoverUnionPairs.description: floor-kernel Phase 3c — scan an NNF TtUnion for ¬N and decide N⊆P where P is every other branch; a decided polarity is exact, while Nothing tries the next complement literal. Internal helper.

engine:ttWellFormedMapCard.label: empty: ttWellFormedMapCard
engine:ttWellFormedMapCard.description: type-substrate P1(a.8) — WELL-FORMEDNESS of a map's key card: can any host value satisfy the card this type CLAIMS? This is NOT a readiness predicate (which asks whether validation holds an eager plan); the distinction is the answer to the review objection that the phase was minting a second trusted readiness doctrine. An OPEN key domain — one neither recogniser reads as finite, including a symbolic `{$expr}` bound — claims no card and is well-formed by default; the gate bites only where a FINITE card is claimed. It is nonetheless a NEW trusted predicate with its own ledger row and its own DISCRIMINATES pin. Why it is needed: `validationFiniteMapCard` (validate.fenel:787) accepts ANY numeric exclusive upper bound with no Nat check, so `$map [0,-1) Number` is recognised as a finite map whose key domain is PROVABLY EMPTY (`decideEmpty` MEASURED `Just true`) — without this gate the keys-empty clause would call it inhabited while validation refuses every value for it. Ledger `t.map.wellformed-card`. Internal helper.

engine:tupleAsIntersect.label: Tuple intersect witness (retired)
engine:tupleAsIntersect.description: Retired ISO-5 entry point. Field-identity Phase 3 makes the old positional-singleton decomposition invalid: list ordinal is semantic identity and cannot survive projection to a singleton field list. Returns the input unchanged rather than fabricating a key-invalid TraversalType; positionalNames is retained only in the pre-release function signature.

engine:tupleSub.label: subset: tupleSub
engine:tupleSub.description: Phase 6 Step 2b / type-substrate P1(a.7) — tuple pairwise ⊆: zip items, subset each positionally (covariant); length mismatch ⇒ Just false. TEXTUALLY UNCHANGED at P1(a.7) BY DESIGN: picker-mode ssApp folds its type-application args through this same function, so a fence written here would move picker decisions. The SOUND caller (ssCompositeSound) wraps it in ttKeepTrue instead, which retires both the arity and the slot refutation — they carry no have-nonemptiness gate, so a Void-factor tuple refuted while its denotation is empty. Internal helper.

engine:tupleToRecord.label: Tuple to identified record
engine:tupleToRecord.description: Convert tuple item types to an identity-total positional record. Each output field has PositionalField(index) and canonical wire projection _index.

engine:tvToMaybe.label: synthesize: tvToMaybe
engine:tvToMaybe.description: decide-substrate Phase 8λ.3 — project a TermVerdict onto the `Maybe witness` the inhabit faces return: TvFound w ⇒ Just w; TvEmpty / TvUnknown ⇒ Nothing. The adapter `seWitnessArrow` uses (tvToMaybe ∘ synthesizeArrow) on its const/vacuous Nothing tail. Mirrors search.fenel's svToMaybe. Internal helper.

engine:twoArgs.label: Two args
engine:twoArgs.description: Extract the first two elements of an arg list ⇒ Just { a0, a1 }; fewer than two ⇒ Nothing. Internal helper.

engine:typeAlgebraOperate.label: Type algebra operate
engine:typeAlgebraOperate.description: Phase 3 identity-total field/type algebra. Validates the recursive semantic view once, executes a FieldKey plan, and validates the result. wireName is used only by explicit rename/projection operations.

engine:typeAlgebraRecordRootPlan.label: Type algebra record-root batch plan
engine:typeAlgebraRecordRootPlan.description: Convert one host-marshalled TraversalType tuple of record roots into TaField batches. Record/refined/Maybe classification and expected-record diagnostics are Fenel-owned; fields carry opaque reattachment tokens.

engine:typeAlgebraTupleItemsPlan.label: Type algebra tuple-item plan
engine:typeAlgebraTupleItemsPlan.description: Validate one tuple root and convert its items to TaType in order. TypeScript supplies only the shared TraversalType tree and reattaches token facts on egress.

engine:typeArrowToSet.label: type-to-set: arrow
engine:typeArrowToSet.description: Project a TraversalType arrow to SeArrow. Parameter order remains positional while each reflected domain retains its semantic key and current wire projection.

engine:typeConstructorName.label: Type constructor name
engine:typeConstructorName.description: structural-dispatch Phase 3 / repr-retire 5a — the head type-constructor NAME of a marshalled TraversalType, the nominal-eq key for the universe-views. TtNamed → its name; TtOpaque → its `$opaque.name` DIRECTLY (List/String/Bool/Nat/Int/Rational/…); TtVariant → "Maybe" / "Result" when the case shape is recognised (Maybe-returns are stored EXPANDED, not as a named ref), else ""; everything else (anonymous record, applied-type with a marshaller-dropped head, type-var, …) → "" (no nominal name). Pure recognizer over the TraversalType ADT. Pre-5a this read the coarse `repr`-derived atom name (number→Number collapsing Nat/Int/Rational, boolean→Boolean); the precise opaque `name` is byte-identical for List/String and the principled fix for the coarse cases (the workstream thesis: repr was too coarse to distinguish Nat from Int).

engine:typeGrammar.label: Type grammar
engine:typeGrammar.description: The expression-annotation profile of the shared type grammar builder: seven named Ty productions plus tyAtom, tyAppAngle and arrowLHS, emitting plain-record type markers. Annotations retain their established no-refinement fragment. Declarations bind a separately named DeclTy profile of the same builder with inline refinements, so declaration support does not widen annotation syntax.

engine:typeIdentityKeepers.label: Type identity keepers
engine:typeIdentityKeepers.description: The keeper table of per-owner type identity: for each type name two bundles declare, the UUID its bare lock row pinned, the owner that keeps that UUID and the other owners (which get new UUIDs). Recorded once, never recomputed from module order.

engine:typeIdentityLockKey.label: Type identity lock key
engine:typeIdentityLockKey.description: The lock key of a type declared by an owner: type/module/<owner>/<Name>, the field-identity owner codec applied to the normalized type owner (system declarations use the owner system).

engine:typeIdentityLockKeys.label: Type identity lock keys
engine:typeIdentityLockKeys.description: typeIdentityLockKey for many (owner, name) coordinates in one call, in input order.

engine:typeIdentityRekeyPlan.label: Type identity re-key plan
engine:typeIdentityRekeyPlan.description: The lock plan of per-owner type identity: for every declaration in the identity roster, rename its bare row in place with its UUID, keep its owner key, or mint one; refuse a two-owner name without a keeper, a keeper UUID mismatch, an unrecorded owner and a retired bare key beside an owner key.

engine:typeIdentityRequired.label: Type identity roster
engine:typeIdentityRequired.description: Whether a declaration holds a type row: a system declaration unless it is parametric or a dispatch class (the retained system types and classes excepted); a bundle declaration unless the system declares the same name (a copy of a system type).

engine:typeIdentityRetainedSystemClasses.label: Retained system class identities
engine:typeIdentityRetainedSystemClasses.description: The dispatch classes that keep a type row although dispatch classes are otherwise outside the identity roster: they are registered by the system as classes only (no bundle declares them) and their rows predate the roster; registration already resolved them.

engine:typeIdentityRetainedSystemTypes.label: Retained system type identities
engine:typeIdentityRetainedSystemTypes.description: The parametric system types that keep a type row although parametric types are otherwise outside the identity roster: their rows predate the roster and registration already resolved them.

engine:typeMapMembershipPred.label: type-to-set: finite-map membership predicate
engine:typeMapMembershipPred.description: Author the canonical JSON-Logic predicate for a total Fin n map: exact length, plus the representable numeric or string element guard. Dynamic operator keys are data supplied to mapSet.

engine:typeMapToSet.label: type-to-set: map
engine:typeMapToSet.description: Project a finite-Fin-keyed TraversalType map to its canonical SeWhere membership predicate; open or malformed key domains remain unconstrained.

engine:typeNamedToSet.label: type-to-set: named
engine:typeNamedToSet.description: Project the named atom tower and otherwise preserve a named SetExpr reference.

engine:typeNormDetectShorthand.label: type-normalize: detectShorthand
engine:typeNormDetectShorthand.description: Phase 7a — dispatch on sole-key name; emit rewrite markers for $maybe / $list / $result, or fall through to generic walk. Helper to typeNormWalkObject; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormFieldsWithout.label: type-normalize: fieldsWithout
engine:typeNormFieldsWithout.description: signature-substrate Phase 1 — order-preserving TnField-list filter dropping every field with the given name. Helper to typeNormTryStripArrowRequires; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormFindField.label: type-normalize: findField
engine:typeNormFindField.description: Phase 7a — locate the first field with the given name, returning its value as a Maybe. Helper to typeNormTryRewriteResult; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormIsLengthCall.label: type-normalize: isLengthCall
engine:typeNormIsLengthCall.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — True iff the node is `{ call: ["length", …] }`. Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormLengthEqN.label: type-normalize: lengthEqN
engine:typeNormLengthEqN.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — recognise a `$where { ==: [length(value), <literal n>] }` SetExpr and return the literal n node (the `==`-only fence; inequalities + symbolic bounds ⇒ Nothing). Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormListElem.label: type-normalize: listElem
engine:typeNormListElem.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — extract the element type of a List-shaped base (`String`⇒Char / `$opaque List`⇒Cons.head / `$list`⇒elem). The String=List Char + canonical-List arms of the Vec normalization law. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormLiteralNumber.label: type-normalize: literalNumber
engine:typeNormLiteralNumber.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — Just the node iff it is a literal TnNumber (else Nothing — the symbolic-bound fence). Helper for the Vec normalization law; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormOpaqueListElem.label: type-normalize: opaqueListElem
engine:typeNormOpaqueListElem.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — navigate an `$opaque List`'s pure $variant to the Cons.head element type. Helper for typeNormListElem; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormTryRewriteResult.label: type-normalize: tryRewriteResult
engine:typeNormTryRewriteResult.description: Phase 7a — emit TnResultRewrite when the inner value has both `err` and `ok` fields; otherwise fall back to generic walk. Helper to typeNormDetectShorthand; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormTryRewriteVec.label: type-normalize: tryRewriteVec
engine:typeNormTryRewriteVec.description: array-substrate Phase 1a.5 — emit TnVecRewrite (⇒ `$map (Fin n) elem`) when the `$refined` inner is a List-shaped base refined by EXACTLY `length(value) == <literal n>`; else generic walk. The normalization law `refined(C, length==n) ≡ Vec n a`. Helper to typeNormDetectShorthand; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormTryStripArrowRequires.label: type-normalize: tryStripArrowRequires
engine:typeNormTryStripArrowRequires.description: signature-substrate Phase 1 — emit TnArrowRequiresStripped (⇒ `{$arrow: …}` minus the retired `requires` slot + a distinct boundary diagnostic) when a foreign `$arrow` envelope still carries `requires`; else generic walk. Capability constraints live on the function spec (judgment 2, design/signatures-and-contracts.md §6), never in the arrow value type. Helper to typeNormDetectShorthand; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormUnwrapFirstField.label: type-normalize: unwrapFirstField
engine:typeNormUnwrapFirstField.description: Phase 7a — extract the first field of a length>=1 list. Helper to typeNormWalkObject; tagged engine-internal. Prefixed `typeNorm…` to avoid colliding with normalise-to-core.fenel's `unwrapFirstField` which has the same shape but a different (JlField-typed) input.

engine:typeNormWalk.label: type-normalize: walk
engine:typeNormWalk.description: Phase 7a — main dispatch over a TypeNorm node. Helper to normalizeFenelTypeShorthand; tagged engine-internal so the editor catalog hides it from the public picker. Prefixed `typeNorm…` to avoid colliding with similarly-named helpers in normalise-to-core.fenel. See fenel/modules/engine/type-normalize.fenel for the per-function comment block.

engine:typeNormWalkArray.label: type-normalize: walkArray
engine:typeNormWalkArray.description: Phase 7a — walk each element of a TnArray, accumulating rewrites. Helper to typeNormWalk; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormWalkArrayInner.label: type-normalize: walkArrayInner
engine:typeNormWalkArrayInner.description: Phase 7a — accumulator-threaded loop over array items. Helper to typeNormWalkArray; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormWalkObject.label: type-normalize: walkObject
engine:typeNormWalkObject.description: Phase 7a — detect sole-key shorthand or recurse into fields. Helper to typeNormWalk; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormWalkObjectFields.label: type-normalize: walkObjectFields
engine:typeNormWalkObjectFields.description: Phase 7a — accumulator-threaded loop over object fields. Helper to typeNormWalkObjectGeneric; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeNormWalkObjectGeneric.label: type-normalize: walkObjectGeneric
engine:typeNormWalkObjectGeneric.description: Phase 7a — walk every field's value, accumulating rewrites. Helper to typeNormWalkObject / typeNormDetectShorthand / typeNormTryRewriteResult fall-through; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeRecordToSet.label: type-to-set: record
engine:typeRecordToSet.description: Project a TraversalType record to its synthetic empty-name SeCtor using semantic field keys.

engine:typeReferences.label: Type references
engine:typeReferences.description: Phase 7a — boolean shortcut: does the FenelType tree reference `targetName` either as a `$named` atom or as a `$tagged`-phantom entity name? Short-circuits on first match. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedTypeReferences` in engine-bodies-dispatch.ts. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/type-traversal.ts:typeReferences (now a thin shim).

engine:typeRefinedToSet.label: type-to-set: refined
engine:typeRefinedToSet.description: Compose a refined TraversalType base with its canonical SetExpr view.

engine:typeSubsumes.label: Type subsumes
engine:typeSubsumes.description: structural-dispatch Phase 4a / containment Step 2 / type-substrate P1(a.5–a.6) — `typeSubsumes have want` decides `have <: want` (can a value of return type `have` be used where `want` is expected) over the marshalled TraversalType. The picker-view of the containment relation's subset core: typeSubsumes = collapse(subsetW True) (Nothing → True — REACHABLE, correcting the previous "unreachable since picker mode is total": `subsetWK`'s want-side complement arm calls `ttDisjoint` with no picker flag, so a picker subset against a `¬X` want rides the SOUND disjoint face and can return Nothing, which this collapse then maps to True). P1(a.5)'s changed cells all moved Just true → Nothing and therefore kept their picker answers, but that is not a general admission-monotonicity law: P1(a.6)'s exact-Maybe M4 is a live-null-witnessed opposite definite whose flagless transit is `proved-refute-exclude`, with the direct picker route unchanged. A type-variable in `want` accepts any `have`; refined/opaque layers are transparent; at a `$refined`-vs-`$refined` leaf it consults the SHIPPED `set:decideSubset`, an undecided leaf falling through to base congruence (the picker's UX-honest default); named leaves match nominally; Maybe recurses on its inner; record/variant/arrow/map/tuple match at constructor level; tagged recurses on the phantom. The editor's FunctionPicker ⊆-arm; the precise sibling is `engine:subset` (= subsetW False).

engine:typeToSetExpr.label: Type to set expr
engine:typeToSetExpr.description: Internal presentation-only compatibility view of typeToSetProjection.set. Evidence consumers must use the envelope and reject known projection loss; the raw shape carries no exactness promise.

engine:typeToSetProjection.label: Type to set projection
engine:typeToSetProjection.description: Project a TraversalType together with the Fenel-owned known-loss flag. The set retains its historical presentation shape; degraded means evidence must abstain and inference must widen. False means no known projection loss was found, not that every independent type/map semantic rule is proved sound.

engine:typeToSetSemanticError.label: Type-to-set semantic input error
engine:typeToSetSemanticError.description: Validate the shared TraversalType boundary before type-to-set projection. Nothing means identity-total and structurally admissible; Just carries the first Fenel-owned diagnostic.

engine:typeTraversalAddName.label: type-traversal: addName
engine:typeTraversalAddName.description: Phase 7a — dedupe-then-append. Insertion order preserved. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalAddPhantomName.label: type-traversal: addPhantomName
engine:typeTraversalAddPhantomName.description: Phase 7a — dispatch on Maybe<String>; only append when the phantom resolved to Just. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCheckArrowParamsForR.label: type-traversal: checkArrowParamsForRef
engine:typeTraversalCheckArrowParamsForR.description: Phase 7a — short-circuit check across an arrow-params list. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCheckCasesForRef.label: type-traversal: checkCasesForRef
engine:typeTraversalCheckCasesForRef.description: Phase 7a — short-circuit check across a variant-cases list. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCheckFieldsForRef.label: type-traversal: checkFieldsForRef
engine:typeTraversalCheckFieldsForRef.description: Phase 7a — short-circuit check across a record-fields list. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCheckListForRef.label: type-traversal: checkListForRef
engine:typeTraversalCheckListForRef.description: Phase 7a — short-circuit check across a TraversalType list. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCheckPhantomForRef.label: type-traversal: checkPhantomForRef
engine:typeTraversalCheckPhantomForRef.description: Phase 7a — check whether the pre-extracted phantom-entity name equals the target. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCheckReferences.label: type-traversal: checkReferences
engine:typeTraversalCheckReferences.description: Phase 7a — recursive check: does this TraversalType subtree reference `targetName`? Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalCollectParamNamesByR.label: type-traversal: collectParamNamesByRef
engine:typeTraversalCollectParamNamesByR.description: Phase 7a / field-identity Phase 3 — collect identity-bearing arrow-param slots whose type references targetName. Arrow order is retained; keys never reorder the list. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalFieldsReferencingFro.label: type-traversal: fields referencing from type
engine:typeTraversalFieldsReferencingFro.description: Select an entity record through Refined and exact canonical Maybe wrappers, then filter its identity-bearing fields. Non-record shapes return the supplied empty list. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalFilterFieldsByRef.label: type-traversal: filterFieldsByRef
engine:typeTraversalFilterFieldsByRef.description: Phase 7a / field-identity Phase 3 — accumulator-threaded filter: keep identity-bearing field slots whose type references targetName. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalFirstError.label: type-traversal: first semantic error
engine:typeTraversalFirstError.description: Keep the first semantic-slot error, otherwise evaluate to the later result. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalMaybeInner.label: type-traversal: exact Maybe inner
engine:typeTraversalMaybeInner.description: Recognize exactly Nothing | Just<T>: two cases, nullary Nothing, and one ordinal-0 Just field. Returns that field's marshalled TraversalType, never its wire spelling. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalPhantomEntityName.label: type-traversal: phantom entity name
engine:typeTraversalPhantomEntityName.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — recognize a tagged phantom's refined-enum first member as an entity name only when it is a string. Semantic policy is wholly Fenel-owned. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalPhantomFirst.label: type-traversal: phantom first
engine:typeTraversalPhantomFirst.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — select TtTagged.phantom and apply refined-enum-first policy in Fenel. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalPrefixError.label: type-traversal: prefix semantic error
engine:typeTraversalPrefixError.description: Add a readable container projection to a semantic-slot diagnostic. Names are diagnostic only. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalRefinedEnumFirst.label: type-traversal: refined enum first
engine:typeTraversalRefinedEnumFirst.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — read the first value only when a TraversalType is a refined type whose complete canonical SetExpr is SeEnum. Internal helper; no host-side enum classifier.

engine:typeTraversalScanFnsForUsages.label: type-traversal: scanFnsForUsages
engine:typeTraversalScanFnsForUsages.description: Phase 7a / field-identity Phase 2b — stack-safe fold step over FunctionUsageInput entries. Emits one FunctionUsageEntry when a signature references the target. The former list-tail self recursion overflowed the browser evaluator on the repository's full function catalog.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticCasesError.label: type-traversal: semantic cases error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticCasesError.description: Stack-safe fold over variant cases. Case tags remain names; only payload axes use FieldKey. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticFieldChildre.label: type-traversal: semantic field children error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticFieldChildre.description: Stack-safe fold over nested TtField types, retaining the first error. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticFieldProject.label: type-traversal: semantic field projections
engine:typeTraversalSemanticFieldProject.description: Project TtFields to the shared semantic-slot validator shape. Raw source key/name/token/type metadata is deliberately excluded. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticFieldsError.label: type-traversal: semantic fields error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticFieldsError.description: Validate one record/variant field container, then validate every nested occurrence type. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticNodeError.label: type-traversal: semantic node error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticNodeError.description: Recursive identity-total validation over one TraversalType node. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticParamChildre.label: type-traversal: semantic param children error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticParamChildre.description: Stack-safe fold over nested arrow-param types, retaining the first error. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticParamProject.label: type-traversal: semantic param projections
engine:typeTraversalSemanticParamProject.description: Project TtArrowParams to the shared semantic-slot validator shape. Arrow list order is retained exactly. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticParamsError.label: type-traversal: semantic params error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticParamsError.description: Validate one arrow's local parameter container, then validate every parameter occurrence type. Arrow variance remains list-positional. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalSemanticTypeListErro.label: type-traversal: semantic type list error
engine:typeTraversalSemanticTypeListErro.description: Stack-safe fold over a list of TraversalType children, retaining the first error. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalWalkArrowParamsForNa.label: type-traversal: walkArrowParamsForNames
engine:typeTraversalWalkArrowParamsForNa.description: Phase 7a — walk every arrow param's type. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalWalkCasesForNames.label: type-traversal: walkCasesForNames
engine:typeTraversalWalkCasesForNames.description: Phase 7a — walk every variant case's fields. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalWalkFieldsForNames.label: type-traversal: walkFieldsForNames
engine:typeTraversalWalkFieldsForNames.description: Phase 7a — walk every record-field's type, accumulating names. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalWalkForNames.label: type-traversal: walkForNames
engine:typeTraversalWalkForNames.description: Phase 7a — main recursive walk for collectTypeNames. Threads the accumulator list through every visit. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalWalkListForNames.label: type-traversal: walkListForNames
engine:typeTraversalWalkListForNames.description: Phase 7a — walk every TraversalType in a list. Used by tuples + applications. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:typeTraversalWalkRaw.label: type-traversal: walk raw
engine:typeTraversalWalkRaw.description: Pre-order structural traversal over TraversalType, appending each raw node before its children. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalWalkRawCases.label: type-traversal: walk raw cases
engine:typeTraversalWalkRawCases.description: Walk variant cases and their fields in declaration order. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalWalkRawFields.label: type-traversal: walk raw fields
engine:typeTraversalWalkRawFields.description: Walk record or variant field types in declaration order. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalWalkRawList.label: type-traversal: walk raw list
engine:typeTraversalWalkRawList.description: Walk a TraversalType list in source order. Internal helper.

engine:typeTraversalWalkRawParams.label: type-traversal: walk raw params
engine:typeTraversalWalkRawParams.description: Walk arrow parameter types in positional order. Internal helper.

engine:typeVariantToSet.label: type-to-set: variant
engine:typeVariantToSet.description: Project a non-coercing TraversalType variant to a union of identity-bearing SeCtor branches.

engine:typedefFrame.label: Typedef frame
engine:typedefFrame.description: Assemble a `{type_def: {name, constructors?, alias?, opaque?, refined?, params?, discriminator?, directives?}}` frame: constructors get label=Nothing + fields {name,label,type-marker}; alias kept as a marker; a refinement `refined` marker passes through (base + enum/interval set kept as markers for the TS `$`-key marshal; a predicate set's Syntax lowered Fenel-side); @discriminator lifted from directives; params/directives omitted when empty (TS-parse parity). parser-substrate Phase 5a (refined: Phase 4h batch 3).

engine:unboxBoolFuncType.label: unboxBool func type
engine:unboxBoolFuncType.description: Build the (externref) -> i32 WasmFuncType for the $fenel.unboxBool runtime helper used by coerceDomain when produced=DomRef, target=DomBool.

engine:unboxNumFuncType.label: unboxNum func type
engine:unboxNumFuncType.description: Build the (externref) -> f64 WasmFuncType for the $fenel.unboxNum runtime helper used by coerceDomain when produced=DomRef, target=DomNum.

engine:uncurryType.label: Uncurry arrow type
engine:uncurryType.description: signature-substrate Phase A — normalize an arrow to its flat n-ary spine: DELEGATES the structural transform to ttArrowFlatten (containment.fenel — the floor-kernel Phase-2 curry-normal form; ⟦(A)→((B)→C)⟧ = ⟦(A,B)→C⟧), then re-derives container-relative positional identity at the new flat ordinals (the P3 container law); NamedField params ride unchanged. Non-arrow values pass through. Honest fence: duplicate authored wire names across merged layers have no identity-total flat spelling — downstream validation rejects that container honestly.

engine:unionRows.label: rel-solve: unionRows
engine:unionRows.description: decide-substrate Phase 4T Step C — append each row of a branch's binding-row list onto the running union unless a STRUCTURALLY equal row (valueMember / deepEqValue) is already present — cross-branch set semantics for the DNF union. Internal helper.

engine:unionToVariant.label: Tagged union to variant
engine:unionToVariant.description: ISO-2 bwd witness (LEFT-inverse only, design-lock §1.1): the partial inverse of `variantToUnion`. Defined on a `TtUnion` whose branches are each single-case variants (the tagged-disjoint reading) — merges their cases back into one `$variant`. `Nothing` on an UNTAGGED union (`Int ∪ String`) — that union has no variant preimage (it lost the injection tags). This is the precise content of 'variant : union :: labelled coproduct : lattice join'.

engine:unionToVariantFold.label: iso: unionToVariantFold
engine:unionToVariantFold.description: ISO-2 helper: fold a TtUnion's branches, accumulating each single-case-variant branch's case into one variant's case list; `Nothing` the moment a branch is not a single-case variant (the untagged-union refusal). Internal helper.

engine:unionTouchingIntervals.label: set-algebra: unionTouchingIntervals
engine:unionTouchingIntervals.description: Phase 7b-continuation — union of two touching intervals: wider lo, wider hi.

engine:unitLen.label: Source code-unit length
engine:unitLen.description: The UTF-16 code-UNIT length of a source string — the lexer's end bound.
