NOT `length` (which counts code POINTS via the `List Char` pure view): the driver indexes via code-unit `charAt`/`slice` (JS `String.slice`), so its `n` bound must be code-unit too, or the loop stops `(codeUnits − codePoints)` units early on files containing astral chars (the Phase-7k truncation bug). Code-unit length = code-POINT length (`length`) + the astral-char COUNT, since each astral char contributes exactly one code unit beyond its single code point. Uses only native `length`/`filter` (SHALLOW TS loops) — NO per-char Fenel recursion (a tail-recursive Fenel fold would overflow the interpreted stack on large files, the depth-test fence; `sum` is not in the compiled-parser native contract). For BMP-only sources the astral count is 0 ⇒ identical to `length`; only astral files differ (aligning the Fenel lexer to the code-unit TS oracle). parser-substrate Phase 7k.

engine:untaggedBuildCases.label: type-algebra: untaggedBuildCases
engine:untaggedBuildCases.description: Build output cases in candidate order from the Fenel-owned TraversalType name fold, deduplicating with base/base2/base3 suffixes.

engine:untaggedDedup.label: type-algebra: untaggedDedup
engine:untaggedDedup.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — first-free case name: `base` if unused, else `base2`/`base3`/… (untaggedDedupSuffix from n=2). Mirrors the TS `while (used.has(name)) name = base + n++`. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:untaggedDedupSuffix.label: type-algebra: untaggedDedupSuffix
engine:untaggedDedupSuffix.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — the numeric-suffix tail of untaggedDedup: return the first `base<n>` (n from 2 upward) not already used. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:untaggedFirstNonDisjoint.label: type-algebra: untaggedFirstNonDisjoint
engine:untaggedFirstNonDisjoint.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — outer loop of untaggedToVariant's pairwise disjointness check: compare cand[i] against every cand[j>i] (untaggedInnerDisjoint), returning the first not-provably-disjoint pair's error message (byte-identical to the TS oracle) or Nothing if all pairs are disjoint. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:untaggedInnerDisjoint.label: type-algebra: untaggedInnerDisjoint
engine:untaggedInnerDisjoint.description: containment-substrate Phase 6 — inner loop of untaggedToVariant's pairwise check: test cand `c` (index i) against each remaining cand `d` (index j); the first pair with `disjoint c.op d.op` NOT a positive proof (containmentProven) yields the not-provably-disjoint error. Helper; tagged engine-internal.

engine:untaggedToVariant.label: Untagged to variant
engine:untaggedToVariant.description: Desugar a list of candidate types into a tagged `$variant`, erroring when any pair is not provably disjoint. TraversalType classification and case naming are Fenel-owned; the host supplies only the canonical List-head FieldKey and authors the final `$variant` envelope.

engine:unwrapFirstField.label: Unwrap first field
engine:unwrapFirstField.description: Take the head field out of a JlField list.

engine:unwrapSingletonAst.label: Unwrap singleton AST
engine:unwrapSingletonAst.description: Extract the only element from a 1-element JsAst list. Used by CeDo's single-expr unwrap and CMUnary's single-arg path.

engine:upperOk.label: Upper bound ok
engine:upperOk.description: The upper-bound half of intervalMember. Internal helper.

engine:valTypeEq.label: Wasm valType equality
engine:valTypeEq.description: Structural $tag-equality on the simple WasmValType variants the closure-body lowering emits (I32 / I64 / F32 / F64 / Externref / Funcref). RefStruct / RefArray fall through to false since the closure body never emits them; full structural equality (with typeIdx compare) is deferred to a future commit if needed.

engine:validateBodySpellings.label: Validate body spellings
engine:validateBodySpellings.description: Validate one mechanically collected body-spelling batch against supplied constructor/function field tables. A known unambiguous constructor-pattern miss rejects structurally; unknown/ambiguous targets and record payloads that can denote positional arguments remain lenient because there is no unique name authority before Phase 5's type-directed classifier.

engine:validateBoolean.label: validate: validateBoolean
engine:validateBoolean.description: Phase 8a sub-step 1 — pure dispatch on ValBoolSchema (VbsTrue / VbsFalse / VbsCoerceTrue / VbsCoerceFalse / VbsInvalid) emitting a FieldResult. The TS wrapper does the typeof/coercion check + classifies to a schema. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateBoolean` in engine-bodies-dispatch.ts. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/validate.ts:validateBoolean.

engine:validateCanonicalFieldDeclaration.label: Validate canonical field declarations
engine:validateCanonicalFieldDeclaration.description: Reject declaration-level FieldDef label/UI values on the normal authoring path. Presentation belongs to UUID facets; the migration command is the only authority that lifts legacy inline slots.

engine:validateDate.label: validate: validateDate
engine:validateDate.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — Date string + set membership. The wrapper pre-computes new Date(str)/isNaN, contains(set, str), the SetExpr-as-value branch. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateDate`.

engine:validateFieldResurrectionUses.label: Validate field resurrection uses
engine:validateFieldResurrectionUses.description: Require every explicitly selected tombstone to occur in the desired graph and only inside its retained original owner (including inline-nominal descendants).

engine:validateFieldReuseVisibility.label: Validate field reuse visibility
engine:validateFieldReuseVisibility.description: Validate the complete desired owner graph against durable Field visibility. Owner-only Fields remain inside their retained origin owner (including inline-nominal descendants), account-reusable Fields remain account-local, and only explicitly repository-reusable Fields may cross the repository/account boundary.

engine:validateFieldTombstoneReferences.label: Validate tombstone references
engine:validateFieldTombstoneReferences.description: Reject a desired graph that merely reuses a reserved tombstone. Tombstones are admitted to normalization only so this Fenel authority can distinguish ordinary reuse from the separately selected resurrection action.

engine:validateFile.label: validate: validateFile
engine:validateFile.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — File descriptor structural shape check (notObject / missingUrl / missingMimeType flags pre-computed by the wrapper); body accumulates per-flag errors. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateFile`.

engine:validateLegacyFieldIdentities.label: Validate legacy field identities
engine:validateLegacyFieldIdentities.description: Reject UUID-as-name ingress until the one-shot migration has an explicit readable Codeable mapping. The host reports source facts but does not decide migration policy.

engine:validateList.label: validate: validateList
engine:validateList.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — array of inner items. The wrapper pre-computes notArray + recursively validates each item by calling validateFieldByType TS-side (sub-step 3 will port that); the body just accumulates errors + values. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateList`.

engine:validateListMergeErrors.label: validate: validateListMergeErrors
engine:validateListMergeErrors.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — append each error from `src` into `dst` preserving encounter order. Equivalent to `[...dst, ...src]`. Internal helper; reused by validateRecord + validateUnion.

engine:validateListWalk.label: validate: validateListWalk
engine:validateListWalk.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — recursive walk threading {errors, values} through the pre-validated item FieldResults. Internal helper.

engine:validateLocaleString.label: validate: validateLocaleString
engine:validateLocaleString.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — plain string OR locale map { [locale]: text }. The wrapper pre-classifies into a ValLocaleStringShape ADT (VlsPlainStringOk / VlsPlainStringFail / VlsMap / VlsInvalid) with each map row pre-validated (unknown locale, non-string text, set fail). Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateLocaleString`.

engine:validateLocaleStringWalkEntries.label: validate: validateLocaleStringWalkEntries
engine:validateLocaleStringWalkEntries.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — append one error per failed VlsMapEntry (unknownLocale / nonStringText / setFail). Internal helper.

engine:validateMarkup.label: validate: validateMarkup
engine:validateMarkup.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — Markup ADT structural check + subset membership. The wrapper pre-computes notObject / badCase / subsetName / subsetMatch flags; body emits FieldResult. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateMarkup`.

engine:validateNumber.label: validate: validateNumber
engine:validateNumber.description: Phase 8a sub-step 1 — Number / Int / Nat validator. The TS wrapper pre-computes Number(value)/isNaN, contains(set, num) (when a set constraint applies), formatSetError(set), and the SetExpr-as-value branch (pre-computed FieldResult from validateSetExprValue). The body dispatches on a ValNumSchema record. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateNumber`.

engine:validateRecord.label: validate: validateRecord
engine:validateRecord.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — recurse over declared fields with strict-mode checks. The wrapper pre-computes notObject / emptySchema / addedErrors (rejectAdded keys) + pre-validates each FieldDef by calling validateFieldByType TS-side; the body accumulates errors + assembles the output record. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateRecord`.

engine:validateRecordStep.label: validate: validateRecordStep
engine:validateRecordStep.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — one step of the validateRecordWalk: VrfOmittedMaybe / VrfRequiredAbsent / VrfValidated dispatch. Internal helper.

engine:validateRecordWalk.label: validate: validateRecordWalk
engine:validateRecordWalk.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — recursive walk threading errors + fields through the per-field ValRecordFieldEntry rows. Internal helper.

engine:validateRef.label: validate: validateRef
engine:validateRef.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — UUID-shaped string ref validator. The wrapper pre-computes String(value) + matches the canonical UUID regex; the body emits the FieldResult. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateRef`.

engine:validateSetExprValue.label: validate: validateSetExprValue
engine:validateSetExprValue.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — structural validation of a SetExpr-as-value. The wrapper pre-classifies the SetExpr's variant into a ValSetExprShape (SesEnumValid / SesEnumNonArray / SesIntervalValid / SesIntervalNonObject / SesUnionValid / SesUnionNonArray / SesIntersectValid / SesIntersectNonArray / SesDiffValid / SesDiffMalformed / SesKnownNoCheck / SesUnrecognized); the body emits the FieldResult with the matching error message. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateSetExprValue`.

engine:validateString.label: validate: validateString
engine:validateString.description: Phase 8a sub-step 1 — String validator with multi-select + single-value branches. The TS wrapper pre-computes String(value), Array.isArray(value), contains() per item (multi-select), contains() over String(value) (single), formatSetError(set), and the SetExpr-as-value branch. The body dispatches on a ValStrSchema record. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateString`.

engine:validateUnion.label: validate: validateUnion
engine:validateUnion.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — variant-tagged record. The wrapper extracts the discriminator key + classifies (empty / unknown / matched), pre-validates each field of the matched variant. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateUnion`.

engine:validateUnionBadKey.label: validate: validateUnionBadKey
engine:validateUnionBadKey.description: Phase 8a sub-step 2 — true if the union's variantKey is empty OR not in the variant table. Internal helper.

engine:validateWithHints.label: validation-hints: validateWithHints
engine:validateWithHints.description: Phase 8b sub-step 2 — top-level dispatcher for validateWithHints. Dispatches on VwhSchema (VwhIntersect / VwhUnion / VwhLeaf) and computes the valid flag via constraintsAllPassed/constraintsAnyPassed/c.passed, then assembles the ValidationHint output with Maybe-typed optional fields (cursor / fieldHints / suggestedNext / listHint). The TS wrapper does the per-constraint pre-computation + expandNamed + FieldHint/ListHint construction (the latter two are sub-step 3 carve-outs). Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedValidateWithHints`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/validation-hints.ts:validateWithHints.

engine:validationAccessPlan.label: Validation access plan
engine:validationAccessPlan.description: field-identity Phase 3 — build the one identity-total field access plan used by validation and JSON Schema. Rejects missing/malformed/duplicate keys, duplicate current-wire projections, and positional ordinal/projection mismatches before producing semantic/readable paths and known/required key sets.

engine:validationAccessPlanFromTraversal.label: Validation access plan from traversal
engine:validationAccessPlanFromTraversal.description: Field-identity Phase 3 repair — audit a shared TraversalType and elaborate its root record entirely in Fenel before building the identity-total access plan.

engine:validationRuntime.label: Validation runtime
engine:validationRuntime.description: field-identity Phase 3 / absorbed ux-parity Phase 16 — canonical Fenel-owned validation entry. Audits the complete identity-bearing type plan before value decisions, then owns type-branch selection, recursion, strict/optional policy, path/error accumulation, and record/list/variant result assembly. Host seams are limited to `$`-barrier marshalling, parser/codec leaves, registry facts, and set/dependent re-entry.

engine:valueMapStable.label: Value map stable
engine:valueMapStable.description: Positional Just/Nothing-PRESENCE equality of two `[{ name, val: Maybe a }]` assumption maps. Presence stability ⇒ value stability (first-Just-wins, no Just→Just' flip), so this is a sound convergence test for the parseNull Kleene iteration. Internal helper.

engine:valueMember.label: enumerate: valueMember
engine:valueMember.description: Phase 15 / decide-substrate Phase 3 Step D — true when a value is STRUCTURALLY equal (deepEqValue; scalars byte-identical to shallow std `eq`) to some element of a list. Internal helper for dedupe + the exact enum-intersection filter — object-element enums now intersect correctly.

engine:variantCaseSub.label: subset: variantCaseSub
engine:variantCaseSub.description: Phase 6 Step 2b / field-identity Phase 3+4 — one have-case's verdict: find a want-case of the same tag; present ⇒ variantPayloadSub with named UUID and positional-ordinal alignment. An ABSENT tag refutes only when the have-case is INHABITED (review F2: a case whose payload product is empty contributes ∅ to the have sum — its absence from want cannot witness non-containment); provably-empty ⇒ Just true for this case, undecided ⇒ Nothing. Case tags remain names. Internal helper.

engine:variantCaseTags.label: Variant case tags
engine:variantCaseTags.description: Project a `$variant`'s constructor-tag set (the marshalled `TtVariant`'s case names) — the scrutinee's tag set for `caseTagsCover`. The tag layer is a singleton dependent predicate per case (design-lock §1.3); this reads it off the cases. Non-variant ⇒ [].

engine:variantDiscriminator.label: field-meta: variantDiscriminator
engine:variantDiscriminator.description: Phase 10c sub-step 1 — read $variant.discriminator field on a FenelType. The TS wrapper pre-extracts the discriminator string into VdInput (VdHasDisc disc / VdNoDisc); the body returns the Maybe directly. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedVariantDiscriminator`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/field-meta.ts:variantDiscriminator.

engine:variantFieldDefs.label: field-meta: variantFieldDefs
engine:variantFieldDefs.description: Phase 10c sub-step 1 — record of per-variant payload FieldDefs from a $variant-typed FieldDef. The TS wrapper extracts $variant.cases and emits VfdInput (VfdVariant cases / VfdNone) with each nominal VfdCase carrying the variant name plus its original untagged FieldDef payload list. The body returns the VfdCase list passthrough; the wrapper materializes Record<string, FieldDef[]> while preserving each opaque field record. Boundary adapter; dispatched via `dispatchedVariantFieldDefs`. Mirrors implementations/typescript/engine/src/field-meta.ts:variantFieldDefs.

engine:variantPayloadSub.label: subset: variantPayloadSub
engine:variantPayloadSub.description: Phase 5 / type-substrate P1(a.6) — matched variant payloads reuse recordSubGated, including the full dual-coordinate plan/occurrence fence, semantic-FieldKey depth alignment, open-product absent-erasable abstention, and empty-have vacuity gate.

engine:variantShapeName.label: universe-views: variantShapeName
engine:variantShapeName.description: structural-dispatch Phase 3 — recognise a canonical inline variant SHAPE from its case list: a Nothing+Just pair ⇒ "Maybe"; an Err+Ok pair ⇒ "Result"; anything else ⇒ "" (an anonymous / user variant carries no nominal universe name here). The cases are TtVariantCase records; membership is by case `name`. Internal helper for typeConstructorName.

engine:variantSub.label: subset: variantSub
engine:variantSub.description: Phase 6 Step 2b — variant case-wise ⊆: every have-case present in want-cases (by tag) with its payload subset; have may have fewer cases. Folds mAnd over the have-cases. Internal helper.

engine:variantToUnion.label: Variant to tagged union
engine:variantToUnion.description: ISO-2 fwd witness (containment-substrate Phase 2 Step 2): re-read a `$variant` (marshalled `TtVariant`) as the tagged-disjoint `∪` over its cases — each case becomes a single-case-variant branch (its tag-singleton ∩ field-record), the union over them is the floor reading. Identity on VALUES; the iso is at the TYPE level. Works at the marshalled `TraversalType` level (the $-key barrier — the body cannot author `{$union}`). WITNESS, not rewrite: `$variant` stays the efficient primitive. Non-variant input passes through unchanged.

engine:vcaAnyDottedBinding.label: Carrier any dotted binding
engine:vcaAnyDottedBinding.description: Does any binding entry in this layout install a binder spelling carrying the runtime's path separator? Internal helper.

engine:vcaAnyDottedName.label: Carrier any dotted name
engine:vcaAnyDottedName.description: Does any binder spelling in this vector carry the runtime's path separator? The runtime's resolveVar splits a var spelling on dots before consulting the binder scope, so a dotted binder is a binding no read can name. Internal helper.

engine:vcaAssemble.label: Carrier assemble
engine:vcaAssemble.description: Package a reconciled carrier: its snapshot, its whole-ledger readiness, its live occurrence identities and its recorded fences. Internal helper.

engine:vcaBinderNames.label: Carrier binder names
engine:vcaBinderNames.description: The ordered literal binder spellings of a lambda layout's parameters — the vector the bidirectional lambda-argument rule binds against. A name the decomposition refuses to reproduce contributes the empty spelling, which the namesTotal gate has already fenced. Internal helper.

engine:vcaBindingForm.label: Carrier binding form
engine:vcaBindingForm.description: `let` / `do` / `where`: sequential binding forms that are NOT cases of the locked seven-case core Expr, so they carry an explicit unsupported projection while still bundling their children faithfully, at the exact segments the ledger walked.

engine:vcaBindings.label: Carrier let bindings
engine:vcaBindings.description: Bundle a sequential `let` binding list at VpsBinding, in the runtime's order. Internal helper.

engine:vcaBuildNode.label: Carrier build node
engine:vcaBuildNode.description: Build one annotated node: join every ledger row naming this exact path, check the joined row's raw spelling against the INDEPENDENTLY derived expected key, derive the occurrence identity and the closed route, and bundle the already-walked children. A path claimed by two rows is a closed fence rather than a chosen row.

engine:vcaCallExpectedKey.label: Carrier call expected key
engine:vcaCallExpectedKey.description: The raw spelling the ledger records for a call layout, derived independently from the layout: a literal callee name, the `$` vehicle's own spelling, an indirect `{var}` name, or the bare form name when the callee is neither. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCallOp.label: Carrier call op
engine:vcaCallOp.description: `{call: [callee, ...args]}` through the shared call layout: the callee bundled at VpsCallee when it is an expression position (the `$` application vehicle included), the actuals at their logical VpsArg indices.

engine:vcaCallProjection.label: Carrier call projection
engine:vcaCallProjection.description: The checker projection of a call layout: a literal name is ECall; every indirect head (the `$` vehicle, a bound variable callee, an expression callee, an absent callee) is explicitly unsupported. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCalleeChildren.label: Carrier callee children
engine:vcaCalleeChildren.description: Bundle a non-name call callee as an ordinary expression at VpsCallee so no nested use disappears. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCarrier.label: Validation occurrence carrier
engine:vcaCarrier.description: Build the occurrence-keyed annotated carrier for one raw stored body. Walks the RAW body through the shared form decomposition (never the re-lift), joins each ledger row onto the node whose path it names, closes the constructor reading alias so one runtime occurrence yields at most one identity, and fences any occurrence whose FROZEN source-frame target disagrees with the FLAT runtime target. Reconciliation is bidirectional and total: every row is claimed exactly once, every node that DEMANDS a row has exactly one, every node that demands none has none, and no two node paths coincide. DORMANT — mints no authority and has no production caller.

engine:vcaCarrierContract.label: Carrier contract
engine:vcaCarrierContract.description: The obligations any consumer of this carrier must satisfy — occurrence-keyed observation targets, no spelling keys, no fallback on a lookup miss, whole-ledger readiness before any table is populated, and flat-target agreement before any occurrence supplies evidence. Executable so slice 3g cannot quietly keep the spelling key.

engine:vcaCarrierVersion.label: Carrier version
engine:vcaCarrierVersion.description: The occurrence-carrier construction version, part of every snapshot. A table built by a different construction is stale. Takes a unit argument so the name evaluates to its VALUE in argument and record-field position rather than to a reference handle.

engine:vcaCollectFences.label: Carrier collect fences
engine:vcaCollectFences.description: Every closed fence reason the carrier records, in walk order. Retained as diagnostics; a nonempty list refuses the preflight.

engine:vcaCollectFencesKids.label: Carrier collect fences in children
engine:vcaCollectFencesKids.description: Fold the fence collection over a bundled child list. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCollectIdentities.label: Carrier collect identities
engine:vcaCollectIdentities.description: Every live occurrence identity the carrier issues, in walk order. Mirrored, aliased, inert and fenced nodes issue none.

engine:vcaCollectIdentitiesKids.label: Carrier collect identities in children
engine:vcaCollectIdentitiesKids.description: Fold the identity collection over a bundled child list. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCollectPaths.label: Carrier collect paths
engine:vcaCollectPaths.description: Every node path in the carrier, in walk order. Compared pairwise to prove injectivity.

engine:vcaCollectPathsKids.label: Carrier collect paths in children
engine:vcaCollectPathsKids.description: Fold the path collection over a bundled child list. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCollectRows.label: Carrier collect rows
engine:vcaCollectRows.description: Every ledger row any node in the carrier claimed. Compared by COUNT against the ledger to prove the walk reached each row exactly once.

engine:vcaCollectRowsKids.label: Carrier collect rows in children
engine:vcaCollectRowsKids.description: Fold the row collection over a bundled child list. Internal helper.

engine:vcaConstructOp.label: Carrier construct op
engine:vcaConstructOp.description: `{construct: [ctor, ...]}` through the shared constructor layout. When the payload's named-record reading is live the layout ALSO says the decision needs the registered field table a pure body does not carry, so the carrier walks BOTH readings — and issues at most ONE identity for them. Where the two readings provably COINCIDE (a plain multi-key record payload) the named side is canonical and the positional copy is a mirror; where they do not, BOTH sides are aliased and neither issues an identity.

engine:vcaCtorFieldCount.label: Carrier constructor field count
engine:vcaCtorFieldCount.description: How many constructor field-layout rows name one source spelling. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCtorFieldFirst.label: Carrier constructor field first
engine:vcaCtorFieldFirst.description: The field vector of the first row naming a source spelling, called only after the count is exactly one. Internal helper.

engine:vcaCtorFieldsFor.label: Carrier constructor fields for
engine:vcaCtorFieldsFor.description: The ordered semantic-key/wire-name field vector a registered constructor publishes, or the empty vector when the table names it zero times or more than once. Internal helper.

engine:vcaDemandSatisfied.label: Carrier demand satisfied
engine:vcaDemandSatisfied.description: Does this node's joined row count match its demand? Exactly one for a node that requires an occurrence, exactly none otherwise. Internal helper.

engine:vcaDoItems.label: Carrier do items
engine:vcaDoItems.description: The do-list worker: an inline-let item bundles only its binding values, in sequential scope; every other item is an ordinary expression. Internal helper.

engine:vcaDoOp.label: Carrier do op
engine:vcaDoOp.description: `{do: [...]}` — a FLAT statement list. An item carrying a `let` KEY has only its binding values walked, exactly as the runtime evaluates it; every other item is an ordinary expression at VpsSeq.

engine:vcaEnvSuppress.label: Carrier suppress
engine:vcaEnvSuppress.description: Rebuild the carrier walk environment with a replacement identity-suppression mode (the mirrored or aliased constructor payload readings). Internal helper.

engine:vcaFirstDemandViolation.label: Carrier first demand violation
engine:vcaFirstDemandViolation.description: The first node whose row count disagrees with its demand: a node that requires an occurrence and joined none or two, or a node that requires none and joined one. Internal helper.

engine:vcaFirstDemandViolationKids.label: Carrier first demand violation in children
engine:vcaFirstDemandViolationKids.description: Fold the demand check over a bundled child list. Internal helper.

engine:vcaFirstUnsupportedIdentity.label: Carrier first unsupported identity
engine:vcaFirstUnsupportedIdentity.description: The first node that projects to an UNSUPPORTED form and nevertheless issues a live occurrence identity. Nothing when no node does.

engine:vcaFirstUnsupportedIdentityKids.label: Carrier first unsupported identity in children
engine:vcaFirstUnsupportedIdentityKids.description: Fold the unsupported-identity check over a bundled child list. Internal helper.

engine:vcaFlatAgreement.label: Carrier flat agreement
engine:vcaFlatAgreement.description: Confirm the FLAT runtime route for this occurrence's raw spelling exists, is itself resolved, and names the same target as the frozen source frame. A missing flat route is a fence, not an admission: absence of a second opinion is not agreement.

engine:vcaFlatRouteExempt.label: Carrier flat route exempt
engine:vcaFlatRouteExempt.description: Whether an occurrence takes no flat runtime route at all and so has nothing to agree with: a known-op intrinsic, which `KNOWN_OPS` dispatches structurally before any registry lookup.

engine:vcaFlatRouteInverted.label: Carrier flat route inverted
engine:vcaFlatRouteInverted.description: Whether an occurrence's agreement condition is INVERTED — true only for a builtin-op-native FALLBACK row, where the frozen frame missed the spelling and the flat registry must miss it too. A known-op row dispatches structurally before any registry lookup and is not inverted; every other role uses the ordinary agreement.

engine:vcaFlatRouteRelevant.label: Carrier flat route relevant
engine:vcaFlatRouteRelevant.description: Which roles route through the FLAT runtime registry and therefore have to agree with it: a call, a bare registered reference, and an INTRINSIC rule — an intrinsic row means the frozen frame MISSED and the builtin fallback took over, so a flat registry that resolves the same spelling is a disagreement, not a coincidence. A constructor, a capability dispatch and a lexical binding do not take that route.

engine:vcaFnOp.label: Carrier fn op
engine:vcaFnOp.description: `{fn: [...]}` through the shared lambda layout: the body at VpsLambdaBody. A parameter spelling the runtime coerces but this walk cannot reproduce fences the whole lambda, exactly as the ledger does, and its body is then NOT walked — an incomplete binder set could mint a positive identity for a target the runtime never reaches.

engine:vcaFormOp.label: Carrier form op
engine:vcaFormOp.description: Dispatch one KNOWN_OP through the shared schedule, mirroring the ledger walk arm for arm. Only the forms the locked seven-case core Expr can express receive a checker projection; every other form is an EXPLICIT unsupported node that fences, never a strictified stand-in.

engine:vcaHashEq.label: Carrier hash equality
engine:vcaHashEq.description: Exact equality of two domain-tagged validation digests: same domain literal AND same hex. A domain mismatch is false — a boundary rejection rather than a hex comparison across incomparable kinds.

engine:vcaIdentitiesCollide.label: Carrier identities collide
engine:vcaIdentitiesCollide.description: True when two live occurrence identities in one carrier are structurally equal — the functional-identity violation the whole projection exists to make impossible. A hard fence, never a silent merge.

engine:vcaIdentityChecked.label: Carrier identity checked
engine:vcaIdentityChecked.description: The occurrence identity, refused first when the joined row's raw spelling disagrees with the independently derived expected key. A disagreement means the projection and the ledger walk are describing different positions, which no downstream comparison would catch.

engine:vcaIdentityOf.label: Carrier identity of
engine:vcaIdentityOf.description: Derive one node's occurrence identity. No row is inert; two rows on one path is a closed fence; a negative row fences with its exact reason; a suppressed reading (the mirrored or aliased constructor payload) issues no identity; and a positive row issues an identity only after the FROZEN source-frame target is confirmed to agree with the FLAT runtime target.

engine:vcaIssuesIdentity.label: Carrier issues identity
engine:vcaIssuesIdentity.description: Does this identity status issue a live occurrence identity? Internal helper.

engine:vcaKeyAsFnId.label: Carrier key as fnId
engine:vcaKeyAsFnId.description: The universal key-as-fnId call form, decided by RESOLUTION exactly as the runtime and the ledger decide it: the frozen frame first, then the builtin-op-native intrinsic fallback, then the unresolved fallback the shared plan attached (an inert `$`-marker with no children, or a single-field record literal).

engine:vcaLeaf.label: Carrier leaf
engine:vcaLeaf.description: A childless annotated node. Internal helper.

engine:vcaMatchArm.label: Carrier match arm
engine:vcaMatchArm.description: One arm: the pattern position as an explicit node (the ledger's non-total-binder fence lands there), the guard condition when present, and the body. Internal helper.

engine:vcaMatchArms.label: Carrier match arms
engine:vcaMatchArms.description: Bundle every arm of the shared match layout. Internal helper.

engine:vcaMatchOp.label: Carrier match op
engine:vcaMatchOp.description: `{match: [scrut, p1, b1, ...]}` through the shared match layout: the scrutinee at VpsScrutinee, each arm's PATTERN position as an explicit pattern node (which is where the ledger places its non-total-binder fence), each guard at VpsArmGuard and each body at VpsArmBody, and a lone trailing default arm as a body.

engine:vcaNodeAt.label: Carrier node at
engine:vcaNodeAt.description: Build one STRUCTURAL annotated node — one the ledger mints no row for. Joining a row here is a reconciliation violation, not a silently accepted extra.

engine:vcaPathEq.label: Carrier path equality
engine:vcaPathEq.description: Exact structural equality of two typed use-site paths — same length, same segments, same order. The injectivity the occurrence identity rests on.

engine:vcaPathMember.label: Carrier path member
engine:vcaPathMember.description: Is this path structurally present in the list? Internal helper.

engine:vcaPathsCollide.label: Carrier paths collide
engine:vcaPathsCollide.description: True when two carrier node paths are structurally equal — two distinct nodes claiming one position, which a duplicate sibling field key can produce.

engine:vcaRawRuleForm.label: Carrier raw-rule form
engine:vcaRawRuleForm.description: The raw-rule intrinsics (map / filter / reduce / all / some / none): the evaluated slots plus the RULE slot, which the runtime evaluates per element in a derived data context. Unsupported, because the rule's bare variables may bind to item fields rather than to any lexical binder.

engine:vcaReconcile.label: Carrier reconcile
engine:vcaReconcile.description: The bidirectional reconciliation: the claimed-row count equals the ledger's, every node demanding a row has exactly one, every node demanding none has none, and all node paths are distinct. Nothing when the carrier reconciles.

engine:vcaRoleTag.label: Carrier role tag
engine:vcaRoleTag.description: The closed role tag string of a use role — an exact total projection of the UseRole constructor, used as identity material rather than as a display name.

engine:vcaRouteKindOf.label: Carrier route kind of
engine:vcaRouteKindOf.description: The authority kind the frozen source-frame row published for this occurrence, so the flat route's own kind can be compared against it rather than only its target. Internal helper.

engine:vcaRouteOf.label: Carrier route of
engine:vcaRouteOf.description: The CLOSED route a joined row describes: a registered target with its authority kind, an intrinsic language rule, a lexical binder, a fence, or none at all. What distinguishes a registered function named `if` from the intrinsic `if` the checker reaches first.

engine:vcaRowIdentity.label: Carrier row identity
engine:vcaRowIdentity.description: The identity of one positive or negative ledger row. A resolved CALL or REFERENCE must additionally agree with the flat runtime route: the frozen source frame gives a local declaration priority while the runtime's key-as-fnId path asks the flat registry first, so two positive answers can differ and the disagreeing occurrence must fence before it can supply evidence.

engine:vcaRowLeaf.label: Carrier row leaf
engine:vcaRowLeaf.description: A childless annotated node that DEMANDS a ledger row under an independently derived raw key. Internal helper.

engine:vcaRowNode.label: Carrier row node
engine:vcaRowNode.description: An annotated node that DEMANDS a ledger row under an independently derived raw key, with bundled children. Internal helper.

engine:vcaRowRefused.label: Carrier row refused
engine:vcaRowRefused.description: A node that demands a ledger row and REFUSES its occurrence with a closed reason — the projection is unsupported AND no identity is issued, so the position cannot supply evidence. Internal helper.

engine:vcaRowsAt.label: Carrier rows at path
engine:vcaRowsAt.description: Every ledger row whose site path is exactly this path. More than one is the duplicate case the identity derivation refuses. Internal helper.

engine:vcaSegEq.label: Carrier segment equality
engine:vcaSegEq.description: Exact structural equality of two typed use-path segments — same closed constructor tag, same ordinal, same name/key. The triple is injective over all sixteen cases, so this is exact and not a heuristic.

engine:vcaSegIndex.label: Carrier segment ordinal
engine:vcaSegIndex.description: The ordinal of one typed use-path segment, or zero for a segment that carries none. Compared numerically, never rendered.

engine:vcaSegKind.label: Carrier segment kind
engine:vcaSegKind.description: The closed constructor tag of one typed use-path segment. A total projection; combined with the ordinal and the name/key it determines the segment uniquely.

engine:vcaSegName.label: Carrier segment name
engine:vcaSegName.description: The name or key of one typed use-path segment, or the empty string for a segment that carries none.

engine:vcaSnapshotEq.label: Carrier snapshot equality
engine:vcaSnapshotEq.description: Exact equality of two carrier snapshots — the body hash, the AST ABI, the parser provenance and the carrier version. A table built against a different one is stale, not merely different.

engine:vcaUnsupportedWithIdentity.label: Carrier unsupported with identity
engine:vcaUnsupportedWithIdentity.description: Does this node project to an unsupported form while still issuing a live identity? Internal helper.

engine:vcaUseIdEq.label: Carrier use-id equality
engine:vcaUseIdEq.description: Exact structural equality of two occurrence identities: caller, role, typed path, target identity and authority kind. The lookup key comparison — no rendering, no hashing, no surrogate.

engine:vcaUseIdMember.label: Carrier use-id member
engine:vcaUseIdMember.description: Is this occurrence identity structurally present in the list? Internal helper.

engine:vcaVarUse.label: Carrier var use
engine:vcaVarUse.description: `{var: name}` — the checker's EVar when the spelling is a literal, and an explicit unsupported node otherwise (the runtime coerces a non-string name, a spelling this walk will not manufacture).

engine:vcaWalk.label: Carrier walk node
engine:vcaWalk.description: The annotated node walk. Delegates form recognition to the shared `fdcNodePlan` exactly as the ledger walk does, so the two cannot disagree about topology; what this adds is the per-node evidence join, the checker projection, and the bundled child list.

engine:vcaWalkArgs.label: Carrier walk args
engine:vcaWalkArgs.description: Walk a positional argument list, each argument bundled under its VpsArg segment. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWalkFields.label: Carrier walk fields
engine:vcaWalkFields.description: Walk a record field list, each value bundled under its VpsField segment. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWalkSeq.label: Carrier walk sequence
engine:vcaWalkSeq.description: Walk a positional item list, each item bundled under its VpsSeq segment. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWalkSlots.label: Carrier walk slots
engine:vcaWalkSlots.description: Walk exactly the argument slots the runtime evaluates, from the shared op schedule, each at its logical VpsArg index. The unevaluated residue is not a child: the runtime never reaches it. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWhereBindings.label: Carrier where bindings
engine:vcaWhereBindings.description: Bundle a `where` binding list at VpsWhereBinding, in the runtime's order. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWireCount.label: Carrier wire count
engine:vcaWireCount.description: How many entries the projection table carries for one source spelling. More than one is an AMBIGUOUS table, and taking the first would make the answer depend on table order. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWireOf.label: Carrier wire of
engine:vcaWireOf.description: The effective wire name a source constructor spelling projects to, or Nothing when the authoritative table carries no entry for it. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWireTagOf.label: Carrier wire tag of
engine:vcaWireTagOf.description: The effective wire spelling for a source constructor, or the empty string when the projection table does not name it unambiguously. Called only after vcaWireVerdict has already passed, so the empty case is the unreachable safe default. Internal helper.

engine:vcaWireVerdict.label: Carrier wire verdict
engine:vcaWireVerdict.description: The refusal reason for a constructor whose effective wire name cannot be read as an ordinary construction: no projection entry at all, an effective Boolean wire (the runtime yields a NATIVE boolean, not a tagged value), or a source-versus-wire Boolean disagreement. The empty string means the construction reads through.

engine:vchAcceptOnly.label: Checker accept only
engine:vchAcceptOnly.description: Soften a decided verdict to accept-only: a decided TRUE stays, a decided FALSE and an undecided answer both become undecided. The synth face over-approximates, so its refutation is never a term refutation.

engine:vchAllNonRecord.label: Checker all branches non-record
engine:vchAllNonRecord.description: Every branch of a union is provably non-record. Internal helper.

engine:vchAllScalar.label: Checker all scalar
engine:vchAllScalar.description: Is every member of this enumeration a scalar the runtime cannot read as a record? Internal helper.

engine:vchAnyEmpty.label: Checker any empty
engine:vchAnyEmpty.description: Is any set in this vector DECIDABLY empty? The vacuity gate: a universal over an empty domain holds. An undecided emptiness is not an empty domain.

engine:vchAnyNonRecord.label: Checker any branch non-record
engine:vchAnyNonRecord.description: Some branch of an intersection is provably non-record, which suffices: an intersection is contained in each of its branches. Internal helper.

engine:vchAppliedSet.label: Checker applied set
engine:vchAppliedSet.description: The synth set of an application of an entry-bearing occurrence: exact (rule a), under-applied (rule b, the residual arrow), or over-applied (rule c, stagewise and Fenel-origin-only). Every arm requires the arguments to fit their unfolded domains decidably and the named-argument side condition to hold; anything unprovable is the top set.

engine:vchArgNodes.label: Checker argument nodes
engine:vchArgNodes.description: The argument children of a call node, in logical index order, or Nothing when the indices are not exactly 0..n-1. The order is checked rather than assumed: an argument vector whose indices have a gap describes a call this arm cannot align with a parameter list, and aligning it anyway would check the wrong argument against the wrong domain.

engine:vchArgNodesGo.label: Checker argument nodes worker
engine:vchArgNodesGo.description: Collect VpsArg children in encounter order while checking each segment's ordinal equals its position. Internal helper.

engine:vchArgsFit.label: Checker arguments fit
engine:vchArgsFit.description: Every supplied argument's synth set is DECIDABLY within its corresponding unfolded parameter domain, through the kernel. An undecided fit is a failure to fit — synthFromSig's own rule, transposed to the unfolded view.

engine:vchArrowReturns.label: Checker arrow returns
engine:vchArrowReturns.description: The immediate return set of an arrow whose parameter layer is EMPTY — the explicit zero-parameter arrow a zero-formal declaration projects to. Nothing for any other shape. Internal helper.

engine:vchAtomHandle.label: Checker atom handle
engine:vchAtomHandle.description: Is this named-set handle one of the projection's own atom-tower spellings, whose inhabitants are host scalars rather than records? Every other handle — including a named RECORD type, which projects to a bare handle exactly like an atom does — is NOT provable.

engine:vchBindingSet.label: Checker binding set
engine:vchBindingSet.description: The synth set of a binding form, threading Γ sequentially in the pure evaluate profile's own order. A let and an inline let are their last binding's set; a where is its body's set under its bindings; a do is its last item's set with inline-let bindings propagated forward.

engine:vchCallSet.label: Checker call set
engine:vchCallSet.description: The synth set of a call node, routed ONCE by occurrence identity and partition class: an entry-bearing occurrence takes the application rules, a rule-class intrinsic takes its versioned image, a rule-class constructor takes the constructor rule, and everything else — an applied lexical callable, a fence, an unidentified node — is the top set.

engine:vchCheck.label: Checker check
engine:vchCheck.description: CHECK mode over one carrier node against a goal set, under the Tri discipline: a decided FALSE is produced ONLY from an exact derivation — a literal's singleton membership, or a conditional whose both branches refute exactly. Every synth-routed node is accept-only, and an inline lambda argument takes the bidirectional rule.

engine:vchCheckBinding.label: Checker check binding
engine:vchCheckBinding.description: CHECK mode over a binding form: Γ is threaded exactly as in synth and the form's VALUE POSITION is then checked against the goal, so a refutation from an exact value position propagates rather than being flattened by an accept-only synth. Internal helper.

engine:vchCheckCall.label: Checker check call
engine:vchCheckCall.description: CHECK mode over a call node: a rule-class three-slot lazy conditional checks BOTH branches against the goal directly (the value is one of the two, so two exact refutations refute); every other call routes through synth, accept-only. Internal helper.

engine:vchCheckLambda.label: Checker check lambda
engine:vchCheckLambda.description: The bidirectional lambda rule against an exact arrow goal: a non-arrow goal is undecided, a decidably empty goal domain passes vacuously, the binder vector must match the unfolded goal arity exactly, and the body is then checked against the goal's residual under the binders. Accept-only in the refuting direction.

engine:vchChildrenOfKind.label: Checker children at segment kind
engine:vchChildrenOfKind.description: Every child whose segment carries a given closed segment tag, in encounter order. Internal helper.

engine:vchClassFor.label: Checker class for node
engine:vchClassFor.description: The re-derived partition class of the occurrence this node issued, or Nothing when it issues no live identity. Read from the identity itself rather than from the entries's class list, so a rule cannot be steered by a supplied classification the preflight has already re-derived anyway.

engine:vchClassify.label: Checker classify
engine:vchClassify.description: The pre-checker classification pass over an entries's entries: every over-saturated occurrence must discharge its certified-eta-stage demand by proving the stagewise rule's side conditions, or the entries refuses with the exact closed class. Nothing when every occurrence is carried.

engine:vchClassifyGo.label: Checker classify worker
engine:vchClassifyGo.description: Walk the minted entries, refusing at the first occurrence whose typed demand this slice cannot discharge. Internal helper.

engine:vchCombineIf.label: Checker combine if
engine:vchCombineIf.description: Combine two conditional branch verdicts: both decided true is true, both decided false is false, anything else is undecided. Internal helper.

engine:vchConstructSet.label: Checker construct set
engine:vchConstructSet.description: The synth set of a construction: the exact SeCtor over the effective WIRE tag and the child-aligned semantic field identities, with each field's set synthesised from its own child. Requires the payload reading to be DECIDED and the field vector to align with the children; anything else is the top set.

engine:vchDescend.label: Checker descend arrow
engine:vchDescend.description: The set reached after supplying k arguments down a projected arrow chain: whole layers are consumed in turn, and a partially consumed layer yields the residual arrow over its remaining parameters. Nothing when the chain runs out of parameter slots or a zero-parameter layer blocks the descent.

engine:vchDoItems.label: Checker do items
engine:vchDoItems.description: The do-item fold: an inline-let item threads its own bindings into the SHARED Γ so later items see them; every other item is an ordinary expression under the Γ built so far. Internal helper.

engine:vchDoSet.label: Checker do set
engine:vchDoSet.description: A do form's set: items in sequence, an inline-let item folding its bindings into Γ for the LATER items, the form's value being the last item's set. Internal helper.

engine:vchEntryByUseId.label: Checker entry by use id
engine:vchEntryByUseId.description: The entries entry keyed by one occurrence identity. Internal helper.

engine:vchEntryFor.label: Checker entry for node
engine:vchEntryFor.description: The minted entries entry for the occurrence this node ISSUED, or Nothing when the node issues no live identity or the entries carries no entry for it. A miss is a miss: there is no fallback to a function-id lookup, because a use-site miss falling back to a function id is exactly the second evidence channel this arm may not have.

engine:vchEntryRefusal.label: Checker entry refusal
engine:vchEntryRefusal.description: The closed class of one entry's undischargeable demand, or Nothing when it is carried. An over-saturated occurrence needs a Fenel-bodied origin, a decidable named-argument shape and a provable stagewise chain; anything else in that family refuses by name so the census can count it.

engine:vchFoldBindings.label: Checker fold bindings
engine:vchFoldBindings.description: Fold a binding-child list into Γ sequentially, returning the extended Γ and the LAST binding's set. Internal helper.

engine:vchGammaBind.label: Checker gamma bind
engine:vchGammaBind.description: Extend Γ with one binding, at the FRONT so it shadows an existing binding at the same spelling. Internal helper.

engine:vchGammaLookup.label: Checker gamma lookup
engine:vchGammaLookup.description: The set bound to a name in Γ, scanning head-first so a later binding shadows an earlier one at the same spelling. Nothing when the name is unbound.

engine:vchGammaThrough.label: Checker gamma through segment
engine:vchGammaThrough.description: Γ as it stands after descending through one path segment: unchanged, or emptied when the segment crosses an untracked binder boundary. Internal helper.

engine:vchIfImage.label: Checker if image
engine:vchIfImage.description: The image of a three-slot lazy conditional: the normalized union of the then and else branch synths, because the value IS one of the two and the condition only selects. A shorter form's missing-else value is host-null, which is not representable, so it stays the top set. Internal helper.

engine:vchIntrinsicSet.label: Checker intrinsic set
engine:vchIntrinsicSet.description: The synth set of a rule-class intrinsic occurrence, selected by the versioned rule id the shared decomposition derived: a lazy three-slot conditional is the union of its branch synths, a notation op is the propagate transfer over its argument synths, and every other intrinsic form is the top set.

engine:vchIsInlineLet.label: Checker is inline let
engine:vchIsInlineLet.description: Is this projection a do item's inline binding group? Internal helper.

engine:vchIsLazyIf.label: Checker is lazy if
engine:vchIsLazyIf.description: Is this node a RULE-CLASS occurrence of the lazy conditional language rule? Decided on the re-derived class plus the versioned rule id, never on the spelling — a registered function named `if` is entry-bearing and takes the application rules in BOTH directions. Internal helper.

engine:vchLetSet.label: Checker let set
engine:vchLetSet.description: A sequential binding list's set: each binding's value synthesised under the bindings before it, the form's value being the last one. An empty binding list is the top set. Internal helper.

engine:vchLitSet.label: Checker literal set
engine:vchLitSet.description: The singleton set of a scalar literal node, or the top set for a shape whose value this arm does not represent.

engine:vchNamedArgumentSafe.label: Checker named-argument safe
engine:vchNamedArgumentSafe.description: Does the named-argument reorder hazard provably not apply to this argument vector? A count other than one is vacuously safe; a single argument is safe only when its synthesised set is provably not a record.

engine:vchNamedCallerHazard.label: Checker named caller hazard
engine:vchNamedCallerHazard.description: Could a single-record invocation of this caller be reordered into positional arguments? True whenever it declares at least one formal and its FIRST declared domain is not provably a non-record — the exact precondition the runtime's named-argument expansion needs. A zero-formal caller cannot be reordered.

engine:vchParamSets.label: Checker param sets
engine:vchParamSets.description: The parameter SETS of one arrow layer, in declaration order. Internal helper.

engine:vchProvablyNonRecord.label: Checker provably non-record
engine:vchProvablyNonRecord.description: Is every inhabitant of this set provably NOT an untagged record? A scalar enumeration, an ordered interval, an arrow and a constructor set whose tag reaches the wire are; a union is only when EVERY branch is, an intersection when ANY branch is. A name handle, a fixpoint, a predicate, a pattern and the top set are NOT provable — the explicit safe default, because the consequence of guessing is a call whose arguments the runtime silently reorders.

engine:vchSeedGamma.label: Checker seed gamma
engine:vchSeedGamma.description: Bind an ordered name vector to an ordered set vector, stopping at the shorter. The seeding used for both a lambda's own binders and the caller's formals.

engine:vchSegMasks.label: Checker segment masks gamma
engine:vchSegMasks.description: Does descending through this path segment cross a binder-introducing boundary the arm does not track? A lambda body and every match-arm position do; the rest do not. Crossing one masks Γ entirely.

engine:vchStageResult.label: Checker stage result
engine:vchStageResult.description: The set an application of k arguments to a target of declaredArity formals produces. A zero-formal target's only exact application is the zero-argument one, which applies its explicit zero-parameter layer; every other arity descends the chain by k.

engine:vchStagewiseSet.label: Checker stagewise set
engine:vchStagewiseSet.description: The synth set of an OVER-applied entry-bearing occurrence: the top set, always. The stagewise rule is not sound without residual-callable provenance — the leftovers go to the RESULT, whose implementation origin no projected set carries — so the occurrence claims nothing here and refuses at the classifier.

engine:vchSuppliedOf.label: Checker supplied of saturation
engine:vchSuppliedOf.description: The argument count a saturation describes, expressed against the declared arity: an exact application supplies exactly the declared count, an under- or over-application carries its own. Internal helper.

engine:vchSynth.label: Checker synth
engine:vchSynth.description: SYNTH mode over one carrier node: an over-approximating set for the values the node can produce. A literal is its singleton; a Γ-class read is its Γ set; an entry-bearing occurrence is its own entry's instance or application result; a rule-class occurrence is its versioned rule image; a binding form threads Γ in the pure profile's order. Everything else is the top set.

engine:vchSynthAll.label: Checker synth all
engine:vchSynthAll.description: The synth sets of a node list, in order. Internal helper.

engine:vchTake.label: Checker take
engine:vchTake.description: The first n elements of a list, in order. Internal helper.

engine:vchUnfold.label: Checker unfold arrow
engine:vchUnfold.description: Flatten a projected curried arrow chain into all of its parameter sets, in order, plus the terminal return set. A non-arrow flattens to no parameters and itself.

engine:vchValidateFunction.label: Checker validate function
engine:vchValidateFunction.description: The whole-FUNCTION membership verdict: the caller's own declared arrow, Γ seeded over its declared formal names, the vacuity gate FIRST, then the body checked against the set at its declared-arity boundary. A decided true passes; a decided false refutes; anything else is indeterminate with a closed reason.

engine:vchVarSet.label: Checker variable set
engine:vchVarSet.description: The synth set of a variable node: a Γ-class lexical read reads Γ (a miss is the top set), an entry-bearing function reference is that occurrence's own minted instance, and every other identity is the top set.

engine:vchVerdictKey.label: Checker verdict key
engine:vchVerdictKey.description: The closed tag of a checker verdict, for diagnostics and test pins.

engine:vchVerdictOf.label: Checker verdict of
engine:vchVerdictOf.description: Project a Tri check verdict into the closed checker verdict. An undecided answer is INDETERMINATE with a closed reason, never a pass.

engine:vchWhereSet.label: Checker where set
engine:vchWhereSet.description: A where form's set: its bindings threaded first, then its body synthesised under them. Internal helper.

engine:vckEntriesCollide.label: Carrier table entries collide
engine:vckEntriesCollide.description: True when two table entries carry structurally equal occurrence keys. Internal helper.

engine:vckEntriesShareSnapshot.label: Carrier table entries share snapshot
engine:vckEntriesShareSnapshot.description: Every table entry was built against exactly this carrier's snapshot. Internal helper.

engine:vckEntryKeyMember.label: Carrier table key member
engine:vckEntryKeyMember.description: Is this occurrence key structurally present among these entries? Internal helper.

engine:vckEveryIdentityHasEntry.label: Carrier every identity has entry
engine:vckEveryIdentityHasEntry.description: Every live occurrence identity has exactly one table entry. Internal helper.

engine:vckLedgerReadiness.label: Carrier ledger readiness
engine:vckLedgerReadiness.description: The WHOLE-LEDGER readiness judgment the aggregate LgoLedger result does not make: any fencing negative row (fenced / missing / ambiguous / dynamic-reflective) refuses the whole ledger, so a positive lookup can never bypass a sibling negative row. A lexical row is a positive occurrence whose monotype a later solve supplies, and is reported separately rather than as a fence.

engine:vckLookup.label: Carrier occurrence lookup
engine:vckLookup.description: The occurrence-keyed instance lookup, with NO FALLBACK OF ANY KIND. A miss is Nothing — never the function id's instance, never the public registry's declaration, never the top set, never a different use's instance. Two uses of the same quantified function in one body therefore receive different ground arrows or none.

engine:vckPendingKindOf.label: Carrier pending kind of detail
engine:vckPendingKindOf.description: The TYPED evidence demand a dynamic-or-reflective row is waiting for, or Nothing when nothing can discharge it. Total over the ledger's closed seventeen-spelling detail vocabulary, defaulting to Nothing — a final fence — so an unclassified spelling can never be treated as pending.

engine:vckPreflightTable.label: Carrier occurrence preflight
engine:vckPreflightTable.description: The DORMANT, NON-AUTHORITATIVE preflight. Refuses before any consumer entry when the whole ledger is not structurally ready, when the carrier recorded any fence, when an entry's snapshot is not this carrier's, when a live identity has no entry, when an entry names no live identity, or when either side carries a duplicate. It is a preflight rather than a checker branch because the checker's own result type cannot publish an Indeterminate. NO production caller, and no fallback anywhere.

engine:vckReadinessGo.label: Carrier readiness worker
engine:vckReadinessGo.description: Scan every ledger row once: the first UNDISCHARGEABLE negative refuses the whole ledger immediately; a row whose evidence demand is nameable accumulates as a TYPED pending entry. A dynamic row whose detail names no known demand is FINAL, not pending — the safe direction, and the default over a closed vocabulary. Internal helper.

engine:vckRowNeedsEtaStage.label: Carrier row needs eta stage
engine:vckRowNeedsEtaStage.description: Does this RESOLVED row carry the over-application demand? True only for a CALL role whose saturation is over — a reference is exact by construction and a constructor's extra arguments become extra positional fields rather than an eta tail.

engine:verdictTagFor.label: Totality verdict tag for a subject function
engine:verdictTagFor.description: THE KERNEL-GATE projection (unified-static-analysis Phase 3g): the totality verdict TAG ("Total" | "Unknown" | "Partial") for `subjectId`, run over the subject + its pre-gathered reachable function records (the {id, params, body, declaredPartial, analyzable} shape censusFunctions takes). TRANSITIVE (2026-10-02 — the earlier text claimed callee folding that analyzeFunctions never did, so a total caller of a non-terminating callee read Total): the call graph is built with spelling-normalized callees over EVERY gathered id (anaSpellingTargets — analyzable or not), the subject's forward reach is taken (anaReachStep), and the verdict is Total only when every reached record lowered (a reached Unanalyzable body ⇒ "Unknown") and every strongly-connected group among the reached records passes analyzeGroup (checkMutualTotality, or Partial for a declared @partial member). The subject's own group verdict is returned when it is not Total; a non-Total callee group makes a Total subject "Unknown" (callee groups are analyzed singletons first and only until the first non-Total one, since a multi-member size-change closure is the expensive step). A subject absent from the records, a reached id with no record, or an exhausted reach bound ⇒ "Unknown" — never a silent "Total". Ids outside the records stay sinks here: verdictTagForIn (the kernel entry) decides the bodyless natives the seam gathers before calling this, and passes only the bodied records. The TS seam threads the result into the kernel's SampleTestResult/PropForall arm, which REJECTS "Unknown"/"Partial" (vpSample). ADVISORY no longer — THIS is the consumer that makes the totality checker load-bearing.

engine:verdictTagForIn.label: Totality verdict tag for a subject function, against the registry ids
engine:verdictTagForIn.description: THE KERNEL-GATE ENTRY (kernel.ts subjectTotalityVerdict dispatches it with the gathered records and the registry's id list, since 2026-10-03). Native records (anaIsNative: bodyless functions the seam gathered) are decided first: a native subject is Total exactly when it is a certified terminating leaf (anaCertifiedNativeLeaves), and any reached native that is not certified makes the verdict "Unknown" (a native that evaluates caller-supplied code can re-enter anything). The bodied records' trusted primitive heads are canonicalized (anaCanonicalizeTrusted: the size-change oracle reads facts only off canonical std ids) and their callees resolved once against the whole registry; a resolved callee with no gathered record ⇒ "Unknown" (anaAnyUngathered, 2026-10-03: a callee the seam lost is no evidence of termination, and a certified native is a sink only when present as a native record). The decision over the bodied records then runs on that adjacency restricted to them (anaVerdictTagOver, verdictTagFor's body; natives are absent there, so a gathered certified native stays a sink), followed by the refusal verdictTagFor cannot make without the registry's id set: a gathered body that APPLIES a reference denoting NO registry id ⇒ "Unknown" (anaAppliesUnchecked: a string call head other than the `if` form, the variable callee of a `$` apply, or a var-head call, whose root no binder binds; 2026-10-03 — before, only string call heads were checked, so `m.k.run $ x` over a bundle member holding the subject read Total), or that applies a gathered bodied function to more arguments than its params ⇒ "Unknown" (anaOverApplies: the evaluator spills the leftovers onto the result, invoking a value the analysis never checked — `idf p r` where p came from data). Such an unresolved reference is a class-method name resolved by dispatch (`fmap`), a host leaf the registry does not hold, a bundle or instance member path, or a free local recursive binding, and may re-enter the subject's group unseen. Applies to every gathered record (the kernel seam gathers exactly the subject's reach).

engine:verifyJudgment.label: Verify judgment
engine:verifyJudgment.description: The one-judgment kernel core (decide-substrate Phase 2). Re-checks a JEmpty/JInhabited lattice claim against ReDecide evidence: the pre-computed witness anti-repurpose facts (witnessLeft always; witnessRight when twoSided — subset/disjoint) must hold, then the pre-computed tri-precision `decision` string is consumed by POLARITY — JEmpty accepts "true" (the set is empty ⇒ ⊆/disjoint/empty holds), JInhabited accepts "false" (the set is non-empty ⇒ inhabited). Ok ⇒ SolverChecked. Subsumes the retired vpDecideTwo/vpDecideOne/vpDecideInhabited cluster onto the single lattice judgment. Internal helper.

engine:verifyMuInduction.label: Verify μ-induction
engine:verifyMuInduction.description: The Park (Knaster-Tarski) kernel rule (decide-substrate Phase 8μ.2 — the first new trusted-kernel rule since verifyWitnessMembership): proves a subset claim `μv.F ⊆ T` by Park induction `F[v:=T] ⊆ T ⟹ μv.F ⊆ T`. Requires s to be a SeMu; gates POSITIVITY (seMuFaceOk — monotone ⇒ the least fixpoint is well-defined ⇒ Park sound); RE-DERIVES the premise F[v:=T] via substSet (never trusts a supplied premise); re-checks it through the ordinary judgment (decideSubset, fuel-bounded). Ok ⇒ SolverChecked on a Just true premise; a Just false (refuted) / Nothing (undecided) premise, or a non-positive / non-SeMu s ⇒ WitnessRejected. SOUND by construction — reads (v, F, T) from the claim, so a bogus proposer premise/witness cannot fool it. Internal helper (the K-native currency; wired at kernel.fenel vpJudgment).

engine:verifyProof.label: Verify proof
engine:verifyProof.description: The kernel's trust-boundary re-checker, Fenel-bodied (expr-substrate Phase 6b0; re-derived onto the one lattice judgment decide-substrate Phase 2). The PRESENTATION DISPATCHER: classifies the proof term via evidenceOfProofTerm (Refl / ReDecide / Sample / Unknown), then Refl proves PropEq via the pre-computed structural-equality facts (the singleton-equality presentation); ReDecide (DecidableSetResult) decomposes the proposition to a JEmpty/JInhabited judgment (judgmentOfProposition) and re-checks it through the single verifyJudgment core (kind↔proposition agreement + witness re-check + the pre-computed tri-precision decision); Sample (SampleTestResult) proves PropForall via the totality gate + propertyId/allPassed/samplesChecked shape checks. Returns a plain-record outcome marker ({ tag = Ok, status } / { tag = Err, etag, reason }); the TS delegate maps it to VerifyResult and grades EpistemicStatus (TS-side output grading, the 6b Q1 lock). Unknown proof-term tags ⇒ the UnknownRule TCB guard.

engine:verifyWitnessMembership.label: Verify witness membership
engine:verifyWitnessMembership.description: The kernel-primary singleton face (decide-substrate Phase 2): proves JInhabited s from a witness w by re-checking {w} ⊆ s via decideSubset (SeEnum [w]) s — membership-as-singleton-subset promoted to a kernel proof rule. Ok ⇒ SolverChecked on Just true; an undecided (Nothing) or refuting (Just false) re-check ⇒ WitnessRejected. SOUND but incomplete for object witnesses (the enum trio's element equality is shallow std eq). Present in the TCB from K1; wired to producers at K2/K3.

engine:virtualFieldsFor.label: field-providers: virtualFieldsFor
engine:virtualFieldsFor.description: Field-identity Phase 3 — list virtual FieldRefs for an explicit provider scope and owner. Binding selection is structural and scope-isolated; readable names are projected only by the caller's registry edge.

engine:vjPolarity.label: verify judgment: polarity decide
engine:vjPolarity.description: decide-substrate Phase 2 — consume the pre-computed tri-precision decision by the judgment's polarity: JEmpty ⇒ Ok SolverChecked on "true" else the recheck WitnessRejected; JInhabited ⇒ Ok SolverChecked on "false" (the inverted arm) else the recheck WitnessRejected. Internal helper.

engine:vjRight.label: verify judgment: right witness
engine:vjRight.description: decide-substrate Phase 2 — the binary-shape (subset/disjoint) second witness-side check: witnessRight must match the proposition's t, then the polarity decision. Internal helper.

engine:vlgAppliedCallStatus.label: Ledger applied call status
engine:vlgAppliedCallStatus.description: The two function-application fences: an overapplication's eta tail, and a single plain-record argument that may be a named-argument application.

engine:vlgAppliedStatus.label: Ledger applied status
engine:vlgAppliedStatus.description: Fence the two saturation shapes whose entering-ness this slice cannot decide: an overapplication (the eta tail enters an unledgered callable) and a single-record underapplication (named arguments expand to positional before the partial check).

engine:vlgBinderNames.label: Ledger binder names
engine:vlgBinderNames.description: Collect the binder names a binding entry list introduces.

engine:vlgBindingForm.label: Ledger binding form
engine:vlgBindingForm.description: Dispatch the three sequentially-scoped binding forms through the shared binding layout.

engine:vlgBindings.label: Ledger bindings
engine:vlgBindings.description: Walk a sequential binding entry list at VpsBinding, threading each binder into scope for the following bindings.

engine:vlgCallOp.label: Ledger call op
engine:vlgCallOp.description: `{call: [callee, ...args]}` - the callee position and actual indices come from the shared call layout. A literal string callee is a direct registered call resolved through the frozen frame; the `$` application vehicle takes its callee from raw slot 1 and bypasses registry resolution, so it is dynamic; a lexically bound {var} callee is DynamicOrReflective; an unbound {var} callee resolves through the frozen frame.

engine:vlgCalleeRow.label: Ledger callee row
engine:vlgCalleeRow.description: Classify a call layout callee into its ledger row: a direct string target, the `$` application vehicle (dynamic - the runtime bypasses registry resolution), a lexically bound name (dynamic), a dotted data-dependent path (dynamic), or a frozen-frame resolution of an indirect name.

engine:vlgClassifyRoot.label: Classify primitive root
engine:vlgClassifyRoot.description: The fail-closed inventory classifier: missing active handler, convert-to-Fenel, non-ground scheme, unattested, and negative-claim cases all fence before any root is required.

engine:vlgClassifyRoots.label: Classify primitive roots
engine:vlgClassifyRoots.description: Apply the inventory classifier to every row, replacing each row's classification slot.

engine:vlgConcatNames.label: Ledger concat names
engine:vlgConcatNames.description: Append every name of the second list to the first.

engine:vlgConstructOp.label: Ledger construct op
engine:vlgConstructOp.description: `{construct: [ctor, ...]}` - the constructor occurrence resolves to its owner-exact semantic target through the frozen frame (never a short wire tag); the payload shape comes from the shared constructor layout.

engine:vlgConstructPayload.label: Ledger construct payload
engine:vlgConstructPayload.description: Walk a constructor payload from the shared layout. The named-versus-positional reading needs the constructor table a pure body lacks, so this consumer walks the UNION of both published readings whenever the named one is live. Choosing one was an under-report: for a one-field op-shaped payload the positional reading walks argument 0 only while the runtime named branch evaluates the whole field value.

engine:vlgCountClass.label: Count root class
engine:vlgCountClass.description: Count inventory rows in one classification bucket (convert / required / fenced).

engine:vlgDoItems.label: Ledger do items
engine:vlgDoItems.description: The do-list worker: an item carrying a `let` KEY has ONLY its binding values walked, in sequential scope, and its binders thread forward; every other item is an ordinary expression at VpsSeq. The runtime never evaluates an inline-let item siblings, so neither does this walk.

engine:vlgDoOp.label: Ledger do op
engine:vlgDoOp.description: `{do: [...]}` - a FLAT statement list walked at VpsSeq (never re-nested into SLet/SDo). An item carrying a `let` key injects its binders forward into the local scope, matching the runtime.

engine:vlgDotFrom.label: Ledger dot scan
engine:vlgDotFrom.description: Scan a spelling for a `.` separator, terminating on an exhausted slice rather than a code-point length (slice indexes UTF-16 units; length counts code points).

engine:vlgDynamicRow.label: Ledger dynamic row
engine:vlgDynamicRow.description: Build a DynamicOrReflective row with its stable classifier reason. Such a row always fences validation.

engine:vlgEnters.label: Ledger enters target
engine:vlgEnters.description: True when a saturated application actually enters the target (supplied >= declared arity). An unknown arity fails closed.

engine:vlgEnvWith.label: Ledger env with binders
engine:vlgEnvWith.description: Rebuild the ledger walk environment with a replacement lexical binder list.

engine:vlgFnOp.label: Ledger fn op
engine:vlgFnOp.description: `{fn: [...]}` - the lambda parameter spellings enter lexical scope and the body is walked at VpsLambdaBody, both taken from the shared lambda layout. Closes two defects: the canonical form no longer drops a non-literal parameter entry (the runtime binds its string coercion), and a flat array parameter is ONE binder under its coerced spelling rather than several.

engine:vlgFormOp.label: Ledger form op
engine:vlgFormOp.description: Dispatch one KNOWN_OP by the shared decomposition's closed semantic form. Replaces four local predicate tables that duplicated the evaluator's classification; the schedule now comes from `fdcOpSchedule`, which is the single table.

engine:vlgHasBinderPath.label: Ledger has binder path
engine:vlgHasBinderPath.description: True when a lexical binder is the name or a dotted-path root of it (`b` binds `b.f`), mirroring the runtime's `resolveVar` field projection.

engine:vlgIntrinsicForm.label: Ledger intrinsic form
engine:vlgIntrinsicForm.description: The lazy and eager intrinsic ops: one exact versioned language-rule row plus the SCHEDULED argument slots. Never a certificate-bearing function edge.

engine:vlgIntrinsicRow.label: Ledger intrinsic row
engine:vlgIntrinsicRow.description: Build an intrinsic-rule row for an exact versioned language form (lazy or eager KNOWN_OP).

engine:vlgIsBuiltinOpNative.label: Ledger builtin op native
engine:vlgIsBuiltinOpNative.description: The registry-less BUILTIN_OP_NATIVES fallback set (codeName and notation keys). Consulted only on a frozen-frame miss; yields an intrinsic rule, never a function edge.

engine:vlgIsDotted.label: Ledger is dotted
engine:vlgIsDotted.description: True when a variable spelling contains a `.` path separator.

engine:vlgIsOperatorNotation.label: Ledger operator notation
engine:vlgIsOperatorNotation.description: True for a parser operator/template spelling (`+`, `==`, `cat`, `!`, …). Records template origin; never rewrites the raw key.

engine:vlgJoinClauses.label: Join refuted clauses
engine:vlgJoinClauses.description: Render a closed refutation-clause list as a comma-separated string for the fence reason. Internal helper.

engine:vlgKeyAsFnId.label: Ledger key as fnId
engine:vlgKeyAsFnId.description: The universal key-as-fnId call form, decided by RESOLUTION exactly as the runtime does: the frozen frame first (registry precedence), then the builtin-op-native intrinsic fallback, then the unresolved fallback the shared plan attached. The raw key is never rewritten to a codeName.

engine:vlgKnownOrigin.label: Ledger known origin
engine:vlgKnownOrigin.description: The closed set of non-Fenel implementation origins this inventory admits.

engine:vlgLedger.label: Validation use ledger
engine:vlgLedger.description: Walk one RAW stored body (the marshalled JsonLogic ADT) into the complete signature-use ledger. Faithful to the runtime evaluator: array literals are literals (no invented appendItem edges), lazy structural ops stay intrinsic, key-as-fnId resolves by resolution not value shape, raw runtime keys are preserved verbatim, `$tag` values are inert, and patterns contribute binders but no uses. Resolution consumes the FROZEN source frame only — a negative row fences and is never retried through another resolver. INERT in slice 2: mints no authority and is consumed by no judgment path.

engine:vlgLetOp.label: Ledger let op
engine:vlgLetOp.description: `{let: {...}}` - sequential bindings, each value walked at its VpsBinding segment with the preceding binders in scope. No separate body at rest (the runtime result is the last binding). A carrier the shared layout reports NOT TOTAL fences rather than silently binding nothing.

engine:vlgLookupArity.label: Ledger lookup arity
engine:vlgLookupArity.description: Look a target's declared parameter count up in the supplied arity table.

engine:vlgLookupRoute.label: Ledger lookup route
engine:vlgLookupRoute.description: Look one spelling up in the frozen source frame. This is the ONLY resolution path available to validation.

engine:vlgMatchArm.label: Ledger match arm
engine:vlgMatchArm.description: One match arm: the pattern binder set (or a fence when it is not total), then the guard condition, then the body, both in the arm-extended scope.

engine:vlgMatchArms.label: Ledger match arms
engine:vlgMatchArms.description: Walk the shared layout arms: pattern binders, then the guard at VpsArmGuard, then the body at VpsArmBody. An arm whose binder writes are not TOTAL fences rather than contributing a partial binder set - under-binding misses a shadow and over-binding erases an evidence edge.

engine:vlgMatchOp.label: Ledger match op
engine:vlgMatchOp.description: `{match: [scrut, p1, b1, ...]}` - scrutinee at VpsScrutinee (and NOT walked at all below two arguments, where the runtime returns before evaluating it); patterns contribute BINDERS but no uses; a guarded arm on EITHER carrier walks its condition at VpsArmGuard and its body at VpsArmBody; a lone trailing element is the default arm body.

engine:vlgMethodOp.label: Ledger method op
engine:vlgMethodOp.description: `{method: [class, method, ...]}` - qualified capability dispatch is ALWAYS ScopeDependentDispatch in this phase (no concrete scope snapshot); no provider, handler, or dictionary datum supplies dependency evidence. The two leading slots are raw names the runtime never evaluates.
